title: filter cross-language INFERRED calls in Surprising Connections (#630)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #630.

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s "Surprising Connections" section can promote impossible cross-language `INFERRED calls` edges (e.g. a Python helper named `normalize` linked to a TypeScript handler with a colliding name) over real, mundane edges, because `_surprise_score` rewards `INFERRED` confidence and cross-file location without checking whether the source/target language pair is plausible.

This PR filters those edges in `_cross_file_surprises()` unless an explicit import bridge between the two source files provides interop evidence.

## Approach

- Added a `_LANG_ECOSYSTEM` map grouping freely-interoperable extensions: TS/JS family, JVM (Java/Kotlin/Scala), C/C++/ObjC. Same-ecosystem inferred calls remain untouched.
- Added `_bridged_file_pairs(G)` which collects source-file pairs connected by `imports` / `imports_from` edges — concrete evidence the two files actually interop (FFI, generated bindings, configured bridge, etc.).
- In `_cross_file_surprises`, skip an edge when **all** of the following hold:
  - `relation == "calls"`
  - `confidence == "INFERRED"`
  - the two source files are in different ecosystems
  - no import edge connects the two files

This preserves the underlying graph as an audit artifact (the edge is still there for tooling that wants it) while keeping the report's first-pass navigation signal cleaner. AMBIGUOUS edges, EXTRACTED edges, semantic-similarity edges, and same-ecosystem inferred calls are all unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression test: Python→TypeScript `INFERRED calls` with no bridge is filtered out of Surprising Connections.
- [x] New regression test: cross-language `INFERRED calls` with an `imports` edge between the source files is kept (interop is plausible).
- [x] New regression test: TS↔JS `INFERRED calls` (same ecosystem) is kept.
- [x] Full suite green: `444 passed`.

title: boost exact-match seeds and stop hubs hijacking query output
body:
## What

`_score_nodes` gets an `EXACT_MATCH_BONUS` for terms that equal a node's `norm_label` (or `norm_label` with trailing `()` stripped, since the AST extractor emits function labels as `foo()`), and `_subgraph_to_text` accepts an optional `seeds` arg so the rendered output emits seeds first in score order before the BFS expansion sorted by degree desc.

## Why

Single-token identifier queries — by far the most common usage — get buried under high-degree hub modules. Two issues compound:

1. `_score_nodes` only used substring matching, so the seed function and every sibling that mentioned the symbol tied at score 1; ties broke alphabetically on node id.
2. `_subgraph_to_text` always re-sorted the rendered nodes by `G.degree(n)` descending, so even when `_score_nodes` returned the right seed, the hub it expanded into (e.g. `app.js`, `controller.js`) always rendered first.

### Before

```
$ graphify query "pasteFromClipboard" --budget 600
NODE app.js [src=frontend/app.js loc=L1 community=3]
NODE now() [src=frontend/modules/core/perf.js loc=L1 community=1]
NODE .filter() [src=backend/tests/_fake_inventory.py loc=L80 community=6]
NODE draw() [src=frontend/app.js loc=L4047 community=3]
NODE FakeInventoryQuery [src=backend/tests/_fake_inventory.py loc=L18 community=1]
...
```

`pasteFromClipboard()` does not appear in the first 30 NODE lines on a ~6k-node graph.

### After

```
$ graphify query "pasteFromClipboard" --budget 600
NODE pasteFromClipboard() [src=frontend/app.js loc=L4847 community=3]
NODE app.js [src=frontend/app.js loc=L1 community=3]
NODE now() [src=frontend/modules/core/perf.js loc=L1 community=1]
...
```

## Scope of behavior change

- `seeds=None` in `_subgraph_to_text` preserves the previous degree-desc ordering exactly. The only call sites updated to pass `seeds=` are `_tool_query_graph` (MCP) and the `query` CLI handler in `__main__.py`. `_tool_shortest_path` and the `path` CLI use `_score_nodes` only for endpoint resolution and do not render via `_subgraph_to_text`, so they automatically benefit from the bonus without further changes.
- Multi-term / prose queries are unaffected because the bonus only fires on `term == norm_label` exactly. Substring scoring is untouched.
- `EXACT_MATCH_BONUS = 100.0` swamps any plausible substring sum (substring score caps at ~1.5/term).

## Tests

Six new cases in `tests/test_serve.py`:

- `test_score_nodes_exact_match_beats_substring` — exact match outranks substring distractors on the same graph.
- `test_score_nodes_exact_match_strips_function_parens` — `saveDiagram()` matches term `savediagram`.
- `test_score_nodes_exact_match_no_false_positive` — unrelated term still returns no matches.
- `test_subgraph_to_text_seeds_render_first` — seed before hub when `seeds=[...]`.
- `test_subgraph_to_text_no_seeds_preserves_legacy_order` — `seeds=None` matches no-arg call (back-compat guard) and hub still wins on degree.
- `test_query_pipeline_exact_match_ranks_above_hub` — end-to-end `_score_nodes -> _bfs -> _subgraph_to_text(seeds=...)`.

Full suite (447 tests) green.

title: Add --force flag (and GRAPHIFY_FORCE env var) to graphify update + git hooks
body:
## Summary

The node-count safety check in `to_json` (added in #479) refuses to overwrite `graph.json` when the rebuild has fewer nodes. The warning text directs users to *\"Pass force=True to override\"* — but `force` was only reachable from the Python API, with **no CLI escape hatch**.

This is painful for legitimate shrinks: refactors that delete or rename packages produce a smaller graph by design. Without a CLI flag, users get stuck unless they monkey-patch `to_json`.

## Changes

- `watch._rebuild_code`: accept `force` kwarg, propagate to `to_json`.
- `__main__` update handler: parse `--force`; also honor `GRAPHIFY_FORCE` env var.
- Hooks (post-commit + post-checkout): honor `GRAPHIFY_FORCE` env var, so automated rebuilds can opt in without editing the hook script. (Useful when a refactor PR's commit triggers the post-commit hook.)
- Help text updated.

## Reproduction (before this PR)

```bash
# After a refactor that legitimately deletes packages:
$ graphify update .
[graphify] WARNING: new graph has 1125 nodes but existing graph.json has 1139.
  Refusing to overwrite — you may be missing chunk files from a previous session.
  Pass force=True to override.
Nothing to update or rebuild failed — check output above.

# No CLI flag accepted:
$ graphify update . --force
(same warning — flag silently ignored)

$ FORCE=1 graphify update .
(same warning)
```

The only escape was a Python monkey-patch:

```python
import graphify.export as ex
orig = ex.to_json
ex.to_json = lambda *a, **k: orig(*a, force=True)
```

## After this PR

```bash
$ graphify update . --force
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 1125 nodes, 1591 edges, 90 communities
[graphify watch] graph.json, graph.html and GRAPH_REPORT.md updated in graphify-out

# or
$ GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1 graphify update .
(same — works)

# or for the post-commit hook:
$ GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1 git commit -m \"refactor: delete dead package\"
(rebuild succeeds, no manual intervention)
```

## Tested

Verified all three paths against a real corpus (200 files, ~187k words) on macOS / Python 3.12:

- No flag → still refuses (existing behavior preserved)
- `--force` → overwrites cleanly
- `GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1` → overwrites cleanly
- Help text shows the new option

## Test plan

- [ ] `graphify update . --force` overwrites a smaller graph
- [ ] `GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1 graphify update .` overwrites a smaller graph
- [ ] `graphify update .` (no flag) still refuses on shrink — safety preserved
- [ ] `GRAPHIFY_FORCE=1` honored by the post-commit hook script

## Notes

- Watch mode (`graphify watch`) intentionally **not** changed. The continuous file watcher is incremental by nature; forcing every rebuild would defeat the safety check entirely. If desired in a follow-up PR, it can read `GRAPHIFY_FORCE` at startup.
- Closes the gap referenced by the warning text in #479.

title: Add a true OpenCode semantic extraction backend in graphify/llm.py
body:
## Summary
Graphify currently supports OpenCode as a platform install and assistant-skill orchestration path, but not as a true direct semantic backend in `graphify/llm.py`.

Today:
- `graphify/llm.py` supports `claude` and `kimi`
- `graphify/skill-opencode.md` uses OpenCode agent orchestration
- `graphify update` remains AST-only
- OpenCode install writes `AGENTS.md` plus a bash-only plugin reminder

This leaves a gap for OpenCode users who want a first-class direct semantic backend, similar to the current direct backend layer, without depending on Claude-specific auth or the assistant-skill path.

## Motivation
- OpenCode is already a documented first-class platform in Graphify.
- The current architecture has an asymmetry: OpenCode exists as orchestration/install support, but not as a direct backend entry in `graphify/llm.py`.
- The current code/comments/docs can be confusing because backend capability, assistant orchestration, and AST-only update behavior are described in different places.

## Proposed Solution
Add `backend="opencode"` to `graphify/llm.py` as a direct semantic extraction backend.

MVP scope:
- Implement the backend via `opencode run --format json`
- Reuse the existing `_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM` and `_read_files(...)` prompt-building flow
- Parse OpenCode JSON event streams and extract the final assistant `text` payload
- Pass that payload through the existing `_parse_llm_json(...)` normalization path
- Keep `extract_corpus_parallel(...)` behavior unchanged apart from supporting the new backend

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `graphify.llm.extract_files_direct(..., backend="opencode")` returns valid Graphify extraction fragments
- [ ] `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(..., backend="opencode")` works with existing chunk merge behavior and callbacks
- [ ] Subprocess failure, missing CLI, missing text payload, and malformed JSON outputs fail with deterministic errors
- [ ] README and OpenCode skill docs clearly distinguish direct backend support from assistant orchestration and from AST-only `graphify update`
- [ ] Tests cover success and failure cases for the new backend transport

## Non-Goals
- Do not implement `opencode serve` in the first PR
- Do not redesign `graphify update` into a full semantic-update CLI
- Do not rely on `--file` / `--attach` in the MVP transport
- Do not remove the existing `skill-opencode.md` orchestration path

## Alternatives Considered
- `opencode serve` / SDK transport first: more moving parts, larger scope
- Keep OpenCode as skill-only orchestration: preserves the current backend gap
- Attachment-based transport: local validation suggests inline prompt text is the safer first step

## Notes
During local validation, `opencode run --format json --pure --dangerously-skip-permissions` already produced a machine-readable JSON event stream with a final `text` event, which makes it a plausible MVP transport.

Also worth noting: `graphify/llm.py` comments currently imply a public direct-backend usage path, but the visible CLI path in `__main__.py` does not currently expose a general `--backend` switch. If maintainers agree, this issue can stay scoped to the backend-layer MVP and leave CLI exposure/docs cleanup as follow-up or adjacent work.

title: Enhance pipx support, fix PowerShell output, and update documentation
Enhancement: Decouple .graphifyignore discovery from .git boundaries
body:
The current ```_load_graphifyignore``` implementation relies exclusively on the presence of a ```.git/``` directory to stop its upward search for ignore rules.

### The Problem
Currently, ```graphify``` assumes that every project is managed by Git. If a user runs the tool on a directory that is not a Git repository (e.g., a simple folder of research papers or a project using Mercurial/SVN), the logic will:

1. Continue climbing the directory tree past the intended project folder.

2. Potentially reach the user's home directory or the filesystem root.

3. Accidentally pick up and apply ```.graphifyignore``` rules from unrelated projects found higher up in the hierarchy.

This makes the tool less predictable when used outside of a strictly Git-centric workflow.

title: [ENH] Refactor .graphifyignore engine to match .gitignore semantics
body:
This replaces the ```fnmatch```-based ignore logic with a robust matching engine that maintains functional parity to .gitignore. This resolves Issue #628 by supporting ordered negation (!).

### Features & Enhancements

1. Full GitWildMatch Semantics
The new engine moves beyond simple string matching to a regex-based compiler that supports the full Git specification:
- Ordered Negation (!): Implements "last-match-wins" logic, allowing users to broadly exclude paths and re-include vetted exceptions.
- Recursive Wildcards (`/`):** Correctly handles zero or more directory segments.
- Path Anchoring: Distinguishes between root-anchored patterns (/main.py) and unanchored global patterns (main.py).
- Directory-Only Matching: Respects trailing slashes (e.g., vendor/) to match only directories while leaving files with the same name included.
- Character Classes: Full support for bracket expressions ([abc], [!abc]) and POSIX classes ([[:alpha:]], [[:digit:]]).

2. High-Performance Traversal
Optimization of the discovery and extraction loops to handle repositories efficiently:
-  In-Place Pruning: Both detect.py and extract.py now prune dirnames in-place during os.walk. Massive ignored subtrees (like node_modules/ or vendor/) are skipped at the structural level rather than being traversed and filtered per-file.
- Redundant Stat Removal: The ignore checker now accepts an explicit is_dir flag. By passing is_dir=False for confirmed files, we eliminate unnecessary filesystem stat() calls during deep scans.

3. Bug Fixes & Alignment
-  Memory Re-indexing Fix: Resolved a conflict where ```graphify-out/memory/``` files were being incorrectly ignored. These are now explicitly exempted so the graph can always learn from past query results.
- Watcher Alignment: The file watcher (```watch.py```) now respects ```.graphifyignore```, preventing redundant graph rebuilds when ignored files change.
-  Whitespace Integrity: Ported Git's exact ```trim_trailing_spaces``` to handle backslash-escaped trailing spaces correctly.

Verification Results
- Conformance Suite: Added tests/test_ignore_rules.py covering anchoring, negation chains, and directory pruning.
- Unit Tests: Updated tests/test_detect.py to verify the new engine against standard ignore categories.

title: fix(detect): hermetic .graphifyignore discovery + correct gitignore   semantics
body:
Refines 6b68de1 and 8a6306f. Closes #643. Related to #628. Adding on from #644 
 
 ### Features implemented:

- **No-VCS ceiling**: when no VCS root is found, the walk stops at the scan root, not the home directory. The home guard still allows leakage across sibling projects under a shared workspace (`~/work/project-alpha` picking up `~/work/.graphifyignore`). Stopping at the scan root eliminates that entirely.

- **Correct pattern ordering**: parent `.graphifyignore` patterns are evaluated outermost-first so inner (closer) patterns win via
  last-match-wins. The prior ordering let VCS-root patterns override a file's own `.graphifyignore`.

- **Escaped trailing spaces preserved**:  `line.strip()` silently drops `vendor\ ` patterns. Replaced with `rstrip()` + escape-awareness so `vendor\ ` correctly matches a path named `vendor ` (per gitignore spec).

- **`\]` escape**: `]` was missing from the backslash-escape set in `_pattern_to_regex`; `\]` was being converted to a path separator
  instead of a literal `]`.

- **Anchored pattern misfire**: a leading-slash pattern (e.g. `/vendor/`) in a parent `.graphifyignore` was incorrectly matching `src/vendor/` when `detect()` was called on `src/`. Added a guard so anchored patterns only evaluate relative to their own anchor directory, not the scan root.

title: post-commit/post-checkout hooks block git for the duration of full rebuild — should detach
body:
## Problem

The `post-commit` and `post-checkout` hooks installed by `graphify hook install` run the rebuild **synchronously** — `git commit` (and `git checkout`) does not return until the full repo rebuild completes.

On a moderately large repo (~9k files), the rebuild can take several hours. While it runs:

- `git commit` blocks the developer's shell for the entire duration
- Any tooling that triggers a commit (Claude Code, IDE hooks, automation) stalls or holds open file descriptors
- A subsequent commit before the prior rebuild finishes silently queues another rebuild on the same files

**Reproduction (frank-ai-brain, ~9k files):**

```
$ time git commit -m "..."
[graphify hook] N file(s) changed - rebuilding graph...
  AST extraction: 1/8903 files (0%)
  ...
[blocks for 4+ hours]
```

`ps aux` showed the rebuild process accumulating 256+ CPU minutes while the parent `git commit` was still waiting on it.

## Why this matters

A post-commit hook should not block the developer's workflow. The rebuild is producing observability output (`graphify-out/`), not state needed by the next git command. Stalling the developer to update an out-of-band artifact violates the principle that side effects belong out of band.

## Suggested fix

Detach the rebuild so the hook returns immediately and the rebuild orphans into the background. Standard portable shell idiom: `nohup ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null &` followed by `disown`.

Patch against [`graphify/hooks.py`](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/blob/main/graphify/hooks.py) `_HOOK_SCRIPT`:

```diff
 export GRAPHIFY_CHANGED="$CHANGED"
-$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON -c "
+
+# Run rebuild detached so the commit returns immediately. Full repo rebuild
+# can take hours; blocking the post-commit hook stalls every commit.
+LOG_FILE="$HOME/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log"
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")"
+echo "[graphify hook] launching background rebuild (log: $LOG_FILE)"
+nohup $GRAPHIFY_PYTHON -c "
 import os, sys
 from pathlib import Path

 changed_raw = os.environ.get('GRAPHIFY_CHANGED', '')
 changed = [Path(f.strip()) for f in changed_raw.strip().splitlines() if f.strip()]

 if not changed:
     sys.exit(0)

 print(f'[graphify hook] {len(changed)} file(s) changed - rebuilding graph...')

 try:
     from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code
     _rebuild_code(Path('.'))
 except Exception as exc:
     print(f'[graphify hook] Rebuild failed: {exc}')
     sys.exit(1)
-"
+" > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
+disown 2>/dev/null || true
 # graphify-hook-end
```

Same change for `_CHECKOUT_SCRIPT`. The rebuild's stdout/stderr go to `~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log` (truncated each run) so users can `tail -f` it for status.

## Result of applying this patch locally

```
$ time git commit -m "..."
[graphify hook] launching background rebuild (log: /Users/.../.cache/graphify-rebuild.log)
[branch hash] commit message
real    0m0.137s
```

Down from 4+ hours to 137 ms. Background rebuild continues independently and writes the graph as before.

## Optional follow-ups

1. **Lock file** — `~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.lock` to prevent two rebuilds from racing if commits land back-to-back.
2. **Incremental rebuild** — if `_rebuild_code` already supports incremental updates, the changed-file list (`GRAPHIFY_CHANGED`) could feed it directly instead of re-walking the whole tree. Would obsolete most of the runtime issue.
3. **Opt-in flag** — `graphify hook install --detached` (default) vs `--blocking` for users who want CI-style commit gating.

Happy to open a PR if the patch shape works for you.

title: graphify update / post-commit hook drops code-file semantic nodes and is then blocked by to_json safety check
body:
## Summary

After a full `/graphify .` run, subsequent invocations of `graphify update <path>`, the post-commit hook, and the post-checkout hook all silently no-op with:

> [graphify] WARNING: new graph has X nodes but existing graph.json has Y. Refusing to overwrite — you may be missing chunk files from a previous session. Pass force=True to override.
> Nothing to update or rebuild failed — check output above.

## Repro

1. Build a graph with the full pipeline so it contains semantic edges on code files: `/graphify .` (this dispatches LLM subagents that produce nodes with `file_type=\"code\"` plus INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS edges).
2. Touch any code file (or `git pull` a code change) so the AST output is slightly different from before.
3. Run `graphify update .`, or commit so the post-commit hook fires.

Observed in v0.6.2 on a Python + TypeScript + Swift project:
- Full run: 4,121 nodes (2,618 AST + 1,503 semantic, ~1,400 of which had `file_type=\"code\"` because subagents extracted call/data-flow edges that AST cannot see).
- After `graphify update .`: 2,981 nodes — the ~1,400 code-typed semantic nodes are gone. Safety check fires, write refused, hook reports failure.

## Root cause

`graphify/watch.py:_rebuild_code` lines 65–82 try to preserve semantic data:

\`\`\`python
existing = json.loads(existing_graph.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
code_ids = {n[\"id\"] for n in existing.get(\"nodes\", []) if n.get(\"file_type\") == \"code\"}
sem_nodes = [n for n in existing.get(\"nodes\", []) if n.get(\"file_type\") != \"code\"]
sem_edges = [e for e in existing.get(\"links\", existing.get(\"edges\", []))
             if e.get(\"confidence\") in (\"INFERRED\", \"AMBIGUOUS\")
             or (e.get(\"source\") not in code_ids and e.get(\"target\") not in code_ids)]
\`\`\`

The filter \`n.get(\"file_type\") != \"code\"\` drops every semantic node whose source happens to be a code file. In practice that is most of the value of the LLM pass — INFERRED call/data-flow edges and the nodes they connect live exclusively on code files.

Then at \`graphify/export.py:300-314\`, \`to_json\`'s post-#479 safety check correctly notices the new graph is smaller and refuses to overwrite. The hook returns failure. The user sees no obvious indication that the graph is now stale; subsequent \`graphify query\` answers from the old graph until they re-run the full pipeline.

## Suggested fix

Filter by \`source_file\`, not \`file_type\`. Keep semantic nodes/edges from files that were not re-extracted in this rebuild. Roughly:

\`\`\`python
new_ast_ids = {n[\"id\"] for n in result[\"nodes\"]}
preserved_nodes = [n for n in existing.get(\"nodes\", [])
                   if n[\"id\"] not in new_ast_ids]
preserved_node_ids = {n[\"id\"] for n in preserved_nodes}
all_node_ids = new_ast_ids | preserved_node_ids
preserved_edges = [
    e for e in existing.get(\"links\", existing.get(\"edges\", []))
    if e.get(\"source\") in all_node_ids and e.get(\"target\") in all_node_ids
]
\`\`\`

Or, more surgically: use \`detect_incremental\` to identify only changed files, AST-extract just those, and replace nodes whose \`source_file\` matches — keeping every other node and edge intact. This is what the \`--update\` flow documented in \`skill.md\` actually does, but \`_rebuild_code\` does not. The post-commit/post-checkout hooks would benefit most from this surgical path.

## Workaround

Manual incremental update — read \`graph.json\`, AST-extract only changed files via \`detect_incremental\`, remove old nodes by \`source_file\`, add new ones, write with \`to_json(..., force=True)\`. Working code:

\`\`\`python
from graphify.detect import detect_incremental
from graphify.extract import collect_files, extract
from networkx.readwrite import json_graph
import json
from pathlib import Path

result = detect_incremental(Path(\".\"))
ROOT = Path(\".\").resolve()

ast_files = []
for f in result.get(\"new_files\", {}).get(\"code\", []):
    p = Path(f)
    ast_files.extend(collect_files(p) if p.is_dir() else [p])

ast = extract(ast_files, cache_root=Path(\".\"))
data = json.loads(Path(\"graphify-out/graph.json\").read_text())
G = json_graph.node_link_graph(data, edges=\"links\")

changed_rel = {str(Path(f).resolve().relative_to(ROOT)) for f in ast_files}
to_remove = [n for n, d in G.nodes(data=True) if d.get(\"source_file\") in changed_rel]
G.remove_nodes_from(to_remove)

for n in ast[\"nodes\"]:
    G.add_node(n[\"id\"], **{k: v for k, v in n.items() if k != \"id\"})
for e in ast[\"edges\"]:
    if e[\"source\"] in G and e[\"target\"] in G:
        G.add_edge(e[\"source\"], e[\"target\"], **{k: v for k, v in e.items() if k not in (\"source\",\"target\")})

# write back; preserved semantic nodes/edges remain intact
\`\`\`

After this, \`G\` has all original semantic nodes plus refreshed AST for the changed files, and the safety check passes because node count holds steady or grows.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.6.2 (\`uv tool install graphifyy\`)
- Python 3.13, macOS 14 (Darwin 25.4.0)

title: feat: implement parallel AST extraction with benchmarking support
body:
## Description
Parallelizes AST extraction in `extract()` using `ProcessPoolExecutor` to eliminate the CPU bottleneck on large repositories. 

`importlib.import_module` holds the Python GIL, so processes were chosen over threads to ensure true parallelism.

## Changes
- **Parallel Dispatch**: Refactored `extract()` to split cached vs. uncached files upfront. If `uncached >= 20` (to account for ~50ms process spawn overhead), extraction is dispatched to a process pool.
- **Pickle-safe Workers**: Moved the extractor dispatch dictionary (`_DISPATCH`) and the worker function (`_extract_single_file`) to the module level so they can be pickled by the executor.
- **API Continuity**: Added `parallel=True` and `max_workers=None` as keyword-only arguments to `extract()`. Existing callers are fully backward compatible. Defaults to `min(os.cpu_count() or 4, num_files, 8)` workers to prevent memory explosion.
- **Benchmark Script**: Added `tests/bench_extract.py` to measure sequential vs parallel time and validate identical node/edge counts.

## Performance
Measured via `uv run python tests/bench_extract.py .` on the graphify repo itself (84 files):
- **Sequential**: 0.77s
- **Parallel (8 workers)**: 0.46s
- **Speedup**: 1.66x

*Note: Speedup scales non-linearly with repo size. Expect 3-5x on 1k+ file repos where process spawn overhead is negligible relative to parsing time.*

## Testing
- Automated tests pass (`442 passed`) with zero regressions.
- Validated that parallel execution produces identical `nodes` and `edges` output (order-agnostic) as sequential execution.

title: save_semantic_cache crashes on directory-path source_file (IsADirectoryError)
body:
**Where:** `graphify/cache.py:31` — `file_hash` calls `Path.read_bytes()` on `p`, but `save_semantic_cache` (around line 166) only checks `p.exists()` before calling `save_cached`. When a node's `source_file` resolves to a directory (e.g. a folder inside a vault corpus), `p.exists()` returns True, and `read_bytes` raises `IsADirectoryError`.

**Version:** graphify 0.4.23 (pipx-installed `graphifyy` package).

**Reproduction:**
\`\`\`python
from graphify.cache import save_semantic_cache
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
    root = Path(root)
    (root / "subdir").mkdir()
    nodes = [{"id": "n", "label": "L", "source_file": str(root / "subdir")}]
    save_semantic_cache(nodes, [], root=root)  # IsADirectoryError on 0.4.23
\`\`\`

**Fix shape:** in `save_semantic_cache`, replace `p.exists()` with `p.is_file()` so directory-path nodes are skipped silently. Single-line change. Surfaced during a 232-node / 389-edge run on a multi-folder corpus where a few nodes had directory-shaped source paths.

title: sanitize_label crashes on None source_file (TypeError) — to_html falls over for graphs containing null source_file values
body:
**Where:** `graphify/security.py:200` — `_CONTROL_CHAR_RE.sub("", text)`. When `text` is `None` (e.g. a node entered `graph.json` with `source_file: null`), the regex `sub` call raises `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object`. `to_html` calls `sanitize_label(data.get("source_file", ""))` in `export.py`, but `dict.get` returns `None` if the key is present with a `None` value — the default `""` is only used when the key is absent.

**Version:** graphify 0.4.23 (pipx-installed `graphifyy` package).

**Reproduction:**
\`\`\`python
from graphify.security import sanitize_label
sanitize_label(None)  # TypeError on 0.4.23
\`\`\`

**Fix shape:** at the top of `sanitize_label`, return `""` if `text is None`. Annotate the parameter as `str | None` to make the contract explicit. Single-function change. Protects every call site (export.py, serve.py) without per-site `or ""` clutter.

Surfaced during a real run where 42 of the graph nodes had `source_file: null` (rationale-shaped nodes inferred during chunk extraction) — `to_html` crashed before HTML export could complete.

title: Chunk-extraction prompt omits rationale from valid file_types — model hallucinates 'concept' on every doc/paper run
body:
**Where:** `graphify/skill.md` (and per-IDE variants `skill-claw.md`, `skill-codex.md`, etc.) around line 305 — the JSON schema example for chunks lists `"file_type":"code|document|paper|image"`, omitting `rationale` even though `validate.py:VALID_FILE_TYPES` accepts it. The prompt earlier (around line 267) describes rationale extraction in prose but never declares the file_type. The model fills the gap by inventing `concept`, which the validator rejects on every node.

**Version:** graphify 0.4.23 (pipx-installed `graphifyy` package). Observed: **112 `concept` warnings on a single multi-folder vault run**.

**Fix shape:**
1. In the schema example, change `"code|document|paper|image"` → `"code|document|paper|image|rationale"`.
2. In the prose at the doc/paper-files bullet, add: "Use `file_type:'rationale'` for concept-like nodes (ideas, principles, mechanisms, patterns). Do NOT invent new file_types like `concept` — the only valid values are `code|document|paper|image|rationale`."

Lower-blast-radius than expanding `VALID_FILE_TYPES` because it leaves the validation surface unchanged.

title: cost.json always reports 0 tokens — chunk JSON placeholders never overwritten with real Agent usage values
body:
**Where:** `graphify/skill.md` Step B3 (around line 308). The subagent's chunk JSON template includes `"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0` because the subagent cannot know its own token usage. The orchestrator (parent Claude) DOES receive `usage.input_tokens` / `usage.output_tokens` in the Agent tool result for each chunk, but the skill never tells the orchestrator to write those back into the chunk JSON before merging. The merge step (around line 340) reads `new.get('input_tokens', 0)` — which is the placeholder zero — and writes `0` into `cost.json`.

**Version:** graphify 0.4.23 (pipx-installed `graphifyy` package).

**Symptom:** A real run reported 0 tokens for ~332K of consumption (162,904 input on chunk 1 + 169,595 input on chunk 2 per the Agent tool's actual usage values).

**Fix shape:**
1. New bullet at Step B3 telling the orchestrator to overwrite each `.graphify_chunk_NN.json`'s `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` with the real Agent tool result values before merging.
2. New explicit Python merge block that globs `.graphify_chunk_*.json`, sums `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` across chunks, and writes the aggregate to `.graphify_semantic_new.json`. Previously the merge step was implicit and the tokens were dropped.

Smoke-tested locally with two synthetic chunk JSONs holding 162,904 + 169,595 input tokens — output: `Merged 2 chunks: 332499 in / 9999 out tokens`.

title: Kotlin call-walker: accept both `simple_identifier` and `identifier`
body:
`extract_kotlin` previously emitted zero `calls` edges (and zero `raw_calls` entries) on the current PyPI grammar. The Kotlin branch of `walk_calls` only matched node type `simple_identifier`, but PyPI's `tree_sitter_kotlin` produces `identifier` for the equivalent plain-identifier node. The `simple_identifier` ↔ `identifier` rename is a generation gap between tree-sitter-kotlin grammar versions — older forks (and the JVM `io.github.bonede:tree-sitter-kotlin` binding) still use `simple_identifier`.

Accept both names so the extractor works across grammar generations. Also widens `_KOTLIN_CONFIG.name_fallback_child_types` for the same reason (defensive — currently the `name` field path covers class/function name resolution, but if that field is dropped in a future grammar update the fallback would face the same rename).

Tested against `tests/fixtures/sample.kt`: edges go from 6 (file-contains + class-method only) to 10 (adds 4 in-file `calls` edges resolved by the walker:
  - .get() → .buildRequest() @ L8
  - .post() → .buildRequest() @ L12
  - createClient() → Config @ L21
  - createClient() → HttpClient @ L22).

A new regression test `test_kotlin_emits_in_file_calls` asserts the four edges so this exact bug can't recur.

title: fix(extract): emit symbol-level edges for TS/JS named imports
body:
## Problem

`_import_js` creates a file→file `imports_from` edge but never walks the `import_clause` to emit edges for individual named specifiers. This leaves named imported symbols — error classes, type aliases, constants — as degree-1 orphans connected only to their defining file, with no edges to any of their consumers.

**Example:** `import { CookieJarCorruptionError } from '../pipeline/cookie-jar.js'` produced no edge between `wb-source.ts` and the `CookieJarCorruptionError` node. The symbol appeared isolated in the graph despite being actively used.

## Fix

Track `resolved_path` when the import target resolves to a local file (relative path or tsconfig alias). After emitting the file-level `imports_from` edge, walk:

```
import_statement → import_clause → named_imports → import_specifier → name
```

For each specifier, emit a `file → symbol` `EXTRACTED` edge using `_make_id(target_stem, name)` — the same key `_extract_generic` uses when defining the symbol. This wires importer files directly to existing symbol nodes with no new node creation.

`type`-only import specifiers are included (they are structural dependencies). Renamed imports (`Foo as Bar`) use the original name `Foo` via `child_by_field_name("name")`. External package imports (no `resolved_path`) are unaffected.

## Impact

Tested on a 1,696-file TypeScript monorepo:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Edges | 8,530 | 11,267 |
| New edges | — | +2,737 |
| Communities | 878 | 604 |

The 274 fewer communities reflect formerly isolated symbols now correctly grouped with their consumers.

title: cluster-only: thin community noise dominates GRAPH_REPORT.md on large sparse graphs
body:
## Problem

On large packages, `graphify cluster-only` produces reports where the majority of communities are 1–2 node singletons, making `GRAPH_REPORT.md` nearly unusable as a navigation document.

**Example (admin package, 4506 nodes / 5523 edges):**
- Total communities: 577
- Thin (1-node): 335
- Thin (2-node): 64
- **Thin total: 399 — 69% of all communities**
- Report length: 3846 lines, 451 flagged as noise

The report becomes too long to load in context and the meaningful community hubs are buried.

## Root cause

Louvain clustering leaves sparsely-connected nodes as singleton communities. The report generates a full `### Community N` section for every cluster including singletons, and also lists them again under `## Knowledge Gaps`. Duplicate noise.

## Proposed fix

Two options (either or both):

### Option A — `--min-community-size N` flag (recommended)
Add a flag to `cluster-only` (and the main run) that suppresses community sections below N nodes from the report. Default could be `--min-community-size 3`.

```bash
graphify cluster-only packages/admin --min-community-size 3
```

Thin communities would still be counted in the summary line but not rendered as individual sections.

### Option B — collapse thin communities in Knowledge Gaps
Instead of listing every thin community as a separate bullet in `## Knowledge Gaps`, emit a single summary line:

```
- **399 thin communities (1–2 nodes) omitted** — run `graphify query` to explore isolated nodes
```

## Related

- `--no-viz` flag is documented in error messages and skill files but not wired into `cluster-only` command handler. Had to patch `__main__.py` locally to add it. Should be a 3-line fix in the `elif cmd == "cluster-only":` block.

## Environment

- graphifyy version: installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`
- Graph: Elixir/Phoenix monorepo package, 4506 nodes, 5523 edges
- Platform: macOS, Claude Code

title: Fix #535: re-add Godot .gd script file detection
body:
## Summary

Regression fix: `.gd` files were detected in v0.4.26 but silently dropped after upgrade, causing Godot users to see *"No code files found - nothing to rebuild"* even when `.gd` files were present in their project.

Add `.gd` to:

GDScript has no tree-sitter binding on PyPI, so AST extraction silently skips `.gd` files (existing behavior for unmapped extensions). The files now appear in detect output again and are processed by the LLM-based semantic extraction subagents as code, restoring the pre-regression behavior.

Closes #535

- [x] `tests/test_extract.py::test_collect_files_picks_up_godot_gd` — verifies `collect_files()` finds `.gd` files in a directory scan
- [x] Updated `test_collect_files_from_dir` supported set to include `.gd`

title: Pin UTF-8 encoding for cache and manifest I/O
body:
## Summary

On Windows the default text codec is cp1252, so `Path.read_text()` / `Path.write_text()` raise `UnicodeDecodeError` / `UnicodeEncodeError` whenever the graphify cache or manifest holds non-ASCII content — for example:

- Chinese / Japanese / Korean identifier names extracted from source code
- File paths under directories with accented Latin or CJK characters
- Emoji or non-ASCII labels in semantic extraction output

Four call sites are affected:

- `cache.load_cached()` — `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` + catch `UnicodeDecodeError`
- `cache.save_cached()` — `write_text(encoding="utf-8")` with `ensure_ascii=False` so CJK/emoji stay readable UTF-8 instead of `\uXXXX` escapes
- `detect.load_manifest()` — `read_text(encoding="utf-8")`
- `detect.save_manifest()` — `write_text(encoding="utf-8")` with `ensure_ascii=False`

The repo already uses `encoding="utf-8"` in `__main__.py` and `export.py`; this extends the same convention to the file types most likely to hold user data.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/test_encoding.py` (13 tests) covers cache + manifest roundtrips with CJK, Japanese, Korean, accented Latin, emoji, and mixed-script payloads — including non-ASCII filenames
- [x] Verifies cache files on disk are valid UTF-8 JSON readable by external tools
- [x] No regressions in existing tests

title: Fix #535: re-add Godot .gd script file detection
body:
## Summary

Regression fix: `.gd` files were detected in v0.4.26 but silently dropped after upgrade, causing Godot users to see *"No code files found - nothing to rebuild"* even when `.gd` files were present in their project.

Add `.gd` to:
- `CODE_EXTENSIONS` in `detect.py` so `detect()` classifies Godot scripts as code
- `_EXTENSIONS` in `extract.collect_files()` so recursive directory scans pick them up

GDScript has no tree-sitter binding on PyPI, so AST extraction silently skips `.gd` files (existing behavior for unmapped extensions). The files now appear in detect output again and are processed by the LLM-based semantic extraction subagents as code, restoring the pre-regression behavior.

Closes #535

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_detect.py::test_classify_godot_gd` — verifies `classify_file()` returns `FileType.CODE` for `.gd` paths
- [x] `tests/test_extract.py::test_collect_files_picks_up_godot_gd` — verifies `collect_files()` finds `.gd` files in a directory scan
- [x] Updated `test_collect_files_from_dir` supported set to include `.gd`
- [x] No regressions in existing tests

title: Surface tree-sitter version-mismatch hint instead of bare TypeError
body:
## Summary

When a user has an older `tree-sitter` paired with a newer language binding (or vice versa), `Language()` raises `TypeError` with messages like *"missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'"*. The current catch-all `except Exception` in `_extract_generic()` stores that bare message in the per-file `error` field, leaving users no actionable signal.

Add a dedicated `TypeError` branch that returns the upgrade hint:

> tree-sitter version mismatch for `tree_sitter_python`: missing 1 required positional argument: 'name'. Try: `pip install --upgrade tree-sitter tree-sitter-languages`

Behavior is unchanged for all non-version-mismatch errors — the broader `Exception` handler still runs.

This PR replaces the old #96 (which targeted stale v3 and bundled three changes). The other two changes from #96 are no longer needed:
- Progress logging — already implemented in v6 (parallel/sequential extraction emit it).
- HTML sampling — overlaps with v6's `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT` env-var approach, so leaving v6's design as-is.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_generic_surfaces_tree_sitter_version_mismatch_hint` — uses `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, ...)` to inject a fake `tree_sitter` whose `Language()` raises `TypeError`, then asserts the returned error contains both `"tree-sitter version mismatch"` and `"pip install --upgrade"`.
- [x] All existing tests still pass; no behavior change for any path that doesn't hit `TypeError`.

title: Fix #660: silence 'invalid file_type None' warning on legacy graphs
body:
## Summary

Users running `graphify update .` see this warning when the existing graph.json contains nodes preserved from older graphify versions:

```
[graphify] Extraction warning (31 issues): Node 1661 (id='telepathy_app') has invalid file_type 'None' - must be one of ['code', 'concept', 'document', 'image', 'paper', 'rationale']
```

**Cause:** `_rebuild_code` in `watch.py` preserves nodes from the existing graph.json that aren't in the new AST output. Some of those nodes (stubs, semantic concepts created by older graphify versions that didn't always populate `file_type`) have `file_type: null` in the on-disk JSON, which loads as Python `None`. The validator at `validate.py:33` then flags every such node, polluting the user's CLI output.

**Fix:** Add a normalization step in `build_from_json` next to the existing `source` → `source_file` legacy canonicalization. If a node's `file_type` is `None` or empty, default it to `"concept"` (the most generic VALID type, recently added in #601) before validation runs.

This silences the false positive while keeping the validator strict for genuinely invalid values like `"weird_type"`.

Closes #660

## Test plan

3 new tests in `tests/test_build.py`:
- `test_none_file_type_defaults_to_concept` — `file_type=None` is canonicalized; no warning emitted
- `test_missing_file_type_defaults_to_concept` — completely missing `file_type` field also canonicalized
- `test_real_invalid_file_type_still_warns` — `file_type="weird_type"` still produces the warning (regression guard, ensures we didn't make the validator too lenient)

All existing build / extract / validate tests still pass; no behavior change for any extraction whose nodes already have a valid `file_type`.

title: Add --with-wiki flag to 'graphify hook install' (#549)
body:
## Summary

Issue #549 reports that the post-commit hook rebuilds `graph.json` / `graph.html` / `GRAPH_REPORT.md` but skips the wiki, so agents following the integration guidance (reading `graphify-out/wiki/index.md`) navigate stale community articles after every code change. The reporter's workaround was either running `graphify <path> --wiki` manually or hand-editing the hook (clobbered by the next `graphify hook install`).

This adds an opt-in `--with-wiki` flag:

```
graphify hook install               # unchanged - no wiki rebuild
graphify hook install --with-wiki   # post-commit hook now also rebuilds graphify-out/wiki/
```

Implementation matches the design in #549: no LLM cost, reuses the freshly-written `graph.json` plus `.graphify_labels.json` to call `wiki.to_wiki()`.

### Diff

- `graphify/hooks.py` — extracted `_HOOK_SCRIPT` into a `_build_hook_script(with_wiki: bool)` factory; `install()` takes a `with_wiki=False` kwarg
- `graphify/__main__.py` — parse `--with-wiki` for `hook install`; updated help text
- `tests/test_hooks.py` — 4 new tests

### Backward compatibility

Default behavior unchanged: `graphify hook install` produces the same script as before. A regression test (`test_build_hook_script_wiki_block_only_when_requested`) asserts byte-for-byte equivalence with the legacy `_HOOK_SCRIPT` constant when `with_wiki=False`. Existing installations don't need any action.

Closes #549

## Test plan

4 new tests:
- `test_install_default_omits_wiki_rebuild` — without flag, hook script doesn't import `to_wiki`
- `test_install_with_wiki_injects_wiki_rebuild` — with flag, hook contains the wiki block + AST rebuild + `--with-wiki` marker
- `test_install_with_wiki_then_uninstall_clean` — uninstall removes the entire graphify section, no wiki residue
- `test_build_hook_script_wiki_block_only_when_requested` — `_build_hook_script(with_wiki=False) == _HOOK_SCRIPT` byte-for-byte

All existing tests pass; no behavior change for non-opt-in users.

title: Fix #228: emit mixed [[label]](filename.md) wiki links for non-Obsidian agents
body:
## Summary

Issue #228 reports that the wiki's `--wiki` output is described as "agent-crawlable", but the wikilinks emitted in `index.md` and inside articles use bare Obsidian syntax:

```markdown
- [[API: Auth & Session Layer]] — 38 nodes
```

The actual file on disk is `API-_Auth_&_Session_Layer.md` (via `_safe_filename` substitutions). Any agent not running inside Obsidian — an LLM reading files from a git clone, a plain markdown renderer, GitHub's web view, etc. — sees the wikilink and cannot resolve it to a file path.

This PR switches every wiki-internal reference to a **known article** to the mixed form:

```markdown
- [[API: Auth & Session Layer]](API-_Auth_&_Session_Layer.md) — 38 nodes
```

Obsidian still parses the `[[…]]` portion as a wikilink (so internal navigation in Obsidian is unchanged); standard markdown viewers and agents follow the explicit relative path. References to nodes that don't have their own article (regular neighbors of a god node) keep the bare `[[label]]` form — emitting a path to a non-existent file would break agent navigation worse than the bare wikilink.

### Touch points

- `index.md` community list
- `index.md` god-node list
- Cross-community links inside community articles
- "Community: …" link at the top of god-node articles

### Implementation

- New `_wikilink(label, slug_map)` helper picks between the two forms based on whether the label maps to a real filename.
- `to_wiki()` pre-computes the full `slug_map` before any article is written so cross-references resolve correctly regardless of generation order.
- Slug map is threaded through `_index_md` / `_community_article` / `_god_node_article` (each gains a `slug_map` kwarg, defaulting to `None` for backward compatibility).

Closes #228

## Test plan

6 new tests in `tests/test_wiki.py` (all 21 wiki tests pass):

- `test_index_uses_mixed_wikilink_for_communities`
- `test_index_uses_mixed_wikilink_for_god_nodes`
- `test_community_article_cross_links_use_mixed_format`
- `test_god_node_article_community_link_is_mixed`
- `test_neighbor_without_article_keeps_bare_wikilink` — guards the non-article fallback
- `test_filenames_unique_under_collisions` — every link in index.md must resolve to an existing file even when `_safe_filename` collides

All existing wiki tests still pass; backward-compatible with Obsidian parsers.

title: .graphifyignore does not support .gitignore syntax. ie: negation patterns (!) not supported
body:
Graphify does not support negation patterns (!).

It would be great if we could just ignore everything except the one directory that we want to parse. This would future proof our workspace from contaminating our graph if we forget to keep the ignore file up to date.

Example .graphifyignore file:
```
# Ignore everything
*

# Allow the directory itself
!src/

# Allow everything inside that directory
!src/**
```
The above is not currently supported, even though it is correct .gitignore syntax.

title: add Pascal/Lazarus support and stabilize LLM semantic extraction
body:
## Summary
This pull request introduces comprehensive support for FreePascal and Lazarus projects while significantly improving the stability and resilience of the semantic extraction pipeline. It integrates robust AST extraction for Pascal files and implements a JSON repair mechanism to handle truncated or malformed LLM responses effectively.

## Key Changes

### 1. FreePascal & Lazarus Support
- **Language Detection**: Updated `detect.py` to recognize `.pas`, `.pp`, `.inc`, `.lpr`, `.lfm`, and `.lpi` extensions.
- **Tree-sitter Integration**: Integrated `tree-sitter-language-pack` via `pyproject.toml` for dynamic Pascal grammar support.
- **Pascal Extraction**: Implemented unit dependency resolution by extracting module names from `uses` clauses.
- **Lazarus Integration**: Added support for Lazarus project (.lpi) and form (.lfm) files.

### 2. Semantic Extraction Stabilization
- **Adaptive JSON Repair**: Added a `_repair_json` utility to recover partial data from truncated LLM outputs (e.g., `gpt-5.4-mini`) by automatically closing unclosed strings and brackets.
- **Robust Parsing**: Updated `_parse_llm_json` to attempt repairs before discarding data, increasing resilience against token limits.
- **Refined Retry Logic**: Modified `_extract_with_adaptive_retry` to distinguish between recoverable truncation and logic errors, reducing log noise and preventing unnecessary retries.

### 3. CLI & Backend Improvements
- **OpenAI Support**: Added `openai` as a supported backend with `gpt-5.4-mini` as the default model.
- **Model Overrides**: Added support for the `GRAPHIFY_MODEL` environment variable to allow easy model switching without code changes.
- **Semantic Update Flag**: Implemented the `--semantic` flag for the `update` command to allow manual triggering of LLM-based enrichment during project updates.

## Verification
- Validated AST extraction and dependency mapping for complex Pascal projects.
- Verified that the JSON repair utility successfully recovers data from intentionally truncated LLM streams.
- Confirmed that the `--semantic` flag correctly triggers enrichment and merges findings into the knowledge graph.

title: Graph fragmentation: path-separator inconsistency splits same file into 2 components + Louvain over-merging via doc-hub edges
body:
Hit two graph-quality issues on a real repo (3103 nodes / 463 connected components, ~13% nodes in giant component). Both reproduce on Windows + cross-OS-source-paths and both are mechanical to fix.

## Issue 1: path-separator inconsistency splits same file across components

**Symptom.** Single source file appears as two disconnected components in the final graph because some emitters write `apps\web\middleware\rate-limit.js` and others write `apps/web/middleware/rate-limit.js`. The `source_file` string is used as a node-attribute key (and shows up in edge `source_file`), so identity-via-source breaks across the two encodings.

**Concrete observation in my run:**

\`\`\`
size= 39  src='apps\web\middleware\rate-limit.js'
            sample=['_resetAuthLinkRateLimiter()', '_resetTurnRateLimiter()', '_readEmailMax()', ...]

size= 28  src='apps/web/middleware/rate-limit.js'
            sample=['createKeyedRateLimitBucket', 'checkCsrf (Origin allow-list)', 'checkAuthLinkRateLimit', ...]
\`\`\`

Same physical file, two graph islands. This compounds across the codebase — graph had **463 connected components** when most of the codebase is genuinely linked. Inflates orphan count, hides cross-cutting edges, distorts community detection.

**Root cause hypothesis.** Mixed sources of `source_file`:
- AST extractor (`graphify.extract`) emits OS-native (`os.sep`) on Windows → backslashes
- Semantic subagents read paths from a list passed in the prompt (whatever encoding I used) → inconsistent
- `graphify.build` does not normalize before treating `source_file` as part of node identity / edge key

**Fix.** In `graphify.build` (or earlier — at JSON ingestion), normalize all `source_file` values via:

\`\`\`python
from pathlib import PurePosixPath
def _norm(p: str) -> str:
    return str(PurePosixPath(*p.replace('\\', '/').split('/')))
\`\`\`

Apply to every node and every edge before building the graph. Keep one canonical encoding (POSIX-style forward-slash) regardless of input platform.

**Repro.** Any Windows host running \`/graphify --update\` on a corpus where AST-extractor and semantic subagents both emit a node from the same file.

---

## Issue 2: Louvain over-merging — doc-of-everything hub drags unrelated subsystems into one community

**Symptom.** A 126-node community labelled \"Admin & Billing Surface\" with cohesion **0.02**. Sub-clustering on the subgraph (Louvain at resolution 1.0 on the induced subgraph alone) splits it cleanly into 10 thematically distinct sub-clusters with negligible inter-sub edges:

| sub | size | theme |
|-----|------|-------|
| 0 | 22 | Mutation testing baseline + Razorpay reducer |
| 1 | 16 | OPS-DASH spend tab + admin memoise |
| 2 | 13 | Razorpay provider methods |
| 3 | 13 | Auth handler refactor (separate cluster) |
| 4 | 13 | CLAUDE.md root invariants |
| 5 | 12 | FilesystemIssueStore methods |
| 6 | 11 | Tenant-issue feedback loop + Composer.jsx + DOMPurify |
| 7 | 11 | Admin polling-stack + ETag |
| 8-9 | <10 | misc |

These have minimal cross-sub edges. They are not one community.

**Root cause hypothesis.** A small number of **doc-of-everything** files (here: \`CLAUDE.md\`, audit consolidated reports) have edges to many otherwise-unrelated nodes. Each such doc node has degree 30-40 and lives in *every* sub-theme. Louvain at resolution 1.0 sees the doc-as-bridge and merges all the sub-themes into one giant community.

**Why this matters.** The cohesion score is honest (0.02 → \"these don't belong together\"), but the auto-generated label and the user-facing \"split this community?\" question fire **after** the bad merge. Users see a 126-node community with a generic name and miss the real structure.

**Fix options (any combination):**

1. **Default Louvain resolution > 1.0.** Currently effectively 1.0. Try 1.3 default; expose as flag. On the same input my 477 communities became cleanly resolvable at higher resolution.
2. **Down-weight edges from doc-hub nodes.** Heuristic: any node whose degree is in the top 1% AND whose `file_type == 'document'` is treated as having edge weight \`1 / log(degree)\` for clustering purposes only (not for visualization or query).
3. **Two-phase clustering.** Run Louvain. For any community with cohesion < 0.05 AND size > 50, recursively re-cluster the subgraph and replace.

Option 3 is the cleanest user-facing fix because it preserves the \"there might be one big community\" outcome when it really is one, and only intervenes when the cohesion score itself flags the merge as suspect.

---

## Environment

- graphify version: \`pip show graphifyy\` (latest as of 2026-05-03)
- Python 3.12 / Windows 11 / PowerShell
- Corpus: ~3K nodes / 3K edges / 477 communities (Louvain at 1.0)

Happy to PR either fix. Issue 1 is one-line; Issue 2 is more design-y — would want to pick which option you prefer first.

title: Adjustments
Should `.github` AI configuration files be included in knowledge graphs?
body:
## Context

I'm using graphify to generate knowledge graphs for repositories that contain GitHub Copilot / VS Code configuration in `.github/`. Currently, graphify's `detect()` function skips hidden directories (starting with `.`), which excludes the entire `.github/` directory.

## The Issue

Modern repositories often contain AI agent configuration in `.github/`:

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` - Root AI agent instructions
- `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` - Scoped instructions
- `.github/agents/*.agent.md` - Custom agent definitions
- `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` - Executable workflow skills

These files represent how AI agents interact with the codebase. Without them, the knowledge graph shows *what the code is* but not *how AI should work with it*.

## The Question

**Should graphify include `.github` AI configuration files in knowledge graphs?**

### Options

**A) Code + Docs Only (Current Behavior)**
- Clean separation: focus on application logic
- Avoids GitHub workflow noise (Actions YAML, PR templates, etc.)

**B) Code + Docs + AI Configuration**
- Complete picture: technical + AI interaction layers
- May include irrelevant GitHub workflow files

**C) Configurable Inclusion**
Add a filter option to `detect()`:
```python
detect(
    root=".",
    include_hidden_dirs=[".github"],
)
```

## Use Case

I ran graphify on a Java REST API repository:
- 8 code files (Java + PowerShell)
- 6 document files (YAML, Markdown, HTML)
- **9+ `.github` AI configuration files (excluded)**

The graph correctly identified handler classes and build scripts, but completely missed the custom agents and instruction files that define how AI should work with this repository.

## Request

Could you clarify the intended scope of graphify knowledge graphs? If AI configuration is out of scope, is there a recommended workaround? If it's within scope, I'd be happy to contribute a PR for configurable hidden directory inclusion.

title: Make default VS Code Copilot graphify instructions stricter so agents stop bypassing GRAPH_REPORT.md
body:
The default ## graphify section that `graphify vscode install` writes to `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is too soft. In practice, Copilot agents (both VS Code Copilot Chat and the GitHub Copilot CLI) frequently bypass it — they answer architecture / how-to / where-is questions straight from memory or by grepping source, instead of reading `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` first. That defeats the whole point of having the graph.

### What this PR changes

Replaces `_VSCODE_INSTRUCTIONS_SECTION` in `graphify/__main__.py` with a more prescriptive version:

- **Mandatory first tool call**: for any architecture/codebase question, the agent's first tool call must be reading `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
- **Explicit trigger list**: ""how do I…"", ""where is…"", ""add a handler"", ""explain the architecture"", etc.
- **Trust the graph**: explicit instruction *not* to re-verify by opening source files after the graph for conceptual questions.
- **Narrow allowlist**: source reads are still allowed for actual code modification / debugging / when the graph is genuinely missing detail or is stale.
- **Self-check**: the agent is told to verify before each reply that its first tool call read the report.

### Why

Tested locally with the Copilot CLI on a Java REST API repo:

- With the soft wording, the agent answered ""what's needed to add a new endpoint?"" without ever reading `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
- With the stricter wording, the agent consistently reads `GRAPH_REPORT.md` first and grounds its answer in god nodes / communities.

### Scope

- Only touches `_VSCODE_INSTRUCTIONS_SECTION` (the VS Code / Copilot install path).
- Does not touch the Antigravity, Kiro, Aider, Claude, Codex, etc. templates — those can be aligned in a follow-up if this approach is accepted.
- Does not change install/uninstall logic; the marker (`## graphify`) is still detected so re-runs and `vscode uninstall` keep working. Note: existing repos that already have the soft section won't be auto-upgraded (the install is a no-op when the marker is present), which is the same behaviour as today.

### Test

`vscode install` / `vscode uninstall` still work end-to-end on a fresh repo and on a repo that already has the new section.
