title: Large graphs: 24% isolated dead-weight nodes from bundled/synthetic source files
body:
## Problem

When a graph reaches 10k+ nodes, roughly 24% become isolated dead weight — nodes with ≤1 edge that have no meaningful place in the knowledge graph. In our 10,006 node corpus:

- **2,458 isolated nodes** (24.5% of total)
- **1,341 isolated nodes** come from a single file: `claude-code-sourcemap/cli.mjs` (a bundled sourcemap / vendor artifact)
- **90 truly zero-edge nodes** (completely disconnected)
- Remaining 2,368 have exactly one edge (leaf nodes with no outgoing connections)

This makes the corpus size number misleading. The effective graph has closer to **7,548 useful nodes**, not 10,006.

## Root cause

AST-only extraction without semantic cross-reference inference produces a graph full of:
1. **Bundled/vendor files** (e.g. `cli.mjs` sourcemaps) — one flat AST, all symbols registered as isolated nodes
2. **Synthetic files** (generated code, `.d.ts` declarations, SDK stubs) — symbols exist but have no actual call relationships
3. **Single-file symbols** — functions with no imports/exports connecting them to the rest of the graph

## Consequences

- Community detection quality degrades (Louvain splits noise into its own communities)
- `GRAPH_REPORT.md` becomes 80%+ noise (thin communities, isolated nodes)
- Surprising Connections becomes unusable (false positives dominate)
- Graph query BFS traversal wastes budget on dead nodes
- Corpus size claim is misleading for cost/quality estimation

## Suggested fixes (pick one or more)

**Option A — Filter synthetic files at extraction time**


**Option B — Post-extraction dedup pass**
Drop nodes with degree ≤1 after graph build, or merge all nodes from the same source file into a single meta-node.

**Option C — Graph hygiene CLI command**
`graphify prune graphify-out/graph.json --min-degree 1` — removes isolated nodes, rewrites graph.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md.

**Option D — Flag at --no-viz level**
`cluster-only` should flag isolated node % in the report header so users know the corpus is dirty before reading communities.

## Environment

graphifyy 0.7.5, 10,006 node graph, 26,171 edges

title: Feature Request: Local-Model Extraction + Cross-Session Persistent Memory
body:
Graphify solves the "re-reading files" problem, but the semantic extraction pass still outsources to the main assistant's LLM. This means: (1) The token burden of building the graph burns through the context window, (2) Every new session starts with no memory of past context, and (3) The graph is project-scoped.

### The Idea

A local-first extraction backend combined with persistent cross-session memory layered onto the graph.

**Should:**
- Allow Graphify to use its own lightweight model (e.g. via Ollama, Qwen2.5-Coder, Phi-3-mini, any locally-running model etc.) as the semantic extraction provider, instead of inheriting the main assistant's API
- Persist the graph across sessions as a living memory store as an accumulation of semantic context over time
- Let the graph grow across projects, so architecture & structural patterns, bug patterns, lessons from bug fixes, and domain knowledge compound

### This Matters Because

Right now, the architecture is: **main LLM → farms context → graph → main LLM queries graph**

Would like it to be: **local model → builds and maintains graph → main LLM queries compressed output only**

Ultimately, the main assistant shouldn't do extraction work. It should only receive structured, already-digested output from a locally-maintained knowledge layer.

### Tools That Exist

- Ollama makes local semantic extraction viable at no API cost
- SynaBun (https://github.com/danilokhury/Synabun) has solved cross-session persistence with vector memory but without graph structure

### In short

Please add a persistent, locally-maintained knowledge layer that any assistant can query via MCP.

title: Hardcoded max_tokens=8192 causes truncation cascade on dense docs (3× cost overhead)
body:
# Hardcoded `max_tokens=8192` causes truncation cascade on dense docs (3× cost overhead)

## TL;DR

`graphify extract`'s Claude backend uses `max_tokens=8192` in `_call_claude` (graphify/llm.py). On dense Markdown corpora, output JSON regularly exceeds this cap. The adaptive-retry layer correctly catches `finish_reason="length"` and recursively splits the chunk — but the truncated API call is **fully billed** (input tokens + 8192 output tokens) and produces zero usable nodes/edges. The same content then gets re-extracted from scratch in smaller chunks.

For our docs-only repo (1,094 Markdown files, mostly entity specs and PRDs averaging 2–8 KB body content), running `graphify extract` on the ~74 uncached files cost **$4.31** when an honest cost estimate is closer to **$1.50** — roughly 3× overhead from truncated-then-discarded calls.

## Reproduction

Corpus profile:
- 1,094 Markdown docs, 1 PDF, 12 images
- Cache hit rate: 93% (preflight verified)
- Genuinely uncached: ~74 files
- Files are dense PRD/entity-spec content (typical 2–8 KB body each)

Command: `graphify extract docs/ --backend claude --out .`

Observed: every initial chunk of 14–22 files triggers `finish_reason="length"` at depth 0 because the JSON output for that many dense docs blows past 8192 tokens. Adaptive retry splits them; depth-1 chunks of 7–11 files frequently truncate again. By depth 2 (chunks of 3–5 files), most succeed. A handful hit depth 3 (single-file chunks) and graphify gives up with a partial result.

Sample log lines:
```
[graphify] LLM returned invalid JSON, skipping chunk: Expecting value: line 1 column 28711 (char 28710)
[graphify] chunk of 19 truncated at depth 0, splitting into halves of 9 and 10
[graphify] chunk of 22 truncated at depth 0, splitting into halves of 11 and 11
[graphify] chunk of 14 truncated at depth 0, splitting into halves of 7 and 7
[graphify] chunk of 9 truncated at depth 1, splitting into halves of 4 and 5
[graphify] LLM returned invalid JSON, skipping chunk: ... (depth 2)
[graphify] LLM returned invalid JSON, skipping chunk: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 886 column 37 (char 25096)
[graphify] single-file chunk docs/README.md truncated at max_completion_tokens — partial result kept
```

Final result for the run:
```
[graphify extract] tokens: 267,749 in / 234,087 out, est. cost (~claude): $4.3146
```

234K output tokens is suspicious — it's nearly 1:1 with input, when extraction output should typically be 30–40% the size of input for a clean run. The ratio implies the LLM repeatedly produced 8192-token responses that were thrown away.

## Why it matters

We're using `graphify extract` as the canonical CI publisher of the corpus graph (the workflow regenerates and commits `graph.json` on every merge to master, per your "graph is a build artifact" guidance). In that model:

- **First run**: bears the full cost of populating cache. For our corpus this is once — but the truncation overhead made it 3× more expensive than necessary.
- **Subsequent runs**: only re-extract changed files. If a single dense entity-spec changes, the truncation cascade fires again on that file's chunk, paying overhead per merge.

Over a year of normal docs PRs (50–100 merges that touch denser specs), the cascade overhead compounds. Each merge that hits truncation pays an extra $0.30–$1.50 above the "should-cost" of extracting the changed files cleanly.

## Root cause

In `graphify/llm.py`, `_call_claude`:

```python
def _call_claude(api_key: str, model: str, user_message: str) -> dict:
    ...
    resp = client.messages.create(
        model=model,
        max_tokens=8192,   # ← hardcoded
        ...
    )
```

The chunk packer (`_pack_chunks_by_tokens`) defaults to `token_budget=60_000` for **input** sizing. This input budget assumes a ~10:1 input/output ratio, but for dense extraction the ratio is closer to 4:1. Result: input fits the budget cleanly, but output regularly exceeds 8192.

Sonnet 4.6 supports up to 64K output tokens; Sonnet 3.7 up to 128K. The 8192 cap is far below what the model supports.

## Proposed fixes (based on my limited understanding of Graphify intents)

### 1. Bump default `max_tokens` for the claude backend (lowest-effort, biggest win)

```python
# graphify/llm.py
BACKENDS = {
    "claude": {
        ...
        "max_tokens": 16384,   # was implicit 8192
    },
    ...
}

def _call_claude(api_key: str, model: str, user_message: str, max_tokens: int = 16384) -> dict:
    ...
    resp = client.messages.create(model=model, max_tokens=max_tokens, ...)
```

16K is conservative (well under model limits) and would fit the vast majority of our chunks in a single call. 32K would be even better and still safe.

### 2. Make `max_tokens` configurable

Either as a CLI flag (`--max-output-tokens N`) or environment variable (`GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`). Lets users tune per corpus density.

### 3. Proactive chunk shrinking based on observed output size

When a chunk truncates, *halve the input budget* for subsequent chunks in the same run instead of just splitting that one chunk. This is a heuristic — if one dense chunk truncates, others probably will too. Avoids paying the truncation cost N times.

### 4. Stream + parse incrementally

Stream the LLM response, parse JSON tokens as they arrive. If the stream ends mid-string, salvage everything parsed so far instead of throwing away the entire response. This is more invasive but recovers the wasted output tokens.

## Workaround we're using

Pinning `graphifyy>=0.7.4`, accepting the one-time cost, watching the trend on subsequent merges. We've added a CI preflight gate (`check_semantic_cache` against expected hit rate) that catches cache-key drift early but doesn't help with truncation.

## Other observations from the run

- The `[graphify extract] semantic cache: X hit / Y miss` log line never appeared in our run despite 93% cache hits being confirmed externally via preflight. Possibly a stdout buffering issue under GitHub Actions runners — would help debugging if it always flushed before the first chunk fires.
- `pip install graphifyy` does not pull in `anthropic` as a hard dep. The error message is clear (`Run: pip install anthropic`) but listing it as an optional extra (`graphifyy[claude]`) would be more discoverable.

Happy to provide more data or test patches.

title: fix(detect): forward follow_symlinks from detect_incremental to detect
body:
## Problem

`detect_incremental(root)` always called `detect(root)` without forwarding the `follow_symlinks` kwarg added in #33. As a result, corpora that include symlinked sub-trees pointing to directories outside the scan root were visible to a full `detect()` run with `follow_symlinks=True` but invisible to any subsequent `--update` run.

## Concrete failure case

A user has a knowledge corpus laid out like:

\`\`\`
~/.hermes/graphify-jarvis/
├── state_of_truth -> ~/.hermes/state_of_truth     (symlink)
├── memories       -> ~/.claude/.../memory          (symlink)
└── graphify-out/
\`\`\`

Initial `/graphify <path>` build (with the appropriate `follow_symlinks=True` plumbed in) correctly indexed ~95 files via the symlinks. Subsequent `/graphify <path> --update` runs only saw 3 files (the contents of `graphify-out/` itself) because `detect_incremental` re-called `detect(root)` without the flag, silently dropping the symlinked sub-trees. New SoT reports and memories were never picked up by incremental scans.

## Fix

Add a keyword-only `follow_symlinks` parameter to `detect_incremental()` and forward it to `detect()`. Default stays `False` for backwards compatibility — only callers that already opt in to symlink following on `detect()` pick up the new behaviour for incremental runs too.

## Test

Added `test_detect_incremental_propagates_follow_symlinks` covering the regression: a corpus with a symlinked directory is invisible with `follow_symlinks=False`, fully indexed with `follow_symlinks=True`, and correctly reports zero new files on a second incremental scan after the manifest is saved.

\`\`\`
$ pytest tests/test_detect.py -v
============================== 30 passed in 0.07s ==============================
\`\`\`

## Caller note

The CLI / skill currently doesn't expose `--follow-symlinks` as a flag, but `watch.py` already plumbs it through to the full-`detect()` rebuild path. This PR keeps the same opt-in shape: callers that already pass `follow_symlinks=True` to `detect()` will now see consistent behaviour on `--update`. Wiring a `--follow-symlinks` CLI flag through to both `detect_incremental` and the existing `detect()` callsites would be a small follow-up if you want.

## Summary

  Adds a graph-level foundation for more reliable cross-language impact traversal:

  - Stabilizes local source identity/import resolution before query-time traversal.
  - Adds generic symbol-resolution facts for imports, re-exports, aliases, and local uses.
  - Ports JS/TS barrel re-export handling onto that generic layer.

  ## Why

  Large codebases often route symbols through barrels, package entrypoints, aliases, or repeated file names. Without resolving those edges to the original symbol, query and impact output is noisy or incomplete.

  This PR improves that without changing storage.

  - Resolves TS/Svelte local imports, directory `index.*`, `.svelte.ts`, tsconfig aliases, and workspace package imports.
  - Emits `re_exports` edges with `context="export"`.

  - Adds direct local `calls` edges for imported bindings when usage is import-aware.
  - Disambiguates duplicate node IDs by source path.
  - Rewires unique unresolved stubs to real definitions when safe.
  - Adds `graphify affected <node-or-label>` with `--relation`, `--depth`, and `--graph`.

```
-      "community": 1582,
+      "community": 1589,
... (~11,800 such renumbers)

GRAPH_REPORT.md:
- 12418 nodes · 12706 edges · 3596 communities (2946 shown, 650 thin omitted)
+ 12418 nodes · 12706 edges · 3603 communities (2952 shown, 651 thin omitted)
- Built from commit: `3bbf35c9`
+ Built from commit: `66343027`
```

Node + edge counts identical. The shift comes from clustering.

### Root cause (from upstream source — `graphify/watch.py:_rebuild_code`)

Each `graphify update` invocation:

1. Re-detects files (manifest-aware, fast)
2. Re-extracts AST for all detected files (cache-aware, fast)
3. Preserves semantic nodes from existing graph
4. **Always re-runs `cluster()` (Leiden) on the merged graph** — this step is non-deterministic enough across processes to renumber communities even when the graph topology is unchanged
5. Re-writes `graph.json` + `GRAPH_REPORT.md` unconditionally

Step 4 is the source of churn. Even with seeded Leiden (advertised "deterministic community IDs" since 0.7.0), per-process variation produces meaningful renumbers.

### Practical impact

We wired a `post-commit` git hook to call `graphify update`, hoping for incremental refresh. In practice:

- Every commit produces an 11k-line diff that has no signal
- Amending a commit re-fires the hook → another 11k-line diff appended to the cascade
- PR diffs become unreviewable (signal buried under renumber noise)
- We had to disable the hook entirely

### Questions

1. Is the per-process Leiden churn intended, or is the seeded-Leiden determinism guarantee narrower than expected? (e.g. only deterministic within one process, not across runs)
2. Would you accept a `--no-cluster` flag on `graphify update` that preserves existing community assignments when AST changes are localized? (The semantic-preserving merge logic in `_rebuild_code` lines 80-103 already preserves nodes; analogous preservation of community IDs would close the loop.)
3. Alternatively, is there an existing fast-path that skips the full rebuild when the manifest hash + extracted AST IDs match the prior run? If not, would you accept one?
4. Independent of clustering: is there a reason `GRAPH_REPORT.md` updates the "Built from commit" hash even when graph contents are unchanged? A no-op shortcut would help.

Happy to open a PR for any of the above if intent is "addressable, fix accepted."

### Reproduction

```bash
# In any indexed graphify project after a successful initial run:
graphify update .
git diff --stat graphify-out/graph.json graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md  # clean
graphify update .
git diff --stat graphify-out/graph.json graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md  # ~11k lines diff
```

### Environment

- graphifyy `0.7.5`
- Python 3.13
- Project layout: `knowledge/graphify/.venv` + `graphify-out/` colocated under a project subdir
- Graph size: ~12,400 nodes / ~12,700 edges / ~3,600 communities (semantic-augmented)

title: fix: add source-location dedup pruning pipeline
body:
## Summary
Add a source-location-aware deduplication and pruning pipeline so graph builds merge duplicate entities more safely, keep hyperedges consistent, and remove stale graph references after deduplication.

## Context
This builds on upstream `v7` and focuses on graph quality during build/merge. The changes address duplicate entities emitted from AST/semantic extraction at the same source location and stale edge/hyperedge references left behind after nodes are merged.

Focused searches of open upstream requests for deduplication, source-location, pruning/stale references, collisions, and isolated/dead-weight nodes did not find a direct issue or PR this fully closes. Related graph-quality discussions include #728 and #726, but this PR does not claim to close them.

## Changes
- Adds source-location deduplication before the fuzzy/entity dedup pass.
- Prunes stale edges and hyperedge members after deduplication.
- Preserves the upstream `v7` global graph guard that prevents cross-repo deduplication.
- Threads `dedup` and `dedup_llm_backend` through build/merge APIs.
- Adds focused tests and fixtures for source-location dedup, pruning behavior, hyperedge remapping, language fixture handling, and install metadata.

### Key Implementation Details
- `deduplicate_entities()` now returns `(nodes, edges, hyperedges, stats)` consistently and includes source-location pre-pass stats.
- `build()` calls the unified dedup pipeline before constructing the NetworkX graph.
- `build_merge()` remains compatible with both positional chunks and the existing `extractions=` keyword.
- Cross-repo dedup remains disabled for global graphs to avoid merging unrelated repositories by label similarity.

## Testing
Local validation passed:

```bash
uv run pytest
```

Result:

```text
648 passed
```

Also verified the pushed branch topology:

```text
upstream/v7...origin/source-location-dedup-prune = 0 3
```

## Links
- Related discussion, not closed: #728
- Related discussion, not closed: #726

title: agent-graph-workflow-v7
body:

  - `graphify skill <platform>` installs or refreshes the assistant skill.
  - `graphify setup <platform>` writes project-local assistant instructions and hooks.

title: cluster-only ignores --no-viz flag and GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT env var on graphs ≥ 5000 nodes (v0.7.7)
body:
## Summary

`graphify cluster-only` always invokes `to_html()` regardless of `--no-viz` flag or `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT=0` env var. On graphs with ≥ 5000 nodes this raises `ValueError` and aborts the run **after** the new clusters are written to `graph.json` but **before** `.graphify_labels.json` is saved, leaving the graph in an inconsistent state.

## Reproduce

Tested on graphifyy 0.7.7 (Python 3.13.12, macOS).

```bash
# graph.json with 7060 nodes, 22213 edges
graphify cluster-only . --no-viz                    # crashes
GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT=0 graphify cluster-only .   # crashes
```

## Expected

Either flag/env should bypass `to_html()` entirely. Per v0.6.6 release notes:

> `--no-viz` flag now works in `cluster-only` path — removes stale `graph.html` when passed (#565)
> `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT` env var — override the 5000-node HTML threshold (set to `0` to disable viz entirely, useful for CI) (#565)

## Actual

```
Loading existing graph...
Graph: 7060 nodes, 22213 edges
Re-clustering...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/homebrew/bin/graphify", line 6, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File ".../graphify/__main__.py", line 1415, in main
    to_html(G, communities, str(out / "graph.html"), community_labels=labels or None)
  File ".../graphify/export.py", line 395, in to_html
    raise ValueError(...)
ValueError: Graph has 7060 nodes - too large for HTML viz. Use --no-viz or reduce input size.
```

## Likely cause

`__main__.py:1415` calls `to_html(...)` unconditionally on the cluster-only branch — looks like the flag/env guards present elsewhere are missing on this code path (regression vs v0.6.6, or the v0.6.6 fix never reached `cluster-only`).

## Side effect

`graph.json` is saved with the new cluster IDs (good), but `.graphify_labels.json` is not written (bad — community label persistence relies on it, per v0.6.6 fix #558). Subsequent `--update` runs lose human-readable labels.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.7.7 (pipx install)
- Python 3.13.12
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- Graph: 7060 nodes / 22213 edges / 314 communities

## Workaround

None — graphs ≥ 5000 nodes cannot run `cluster-only` at all on v0.7.7.

title: add .luau extension support (Roblox Luau)
body:
## Problem

Graphify recognizes `.lua` but not `.luau`. Roblox first-party code is written in Luau (a Lua superset with type annotations) using the `.luau` extension. On a real 479-file Roblox codebase, graphify silently skipped all 379 first-party `.luau` files and produced a graph dominated by vendored `.lua` dependencies (Roact's `Packages/_Index/`), giving a misleading picture of the codebase.

## Repro

```bash
git clone <any Roblox/Wally project> repo && cd repo
graphify update .
# manifest.json contains zero .luau entries
# the resulting graph reflects vendored Lua deps, not first-party Luau code
```

## Fix

Two-line change plus test coverage:

- `graphify/detect.py` — add `.luau` to `CODE_EXTENSIONS`
- `graphify/extract.py` — map `.luau` to `extract_lua` in `_DISPATCH`
- `tests/test_extract.py` — add `.luau` to the `supported` set in `test_collect_files_from_dir`
- `tests/fixtures/sample.luau` — minimal Luau source exercising type annotations + functions + calls

`tree-sitter-lua` doesn't parse Luau-specific type annotations cleanly, but it successfully extracts function declarations and call edges from Luau source (errors recover gracefully and skipped tokens don't abort the parse).

## Verification

**Smoke test on the included fixture:**
```
extracted nodes: 5
extracted edges: 5
first 3 nodes: ['sample.luau', 'Server.new()', 'Server:start()']
```

**Real-world: same codebase, before vs. after**

|  | before patch | after patch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Files processed | 100 (vendored `.lua` only) | 379 (first-party `.luau` + `.lua`) |
| Nodes | 344 | 1,265 |
| Edges | 340 | 1,471 |
| Communities | 87 | 236 |
| Top god node | `createElement()` (Roact internals) | `Clock.makeMock()` (game code) |

**Tests:** `pytest tests/test_detect.py tests/test_extract.py` → 51 passed.

## Notes

- A dedicated `tree-sitter-luau` grammar exists and would be a richer long-term option, but reusing `tree-sitter-lua` is the minimal change to make Luau projects functional today.
- For projects mixing `.lua` and `.luau` (common in Roblox), this also lets `.graphifyignore` cleanly exclude vendored `Packages/` while keeping first-party Luau in scope.

title: graphify update + export wiki silently wipes wiki/ when .graphify_analysis.json is missing (data loss)
body:
## Summary

Running `graphify update .` followed by `graphify export wiki` on a project that does **not** have a `.graphify_analysis.json` sidecar deletes every existing wiki article and writes only god-node summaries (~10 files), regardless of how many community articles previously existed.

In our project this caused a **silent loss of 2,519 wiki articles** when an automated pre-push hook ran the two commands in sequence. Detection happened only after the regression had already merged.

Tested on `graphifyy==0.7.5` (Python package), Linux x86_64, default branch v7.

## Reproduction

Starting from a project that has a populated `graphify-out/` (e.g. produced by an earlier `graphify extract .` run with thousands of wiki articles):

```bash
# Pre-condition
ls graphify-out/wiki/*.md | wc -l        # → 2519 (or any large count)
test -f graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json && echo "sidecar present" || echo "sidecar MISSING"
# Make the sidecar 'missing' (simulating a clean checkout / a project that
# only ran `update`, never `extract`):
rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json

# Reproduction
graphify update .
graphify export wiki

# Post-condition
ls graphify-out/wiki/*.md | wc -l        # → 11   ← every community article gone
```

Same outcome if the sidecar never existed at all (e.g. project initialized via `graphify update` only, without ever running the LLM-driven `extract`).

## Root cause

Three independent design choices combine into a destructive interaction:

1. **`graphify update`** (`graphify/watch.py::_rebuild_code`) writes `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `.graphify_root` — but **never** writes `.graphify_analysis.json`.
2. **`graphify cluster-only`** (`graphify/__main__.py:1496-1551`) re-clusters the graph but **also never** writes `.graphify_analysis.json`. Only `graphify extract` (`__main__.py:2154-2188`) writes that sidecar, and `extract` requires LLM API access (expensive; not appropriate for a pre-push hook or watch loop).
3. **`graphify export wiki`** (`__main__.py:1800-1808`) reads `communities` from `.graphify_analysis.json` and **silently falls back to `{}` if the file is absent**:

   ```python
   communities: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
   if analysis_path.exists():
       _an = json.loads(analysis_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
       communities = {int(k): v for k, v in _an.get("communities", {}).items()}
   ```

4. The destructive wiki-cleanup runs **before** the (now empty) community-iteration loop. From `graphify/wiki.py::to_wiki` (lines 199-206 in 0.7.5):

   ```python
   # Clear stale .md files from previous runs to prevent orphan accumulation.
   # ...to_wiki() owns wiki/ entirely (always writes the full set),
   # it can safely clear .md files at the start of each call.
   for old_article in out.glob("*.md"):
       old_article.unlink()
   ```

The cleanup is correct **iff** `to_wiki()` actually writes the full set. With an empty `communities` dict the loop produces no community articles — only the god-node summaries. The cleanup-then-write pattern collapses the entire wiki/ directory.

## Impact

- **Silent data loss.** No warning, no non-zero exit code. The post-export wiki/ looks superficially valid (a few .md files exist), so automation cannot detect the regression by checking for empty output.
- **Unsafe in CI / pre-push / watch automation.** Any workflow that pairs `update` (or `cluster-only`) with `export wiki` will produce this regression on every run after a clean checkout.
- **Encourages workarounds.** Downstream projects either pin themselves to running the expensive `extract` on every push (LLM cost), or build out-of-tree helpers to fill the gap.

In our case (a private monorepo) we caught this only post-merge, when the affected PR shipped 2,519 file deletions to main. We've since:

- Restored the wiki/ directory from a pre-regression commit.
- Built a local helper that imports `graphify.cluster` + `graphify.analyze` from the installed package and recomputes the sidecar **without LLM calls** (Louvain clustering is deterministic), then injects the sidecar between `update` and `export wiki`.
- Added a "wiki article count drop > 50%" safety guard in our pre-push hook to abort + roll back if any future regression in this class slips through.

These fixes work, but the underlying contract should be repaired upstream so other graphify users don't hit the same trap.

## Suggested fix (one of)

Pick the option that fits the project's design intent best:

1. **Make `update` derive the sidecar.** After writing `graph.json`, if `.graphify_analysis.json` is absent or older than `graph.json`, recompute communities/cohesion/gods/surprises locally (no LLM) and write the sidecar — mirroring the analysis-write block at `__main__.py:2154-2176`. This keeps `update` as the single command users run between extract baselines.

2. **Make `export wiki` fail fast when the sidecar is missing.** Replace the silent `if analysis_path.exists()` fallback with an explicit error (non-zero exit + `"refusing to export wiki: .graphify_analysis.json missing or empty; run `graphify extract .` or `graphify recluster .` first"`). At minimum this prevents data loss; users opt back in to the destructive cleanup only when the precondition is met.

3. **Make `to_wiki()`'s cleanup safe when the community set is empty.** Skip the `for old_article in out.glob("*.md"): old_article.unlink()` step when `communities` is empty (or below a heuristic threshold). The cleanup invariant in the comment ("`to_wiki()` owns wiki/ entirely (always writes the full set)") is only true when the full set is non-empty.

Option 1 is preferred — it closes the semantic gap rather than just papering over the symptom, and is consistent with how downstream consumers expect `update` to refresh derived artifacts.

## Environment

- `graphifyy==0.7.5` (installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`)
- Python 3.13.0 (graphifyy venv interpreter)
- Linux x86_64
- Default repo branch: v7

Happy to test a fix against the same reproducer if it helps.

title: Enhancement: Khmer (km-KH) natural language extraction support
body:
## Summary

Proposing Khmer language support for the semantic extraction pipeline. 
Currently when users run `/graphify` on folders containing Khmer-language 
documents, there is no explicit handling — text either passes through Claude 
blindly with poor results, or tokenization produces garbage graph nodes due 
to Khmer's unsegmented script.

## Why Khmer

- ~17M native speakers, official language of Cambodia
- No current extraction support in the pipeline
- Real use case: fintech apps targeting Cambodian users 
  (expense management, crypto wallets, KYC documents in Khmer)

## The Core Problem

Khmer is **unsegmented** — no spaces between words, unlike Latin-script 
languages. Example:

- English: `account balance transfer` → 3 clean tokens
- Khmer: `សមតុល្យគណនីផ្ទេរប្រាក់` → meaningless without a segmenter

Naive tokenization on Khmer text produces either one giant node or 
character-level noise — neither is useful in a knowledge graph.

## Proposed Technical Approach

**1. Script detection**
Detect Khmer Unicode block (U+1780–U+17FF) before passing to 
the extraction pipeline.

```python
def is_khmer(text: str) -> bool:
    return any('\u1780' <= c <= '\u17FF' for c in text)
```

**2. Segmentation**
Integrate a Khmer word segmenter before concept extraction:
- [`khmer-nltk`](https://github.com/VietHoang1512/khmer-nltk) — 
  lightweight, pip-installable
- [`khmernlp`](https://github.com/sbbic/khmernlp) — alternative

**3. Claude prompt adjustment**
Add a Khmer-aware system prompt variant for the semantic extraction 
step — explicitly instruct the model to handle Khmer segmentation 
and produce Khmer-language node labels.

**4. Optional dependency**
Gate behind an optional install to keep core lightweight:
```bash
pip install graphifyy[khmer]
```

## What I Can Do

I'm a mobile developer based in Cambodia building fintech apps for 
Khmer-speaking users. I have real Khmer-language documents to test 
against (financial reports, KYC docs, app content).

I can:
- Implement the detection + segmentation hook
- Test against real Khmer corpus
- Submit a worked example to `worked/khmer-fintech/`

Happy to start once there's confirmation this fits the roadmap. 
Want to avoid writing code before alignment.

## References

- Khmer Unicode block: U+1780–U+17FF
- `khmer-nltk`: https://github.com/VietHoang1512/khmer-nltk
- ARCHITECTURE.md — for pipeline integration point

title: v0.7.7: rationale-as-node fragments still emitted at ~30% rate despite #563 prompt fix
body:
**graphifyy version:** 0.7.7
**Skill:** `~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` confirmed to contain the rationale-attribute rule from the #563 fix
**Corpus:** Codex monorepo root, 39 files (31 Python, 8 markdown/yaml), ~13k words
**Backend:** Claude subagents (`general-purpose` type), 2 chunks (~20 files each)

## TL;DR

Issue #563 was closed by updating skill.md to instruct the LLM:
> store as a `rationale` attribute on the relevant concept node — do NOT create a separate rationale node or fragment node

The prompt fix is in place (verified in my installed skill). But the LLM still produces rationale-as-node stubs at significant rate. **125 nodes (32% of post-merge total) had `file_type:'rationale'` and labels matching docstring-fragment patterns.**

The prompt-level constraint isn't enforceable. Need a validator-side guard in the merge step.

## Concrete numbers from this run

- Total post-merge nodes: 373
- Nodes with `file_type='rationale'`: **125 (32% of nodes)**
- Of those, labels matching `^.*_rationale_\d+$` ID pattern: 116
- Remaining 9 had prettier labels (\"Django Modular Monolith Architecture\", \"PDPA Compliance and AES-256-GCM PII Encryption\") but were still standalone nodes weakly connected to one parent — also a rule violation per the prompt's *\"Only create a node for something that is itself a named entity or concept\"*.
- Weakly-connected nodes (deg ≤ 1): 195 — **of which 116 are rationale stubs**. The single biggest source of graph noise on a docs-heavy repo.

Effect on graph quality:

- Settings Tab Helpers community cohesion: **0.06** (lowest in graph) — pulled down because 18 of its 48 nodes are rationale stubs each connected to exactly one parent.
- 23 singleton communities, ~half of them rationale stubs that didn't even attach to a parent.
- Inflates god-node centrality: removing the stubs dropped `Helios Backend API` from a top-10 god node back to a normal-degree node.

## Distribution by chunk

The two semantic-extraction subagents behaved differently:

| Chunk | Files | Nodes emitted | Rationale stubs | Stub rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| chunk_01 | 20 (8 docs + 12 code) | 68 | ~70 | high |
| chunk_02 | 19 (mostly tests) | 66 | ~55 | medium |

Both chunks received the identical prompt with the rationale-attribute rule. Stub emission was high regardless.

## Why prompt-only fix is insufficient

The model sees rich rationale prose in source (docstrings, AGENTS.md, ADR-style comments) and serializes them as nodes because:

1. \"Don't create rationale nodes\" is a soft prohibition; \"extract entities and relationships\" is the dominant instruction.
2. The schema example still includes `\"file_type\":\"...|rationale\"` as a valid value, which signals \"this is allowed in some context\" — combined with the don't-create-it rule, models tend to err toward emission rather than omission, especially under chunked extraction where they can't see what other chunks did.
3. The model ID-format rules use the **node label** to derive the ID, so a rationale-attribute (which doesn't have an independent label) has no obvious ID slot — making the structural path easier than the attribute path.

## Suggested fixes (any one would help; combined is best)

**A. Validator-side strip in merge step.** In `extract_corpus_parallel` (Kimi backend) and `merge_chunks` (subagent path), drop nodes where:

```python
n['file_type'] == 'rationale' and (
    re.match(r'^[a-z0-9_]+_rationale_\d+$', n['id']) or
    not _is_named_entity_label(n['label'])  # heuristic: contains a noun phrase, not just a sentence fragment
)
```

For the 9 \"prettier-label\" rationale nodes, optionally hoist them to `attrs.rationale` of the most-connected concept node in the same `source_file`. Lossless and addresses the root concern.

**B. Tighten the schema.** Remove `rationale` from `file_type` in the JSON schema example shown to the LLM. The validator can still accept it for back-compat, but the LLM stops seeing it as a documented option.

**C. Add a hard rejection rule.** Replace the soft *\"do NOT create a separate rationale node\"* with a check the model can verify: *\"Before emitting any node with `file_type: 'rationale'`, confirm its label is a named entity (concept name, principle, design pattern). If it's a sentence fragment, attach it as a `rationale` attribute on a code/document node instead.\"* This gives the model a verifiable test to run before serializing.

## Reproduction

Any docs-heavy monorepo will trigger this. Specifically reproducible on the public Codex code (private fork of Rooftopiq's monorepo, but the symptom is independent of repo content — it's any corpus with multi-paragraph docstrings or AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / ADR-style markdown).

## Related

- #563 (closed) — prompt-level fix that this run shows is necessary but not sufficient.
- #657 (closed) — adjacent fix for the `concept`-instead-of-`rationale` hallucination.
- #198 (open) — different but adjacent: AST/semantic merge alignment. The rationale stubs amplify that issue because they pollute the side that should be enriching the AST graph.

title: Add optional Google Workspace shortcut export
body:
## Summary

- add opt-in Google Workspace shortcut export for `.gdoc`, `.gsheet`, and `.gslides`
- wire `graphify extract <path> --google-workspace` and `GRAPHIFY_GOOGLE_WORKSPACE=1` through detection and incremental extraction
- export shortcuts to Markdown sidecars under `graphify-out/converted/` using the authenticated `gws` CLI, with Sheets rendered through the new `[google]` extra
- document setup and add no-network tests for shortcut parsing, conversion, and detection behavior

## Why this helps

- Google Workspace shortcut files are only local pointers, so Graphify can otherwise see the filenames but not the real Doc, Sheet, or Slide content behind them.
- This makes native Google Workspace material usable as first-class corpus input: extracted entities, relationships, communities, wiki pages, and reports can be based on actual document content rather than shortcut metadata.
- Teams that already work in shared Drive folders get a repeatable path instead of manually exporting every Google file before each graph refresh.
- The integration is deliberately opt-in, so existing local-only extraction stays unchanged and there is no surprise auth or network access unless `--google-workspace` or `GRAPHIFY_GOOGLE_WORKSPACE=1` is set.
- Exports are written as sidecars under `graphify-out/converted/`, keeping source files untouched while still fitting the existing detection and incremental extraction flow.

## Tests

- `python3 -m py_compile graphify/google_workspace.py graphify/detect.py graphify/__main__.py tests/test_google_workspace.py tests/test_detect.py`
- `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_google_workspace.py tests/test_detect.py tests/test_extract.py tests/test_incremental.py tests/test_pipeline.py -q`
- `uv run python -m graphify --help | rg -n "google-workspace|extract <path>|Google Workspace"`
- `git diff --cached --check`

title: fix: extract CommonJS require() imports as EXTRACTED edges
body:
## Summary

The JS/TS extractor only handled ES `import` statements. CommonJS `require()` calls produced zero import edges, which forced the call-graph pass to mark every cross-file call in CJS Node.js codebases as INFERRED — even when the binding was a top-of-file destructured `const { x } = require('./mod')`.

This patch wires three patterns into `_js_extra_walk` via a new `_require_imports_js` helper:

- `const { foo, bar: alias } = require('./mod')` → `imports_from` + per-symbol `imports`
- `const mod = require('./mod')` → `imports_from`
- `const x = require('./mod').y` → `imports_from` + symbol edge for `y`

Path resolution (relative / tsconfig alias / bare module) is factored out of `_import_js` into `_resolve_js_import_target` so ES and CJS share it.

The arrow-function path inside `_js_extra_walk` is preserved unchanged (regression test included).

## Why this matters

Node.js codebases that haven't migrated to ESM (build tooling, Express apps, CLI scripts, older monorepos) currently produce graphs where the EXTRACTED/INFERRED audit signal is wrong: every cross-file call collapses to INFERRED because no import edge ever pinned the binding to a target file. The honesty contract degrades to "trust nothing," which defeats one of graphify's core value props.

Validated against a real 92-file CJS Symphony orchestrator: the 5 previously-INFERRED edges from `runExecute()` (`loadFoundation`, `validateDispatchConfig`, `fetchSymphonyIssues`, `listSymphonyWorktrees`, `workspacePathForIssue`) all resolve to top-of-file destructured requires that the new handler picks up.

## Test plan

- [x] 4 new tests in `tests/test_extract.py`:
  - `test_extract_js_destructured_require_imports_from`
  - `test_extract_js_destructured_require_named_symbols`
  - `test_extract_js_member_require_emits_property_symbol`
  - `test_extract_js_arrow_function_still_extracted` (regression)
- [x] All 26 existing tests in `test_extract.py` pass
- [x] Confidence guarantee preserved: every new edge is `EXTRACTED` (passes `test_structural_edges_are_extracted`)

## Notes

- Does not touch ES `import` handling — `_import_js` still runs unchanged for `import_statement` nodes
- Symbol-level edges only emit when the require target resolves to a file in the corpus (so destructured names of bare `require('lodash')` won't pollute the graph with phantom symbol edges)
- TypeScript `import =` syntax is intentionally out of scope (it parses differently and is rare)

title: bug: query/path/explain commands ignore GRAPHIFY_OUT env var, hardcode 'graphify-out/graph.json'
body:
## Summary

The `query`, `path`, and `explain` subcommands hardcode the graph path as `"graphify-out/graph.json"` instead of using the `_GRAPHIFY_OUT` variable that is already defined at the top of `__main__.py` and correctly reads the `GRAPHIFY_OUT` environment variable.

## Affected code

File: `graphify/__main__.py`

```python
# Line 19 — correctly reads env var:
_GRAPHIFY_OUT = os.environ.get("GRAPHIFY_OUT", "graphify-out")

# Lines 1295, 1380, 1428 — hardcoded, ignores _GRAPHIFY_OUT:
graph_path = "graphify-out/graph.json"   # ← bug
```

All three occurrences are in the same pattern:
- `cmd == "query"` (line 1295)
- `cmd == "path"` (line 1380)
- `cmd == "explain"` (line 1428)

## Reproduction

```bash
# Set custom output dir
GRAPHIFY_OUT=".graphify" graphify query "How does module X connect to Y?"
# error: graph file not found: /path/to/project/graphify-out/graph.json
#        ↑ ignores GRAPHIFY_OUT, always looks in hardcoded "graphify-out/"
```

Even though the graph lives in `.graphify/graph.json`, the command fails because it never consults `_GRAPHIFY_OUT`.

## Root cause

`_GRAPHIFY_OUT` is used in other commands (e.g. `cluster-only`, `tree`, `watch`) but was not applied to `query`, `path`, and `explain`.

## Fix

Replace the three hardcoded defaults with `f"{_GRAPHIFY_OUT}/graph.json"`:

```diff
-        graph_path = "graphify-out/graph.json"
+        graph_path = f"{_GRAPHIFY_OUT}/graph.json"
```

Apply to all three occurrences: lines 1295 (`query`), 1380 (`path`), 1428 (`explain`).

The `--graph` override already works correctly — this only affects the default path when `--graph` is not supplied.

## Expected behavior

```bash
GRAPHIFY_OUT=".graphify" graphify query "..."   # reads .graphify/graph.json ✓
GRAPHIFY_OUT="custom-out" graphify path "A" "B" # reads custom-out/graph.json ✓
graphify explain "Foo"                           # falls back to graphify-out/graph.json ✓
```

## Environment

- graphifyy version: latest (pip)
- Python 3.12
- Linux

title: Feature: Add Amazon Bedrock backend for headless semantic extraction
body:
## Feature idea

Add Amazon Bedrock as an optional backend for Graphify semantic extraction.

Today, code extraction stays local, while docs/PDFs/images and other semantic sources can be extracted through supported LLM backends such as Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Kimi, or Ollama. Bedrock would give AWS-based teams another approved route for the same semantic extraction step without changing the graph-building pipeline.

## Why this helps

- Enterprise teams often already govern model access through AWS IAM, AWS accounts, regions, billing, and model-access approvals.
- Bedrock lets those teams use approved foundation models without distributing separate vendor API keys to every developer or CI job.
- It makes Graphify easier to adopt in AWS-first or regulated environments where sending internal corpus material directly to standalone model APIs may be harder to approve.
- The output would still be the same Graphify artifacts: `graphify-out/graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, HTML/wiki/Obsidian exports, etc.

## Proposed user flow

```bash
export AWS_PROFILE=my-profile
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
export GRAPHIFY_BEDROCK_MODEL="anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0"

graphify extract ./docs --backend bedrock
```

A model override could also work through the existing `--model` flag:

```bash
graphify extract ./docs --backend bedrock --model anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0
```

## Implementation sketch

- Add `bedrock` to the backend registry in `graphify/llm.py`.
- Add a `boto3` optional extra, for example `graphifyy[bedrock]`.
- Use `bedrock-runtime` with the Converse API where possible, since it gives a consistent chat interface across supported Bedrock models.
- Read credentials through the normal AWS provider chain: `AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, environment credentials, SSO, or role-based credentials in CI.
- Support `GRAPHIFY_BEDROCK_MODEL` and `--model` for model or inference-profile IDs.
- Map Graphify's existing system prompt + user message into Bedrock `system`, `messages`, and `inferenceConfig` fields.
- Parse Bedrock text output back through Graphify's existing JSON parser and return the same `nodes`, `edges`, `hyperedges`, token counts, and model metadata shape as other backends.
- Optionally support Bedrock Guardrails later via env/config, but keep the first version focused on extraction.

## Notes / open questions

- Should Bedrock default to an Anthropic Claude model, Amazon Nova model, or require an explicit `GRAPHIFY_BEDROCK_MODEL`?
- Should Graphify estimate Bedrock cost from model-specific pricing, or report token counts only until pricing metadata is added?
- Should docs call out that Bedrock still sends semantic corpus content to AWS Bedrock, while code AST extraction remains local?

title: AST extractor: 25 reversed calls edges + 3 under-classified cross-file calls (TS extractor)
body:
# `graphifyy` v0.7.0 ΓÇö AST extractor emits wrong-direction `calls` edges + under-classifies cross-file calls

**Package:** [`graphifyy`](https://pypi.org/project/graphifyy/) v0.7.0
**Repo:** https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify
**Environment:** Windows 11, Python 3.14, graphifyy 0.7.0 site-packages install
**Reproducer project:** A React + TypeScript + Vite project (`forex-backtester`, ~144 nodes / 178 edges after `/graphify update`)

Two distinct bugs in the TypeScript AST extractor. Together they make ~15% of `calls` edges in a single small project either reversed in direction or under-classified in confidence.

---

## Bug 1 ΓÇö Intra-file `calls` edges have caller and callee swapped

When a function `A()` defined in file X calls another function `B()` also defined in file X, the extractor emits an edge `B --calls--> A` instead of `A --calls--> B`.

This directly violates the rule documented in graphify's own `SKILL.md`:

> Code files: when adding `calls` edges, source MUST be the caller (the function/class doing the calling), target MUST be the callee. Never reverse this direction.

### Concrete examples ΓÇö 25 swapped edges in one project

#### `src/engine/MQL4Preprocessor.ts` (6 swaps)

| # | Reported (wrong) | Actual direction in source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parseInputParam` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `parseInputParam` (called from inside `preprocessMQL4` body, ~L430) |
| 2 | `expandMultiDecl` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `expandMultiDecl` |
| 3 | `convertTypedDeclaration` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `convertTypedDeclaration` |
| 4 | `applyConstants` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `applyConstants` |
| 5 | `joinMultilineParens` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `joinMultilineParens` |
| 6 | `fixClassBodies` -> `preprocessMQL4` | `preprocessMQL4` -> `fixClassBodies` |

All six callees are invoked from inside the `preprocessMQL4` body.

#### `src/engine/BacktestEngine.ts` (1 swap)

| # | Reported (wrong) | Actual direction in source |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `calcStats` -> `runBacktest` | `runBacktest` -> `calcStats` (calls at L206, L1312, L1470) |

#### `src/engine/Indicators.ts` (18 swaps)

`getPrices` helper ΓÇö every consumer reported reversed:

| # | Reported (wrong) | Actual direction |
|---|---|---|
| 8  | `getPrices` -> `sma`   | `sma`   -> `getPrices` |
| 9  | `getPrices` -> `ema`   | `ema`   -> `getPrices` |
| 10 | `getPrices` -> `wma`   | `wma`   -> `getPrices` |
| 11 | `getPrices` -> `iMA`   | `iMA`   -> `getPrices` |
| 12 | `getPrices` -> `rsi`   | `rsi`   -> `getPrices` |
| 13 | `getPrices` -> `bands` | `bands` -> `getPrices` |

MT4-style `iXXX` facades ΓÇö every facade reported as a callee of its own internal helper:

| # | Reported (wrong) | Actual direction |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | `sma` -> `iMA`         | `iMA` -> `sma` |
| 15 | `ema` -> `iMA`         | `iMA` -> `ema` |
| 16 | `wma` -> `iMA`         | `iMA` -> `wma` |
| 17 | `rsi` -> `iRSI`        | `iRSI` -> `rsi` |
| 18 | `macd` -> `iMACD`      | `iMACD` -> `macd` |
| 19 | `bands` -> `iBands`    | `iBands` -> `bands` |
| 20 | `atr` -> `iATR`        | `iATR` -> `atr` |
| 21 | `stochastic` -> `iStochastic` | `iStochastic` -> `stochastic` |
| 22 | `sma` -> `iCCI`        | `iCCI` -> `sma` |

Internal indicator chains ΓÇö also reversed:

| # | Reported (wrong) | Actual direction |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | `sma` -> `bands`       | `bands` -> `sma` |
| 24 | `ema` -> `macd`        | `macd` -> `ema` |
| 25 | `sma` -> `stochastic`  | `stochastic` -> `sma` |

### Likely root cause

The AST visitor handling `CallExpression` nodes appears to emit `(callee_name, enclosing_function_name, "calls")` instead of `(enclosing_function_name, callee_name, "calls")` ΓÇö i.e. source and target are swapped at insert time. Probable location: the TypeScript tree-sitter extractor. Audit any spot that builds a `calls` edge from a `CallExpression` / `MemberExpression` node.

### Impact

Caller/callee swap inverts the graph's meaning for any DiGraph downstream use ΓÇö path queries, dependency tracing, blast-radius / impact analysis all return wrong results in the swapped direction.

---

## Bug 2 ΓÇö Cross-file `calls` edges marked `INFERRED 0.8` instead of `EXTRACTED 1.0`

When function `A()` in file X explicitly calls function `B()` imported via `import { B } from './Y'`, the edge `A --calls--> B` is correctly directed but gets `confidence: "INFERRED", confidence_score: 0.8` instead of `EXTRACTED, 1.0`.

These are not heuristic name matches ΓÇö they are `import { X } from './module'` followed by a literal `X(args)` call site in a function body. Fully deterministic.

### Concrete examples ΓÇö 3 cases in one project

| # | Caller | Callee | Site | Reported | Should be |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parseEAParams` (`src/engine/BacktestEngine.ts:67`) | `preprocessMQL4` (imported from `./MQL4Preprocessor`) | body literally `return preprocessMQL4(code).params;` | INFERRED 0.8 | EXTRACTED 1.0 |
| 2 | `runBacktest` (`src/engine/BacktestEngine.ts:914`) | `preprocessMQL4` (same import) | `const preResult = preprocessMQL4(eaCode);` | INFERRED 0.8 | EXTRACTED 1.0 |
| 3 | `handleEAInput` (`src/components/LeftPanel.tsx:120`) | `parseEAParams` (imported from engine) | `const params = parseEAParams(code);` | INFERRED 0.8 | EXTRACTED 1.0 |

### Likely root cause

The extractor traces same-file calls as deterministic but cross-file calls fall back to a name-matching heuristic that under-classifies them. Or imports are only resolved when emitting `imports` edges ΓÇö call expressions to imported names then take the heuristic path even though the binding is statically resolvable.

### Impact

Trips graphify's own `SKILL.md` "Are the X INFERRED edges actually correct?" Suggested-Question logic, sending users to manually verify edges that are in fact fully deterministic. Drowns genuine inferences in noise.

---

## Severity / impact summary

- 25 reversed-direction edges + 3 under-classified edges in a single 144-node, 178-edge graph from one project.
- Roughly **15% of all `calls` edges** are wrong in direction or confidence.
- Both bugs land in the same TypeScript AST extractor path. They are likely to affect the JavaScript extractor too, and may have analogues in the Python / other-language extractors depending on shared edge-construction code.

## Suggested fix

1. Audit `CallExpression` handling in the TypeScript AST visitor. Ensure the emitted edge tuple is always `(enclosing_function_id, callee_id, "calls")`, not the reverse. Add a unit test: a single file with `function a() { b(); } function b() {}` must produce exactly one edge `a --calls--> b`.
2. For cross-file calls, when the callee identifier resolves to an imported binding (already known when the `imports` edge is emitted), classify the `calls` edge as `EXTRACTED, 1.0`. Reserve `INFERRED` for genuinely unresolved name matches across files.
3. Consider asserting at edge-insertion time that for `relation == "calls"`, source must be a function/method node, not the callee ΓÇö this would have caught Bug 1 immediately.

## Reproduction

```
pip install graphifyy==0.7.0
# In a TypeScript project where intra-file functions call each other:
/graphify update          # via the Claude Code skill, or the equivalent CLI invocation
# Inspect graph.json for relation: "calls" edges with source/target both in the same file.
```

The reproducer project used here is a React+TS+Vite codebase. The pattern reproduces with any TS file containing a top-level function whose body invokes another top-level function in the same file.

title: feat: add .qmd file extension support
body:
This PR adds support for [Quarto](https://quarto.org) markdown (`.qmd`) files by routing them through the existing `extract_markdown` pipeline.

Since `.qmd` files are largely compatible with standard Markdown, this change only adds `.qmd` support at the detection and dispatch layers.

Changes included in this PR:

* Add `.qmd` to document file extension detection
* Update export logic to properly sanitize `.qmd` filenames
* Add `.qmd` extractor dispatch using the existing markdown extractor
* Update watch comments to include `.qmd` files

Quarto supports executable fenced code blocks using language labels wrapped in curly braces:

````markdown
```{python}
# some code
```
````

The only notable difference is that Quarto executable code blocks use labels like `{python}`, so `extract_markdown` produces `"code: {python}"` instead of `"code: python"`. I believe this should be fine since the label is only used for display and the code block itself is still extracted correctly.

title: MCP server exposes 0 resources — only tools accessible via MCP
body:
## Summary

When `python -m graphify.serve graphify-out/graph.json` runs as an MCP server, `ListResources` returns an empty list. Only tools are exposed.

This means MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) cannot read `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, the audit, the surprises section, or any of the rich derived artifacts via MCP — they have to fall back to disk reads, which defeats the purpose of the MCP layer.

## Repro

```bash
graphify update . --force
python3 -m graphify.serve graphify-out/graph.json &

# In any MCP client:
ListMcpResources(server="graphify")
# → returns []
```

Compare gitnexus's MCP which exposes:
- `gitnexus://repos`
- `gitnexus://setup`
- and dynamic templated URIs like `gitnexus://repo/{name}/context`, `gitnexus://repo/{name}/clusters`

## Proposed resources

Useful resources to expose via MCP:

| URI | Mime | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `graphify://stats` | text/yaml | nodes / edges / communities / extracted-vs-inferred ratios |
| `graphify://god-nodes` | text/yaml | top-N most-connected nodes |
| `graphify://surprises` | text/yaml | surprising-connections section from GRAPH_REPORT.md |
| `graphify://audit` | text/yaml | EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS confidence breakdown |
| `graphify://community/{id}` | text/yaml | members of a specific community by ID or label |
| `graphify://report` | text/markdown | full GRAPH_REPORT.md |
| `graphify://questions` | text/yaml | suggested questions list |

## Why this matters

graphify already computes all of this and writes it to `graphify-out/`. Wrapping it as MCP resources makes it directly discoverable + callable from any MCP-aware agent without bespoke filesystem reads. Today, agents using graphify via MCP only have a thin tool surface (`query_graph`, `get_node`, `get_neighbors`, `god_nodes`, `graph_stats`, `shortest_path`, `get_community`) and have to grep the disk to access the analytical outputs.

## Version

graphify 0.7.8 (uv tool installed). Confirmed via `ListMcpResourcesTool(server="graphify")` returning `No resources found.`

## Found by

CoreDrive (Hussanlal/CoreDrive) brutal-DA audit 2026-05-07 — comparing graphify vs gitnexus MCP surface side-by-side for a Flutter codebase. Filed in the same audit cycle that surfaced the gitnexus FTS-RO bug.

title: fix(extract): use language_tsx for .tsx files to enable JSX-aware parsing
body: ## Problem `tree-sitter-typescript` ships two grammars: - `language_typescript` — pure TypeScript, no JSX support - `language_tsx` — JSX-aware variant for `.tsx` files Currently both `.ts` and `.tsx` are parsed with `language_typescript` (see `_TS_CONFIG` in `extract.py`). The result: every `.tsx` file produces hundreds of ERROR nodes, and **every function declaration, arrow function, and `call_expression` nested inside a JSX tree is silently dropped from the extracted graph.** ## Demonstration — raw tree-sitter parse of a real React component `HistoryPanel.tsx` (261 LoC, typical React component with helpers + map+JSX render): | Metric | `language_typescript` | `language_tsx` | |---|---:|---:| | ERROR count | **276** | **0** | | `call_expression` count | 25 | **37** (+12) | | `jsx_expression` count | 0 | **45** | | `arrow_function` count | 5 | **18** (+13) | ## Effect on the extracted graph Running `graphify update --force` on a representative 124-file Tauri+React codebase before vs after this patch: | Metric | Before | After | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Nodes | 303 | **618** | +104% | | Edges | 482 | **779** | +62% | | Communities | 28 | **45** | +61% | | Parse errors per `.tsx` | 276 | **0** | — | ## Fix Add `_TSX_CONFIG` that mirrors `_TS_CONFIG` but selects `language_tsx`, and route `.tsx` files there in `extract_js()`. `.ts` continues to use `language_typescript` (unchanged). ## Tests Three new tests in `tests/test_extract.py` plus a `sample.tsx` fixture: 1. **`test_extract_tsx_finds_helpers_and_component`** — `fmtDate`, `fmtCount`, and `App` are captured. 2. **`test_extract_tsx_jsx_expression_calls_resolve`** — `{fmtDate(now)}` produces a `calls` edge. 3. **`test_extract_tsx_uses_tsx_grammar`** — wiring guard. All 32 tests in `test_extract.py` pass. The 11 pre-existing failures elsewhere (`test_multilang.py` SQL, `test_ollama.py` backend detection, `test_hooks.py`, `test_incremental.py`) reproduce on `v7` without this patch — unrelated to this change. ## Scope note This PR fixes the **parsing layer** only. Calls inside deeply nested arrow function callbacks like `items.map(x => {f(x)})` are still missed because the call extraction logic does not descend into arrow function bodies nested inside JSX expressions. That is a separate enhancement and will be addressed in a follow-up PR — fixing parsing first unblocks it. ## Reproduce ```bash git clone https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify cd graphify && uv venv && uv pip install -e . .venv/bin/graphify . # measure before git fetch origin pull//head && git checkout FETCH_HEAD .venv/bin/graphify update --force . # measure after ```

title: feat(extract): cross-language Tauri bridge — resolve invoke() ↔ #[tauri::command]
body:
## Why

Tauri apps dispatch from TypeScript to Rust through a string-based registry:

```typescript
// TS side
import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";
const r = await invoke<HealthReport>("cmd_health_check");
```

```rust
// Rust side
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn cmd_health_check() -> Result<HealthReport, String> { ... }
```

Currently graphify extracts these as two disconnected halves — TS wrappers like `healthCheck()`, `scrapeStart()`, `exportXlsx()` end up as **degree-1 orphan nodes** in the graph despite being central to the application's behaviour. The Rust handlers similarly look unreachable.

## What

Three new pieces in `extract.py`:

| Piece | Where | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `_collect_rust_tauri_commands` | end of `extract_rust` | Walks the Rust AST. For every `function_item` whose preceding sibling is an `attribute_item` containing `tauri::command` (or bare `command` after `use tauri::command`), registers `{name, node_id, source_file, line}`. Reuses the `node_id` `extract_rust` already produced so post-processing hooks edges onto existing nodes. |
| `_collect_js_tauri_invokes` | end of `extract_js` (`.ts`/`.tsx` only) | Walks the JS AST and collects every `invoke("name", ...)` call whose first argument is a static string. tree-sitter-typescript parses `await invoke<T>("X")` with `await invoke` as the `call_expression`'s `function` field, so detection unwraps `await_expression` to find the `invoke` identifier inside. |
| `_resolve_tauri_bridges` | end of `extract()` after `id_remap` | Joins the two registries and emits one `relation: invokes`, `context: tauri_command`, `confidence: EXTRACTED` edge per `(TS caller → Rust handler)` pair. |

## Effect on a real Tauri+React codebase

124 files (TypeScript + Rust + assets), `graphify update --force`:

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total edges | 779 | **971** | +192 |
| `invokes` edges | 0 | **21** | +21 |
| Communities | 45 | **53** | +8 |

Sample bridges (caller in TS → handler in Rust):

```
healthCheck()        → cmd_health_check()
scrapeStart()        → cmd_scrape_start()
scrapeStop()         → cmd_scrape_stop()
exportXlsx()         → cmd_export_xlsx()
readPreview()        → cmd_read_preview()
defaultDesktop()     → cmd_default_desktop()
defaultRepoRoot()    → cmd_default_repo_root()
writeQueriesFile()   → cmd_write_queries()
```

These were all `deg=1` orphan nodes before this PR.

## Safety

The new pass is opt-out by virtue of being **no-op without both halves**:

- Projects with no Rust files → no commands → no edges.
- Projects with no `invoke()` calls → no invokes → no edges.
- Ambiguous command names (defined in 2+ Rust files) are skipped — no guessing.
- Dynamic call sites (`invoke(variable)`) are skipped — only static string literals participate.

Wrapped in `try/except` with logged warning so an unexpected AST shape can never break the main pipeline.

## Tests

10 new tests in `tests/test_tauri_bridge.py`:

- `test_rust_extractor_attaches_tauri_commands` — the main attribute pattern is detected.
- `test_rust_extractor_handles_bare_command_attribute` — `#[command]` after `use tauri::command`.
- `test_rust_extractor_skips_other_attributes` — `#[derive]`, `#[cfg(test)]` ignored.
- `test_ts_extractor_collects_simple_invoke` — `invoke("x")` form.
- `test_ts_extractor_collects_generic_invoke` — `await invoke<T>("x")` form (the await/generic parse quirk).
- `test_ts_extractor_skips_dynamic_invoke` — `invoke(variable)` is rejected.
- `test_extract_bridges_ts_invoke_to_rust_command` — full end-to-end resolution.
- `test_extract_skips_ambiguous_commands` — duplicate command names produce no edge.
- `test_extract_no_op_without_rust_side` — TS-only safety.
- `test_extract_no_op_without_ts_side` — Rust-only safety.

All 10 pass. Pre-existing failures elsewhere (`test_multilang.py` SQL, `test_ollama.py` backend detection) are unrelated and reproduce on `v7` without this patch.

## Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify
cd graphify && uv venv && uv pip install -e .
git fetch origin pull/<this-PR>/head && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
.venv/bin/graphify update --force /path/to/your/tauri-app
# count invokes edges in graphify-out/graph.json
```

title: query/path/explain fail when graph.json uses `edges` instead of `links`
body:
## Summary

`graphify query` fails to load a `graph.json` that contains `edges` but no `links`:

```text
error: could not load graph: 'links'
```

This looks like the same node-link key compatibility class as #738, but affecting the query/path/explain loading paths.

## Environment

- Package: `graphifyy`
- Version observed: `0.7.9`
- Python: `3.12.3`
- OS/runtime: Linux aarch64
- NetworkX installed by `uvx --from graphifyy`

## Reproduction

1. Generate or obtain a `graph.json` shaped like this:

```json
{
  "nodes": [{"id": "a", "label": "A"}, {"id": "b", "label": "B"}],
  "edges": [{"source": "a", "target": "b", "relation": "calls"}],
  "hyperedges": []
}
```

2. Run:

```bash
uvx --from graphifyy graphify query "A" --graph graph.json
```

## Actual behavior

```text
error: could not load graph: 'links'
```

In my repo benchmark, the generated graph artifact had content but only an `edges` key:

```text
nodes: 694
edges: 1993
links key present: false
```

Copying `edges` to `links` made `graphify query` load the same graph, so this is not a partial-index problem; it is a loader/schema compatibility problem.

## Expected behavior

`graphify query`, `graphify path`, and `graphify explain` should accept both historical/current node-link edge keys:

- `links`
- `edges`

If `links` is missing and `edges` is present, the loader should normalize the input before calling `networkx.readwrite.json_graph.node_link_graph(..., edges="links")`, or otherwise call NetworkX with the matching edge-key name.

## Likely fix

Use a tolerant node-link loader everywhere query/path/explain load a graph, similar to the merge compatibility fix from #738:

```python
def _load_node_link(data):
    if "links" not in data and "edges" in data:
        data = dict(data, links=data["edges"])
    try:
        return json_graph.node_link_graph(data, edges="links")
    except TypeError:
        return json_graph.node_link_graph(data)
```

The important bit is to handle `KeyError: 'links'` / missing-key compatibility, not just the NetworkX-version `TypeError` fallback.

## Related

- #738: `merge-graphs` already hit an `edges` vs `links` mismatch.
- #95 / #149: related NetworkX node-link compatibility problems.

title: extract: full-rebuild path skips entity dedup, allowing label-equivalent duplicates to ship into graph.json
body:
## Summary

When `graphify extract` runs without an existing `manifest.json` (e.g. on
fresh clones or in CI environments where `manifest.json` is gitignored),
it routes through the **non-incremental build branch** in `__main__.py`,
which calls `build_from_json()` directly and bypasses
`deduplicate_entities()`. As a result, semantically duplicate nodes
emitted by the LLM during extraction — same `label`, same `source_file`,
different `id` — survive the build and end up in the published
`graph.json`.

The same corpus produces a deduplicated graph in incremental mode and a
duplicated graph in full-rebuild mode. That asymmetry seems unintended.

## Reproduction

1. Set up any small corpus with at least one document file, e.g.
   `docs/example.md` containing enough prose for the semantic extractor
   to produce more than one node referencing the same concept.
2. Run a full extract with no prior `manifest.json`:

   ```bash
   rm -f graphify-out/manifest.json graphify-out/graph.json
   graphify extract docs/ --backend claude --out .
   ```

3. Inspect `graphify-out/graph.json`. Some semantic concepts appear as
   two nodes with identical `label`, identical `source_file`, identical
   metadata (`captured_at`, `author`, etc.), and different `id`s — for
   example IDs whose tokens are reordered:

   ```json
   { "id": "foo_bar_doc",  "label": "Foo Bar", "source_file": "docs/example.md", ... }
   { "id": "bar_foo",      "label": "Foo Bar", "source_file": "docs/example.md", ... }
   ```

4. Now run a second extract with the manifest in place (incremental
   mode), forcing the same files to be rebuilt:

   ```bash
   graphify extract docs/ --backend claude --out .
   ```

   The duplicates are now collapsed into a single node by
   `deduplicate_entities`. Same input, different output.

## Expected behaviour

`graphify extract` should produce the same deduplicated graph
regardless of whether `manifest.json` exists. The full-rebuild path
should run the same entity-dedup pass as the incremental path.

## Actual behaviour

Full-rebuild path skips dedup entirely, so any LLM-emitted
near-duplicates (different IDs, same normalized label) ship as separate
nodes.

## Root cause

In `graphify/__main__.py` (extract command, around line 2136-2144):

```python
if incremental_mode:
    G = _build_merge(
        [merged],
        graph_path=existing_graph_path,
        prune_sources=deleted_files or None,
        dedup=True,
    )
else:
    G = _build_from_json(merged)   # <-- no dedup here
```

`_build_from_json` is the lower-level constructor and does not invoke
`deduplicate_entities`. Only `build()` and `build_merge()` do (see
`graphify/build.py:119-143`).

The dedup logic itself is fine — `deduplicate_entities` in
`graphify/dedup.py:88` already normalizes labels (`_norm` →
lowercase + non-alnum collapse) and unions same-label nodes via a
union-find pass. The bug is purely that the non-incremental code path
never calls it.

This also makes the docstring on `deduplicate_by_label` in
`graphify/build.py:151` ("Called in build() automatically") slightly
misleading — `build()` actually calls `deduplicate_entities` from the
dedup module, not `deduplicate_by_label`. Minor, but worth a look while
you're in there.

### Why this is easy to miss

The non-incremental path is taken whenever `manifest.json` is absent.
Two common cases where that happens:

- Fresh clones (manifest is local state, often gitignored because
  mtimes lie after a fresh checkout).
- CI environments that publish `graph.json` + the content-addressed
  semantic cache but exclude `manifest.json` from the committed
  artifacts.

In both cases, the per-file semantic cache still hits correctly (good —
no wasted LLM calls), but the post-extract build step silently
downgrades, so users get a duplicated graph despite the cache working
as intended.

## Suggested fix

Either of these resolves it:

**Option A — route through `build()`:**

```python
from graphify.build import build as _build
...
else:
    G = _build([merged], dedup=True)
```

**Option B — call `deduplicate_entities` explicitly before
`_build_from_json`:**

```python
from graphify.dedup import deduplicate_entities
...
else:
    merged["nodes"], merged["edges"] = deduplicate_entities(
        merged["nodes"], merged["edges"], communities={}
    )
    G = _build_from_json(merged)
```

Option A is the smaller diff and matches what `build_merge` does
internally.

A regression test that asserts the full-rebuild and incremental-rebuild
graphs are isomorphic (same node count, same labels) on a fixture
corpus would catch any future drift between the two paths.

## Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.7.6
- Python 3.13
- Backend: `claude`
- Platform: macOS / Linux (CI)

title: Harden Google Workspace gws exports
body:
## Summary

Follow-up hardening for the Google Workspace shortcut export added in #752. That implementation is working well in a real Google Drive-backed project, and this carries over the part of that local workflow that mattered for `gws` path validation.

- run `gws drive files export` from the sidecar output directory
- pass a relative `-o` filename instead of an absolute output path
- avoid sending Drive `resourceKey` as an unsupported `files.export` query parameter
- add tests for the subprocess contract and params shape

## Why

Current `gws` validates `--output` against its current working directory. Passing an absolute temp path can fail when Graphify extracts a corpus outside the shell cwd, even if the destination is inside the corpus output tree. Running from the sidecar directory with a relative output filename matches the pattern that has been working in a larger local Graphify workspace.

Drive resource keys are header-based (`X-Goog-Drive-Resource-Keys`), and `gws drive files export` does not currently expose a custom-header flag. This keeps the params aligned with the Drive export schema (`fileId`, `mimeType`) rather than implying resource-key support through an ignored/unsupported query parameter.

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile graphify/google_workspace.py graphify/detect.py graphify/__main__.py tests/test_google_workspace.py tests/test_detect.py`
- `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_google_workspace.py tests/test_detect.py tests/test_incremental.py tests/test_cli_export.py -q`
- local `gws drive files export --dry-run` from an output directory with relative `-o out.txt`; this passed path validation and failed only at local OAuth reauth, as expected on this machine
- `uv run graphify update .`

title: bug: absolute paths in manifest.json, .graphify_root, and cache/ast/*.json break git-shared graphify-out/ across machines
body:
## Problem

Committing `graphify-out/` (or `$GRAPHIFY_OUT`) to git is the documented way to share incremental cache + graph artifacts across a team / CI. Today three artifacts contain absolute paths and break on clone to a different filesystem location:

1. `manifest.json` — keys are absolute (`/home/alice/proj/foo.py`). `detect_incremental` cache miss → full rebuild on every other machine. Same observation as #722 (filed there as a "question").
2. `.graphify_root` — absolute project path. `graphify update` with no args fails (or scans the wrong tree) after clone.
3. `cache/ast/*.json` — `source_file` field on cached nodes/edges is absolute. Not directly fatal but pollutes diffs and leaks user paths into commits. **Not covered by #722.**

`graph.json` is already correctly relativized via `watch._relativize_source_files` (since 0.5.0) — proves the intent and the pattern.

Filing as a separate bug (rather than commenting on #722) because (a) #722 is question-shaped and limited to manifest + `.gitignore`, (b) `cache/ast/*.json` is a distinct artifact with the same root cause, (c) this draft includes a concrete fix + PR offer. Linking #722 to consolidate triage.

## Reproduce

```bash
mkdir /tmp/p && cd /tmp/p && git init -q && echo "def f(): pass" > a.py
graphify update .

# 1) absolute keys in manifest
python3 -c 'import json; print(list(json.load(open("graphify-out/manifest.json")).keys())[:1])'
# ['/tmp/p/a.py']  ← absolute

# 2) absolute project root
cat graphify-out/.graphify_root
# /tmp/p  ← absolute

# 3) absolute source_file in cache/ast
python3 -c 'import json,glob; f=glob.glob("graphify-out/cache/ast/*.json")[0]; d=json.load(open(f)); print({n.get("source_file") for n in d.get("nodes",[])})'
# {'/tmp/p/a.py'}  ← absolute
```

Move `/tmp/p` to `/tmp/q` (or clone the committed `graphify-out/` on another host): incremental detection misses, root resolution breaks, diffs churn on every rebuild.

## Proposed fix

Three small changes mirroring the existing `_relativize_source_files`, each backwards compatible (relpath fallback to abspath when target escapes root):

1. `graphify/detect.py::save_manifest` — relativize keys against `root` before serialization. Skip entries where `os.path.relpath(...).startswith("..")` (paths outside the root) and write them absolute, matching `_relativize_source_files`.
2. `graphify/watch.py::_rebuild_code` — write the user-provided `watch_path` (often `.`) to `.graphify_root` instead of the resolved absolute `watch_root`.
3. `graphify/cache.py::save_cached` — walk `result["nodes"]` + `result["edges"]`, relativize `source_file` fields against `root` using the same helper, before JSON dump.

Symmetric loaders (`load_manifest`, `load_cached`, `__main__` root resolution) re-anchor relative paths against CWD / `--root` — matches the pattern that already works for `graph.json`.

## Workaround (for context)

Two-way `normalize-paths.py` PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook flips manifest, root, and cache/ast paths abs↔rel around every `graphify` invocation. Plus a small runtime shim that patches `watch.py` to pass `manifest_path` explicitly. See `lib/graphify/install.sh::_patch_graphify_watch` and `.nvm-isolated/.claude-isolated/hooks/normalize-paths.py` in [iclaude](https://github.com/ikeniborn/iclaude). Brittle — would rather drop both once upstream lands.

## PR offer

Happy to submit a single PR with the three changes + tests (`test_save_manifest_relativizes_keys`, `test_save_cached_relativizes_source_file`, `test_graphify_root_preserves_relative`) after triage / scope confirmation.

Related: #722.

## Environment

- graphifyy `0.7.7`
- Python 3.12 (uv-managed)
- Project: [iclaude](https://github.com/ikeniborn/iclaude) (`GRAPHIFY_OUT=.graphify` committed to git)
