title: sql extractor: extract ALTER TABLE foreign keys + schema-qualified names
body:
## Problem

`extract_sql()` misses foreign key relationships defined via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES` — it only extracts inline `REFERENCES` within `CREATE TABLE` column definitions.

Many real-world schemas (pg_dump output, enterprise databases) define FK constraints separately. For example, [AdventureWorks](https://github.com/lorint/AdventureWorks-for-Postgres) (68 tables, 5 schemas) defines all 89 FK relationships via ALTER TABLE — graphify currently finds **zero** of them.

Additionally, `_obj_name()` only reads the first `identifier` child of `object_reference` nodes, so schema-qualified names like `Sales.Customer` are truncated to just `Sales`.

## Goal

Make graphify's SQL parser reliable enough that downstream tools can consume `graph.json` as the single source of truth for database schema relationships — instead of re-parsing SQL with regex.

## Changes

**`graphify/extract.py`:**
- **`_obj_name()`**: Read the full `object_reference` text instead of just the first `identifier` child. This preserves schema-qualified names (`Sales.Customer`) while keeping bare names (`users`) unchanged.
- **`walk()` — new `alter_table` handler**: Extract FK edges from `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES`. Reuses existing `table_nids` lookup to connect to previously-seen CREATE TABLE nodes.
- **Inline FK + `_walk_from_refs()`**: Same fix — read full `object_reference` text for schema-qualified references.

**Tests:**
- `test_sql_alter_table_fk_edge` — ALTER TABLE FK produces a `references` edge with no dangling nodes
- `test_sql_schema_qualified_names` — `Sales.Customer` label is preserved (not truncated to `Sales`)
- `test_sql_schema_qualified_alter_fk` — ALTER TABLE with schema-qualified names produces correct edges

All 6 existing SQL tests continue to pass.

## Before / After

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| AdventureWorks FK edges | 0 | 89 |
| Schema-qualified name `Sales.Customer` | Parsed as `Sales` | Parsed as `Sales.Customer` |

## Downstream use case

I uses graphify's `graph.json` to auto-generate per-table schema documentation for AI database agents. Without ALTER TABLE FK extraction, it had to re-implement SQL parsing with regex — this PR eliminates that need.

title: Deterministic extraction, deduplication hardening, portability, and expanded test coverage
body:
This roll-up bundles several independent lines of work that touch extraction reliability, graph determinism, cross-machine portability, and defense against edge-case regressions.

## Deterministic extraction pipeline

- A source-location pre-pass in deduplication prevents entities sharing the same (source_file, source_location) from being treated as independent, with token-level label containment to avoid wrongly merging same-line symbols.
- A prune pipeline removes stale references to nodes that no longer exist in the working tree after incremental rebuilds.
- Deterministic output: manifest.json uses sort_keys; cluster sorting is stabilized so `graphify update` produces repeatable output on unchanged inputs.

## Portability between machines

- Manifest keys are stored root-relative instead of absolute, so graphify-out/ directories committed to git remain usable when cloned on a different machine.
- Legacy absolute keys in manifests are normalized at load time, including macOS /var to /private/var symlink resolution.

## Edge-case hardening

Eight defects found through systematic review of the build, dedup, detect, extract, watch, and symbol_resolution modules were resolved:

- Stale nodes from deleted or modified source files no longer survive incremental graph merges.
- Watch rebuilds now filter preserved nodes whose source files have been removed.
- build_from_json guards against collapsing parallel edges with different relation types between the same endpoints.
- Intra-file call resolution detects ambiguous duplicate labels and prefers scope-qualified labels over bare ones.
- Cross-file call resolvers now track (source, target, relation) triples instead of only (source, target) pairs.
- Source-location dedup uses token-level rather than character-level substring containment.
- Incremental detection no longer skips content re-hashing when a file's mtime hasn't changed within the second-resolution filesystem clock.
- Normalized endpoint ID collision detection with overlap threshold and suffix disambiguation.

## Additional file format support

- .json and .jsonc are now indexed as document types alongside .yaml and .yml for document extraction.

## Test coverage

- Added unit tests spanning cache, dedup, export, ingest, llm_backends, security, tree_html, cluster, detect, manifest, and watch modules.
- pytest.importorskip guards added for optional dependency imports to keep the suite green on GitHub CI.

**69 files changed, +21,176 / -725 lines**

title: feat(extract): add Pascal/Delphi and Lazarus IDE support
body:
## Summary

  Adds full knowledge-graph extraction for Pascal/Delphi codebases and
  Lazarus IDE project files. Developed with Claude Sonnet 4.6.

  ---

  ### 1 — Pascal/Delphi extractor (`extract_pascal`)

  New extractor for `.pas`, `.pp`, `.dpr`, `.dpk`, `.inc` files via
  [tree-sitter-pascal](https://github.com/Isopod/tree-sitter-pascal).

  **Extracted nodes:** file, unit/program/library, class/interface/helper,
  procedure/function implementations.

  **Extracted edges:**
  - `file → contains → module`
  - `module → imports → dependency` (uses clause, resolved to path-based IDs)
  - `class → inherits → base class / interface`
  - `class/module → contains/method → procedure or function`
  - `procedure → calls → procedure` (in-file call resolution, including bare
    `Reset;`-style calls without parentheses)

  **Key design — import resolution:** Uses clause targets are resolved to
  path-based node IDs by scanning all Pascal files under the project root
  (`_pascal_project_root` + `_pascal_resolve_unit` helpers with caching).
  Without this, bare unit names like `SysUtils` resolve to IDs that never
  match any file node, making the entire import graph invisible.

  **Optional dependency:** `pip install tree-sitter-pascal`
  If not installed, `extract_pascal` returns `{"nodes":[], "edges":[], "error":...}`
  and the rest of the pipeline is unaffected.

  ---

  ### 2 — Inherits-edge fix

  The original `declType`/`typeref` handler built `inherits` edge targets
  with `_make_id(_read(child))` — just the bare class name. But class nodes
  use `_make_id(stem, type_name)`, so targets never matched, making the
  entire class hierarchy invisible in the graph.

  Fix adds `_pascal_class_stem_cache` and `_pascal_resolve_class()`: strips
  the conventional `T`/`I` prefix, locates the defining file by stem lookup
  (same cache mechanism as `_pascal_resolve_unit`), and returns the correct
  `_make_id(file_stem, class_name)` ID. RTL/unresolvable bases (e.g.
  `TObject`) fall back to `_make_id(bare_name)` with an explicit stub node,
  following the same pattern as the Python extractor.

  Also removes the `break` that stopped after the first `typeref`, so all
  parents of multi-inheritance declarations are captured.

  ---

  ### 3 — Lazarus form extractor (`extract_lazarus_form`, `.lfm`)

  `.lfm` files are text-based UI component trees. The extractor parses
  `object Name: TClassName ... end` blocks into a containment graph and
  captures `OnXxx = HandlerName` event bindings as `references` edges
  (context: `"event"`) linking each component to its handler procedure.

  ---

  ### 4 — Lazarus package extractor (`extract_lazarus_package`, `.lpk`)

  `.lpk` files are XML package definitions. The extractor reads the package
  name, required package dependencies (`→ imports` edges), and listed unit
  files (`→ contains` edges). Unit names are resolved to path-based node IDs
  via `_pascal_resolve_unit` so they link to the same nodes produced by
  `extract_pascal` on `.pas` files.

  ---

  ### Files changed

  | File | Change |
  |---|---|
  | `graphify/extract.py` | `extract_pascal`, `extract_lazarus_form`, `extract_lazarus_package`, resolution helpers |
  | `graphify/detect.py` | Add `.pas .pp .dpr .dpk .inc .lfm .lpk` to `CODE_EXTENSIONS` |
  | `tests/test_pascal.py` | 28 new tests covering all three extractors |
  | `tests/fixtures/sample.pas` | Representative Delphi fixture |
  | `tests/fixtures/sample.lfm` | Lazarus form fixture |
  | `tests/fixtures/sample.lpk` | Lazarus package fixture |

  ---

  ### Prerequisites

  pip install tree-sitter-pascal

  Wheel for Windows (cp38 abi3): available at
  https://github.com/Isopod/tree-sitter-pascal

  Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(windows): unblock pipeline on cp1252 console + missing __main__ guards
body:
## Summary

Three small Windows-compatibility fixes that all surface during the same first `/graphify` run on a Windows host.

### `graphify/benchmark.py` — `print_benchmark` Unicode crash on cp1252
`print_benchmark()` unconditionally prints U+2500 (box drawing) and U+2192 (rightwards arrow). On the legacy Windows console (cp1252) the second `print(...)` call raises `UnicodeEncodeError` mid-output:

```
File "C:\...\graphify\benchmark.py", line 121, in print_benchmark
    print(f"{'─' * 50}")
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 0-49: character maps to <undefined>
```

Adds a `_safe(unicode, ascii_fallback)` helper that detects whether the active stdout encoding can carry the glyph and falls back to ASCII (`-`, `->`) otherwise. Two regression tests cover both branches plus a full `print_benchmark` run against a strict-cp1252 stream.

### `graphify/extract.py` — opaque `BrokenProcessPool` failure on Windows-spawn
`ProcessPoolExecutor` on Windows uses `spawn`, so worker subprocesses re-import the calling `__main__`. When the caller is `python -c "..."` (or any script without `if __name__ == "__main__":`), the workers recursively spawn themselves and the pool dies. The user-visible failure is a ~290-line traceback ending in `BrokenProcessPool` — the actual cause (`RuntimeError: An attempt has been made to start a new process before the current process has finished its bootstrapping phase.`) is buried.

`_extract_parallel` now:
- catches `BrokenProcessPool`,
- prints a one-line warning that names the `__main__`-guard idiom and points at `parallel=False`,
- returns `False` so the public `extract()` routes to the existing `_extract_sequential` path.

Two regression tests:
- `_extract_parallel` returns `False` (not raises) when the pool breaks, and the warning includes both `BrokenProcessPool` and `__main__`.
- `extract()` calls `_extract_sequential` when `_extract_parallel` returns `False`, and still produces real nodes.

### `graphify/skill-windows.md` — quote-escaping minefield
Every `python -c "..."` block (30 in total) is replaced with a literal here-string + run + delete pattern:

```powershell
@'
<python source>
'@ | Out-File -FilePath .graphify_step_<name>.py -Encoding utf8
python .graphify_step_<name>.py
Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue .graphify_step_<name>.py
```

Why: any double-quote inside the Python source previously had to be backslash-escaped for the shell, and PowerShell's parser ate them inconsistently — failing on f-strings like `f'AST: {len(result["nodes"])} nodes'`. The new form passes Python source to disk literally, so what the model writes is what Python sees. The AST step's script template also gets an explicit `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard so multi-core extraction works on Windows even before the runtime fallback above kicks in. All 31 resulting heredoc blocks parse cleanly under `ast.parse`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_benchmark.py tests/test_extract.py` — 48 passed (4 new tests)
- [x] `pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_languages.py --ignore=tests/test_multilang.py --ignore=tests/test_ollama.py` — 492 passed, no regressions
- [x] `ast.parse` smoke check across all 31 heredoc Python blocks in `skill-windows.md`
- [x] Verified end-to-end against a real corpus (357 files, 538K words, 4947 nodes / 12352 edges) using a local install before opening this PR

## Notes
- No public API change. `_extract_parallel` returns `bool` instead of `None` but it's underscore-prefixed.
- The skill rewrite touches only `skill-windows.md`. `skill.md` (POSIX) is unchanged.
- Discovered while running `/graphify` on a 357-file Angular/TypeScript codebase; both bugs blocked the pipeline and required local workarounds.

title: Recover from context-window-exceeded API errors in adaptive retry
body:
## Summary

`_extract_with_adaptive_retry` already handles output truncation (`finish_reason="length"`) by splitting a chunk in half and recursing. It does not handle the other shape of context overflow: the API **rejecting the prompt outright** with a 400 because the input plus `max_completion_tokens` doesn't fit in the model's context window.

Today that case bubbles out as an `Exception` from `extract_files_direct`, the chunk fails with no output, and `extract_corpus_parallel` logs `[graphify] chunk N/M failed: …` — even though the two halves of that chunk would fit cleanly.

This is the dominant failure mode for local OpenAI-compatible backends (LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama), where the default context window is 4K-32K and a 60K-token chunk packed for cloud Kimi/Claude blows past it the moment you point graphify at a local URL.

## What changed

- Added `_looks_like_context_exceeded(exc)` — heuristic substring match on common error messages (`\"context size\"`, `\"context_length_exceeded\"`, `\"n_keep\"`, `\"prompt is too long\"`, etc.). Works across SDKs without depending on a specific exception class.
- `_extract_with_adaptive_retry` now wraps the `extract_files_direct` call. On a context-exceeded exception it splits the chunk in half and recurses, identically to the `finish_reason="length"` path.
- Single-file overflow returns an empty fragment instead of raising, so the rest of the corpus keeps running. Unrelated errors (rate limit, auth, network) still propagate unchanged.
- 4 new tests in `tests/test_llm_backends.py` covering: matcher accuracy, the split-recurse-and-merge path, single-file give-up, and unrelated-error pass-through.

## Why

Reproduced against qwen3.5-9b on LM Studio (32K ctx) extracting a 215-file corpus. With current `v7` 11/12 chunks aborted with `Error code: 400 - {'error': 'Context size has been exceeded.'}`. With this change overflowing chunks self-heal by splitting until the halves fit; only chunks where a *single file* still overflows are dropped, with a clear stderr warning.

The matching `finish_reason="length"` path that this mirrors has been in the codebase since the adaptive-retry module was introduced — this just extends the same recovery to the symmetric overflow signal.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_llm_backends.py -q` — 12 passed (4 new + 8 existing)
- [x] Manually verified against LM Studio + qwen3.5-9b on a 215-file mixed code/docs corpus

## Risk

Low. The retry only fires when `extract_files_direct` raises *and* the message matches one of the overflow markers. Misses (false negatives) preserve current behaviour — the chunk fails as it does today. False positives just trigger an extra split-retry and waste one round-trip, with the same recovery semantics already in place for output truncation.

title: Post-commit hook spawns unbounded detached Python rebuilds — multi-repo concurrent commits exhaust memory
body:
## Summary

`graphify hook install` registers a git post-commit hook (`hooks.py:46-93`) that
spawns a detached Python process to rebuild the entire repo's graph. The hook
has no concurrency cap, no memory/CPU limit, no timeout, and does not use the
`GRAPHIFY_CHANGED` data it computes. When multiple repos with the hook commit
in the same time window — or when a single watcher fires `_rebuild_code` across
many projects — the system fills with concurrent multi-GB rebuilds.

This caused a full UI freeze on a Mac mini (32 GB RAM) this morning: ~10
concurrent rebuilds, peak 4.1 GB / 99% CPU each, free RAM dropped to 60 MB,
load average hit 31, mouse clicks froze for 30+ minutes.

## Reproduction

1. `graphify hook install` in three or more repos
2. Trigger commits in all of them within ~10 seconds (e.g. via a multi-repo
   sync tool, autocommit script, or `pre-commit` chain)
3. Observe: N independent `python -c "from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code; _rebuild_code(Path('.'))"`
   processes, each holding the full code graph in memory, no shared state,
   no lock, no nice level

Severity scales with repo size and number of repos. On macOS, runaway
`fseventsd` traffic from rebuild output compounds the problem.

## Code References (v0.7.10)

**Issue 1 — No concurrency control on detached rebuild**
`hooks.py:71-91` — `nohup graphify_python -c "..." > $log 2>&1 &` then `disown`.
No lock file, no semaphore, no `nice`/`ionice`, no max-concurrent-rebuilds env.

**Issue 2 — `GRAPHIFY_CHANGED` computed but discarded**
`hooks.py:75-87` — the inline script reads the env var, parses it into
`changed: list[Path]`, then exits if empty. But the actual rebuild on line 87
calls `_rebuild_code(Path('.'), force=_force)` and ignores `changed` entirely.
`_rebuild_code` re-globs every code file every time. For a 446-file repo this
is ~5 s of CPU + heavy fseventsd traffic per commit, even when one file changed.

**Issue 3 — No timeout on the background process**
If a rebuild leaks memory or hangs (network volumes, Spotlight contention,
parser bug on a specific file), it stays alive indefinitely. macOS has no
default kill-after-N-minutes for detached `nohup` children.

## Suggested Fix

1. **Concurrency lock** — `flock` on `~/.cache/graphify/rebuild.lock` (or
   per-repo lock in `<repo>/graphify-out/.rebuild.lock`). Skip if held; an
   in-progress rebuild covers later commits anyway.

2. **Honour `GRAPHIFY_CHANGED`** — extend `_rebuild_code` signature:
   ```python
   def _rebuild_code(
       watch_path: Path,
       *,
       changed_paths: list[Path] | None = None,
       follow_symlinks: bool = False,
       force: bool = False,
   ) -> bool: ...
   ```
   When `changed_paths` is provided, re-extract only those files and merge
   into the existing graph instead of rebuilding from scratch.

3. **Resource limits** — `nice -n 10`, `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT` (default
   10 min), optional `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB` enforced via
   `resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, ...)` in the inline script.

Happy to send a PR for any/all of these if there's interest.

## Environment

- macOS 15.4 (Sequoia), Apple Silicon Mac mini, 32 GB RAM
- Python 3.14.4 (Homebrew)
- graphify 0.7.10 (PyPI)
- Hook installed across ~17 directories via `graphify_watcher_worker.py`

title: [Feature Request] Enhancing Local LLM Performance (Ollama) & High-Core CPU Scaling via graphify.yaml
body:
I’ve been stress-testing `graphify` on a high-end local workstation (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RTX 5090). While the tool is conceptually brilliant, the current hardcoded limits and environment-variable-only configuration create significant bottlenecks for local-first workflows.

Current Bottlenecks Identified:

1. CPU Underutilization: In `extract.py`, `max_workers` is capped at 8. On a 32-thread CPU, this limits AST extraction performance by 400%.
2. Local API Timeouts: The default `token_budget` (60k) and `max_concurrency` (4) are ideal for Cloud APIs but cause `Request timed out` or VRAM OOMs on local Ollama/llama.cpp instances during semantic extraction.
3. Authentication Friction: The CLI blocks execution if `OLLAMA_API_KEY` is missing, even when targeting a local instance where no auth is required.

Proposed Solution: The `graphify.yaml` Configuration Layer
To support the growing segment of local power users, I suggest introducing an optional configuration file (`graphify.yaml`) to override defaults persistently.

Example `graphify.yaml` Structure:

```yaml
# Performance Tuning
extraction:
  max_workers: 32         # Fully utilize high-end CPUs (9950X3D)
  token_budget: 16384     # Optimized for 24GB+ VRAM (Gemma 4 31b)
  max_concurrency: 1      # Avoid local API queue congestion

# Backend Overrides
backend:
  name: "ollama"
  model: "gemma4:31b"
  base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
  # Suggested: bypass API_KEY check if backend is Ollama and base_url is loopback

# Model Parameters
parameters:
  temperature: 0.3        # Deterministic graph generation
  seed: 42
  num_ctx: 65536

```

Why this is a "Win-Win":

* User Experience: Removes the need to re-export `set/export` commands in every terminal session.
* Scalability: `graphify` becomes the gold standard for high-performance local knowledge graph extraction.
* Maintainability: Decouples hardware-specific tuning from the core logic.

Verified Performance:
By manually patching these values in my local instance, I achieved **95% GPU saturation on an RTX 5090** and reduced AST extraction time significantly. I’m happy to provide more telemetry or contribute code snippets if this aligns with the project roadmap!

title: graphify explain/path still crash on MultiGraph edge access
body:
## Summary

`graphify explain` and some path/MCP edge-rendering paths still access edges as if the graph is always a simple Graph:

```python
edata = G.edges[nid, nb]
edata = G.edges[u, v]
```

When `graph.json` has already loaded successfully as a NetworkX `MultiGraph` / `MultiDiGraph`, this crashes during rendering with:

```text
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)
```

This issue is **not** about the `edges`/`links` node-link key mismatch. That was a separate loader/schema compatibility bug. The failure reported here happens **after** the graph loads and is specifically about MultiGraph edge access.

This is the same bug class as #305, but #305's v0.4.11 fix was applied to `_subgraph_to_text()` / query rendering only, not all CLI/MCP call sites.

## Environment

- Package: `graphifyy`
- Version: `0.7.11`
- Python: `3.14` via `uv run --with graphifyy==0.7.11`
- NetworkX: version installed by `graphifyy==0.7.11`
- OS/runtime: Linux aarch64

## Reproduction

Use any node-link `graph.json` that NetworkX loads as a multigraph, for example one with `multigraph: true` or parallel edges between the same source/target pair.

Then run:

```bash
uv run --with graphifyy==0.7.11 graphify explain "REQ-003: Document And PPM Generation" --graph graph.json
```

Observed output:

```text
Node: REQ-003: Document And PPM Generation
  ID:        req_003_document_ppm_generation
  Source:    architecture/feature/req-003-document-and-ppm-generation.md None
  Type:      document
  Community:
  Degree:    1

Connections (1):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../bin/graphify", line 10, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File ".../site-packages/graphify/__main__.py", line 1558, in main
    edata = G.edges[nid, nb]
            ~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/networkx/classes/reportviews.py", line 1368, in __getitem__
    u, v, k = e
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)
```

I also see the same simple-Graph access pattern in path rendering:

```python
# graphify/__main__.py path/explain call sites in v0.7.11
edata = G.edges[u, v]
edata = G.edges[nid, nb]
```

## Expected behavior

All CLI/MCP graph operations should handle both simple graphs and multigraphs consistently.

For a MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph, edge data access should use `G[u][v]` and select one or iterate all parallel edge attribute dicts.

## Likely fix

Centralize edge-data access in a helper and replace direct `G.edges[u, v]` / `G.edges[nid, nb]` lookups:

```python
def _edge_data_for_pair(G, u, v):
    raw = G[u][v]
    if isinstance(G, (nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph)):
        return next(iter(raw.values()), {})
    return raw
```

For commands that should show all relations, use an iterator instead:

```python
def _edge_datas_for_pair(G, u, v):
    raw = G[u][v]
    if isinstance(G, (nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph)):
        return list(raw.values())
    return [raw]
```

Then `explain` can either print the first edge or all parallel relations.

## Related

- #305 fixed the same bug class for `query` / `_subgraph_to_text()` in v0.4.11.

title: [Critical] Context Window Saturation / Missing Session Reset between Chunks (Ollama Backend)
body:
Hey @safishamsi,

Quick follow-up after testing **v0.7.12** on a high-end local setup (RTX 5090, Gemma 4:31b).

We’ve identified a major bottleneck in how the Ollama backend handles multiple chunks. After about 3-4 chunks, the model starts returning the "very few tokens" warning and essentially stops producing valid JSON.

**The Diagnosis:** It appears that `graphify` is not explicitly resetting the Ollama session/context between chunks.

**What's happening:**
In local inference (especially via Ollama’s `/api/generate` or `/api/chat`), if the `context` parameter (the KV cache) isn't cleared or handled statelessly for each new chunk, the model "saturates." It carries the noise and tokens from Chunk 1 and 2 into the context window for Chunk 3. Even with a large 5090 VRAM, the **attention mechanism** gets overwhelmed by the uncleared history, leading to the "0-token" or "closing-bracket-only" responses we are seeing.

**The Evidence:**

* Chunk 1-2: Fast, perfect inference.
* Chunk 3-4: Sudden drop in token count, "few tokens" warning, but the GPU is still under load (processing the saturated context).
* Restarting the script: Fixes it immediately for the first few chunks again.

**The Fix:**
Each new chunk or file extraction call to the Ollama API should be **stateless**. Please ensure that for every new extraction call, the `context` array is either empty or the session is explicitly reset. A simple flag or a fresh request object per chunk would solve this and prevent the "context-leak" that currently ruins long extraction runs.

Looking forward to v0.7.13! 🚀

title: skill.md --update inline merge bypasses fixed build_merge() — direction-inversion bug from #760 still hits Claude Code skill workflow
body:
**Package:** [`graphifyy`](https://pypi.org/project/graphifyy/) v0.7.13
**Skill version installed:** 0.7.8 (warning printed by CLI)
**Environment:** macOS 24.6.0, Python 3.11 (uv tool install of `graphifyy`)
**Related (closed):** #760

## Summary

Issue #760 fixed the `build_merge()` direction-inversion bug in `build.py`. The fix is correctly used by the CLI `graphify update <path>` command (`__main__.py:2608` calls `_build_merge`).

However, the bundled **`skill.md`** template still ships a hand-rolled merge block in its `--update` section that **never calls `build_merge()`**. It uses the exact `node_link_graph()` round-trip pattern that #760 identified as the root cause. As a result, any AI coding assistant that follows the skill instructions (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) re-introduces the very bug #760 closed.

## Evidence

`graphify-0.7.13/skill.md` line 788 (the `--update` flow):

```python
existing_data = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/graph.json').read_text())
G_existing = json_graph.node_link_graph(existing_data, edges='links')   # round-trip — direction lost
...
G_existing.update(G_new)
to_json(G_existing, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json')             # write back inverted
```

Compare with the fix in `build.py:235`:

```python
def build_merge(...):
    ...
    # Read JSON directly instead of going through node_link_graph().
```

The skill never imports `build_merge`.

## Reproduction

1. Build a TypeScript project graph with a small helper imported by many call sites — e.g. an `axios` wrapper called `requestGet` imported in 100+ API files.
2. Run `/graphify --update` (Claude Code skill path), which executes the inline merge code from `skill.md`.
3. Inspect `graph.json` for edges where `source = requestGet`. They will all be of the form `requestGet --calls--> getXxx()` despite `requestGet` being a callee, not a caller, in every actual source file.

In one real codebase:
- `requestGet` (5-line axios wrapper) — graph reports **105 outgoing `INFERRED 0.8` `calls` edges**.
- `grep` ground truth: **171 files import `requestGet`**, **178 actual call sites**.
- All 105 edges point the wrong way; another 73 actual call sites are missing entirely.
- Same pattern on every other god helper: `requestPost (32)`, `getEncryptUrl (18)`, `usePageMove (17)`, `getApiEncryptKey (17)`, `getDeviceInfo (12)`, `buildUrl (10)`.

(Bug 2 from #760 — `INFERRED 0.8` for deterministic cross-file calls — is also visible because these edges were inserted by an older version, then preserved across every `--update` because the skill's inline path never re-extracts edges that aren't in the changed-file set.)

## Why this matters

- The Claude Code skill is the **default invocation path** for most users (`/graphify` and `/graphify --update`). Fixing `build_merge()` while leaving the skill template broken means almost no end-user gets the fix.
- The skill template duplicates merge logic instead of calling `build_merge()`, so future `build.py` improvements will silently fail to reach skill users — exactly what happened here.
- Skill is overwritten on every `graphify install`. There is no user-side workaround that survives upgrades.

## Suggested fix

Replace the inline merge block in `skill.md`'s `--update` section with a call to the fixed function:

```python
from graphify.build import build_merge

merged = build_merge(
    existing_path='graphify-out/graph.json',
    new_extraction=new_extract,
    deleted_files=incremental.get('deleted_files', []),
    changed_files=incremental['new_files'].get('code', []),
)
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged))
```

(Adjust signature to whatever `build_merge` already exposes.)

This eliminates ~40 lines of duplicated logic, keeps skill flow in sync with CLI flow, and prevents future `build.py` fixes from being orphaned.

### Optional follow-ups

- Same drift risk exists for the `--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, and `add` subcommand instructions — any block that re-implements logic inline rather than calling a graphify Python entry point is a future drift hazard.
- Consider gating the skill on a minimum graphify version (skill 0.7.8 + package 0.7.13 was the warning seen here). If the inline blocks were replaced with library calls, version mismatch would surface as an `ImportError` instead of a silent semantic regression.

## Severity

Medium-high. The bug is invisible (graph.json still loads, all stats render), but the most prominent output of the skill — the "God Nodes" section of `GRAPH_REPORT.md` — gives users a categorically wrong reading of their codebase's call structure.

title: feat: add --publish flag for understand-quickly registry integration
body:
## Why

[`looptech-ai/understand-quickly`](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly) is a public registry of code-knowledge graphs that ships an MCP server and a stable `registry.json` API. Graphify already builds a knowledge graph from any folder of code — exactly the producer shape the registry is designed for. Wiring a `--publish` flag means any user who runs `graphify extract` can land in the registry with one flag, and AI agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor via MCP) can discover and consume their graph immediately — no extra infrastructure on either side.

- **Discoverability.** Every published graph appears at <https://looptech-ai.github.io/understand-quickly/>.
- **No infrastructure.** Graphs stay in the user's repo (`graphify-out/graph.json`); the registry only stores pointers and fetches from `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
- **Agent-consumable.** Schema validation, drift detection (via `metadata.commit`), and a turnkey MCP server.

## What changes

- A new `graphify/publish.py` module (stdlib-only — `urllib`, `subprocess`, `json`).
- A `--publish` flag on `graphify extract` (opt-in).
- README "Publishing to understand-quickly" paragraph.
- Two unit tests in `tests/test_publish.py`.

When `--publish` is set, after the existing `graph.json` write, graphify:

1. Reads the JSON, merges `metadata.{tool, tool_version, generated_at, commit}` (idempotent), writes it back.
2. If `$UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN` is set, fires a `repository_dispatch` at `looptech-ai/understand-quickly` so the registry's sync workflow re-pulls the entry. If unset, it only stamps the local file and prints one informational line — no network call, no exit-1.

`graphify-out/graph.json` is already in the `gitnexus@1` shape (`nodes` / `links` arrays from `node_link_data`). No schema PR is needed for v0; if you'd later prefer a `graphify@1` schema with shape-specific fields (community detection, god-node scores), the registry has a [format-authoring path](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/protocol.md#7-format-authoring).

## Diff stats

```
 README.md             |  22 ++++++++
 graphify/__main__.py  |  20 +++++++
 graphify/publish.py   | 149 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tests/test_publish.py |  65 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 256 insertions(+)
```

Code change is ~170 LoC excluding tests and the README block.

## No-op default

Without `--publish`, behavior is identical to today. With `--publish` but no `UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN`, only the local file is stamped — no network, no failure mode added to the extract path.

## Token setup

Fine-grained GitHub PAT, single permission:

- **Repository access:** `looptech-ai/understand-quickly` only.
- **Permissions:** `Repository dispatches: write`. Nothing else.

The recommended CI step is the [`looptech-ai/uq-publish-action@v0.1.0`](https://github.com/looptech-ai/uq-publish-action) Marketplace Action:

```yaml
- uses: looptech-ai/uq-publish-action@v0.1.0
  with:
    graph-path: 'graphify-out/graph.json'
    format: 'gitnexus@1'
    token: ${{ secrets.UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN }}
```

For environments that can't use Marketplace Actions, the raw `gh api` / `curl` dispatch in [protocol §4](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/protocol.md#4-auto-publish-tool-side) is the fallback.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_publish.py -v` — both tests green locally.
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_export.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_install.py -q` — 67 pre-existing tests still pass.
- [x] `graphify --help` shows the new `--publish` line under `extract`.
- [ ] (Maintainer) `graphify extract . --publish` with `UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN` set and the repo registered fires the dispatch and the registry's `sync.yml` runs within ~1 minute.
- [ ] (Maintainer) `graphify extract . --publish` with the token set but the repo unregistered prints the registration hint; exit code 0.

## Notes

- This is opt-in for early adopters; nothing in graphify's existing surface needs to break.
- Once a few users land in the registry, we can add `safishamsi/graphify` to the [verified-publisher allowlist](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/verified-publishers.md) for auto-merge of registry updates.
- **Licensing for users.** Submitting via `--publish` is governed by the [Understand-Quickly Data License 1.0](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/DATA-LICENSE.md) — see [protocol §10](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/protocol.md#10-licensing-of-submitted-data). It is opt-in, gated on the user setting `UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN`.

## Links

- Registry: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly>
- Code-graph protocol: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/spec/code-graph-protocol.md>
- Reusable Action: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/uq-publish-action>
- `gitnexus@1` schema: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/schemas/gitnexus@1.json>


---

## Current live state (sweep 2026-05-11)

The registry and its publishing surface are tagged and live:

- **Registry release:** [`looptech-ai/understand-quickly` v0.3.0](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/releases/tag/v0.3.0)
- **CLI:** [`@looptech-ai/understand-quickly-cli@0.1.2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@looptech-ai/understand-quickly-cli) on npm
- **MCP server:** [`@looptech-ai/understand-quickly-mcp@0.1.2`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@looptech-ai/understand-quickly-mcp) on npm
- **Python SDK:** [`understand-quickly` 0.1.1](https://pypi.org/project/understand-quickly/) on PyPI
- **Reusable Action:** [`looptech-ai/uq-publish-action@v0.1.0`](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/understand-quickly-publish) on the GitHub Marketplace
- **MCP Registry entry:** `io.github.looptech-ai/understand-quickly`

Nothing in this PR depends on any pre-release surface — all referenced artifacts are pinned versions.

title: dedup: KeyError 'source' in deduplicate_entities when merging extraction into existing graph.json
body:
## Summary

`graphify extract` crashes during deduplication when merging newly-extracted nodes/edges into an existing `graph.json`. Reproducible across multiple Ollama models on different hosts.

## Stack trace

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/graphify/dedup.py", line 236, in deduplicate_entities
    e["source"] = remap.get(e["source"], e["source"])
                            ~^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'source'
```

## Reproduction

1. Bootstrap graphify with a small markdown vault → existing `graph.json` has nodes + links (NetworkX-style: each link has a `source` key).
2. Add new markdown files with YAML frontmatter to the vault.
3. Run `graphify extract /vault --backend ollama --model qwen2.5:7b --out /data`.
4. Extraction completes (cache fills under `graphify-out/cache/semantic/`), but the dedup step crashes with the trace above.

## What I verified

- All 22 cached LLM responses under `cache/semantic/` contain `nodes` + `edges` + `hyperedges` arrays. Every `edges[i]` has the keys `[confidence, confidence_score, relation, source, source_file, source_location, target, weight]` — none missing `source`. Verified with:
  ```
  find … cache/semantic -name '*.json' -exec cat {} \; \
    | jq -s '[.[].edges[] | select(has("source") | not)]'
  ```
  → empty array.
- The pre-existing `graph.json` has 38 `links` and all of them have `source` too.
- Reproducible with both `qwen2.5:7b` and `qwen3.6:35b` on separate Ollama hosts (so it's not a model-output shape issue).

## Hypothesis

Somewhere between `combined["edges"]` construction and `deduplicate_entities()` (around `graphify/dedup.py:226–240`), an edge with no `source` key is being included. Two candidates:

- **Hyperedge → edge promotion.** If hyperedges are being flattened into the edges list during merge and the flattening doesn't always emit a `source` key, that would match.
- **NetworkX-format `links` → edge format mismatch.** The pre-existing `graph.json` stores edges under `links` (NetworkX convention) with `source`/`target` as node-IDs. If those are being loaded back into the dedup pipeline as "edges" but with a slightly different shape (e.g. integer IDs vs string keys, or stripped during a normalization step), one of them might lose `source` before the `remap.get` line.

A simple guard at line 236 (`if "source" not in e: continue` or equivalent, with a debug log of the offending edge) would both fix the crash and surface which path is producing the malformed edge.

## Workaround

Reverted `manifest.json` to a pre-extract backup so graphify reprocesses cleanly. The upstream markdown source files themselves are produced correctly; it's only the merge into the existing graph that fails.

## Environment

- graphify version: `graphifyy[mcp,watch,pdf,ollama]==0.7.13`
- Python: 3.13 (Docker base image)
- Backend: Ollama (qwen2.5:7b on one host, qwen3.6:35b on another — both reproduce)
- Vault: ~50 markdown files with YAML frontmatter

Happy to share a redacted cache dump or a minimal reproduction if it would help.

title: fix(skills): remove invalid OpenCode/Codex agent guidance (#825)
body:
## Summary

Closes #825. The installed OpenCode `SKILL.md` instructed `subagent_type="general-purpose"` — an agent type OpenCode does not support — and blocked large-corpus runs on an interactive subfolder prompt. A cross-skill audit (`.AUDIT/825-cross-skill-check.py`) confirmed the Codex skill had the identical logical bug: it dispatches via `spawn_agent(agent_type="worker", ...)` but still told users to "re-run with `general-purpose` agent" on failure — impossible to follow.

This PR fixes both, makes large-corpus handling deterministic, normalizes returned-agent JSON to per-chunk files, and adds a Python validation boundary so untrusted agent payloads can't exhaust disk/memory or escape the chunk directory.

## Changes (latest commit, `c720f1a`)

**Skill text** (`graphify/skill-opencode.md`, `graphify/skill-codex.md`)
- Large-corpus warns-and-continues instead of blocking for subfolder selection.
- Recovery text uses platform-native dispatch (`@mention` for OpenCode, `spawn_agent` for Codex); removed all Claude `subagent_type="general-purpose"` / `Explore type` / "general-purpose agent" guidance.
- Replaced Claude-specific "MUST use the Agent tool" / "After each Agent call completes" template wording with platform-neutral phrasing pointing at each skill's Step B2.
- 50%-or-more failure threshold is now explicit; recovery advice points at `--max-concurrency 1` (a real CLI flag).
- Chunk index `NN` is derived from the dispatcher, never from agent output (path-traversal safety).

**Python enforcement boundary** (`graphify/semantic_cleanup.py`)
- New `validate_semantic_fragment(fragment) -> list[str]`: ≤ 25 MB payload, ≤ 10,000 nodes, ≤ 100,000 edges, ASCII-only IDs with no path separators (`/`, `\`, `..`), `file_type` whitelist (`code|document|paper|image`).
- New `load_validated_semantic_fragment(path) -> tuple[dict | None, list[str]]`: `stat().st_size` guard runs **before** `read_text()` / `json.loads()`, so oversize chunk files are rejected without allocation. JSON decode errors return as `errors` instead of raising.
- Both skill merge snippets now go through the new loader.

**Tests**
- 7 new install + source regressions in `tests/test_install.py` covering OpenCode and Codex (agent-type ban, non-interactive large-corpus, returned-JSON normalization, platform-neutral dispatch language).
- 10 new tests in `tests/test_semantic_cleanup.py` (validation + load helper: valid, non-object, oversize, too-many-nodes, too-many-edges, path-traversal ID, invalid file_type, oversize-before-parse, invalid-JSON-no-raise, valid-load).
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## Unreleased`.

## Audit artifact

`.AUDIT/825-cross-skill-check.py` reads each `graphify/skill-*.md` and treats platform-override blockquotes as the authoritative dispatch contract. After this PR it exits `0`. `skill-droid.md` and `skill-trae.md` remain `NEEDS-EXTERNAL-VERIFICATION` (their Task-tool variants need platform-runtime contract confirmation) and are deliberately out of scope; `skill-copilot.md` warrants a separate investigation issue because it has no platform-override block.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider` → **2180 passed** in 15 s
- `.venv/bin/python .AUDIT/825-cross-skill-check.py` → exit `0`
- `rg -n "general-purpose|subagent_type|Explore type|MUST use the Agent tool here|After each Agent call completes|ask which subfolder to run on|wait for the user's answer before proceeding" graphify/skill-opencode.md graphify/skill-codex.md` → no matches
- `graphify install --platform codex` against the new template → installed `SKILL.md` verified clean by the same extended grep
- `graphify update . --force` → graph regenerated (7443 nodes, 12057 edges, 546 communities)
- `git apply --check` was the verification gate during the runbook revision pass

## Previously included work (12 prior fork commits on this branch)

The branch also carries 12 fork commits that this PR's #825 fix depends on (notably `graphify/semantic_cleanup.py` was introduced earlier in this stack and this PR extends it). Brief summary, newest first:

- `fix`: restore local graphify fixes after upstream sync
- `feat`: callflow HTML offline-ready (vendored Mermaid 11.14.0 with SRI fallback)
- `fix`: graph path / parser hardening
- `test`: hollow response expectations after upstream rebase
- `ci`: install action test dependencies
- `fix`: graph rebuild validation and manifest handling
- `test`: escape elixir interpolation fixture
- `fix`: pypdf for PDF image extraction
- `feat`: upstream issue rollup — wiki links, rationale guard, offline viz, PPTX/PDF, GitHub Action, corpus docs
- `fix`: security hardening (9 findings from systematic review) — **introduces `graphify/semantic_cleanup.py`**
- `feat`: bash shell script extraction + ForgeCode install platform support
- Rollup: deterministic extraction, deduplication hardening, portability, expanded test coverage

If preferred, the prior commits can be split into a separate PR — but a direct cherry-pick of the #825 commit onto `upstream/v7` will fail because `semantic_cleanup.py` doesn't exist there yet.

title: Update sample.F90
skill: prevent AST/semantic ghost duplicates in extraction merge
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes to `graphify/skill.md` that prevent the subagent extraction phase from producing ghost-duplicate nodes that split one entity across two communities.

## The bug

The subagent prompt currently shows only `filestem_entityname` as a placeholder, with no rule for how to derive `filestem`. In practice subagents tend to use the bare filename (e.g., `session_validatetoken`) while the AST extractor uses a path-based stem (e.g., `src_auth_session_validatetoken`). The Part C merge dedupes by exact string, so the two forms coexist as separate nodes.

Symptoms observed in the wild on a real ~1500-node Python project:
- `audit_auditlogger` AND `comfyui_mcp_audit_auditlogger`
- `client_comfyuiclient` AND `comfyui_mcp_client_comfyuiclient`
- 67 such pairs total

The semantic side's INFERRED edges land on the ghost; the AST side's structural edges land on the canonical. Louvain clusters them into separate communities, splitting what should be one entity into two and producing misleading "cross-cutting hub" communities.

## Fix 1 — explicit stem rules in the subagent prompt

Adds a node-ID-format section right before the `Output exactly this JSON` line. Three rules:

1. **Stem is the relative path including parent directories**, not just the filename.
2. **Drop leading underscores from entity names** (e.g., `_helper` → `helper`) — the AST extractor does this, so the subagent must too. Without this rule, a function `_closure_values` becomes `tests_test_foo__closure_values` (double underscore) on the semantic side and `tests_test_foo_closure_values` (single underscore) on the AST side.
3. **Module-level constants and aliases**: AST only extracts functions and classes, but if the subagent adds a node for a constant/alias, it should still use the path-based stem so it joins the right community.

## Fix 2 — prefix-aware alias rewrite in Part C merge

Even with the new prompt, a subagent could still produce a shorter stem. Added a defensive alias-rewrite pass: if a semantic node's id has an AST counterpart ending in `_<sem_id>`, the ghost id is rewritten to the canonical AST id, and `sem`-side edges are routed through the alias map so they land on the canonical node.

This is purely additive — graphs that already had clean ids see zero behavior change because `_alias_for` returns the input unchanged when no candidate matches.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual run on a real Python project (~74 source files, 1,484 node graph): 67 ghost pairs detected and merged in one pass; community count dropped from 206 → 201 (the 5 phantom communities collapsed into the right ones); previously-stranded `rationale_for` edges from saved-query memories now land on the AST-canonical nodes.
- [x] No-op verification: re-running the alias logic against a graph with no ghosts produced 0 rewrites.
- Did not add a unit test in this PR — the merge logic is inline in the skill markdown, executed via `python3 -c`, not a callable function. Happy to add a test if you'd like to extract it into `graphify/extract.py` or similar; that's a larger refactor I didn't want to bundle here.

## What this does not change

- AST extractor behavior — untouched.
- Existing graphs — won't be retroactively cleaned. Users with already-built graphs would need to re-run extraction or run a one-off cleanup script. Happy to PR that separately if useful.
- The `seen` set semantics — `if new_id not in seen` is preserved; only the id resolution changed.

title: Claude Code subagents can't write to graphify-out/ (skill.md): chunks silently lost during /graphify --update
body:
## Summary

When `/graphify --update` dispatches `general-purpose` Claude Code subagents for semantic extraction (Step B2), each subagent successfully extracts the JSON but **cannot persist** it because the bundled `skill.md` instructs them to write to `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` — a path outside Claude Code's `general-purpose` subagent sandbox allowlist.

The subagent does the work, then fails with "Write tool is denied" for that path. Step B3 then can't find the chunks, the merge gets empty input, and docs/images are silently dropped from the graph.

## Reproducer

1. `uv tool install graphifyy` (v0.6.7 confirmed)
2. `graphify install --platform claude` in a project
3. In Claude Code, run `/graphify --update` against a project with mixed code + docs/images
4. Step B2 dispatches `general-purpose` subagents per `skill.md` lines 351–368
5. Each subagent attempts `Write` to `<project>/graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json`
6. **Observed:** subagent reports "Write tool is denied". It returns gracefully after burning ~3 min of inference per chunk.
7. Step B3 reads `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json` → empty → `.graphify_semantic_new.json` has 0 nodes added → docs/images effectively skipped from the update.

## Root cause

Claude Code's `general-purpose` subagent runs in a sandbox that does NOT inherit the orchestrator's filesystem allowlist. As of 2026-05 the writable paths for a typical project layout are:

- The specific app/component subdirs the user has open (e.g. `apps/mobile`, `src/`)
- `<project>/.claude/`
- `/tmp`

Notably **NOT** writable from a `general-purpose` subagent:
- `<project>/graphify-out/`
- The project root itself

The bundled `skill.md` assumes the orchestrator's permissions propagate. They don't.

## Cost data point

A `/graphify --update` on a ~400-file Expo monorepo on 2026-05-08 lost **~16 min and ~290k tokens** across two retry cycles before the issue was diagnosed by reading the subagent's error output. Both subagents reported "Write tool is denied" after completing the extraction work in memory.

## Proposed fix

Route subagent chunk writes through `/tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json` — universally writable across every Claude Code sandbox configuration I've tested. The orchestrator's merge step copies them into `graphify-out/` before the existing glob+merge logic, so cache semantics + the rest of the pipeline are unchanged.

Four small edits to `graphify/skill.md` (1437 lines → 1437 lines, net):

1. **Step B2 prompt template (~line 354)** — replace "Output exactly this JSON" with explicit "Write to `/tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json`" instruction + sandbox rationale comment.
2. **Step B3 success-signal check (~line 361)** — change path from `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` to `/tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json`.
3. **Step B3 merge step (~line 374)** — insert 4 lines that `shutil.copy` `/tmp/graphify_chunk_*.json` → `graphify-out/` before the existing glob (200+ lines unchanged).
4. **Step 9 cleanup (~line 838)** — also `rm -f /tmp/graphify_chunk_*.json`.

PR coming next with the exact diff.

## Tradeoffs of `/tmp`

- Universally writable across every Claude Code sandbox I've seen
- Auto-cleared on reboot (cleanup-friendly)
- Theoretical concurrency collision: two `/graphify` runs from different projects could clash on filenames. Mitigation: subdirectory-per-run if it ever bites in practice (it hasn't for me across ~30 update runs).
- Doesn't survive reboot mid-run. Acceptable — `/graphify --update` completes in <10 min.

## Why not project-level `additionalDirectories`

Per-project busywork that doesn't help users running graphify across multiple projects, and would silently regress for any user who hasn't applied it. The `/tmp` path is portable and works everywhere by default.

## Other affected platforms?

The bundled package has 12 platform-specific `skill-*.md` files. Only `skill.md` (Claude Code default) is confirmed affected by me. The fix likely applies to other platforms with similar subagent sandbox models — needs verification per-platform. I can scope this PR to `skill.md` only and let other contributors validate the parallel files.

title: Add AST call handoff and LSP graph enrichment pipeline
body: AST finds unresolved calls, optional LSP hooks try to resolve them, and only boringly safe evidence gets promoted back into the graph. No more turning every `first`, `map`, or `id` into a fake god node. Hooks are opt-in, cached, documented, and wired.

title: Chinese/CJK function names cause ID collisions in _make_id, silently dropping most functions from extraction
body:
## Bug Report: Unicode function names cause ID collisions and silent data loss

### Summary

The `_make_id()` function in `extract.py` and `_normalize_id()` in `build.py` use an ASCII-only regex `[^a-zA-Z0-9]+` that strips all Unicode characters (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.) from node IDs. When processing Lua files with Chinese function names, this causes massive ID collisions, and the `seen_ids` deduplication in `add_node()` silently drops the vast majority of functions.

### Affected versions

Current main branch (also affects the pip-installable version).

### Reproduction

1. Create a Lua file with Chinese method names:
```lua
function 角色处理类:绑定等级物品() end
function 角色处理类:获取身上装备数据() end
function 角色处理类:初始化() end
```

2. Run graphify extraction on the file.

### Expected behavior

All three function declarations should appear as separate nodes in the extracted graph.

### Actual behavior

All three names are stripped to empty strings by `_make_id`, producing the same ID. Only one node survives deduplication.

**Real-world impact**: On a 17,000-line Lua file (830KB) with 203 `function_declaration` nodes using Chinese names like `function 道具处理类:附灵洗练1(连接id,id,gz)`, only **8 nodes** were extracted instead of 203.

### Root cause

**`extract.py`, `_make_id()` (around line 32-36)**:
```python
def _make_id(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Build a stable node ID from one or more name parts."""
    combined = "_".join(p.strip("_.") for p in parts if p)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "_", combined)  # <-- strips ALL Unicode
    return cleaned.strip("_").lower()
```

**`build.py`, `_normalize_id()` (around line 32-39)**:
```python
def _normalize_id(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalize an ID string the same way extract._make_id does."""
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "_", s)  # <-- same issue
    return cleaned.strip("_").lower()
```

The regex `[^a-zA-Z0-9]+` removes every character that is not an ASCII letter or digit. For Chinese identifiers like `道具处理类:附灵洗练1`, this strips everything except `1`, producing the empty string (after `.strip("_")`). When 195+ functions all produce empty-string IDs, `seen_ids` deduplication causes all but one to be silently dropped.

### Proposed fix

Change the regex from `[^a-zA-Z0-9]+` to `[^\w]+` with the `re.UNICODE` flag in both files:

**`extract.py`**:
```python
def _make_id(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Build a stable node ID from one or more name parts."""
    combined = "_".join(p.strip("_.") for p in parts if p)
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "_", combined, flags=re.UNICODE)
    return cleaned.strip("_").lower()
```

**`build.py`**:
```python
def _normalize_id(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalize an ID string the same way extract._make_id does."""
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "_", s, flags=re.UNICODE)
    return cleaned.strip("_").lower()
```

### Verification

After applying the fix to both files:
- `_make_id('道具处理类:附灵洗练1')` produces `道具处理类_附灵洗练1` (unique)
- `_make_id('道具处理类:装备强化')` produces `道具处理类_装备强化` (unique)
- Full extraction on the 17,000-line test file went from **8 nodes** to **204 nodes**

### Additional note

Tree-sitter-lua correctly parses all Chinese function names. The issue is purely in graphify's ID generation logic.

### Environment

- Python 3.14
- graphify installed via pip
- Windows 11
- Test file: Lua with 203 `function_declaration` nodes using Chinese method names in the `Class:Method()` pattern

title: Chinese/Unicode identifiers cause silent node deduplication — only 8 of 202 functions captured
body:
## Bug: Chinese/Unicode function names cause massive node ID collisions

### Problem

The `_make_id()` function in `extract.py` (line 35) uses `re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "_", combined)` which strips all non-ASCII characters from node IDs. When processing files with Chinese (or other Unicode) function names, all non-ASCII characters are removed, leaving empty strings or just digits as identifiers. This causes massive silent deduplication — the graph ends up missing the vast majority of functions.

### Impact

On a Lua file with Chinese function names (17,000 lines, 828KB):

| Function Name | Generated ID (broken) |
|---|---|
| `道具处理类:初始化` | `""` (empty string) |
| `道具处理类:附灵洗练1` | `"1"` |
| `道具处理类:数据处理` | `""` (duplicate of above!) |
| `道具处理类:附灵洗练2` | `"2"` |

- Only **8 of 202** functions were captured in the knowledge graph.
- **194 functions were silently deduplicated** due to ID collisions.
- Tree-sitter correctly parses ALL functions — the bug is purely in graphify's ID generation layer.

### Root Cause

Two locations use the same ASCII-only regex pattern:

1. **`graphify/extract.py` line 35** — `_make_id()` uses `re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "_", combined)`
2. **`graphify/build.py` line 38** — `_normalize_id()` uses the same `[^a-zA-Z0-9]+` pattern

Both strip every non-ASCII character, causing Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, and other Unicode identifiers to collapse into empty strings or bare digits.

### Suggested Fix

Change the regex from `[^a-zA-Z0-9]+` to `[^\w]+` with `flags=re.UNICODE`:

```python
# extract.py _make_id():
cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "_", combined, flags=re.UNICODE)

# build.py _normalize_id():
cleaned = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "_", s, flags=re.UNICODE)
```

This preserves Unicode word characters (CJK ideographs, accented Latin, etc.) while still replacing punctuation and whitespace with underscores.

### Before/After Comparison

| Function Name | Before (broken) | After (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| `道具处理类:初始化` | `""` | `"道具处理类_初始化"` |
| `道具处理类:附灵洗练1` | `"1"` | `"道具处理类_附灵洗练1"` |
| `道具处理类:数据处理` | `""` (duplicate!) | `"道具处理类_数据处理"` |

### Verification

After applying the patch locally, extraction went from **8 nodes to 204 nodes** on the same file (道具处理类.lua, 828KB, 17,000 lines).

### Environment

- Python 3.14
- Windows 11
- graphify latest
- Processing a Chinese Lua game server codebase

title: fix(skill): route subagent chunk writes through /tmp to survive Claude Code sandbox
body:
## Summary

Fixes #808. Claude Code's `general-purpose` subagent is sandboxed away from `graphify-out/` at the project root, so the Step B2 chunk write silently fails with "Write tool is denied". The extraction work completes in memory but the chunk is lost; Step B3's merge then reads zero files, and `/graphify --update` drops docs/images from the graph without surfacing the error.

This PR routes chunk writes through `/tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json` — universally writable across every Claude Code sandbox configuration — then has the orchestrator copy them into `graphify-out/` before the existing glob+merge logic runs. Cache semantics and the rest of the pipeline are unchanged.

## What changed (4 small edits to `graphify/skill.md`)

| # | Where | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Step B2 instruction (~line 345) | Replace `Output exactly this JSON (no other text):` with explicit `Write to /tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json` instruction + sandbox rationale comment |
| 2 | Step B3 success-signal check (~line 352) | Change path from `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` → `/tmp/graphify_chunk_NN.json` |
| 3 | Step B3 merge block (~line 365) | Insert 4 lines that `shutil.copy` `/tmp/graphify_chunk_*.json` → `graphify-out/` before the existing glob (200+ lines unchanged) |
| 4 | Step 9 cleanup (~line 681) | Also `rm -f /tmp/graphify_chunk_*.json` |

Net diff: +15 / -4.

## Reproducer & validation

Reproducer is in #808. Validation here:

- Applied the same patch locally to `~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` on 2026-05-08
- Ran `/graphify --update` on a ~400-file Expo monorepo with mixed code + docs + images
- **Before patch:** 2 subagents dispatched, both reported "Write tool is denied", chunks lost, ~16 min and ~290k tokens burned across two retries
- **After patch:** 2 subagents wrote to `/tmp` cleanly, orchestrator copied to `graphify-out/`, merge proceeded normally. Graph grew from 901 → 1057 nodes; 156 new doc/image-derived nodes
- No regression on subsequent `--update` runs (~6 runs to date)

## Tradeoffs of `/tmp`

- ✅ Universally writable across every Claude Code sandbox I've encountered
- ✅ Auto-cleared on reboot (cleanup-friendly)
- ⚠️ Theoretical concurrency collision: two `/graphify` runs from different projects could clash on filenames. Hasn't happened in practice; mitigation if it ever bites is `/tmp/graphify_<run_id>/chunk_NN.json`. Punted as YAGNI for now.
- ⚠️ Doesn't survive reboot mid-run. Acceptable — `/graphify --update` completes in <10 min.

## Scope

This PR only touches `graphify/skill.md` (Claude Code default). The package ships 12 platform-specific `skill-*.md` variants. Several likely share the same sandbox issue, but I haven't validated on other platforms — left for follow-up PRs by people running those stacks. The fix pattern is identical wherever the bug applies.

## Why not project-level `additionalDirectories`

Per-project busywork that doesn't help users running graphify across multiple projects, and silently regresses for anyone who hasn't applied it. The `/tmp` path is portable and works everywhere by default.

---

title: Feature Request: Project-scoped skill installation (graphify install --project)
body:
## Summary
 
Add a `--project` flag to `graphify install` (and the per-platform subcommands) that installs the skill manifest and platform configuration files into the current project directory (project scope) rather than the user's home directory (global scope). This makes Graphify a first-class repository citizen: versionable, auditable, team-shareable, and scoped to the projects that actually use it.
 
---
 
## Current behavior
 
`graphify install` always writes to the user's home directory:
 
```
~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md        # skill manifest
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md                        # skill registration block
```
 
The per-platform variant (`graphify claude install`) writes the always-on hook and CLAUDE.md section at project scope, but still relies on the user-scope skill manifest to make `/graphify` resolvable. There is no CLI mechanism to install the skill manifest at project scope.
 
The only current workaround is a manual file copy:
 
```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills/graphify
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/safishamsi/graphify/v6/graphify/skill.md \
  > .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
```
 
This is undocumented, fragile against version skew, and requires every new contributor to know it exists.
 
---
 
## Requested behaviour
 
```bash
# Install skill and platform config at project scope (new flag)
graphify install --project
graphify install --project --platform codex
 
# Per-platform subcommands honour the same flag
graphify claude install --project
graphify codex install --project
graphify cursor install --project
# ... and so on for all supported platforms
```
 
Expected output for `graphify install --project` run from inside a repository:
 
```
skill installed  ->  .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
CLAUDE.md        ->  .claude/CLAUDE.md  (project scope)
 
Project-scoped install. Add to version control:
  git add .claude/
```
 
And the corresponding uninstall:
 
```bash
graphify uninstall --project
graphify claude uninstall --project
```
 
---
 
## Motivation
 
### 1. All major AI coding assistants already support project-scoped skills
 
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Kiro all resolve skills and agent instructions from both user scope and project scope. The project-scope paths are specifically designed to be committed to source control so the entire team gets the same configuration on `git pull`:
 
| Platform | User scope | Project scope |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` | `.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/` | `.codex/` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/rules/` | `.cursor/rules/` |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/skills/` | `.gemini/skills/` |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/skills/` | `.opencode/` |
| Kiro | `~/.kiro/skills/` | `.kiro/skills/` |
 
When a project-scope skill exists it takes precedence over the user-scope one for that project. Graphify's own `graphify claude install` and `graphify hook install` already write to project scope (`.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.git/hooks/`) — the skill manifest is the only artifact still written globally.
 
### 2. Global installation creates unintended cross-project LLM context
 
When the skill manifest lives at `~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, Claude Code sees the Graphify skill in every project the user opens — including projects that have never been graphified, projects where `graphify-out/` doesn't exist, and projects where a different team deliberately chose not to use Graphify. This produces noisy, incorrect, or confusing behaviour:
 
- Claude may attempt to call `/graphify` on a project that has no `graphify-out/` directory, generating spurious tool calls or error output.
- The `GRAPH_REPORT.md` hook fires on every file-read in every project, even when no graph exists, adding latency with no benefit.
- For multi-repo or monorepo setups where only some sub-projects are graphified, the global skill creates asymmetric behaviour that is difficult to debug.
- Developers working across both graphified and non-graphified repositories have to toggle the skill manually or accept inconsistent assistant behaviour.
The correct mental model is: **the Graphify skill is a property of the repository, not the developer**. A repository either has a knowledge graph or it doesn't. The skill should follow the same scoping rules as the `graphify-out/` artifacts it reads.
 
### 3. Security and auditability
 
Global installs in `~/.claude/skills/` are opaque to code review. Nobody reviewing a PR for a repository can see that the repository's contributors are running the Graphify skill, what version of the skill manifest is in use, or whether the skill has been customised.
 
Project-scoped installation at `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` means:
 
- The skill manifest is visible in `git log` and `git diff` alongside the code it describes.
- Version upgrades to the skill are explicit commits, not silent global updates.
- A reviewer can audit exactly what instructions Claude Code is operating under when working in that repository.
- Security-sensitive projects can pin to a reviewed version of the skill manifest and block updates until they've been audited.
This aligns with the security posture already documented in `SECURITY.md`: Graphify is positioned as a local-first, auditable tool. The skill manifest itself contains substantial instructions that shape LLM behaviour — those instructions should be subject to the same version-control discipline as the rest of the project's AI configuration.
 
### 4. Team reproducibility
 
Today, to get a consistent Graphify setup across a team:
 
1. Every developer must run `graphify install` on their own machine.
2. There is no guarantee they install the same version.
3. New team members onboarding to the repo get no signal from the repo itself that Graphify is in use.
4. CI environments and ephemeral dev containers require custom setup scripts.
With project-scope installation:
 
1. One developer runs `graphify install --project` and commits `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.
2. Every subsequent `git clone` or `git pull` makes the skill available to all contributors automatically.
3. CI, GitHub Codespaces, devcontainers, and any other environment that clones the repo gets the correct skill without additional configuration.
4. The `.graphify_version` file (already written by the current installer) can be committed alongside the skill to make version pinning explicit.
### 5. Aligns with the architecture review recommendation
 
Issue #63 identified "Introduce a project config file for output dirs, watch behavior, and install preferences" as a medium-priority improvement. Project-scoped install is a natural step in that direction: it makes the install itself a project artifact rather than a user preference.
 
---
 
## Proposed implementation
 
The installer logic lives in `graphify/__main__.py`, specifically `_PLATFORM_CONFIG` and the `install()` function. The change is additive and backwards-compatible.
 
### Suggested approach
 
1. Add `--project` as an optional flag to `install`, `uninstall`, and all per-platform subcommands.
2. When `--project` is set, resolve destination paths relative to `cwd` instead of `Path.home()`:
```python
# Current
SKILL_DEST = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills" / "graphify"
 
# With --project
if args.project:
    SKILL_DEST = Path.cwd() / ".claude" / "skills" / "graphify"
else:
    SKILL_DEST = Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills" / "graphify"
```
 
3. Apply the same cwd-vs-home switch to the `CLAUDE.md` registration path and any other user-scope config files written by the installer.
4. Print a `git add` hint after project-scope installation (see expected output above).
5. Update `graphify uninstall --project` to remove project-scope artifacts only, leaving user-scope untouched.
The logic is essentially the same for all platforms — each `_PLATFORM_CONFIG` entry maps a skill manifest to a destination directory. Adding a `project` boolean to the resolution function handles all platforms uniformly.
 
### `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes` considerations
 
The README already recommends committing `graphify-out/` (minus `manifest.json` and `cost.json`). The project-scope skill at `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` should similarly be committed. The documentation update should make this explicit and include a recommended `.gitignore` entry for anything in `.claude/` that should *not* be committed (e.g. any local-only override files).
 
---
 
## What this does not change
 
- **Default behaviour is unchanged.** `graphify install` without `--project` continues to write to user scope exactly as it does today. No existing workflows break.
- **The `graphify extract` pipeline is unaffected.** This is purely an installer change.
- **`graphify claude install` and `graphify hook install` are unaffected.** They already write to project scope. The only gap being closed is the skill manifest itself.
- **User-scope install remains appropriate for personal use.** Developers who work alone and always want Graphify available everywhere should continue using the default. The `--project` flag is opt-in.
---
 
## Reproducible demonstration of the gap
 
To see the issue today:
 
```bash
# Create two projects
mkdir /tmp/project-a /tmp/project-b
cd /tmp/project-a && git init && graphify install && graphify claude install
 
# Now open project-b in Claude Code — it sees the Graphify skill
# even though it has never been graphified and has no graphify-out/
cd /tmp/project-b
# Ask Claude: "does this project have a knowledge graph?"
# → Claude will attempt /graphify or look for GRAPH_REPORT.md,
#   find nothing, and produce confusing output
```
 
With `--project`, the skill manifest only appears in project-a where it was installed. Project-b is unaffected.
 
---
 
## Acceptance criteria
 
- [ ] `graphify install --project` copies the skill manifest to `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` (or the platform-equivalent project-scope path) relative to cwd.
- [ ] `graphify <platform> install --project` writes all platform config to project scope for the named platform.
- [ ] `graphify uninstall --project` removes project-scope artifacts without touching user-scope files.
- [ ] A `git add` hint is printed after project-scope install.
- [ ] Default behaviour (no `--project`) is unchanged.
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new tests cover project-scope install/uninstall round-trip for at least Claude Code and Codex platforms.
- [ ] README and platform install tables updated to document the flag.
---
 
## Related
 
- Issue #63 — architecture review; recommendation to "Introduce a project config file for output dirs, watch behavior, and install preferences"
- Issue #281 — global vs project-local install conflation in the Cursor installer (a symptom of the same underlying gap)
- [`graphify/__main__.py`](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/blob/v6/graphify/__main__.py) — installer implementation
- [Claude Code docs: project vs user scope for skills](https://docs.claude.ai/en/docs/claude-code/skills)
