title: feat: glob-match `*/worktrees/` in `_SKIP_DIRS` to catch nested placements (`.claude/worktrees/`)
body:
## Real-world incident

On 2026-05-26, a graphify extract on a TypeScript+Python project enumerated **29,417 source files** before any filtering. The actual project-source surface is **587 files** — a **50x inflation**.

The inflation source: agent dispatch tooling creates per-task worktrees at `.claude/worktrees/<slice>/`, not at `./.worktrees/`. Each worktree is a full sibling checkout of the same repo, so 50 active dispatch slices put 50 duplicate copies of the project tree under one nested directory.

The current `_SKIP_DIRS` in `graphify/detect.py` matches `.worktrees` exactly:

```python
_SKIP_DIRS = {
    ...
    ".worktrees",  # git worktree convention (#947) — sibling checkouts, always redundant
}
```

`_is_noise_dir` checks `if part in _SKIP_DIRS` against each path component. The literal-string set match means `.worktrees/` directly under repo root is pruned, but `.claude/worktrees/` is not — `.claude` is checked, then `worktrees` is checked, and `worktrees` (without the leading dot) is not in the set.

The user-side workaround is a project-local `.graphifyignore` with `.claude/worktrees/`. That works, and we shipped it on two repos, but every repo that adopts the agent-worktree-under-`.claude/` convention pays the 50x scan-and-rebuild cost on the first extract before someone notices and authors the ignore file.

## Suggested fix

Move the worktree match from exact-string to suffix/glob, so both placements are pruned by default:

- `.worktrees` (current convention, repo root) — already pruned, no change
- `worktrees` directly under any directory whose name suggests agent-tooling scope (`.claude/worktrees/`, `.agent/worktrees/`, `.codex/worktrees/`, etc.) — newly pruned

Two implementation shapes worth considering:

1. **Glob-match** in `_is_noise_dir`: add a check like `if part == "worktrees" and parent_part.startswith("."):` — prunes any `worktrees` directory nested one level under a dotted scope dir. Cheap, no path-walking changes.
2. **Path-suffix match** against a small set of glob patterns (e.g. `*/worktrees/`) using `fnmatch` or `pathlib.PurePath.match`. More general; allows future patterns like `tmp/*/worktrees` if those emerge.

Shape (1) is the smaller change and covers the observed incident class (agent-tooling scope dirs are conventionally dotted). Shape (2) is more flexible if other placements emerge later.

## Why this matters beyond one project

The `.claude/worktrees/<slice>/` convention is becoming common across agent-dispatch tooling (Claude Code's worktree-isolation pattern, similar conventions in other agent frameworks). Any user running graphify on a repo with active agent dispatches hits the inflation today. The fix would mean the out-of-the-box experience does the right thing without requiring every adopter to discover the pattern, write the ignore file, and rerun the extract.

## Reproduction

1. Clone any repo and add a few dispatch-style worktrees: `mkdir -p .claude/worktrees && for i in 1 2 3; do git worktree add .claude/worktrees/slice-$i HEAD; done`
2. Run a graphify extract — observe enumerated-files count includes every file in each `.claude/worktrees/slice-N/` copy.
3. Add `.graphifyignore` with `.claude/worktrees/` and rerun — observe count drops to the de-duplicated project surface.

The user-side fix works; this issue asks whether the default `_SKIP_DIRS` should cover the nested placement so step 3 is unnecessary.

title: cluster-only skips overlap-based community remapping, so labels become misaligned after re-clustering
body:
## Summary
`graphify cluster-only` re-runs Leiden clustering and then re-applies the existing
`.graphify_labels.json` by raw cid index, without invoking the
`remap_communities_to_previous` safety net that PR #822 introduced for the
`watch` / `update` paths. As a result, community labels attach to clusters whose
members are unrelated to the original label's meaning whenever the underlying
graph has changed between the labeling pass and the `cluster-only` invocation.

## Reproduce
```bash
# 1) Full build with Step 5 labeling
/graphify .                          # or any equivalent that writes .graphify_labels.json

# 2) Make any code change that alters cluster sizes

# 3) Re-extract code without clustering (the official #822 workflow)
graphify update --no-cluster .

# 4) Re-cluster
graphify cluster-only .

# 5) Inspect graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md or graph.html
#    → community labels are attached to clusters whose actual members
#      are unrelated to the label's original meaning.
```

The mismatch is deterministic: `cluster()` reindexes communities by size-descending
after each run, and the prior labels file is read back verbatim by cid index in
`graphify/__main__.py:1714-1722`.

## Expected
After `cluster-only`, labels should follow the same overlap-based remapping that
PR #822 added to the watch/update paths — a label associated with a previous
community should attach to the new community whose node set most overlaps with
the old one.

## Actual
Labels in `.graphify_labels.json` are reapplied verbatim by cid index, producing
misalignment whenever the graph topology has changed between labeling and
re-clustering.

## Affected file
`graphify/__main__.py:1714-1722` — the `elif cmd == \"cluster-only\":` branch.

The neighbouring code path in `graphify/watch.py` (`_rebuild_code`, around
lines 465-468) calls `remap_communities_to_previous` correctly — `cluster-only`
is the only re-clustering entry point that omits it.

## Suggested fix
Mirror the working pattern from `watch.py`. Immediately after
`communities = cluster(G)` in the `cluster-only` branch, build the previous
node→community map from `_raw` (already loaded a few lines above) and apply
the remap:

```python
from graphify.cluster import remap_communities_to_previous

previous_node_community = {
    n[\"id\"]: n[\"community\"]
    for n in _raw.get(\"nodes\", [])
    if n.get(\"community\") is not None and n.get(\"id\") is not None
}
if previous_node_community:
    communities = remap_communities_to_previous(communities, previous_node_community)
```

This matches the design intent stated in PR #822:

> \"stabilize clustering output with deterministic partition input ordering,
>  seeded Leiden when supported, and overlap-based remapping of new communities
>  to prior IDs\"

It looks like `cluster-only` was missed when #822 was applied. If this was an
intentional omission (e.g. for a reason that does not apply to `watch`/`update`),
I'd love to understand the rationale before proposing a PR — happy to send one
mirroring the fix otherwise.

## Environment
- `graphifyy` 0.7.18 (PyPI)
- Python 3.12.3
- Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu 24.04)

title: fix(cli): apply remap_communities_to_previous in cluster-only path
body:
## Summary
`cluster-only` re-runs Leiden clustering and then re-applies the existing
`.graphify_labels.json` by raw cid index, without invoking the
`remap_communities_to_previous` safety net that #822 added to the
`watch` / `update` paths. As a result, labels become misaligned with the
actual community contents whenever the graph has changed between the
labeling pass and the `cluster-only` invocation — including the official
`update --no-cluster` + `cluster-only` workflow introduced by #822.

Closes #1027.

## What changed
Mirror the existing pattern in `graphify/watch.py:_rebuild_code`:

- Build `previous_node_community` from `_raw` (already loaded a few lines
  above) using each node's `community` attribute.
- Call `remap_communities_to_previous(communities, previous_node_community)`
  immediately after `cluster(...)` so the existing labels file keeps
  tracking the same conceptual communities by node-overlap, not by raw
  cid index.

Diff is contained to the `elif cmd == "cluster-only":` branch in
`graphify/__main__.py` (one import addition, one block right after the
`cluster(...)` call).

## Test
Added `tests/test_cli_export.py::test_cluster_only_remaps_labels_to_previous_cids`.

The test tags every node with out-of-band sentinel community ids
(`4242` / `9999`), writes a labels file keyed on those ids, then runs
`graphify cluster-only`. With the fix, at least one sentinel cid still
appears in the final `graph.json` community attributes (= remap matched
by node overlap). Without the fix, Leiden renumbers to `0, 1, ...` and
the prior labels become orphaned.

Verified locally:

```
=== WITH fix ===
1 passed in 17.56s

=== WITHOUT fix (stashed source change) ===
FAILED tests/test_cli_export.py::test_cluster_only_remaps_labels_to_previous_cids
1 failed in 17.14s
```

Full suite passes:
```
pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/bench_extract.py
1317 passed in 58.20s
```

## Open question
The `remap_communities_to_previous` helper already exists in
`graphify.cluster` and is used correctly in `watch.py:_rebuild_code`.
#822's description explicitly mentions:

> "stabilize clustering output with deterministic partition input
>  ordering, seeded Leiden when supported, and overlap-based remapping
>  of new communities to prior IDs"

— but `cluster-only` was not updated alongside the watch/update path. The
neighbouring code paths re-applying labels (`watch.py:_rebuild_code`,
`update`) all go through remap; `cluster-only` is the only
re-clustering CLI entry point that omitted it.

Was there a design reason to deliberately keep `cluster-only` without
the remap (e.g. a use case where label inheritance is undesirable)?
If so, happy to revise this PR — for example, gate the remap behind an
opt-out flag, or expose a `--reset-labels` switch instead. Otherwise it
looks like a simple miss when #822 was applied and this PR just mirrors
the existing pattern.

## Refs
- Issue: #1027
- Stability work that introduced `remap_communities_to_previous`: #822

title: Copilot-integrated /graphify <workspace> stops before semantic chunk processing begins
body:
### Summary

On a large local multi-repo workspace, the VS Code / Copilot-integrated `/graphify <workspace>` flow completes detect and AST, but then stops before semantic chunk processing begins.

This was observed on the first native run and was reproduced again after removing `graphify-out/` and retrying from a clean state.

The run does not produce semantic chunk artifacts, semantic output, or final graph/report/html outputs for the current cycle, and there is no clear user-visible error or warning explaining why.

This is not a headless `graphify extract --backend ...` report. This is specifically about the Copilot-integrated `/graphify <workspace>` flow.

### Environment

- graphify package: 0.8.19
- platform: macOS
- execution surface: VS Code / Copilot-integrated `/graphify <workspace>` flow
- corpus shape: large mixed workspace with code, docs, and images
- rough scale:
  - about 21k files total
  - about 9.8k code files
  - about 11.4k uncached non-code files requiring semantic work

### Observed behavior

Both the initial run and the later clean retry reached the same boundary. The run consistently reaches these stages:

1. detect completes
2. AST completes successfully
3. semantic phase does not visibly begin
4. no semantic chunk files appear for the current run
5. no fresh semantic output appears
6. no fresh final graph/report/html appears

An external runtime watcher classified the state as effectively:

- after AST completion before semantic merge

On the clean retry, the watcher eventually classified the state as `stalled-before-semantic-merge`, with:

- 0 observed semantic chunk files
- no fresh `.graphify_semantic.json`
- no fresh `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, or `graph.html`
- no active Graphify process remaining

### Expected behavior

After detect and AST complete, the semantic phase should begin and either:

- create semantic chunk activity and continue to final outputs, or
- fail loudly with a clear error message and non-ambiguous failure state

### Actual behavior

Detect and AST finish, but semantic work does not appear to start for the current run, and there is no clear surfaced reason.

This remained true after a clean retry, so this looks like a reproducible bug rather than a one-off stale-state failure.

### What was checked

- detect output was present for the current run
- AST output was present for the current run
- semantic output for the current run was absent
- final graph/report/html for the current run were absent
- observed semantic chunk count stayed at 0 for the current run
- the same missing-semantic outcome was reproduced after deleting `graphify-out/` and retrying from a clean state
- local Copilot transcript/debug output was searched for obvious signals like:
  - 429
  - timeout
  - network request failed
  - cancellation
- no clear smoking-gun error string was found

### Why this seems like a Graphify issue

There are related upstream issues around semantic chunk failures and silent partial failure behavior, but no obvious existing issue was found that exactly matches this case where the Copilot-integrated flow seems to stop before chunk production begins.

This report is specifically:

- Copilot-integrated path
- large workspace
- detect and AST succeed
- semantic chunk stage never visibly starts
- behavior reproduced after clean reset

### Questions

1. Is there a known limit or handoff boundary in the Copilot-integrated semantic path that could cause the run to stop before chunk dispatch?
2. Should the Copilot-integrated path emit an explicit phase or error marker if semantic planning or dispatch fails before the first chunk is written?
3. Is there a recommended way to enable more detailed semantic-phase diagnostics for `/graphify <workspace>` runs?

title: Command contains malformed syntax that cannot be parsed: Command too long for parsing (1823 bytes). Maximum supported length is 965 bytes.
AST and semantic extractors generate mismatched node IDs for the same file, splitting it into two disconnected nodes
body:
Related to #952 (same root cause, opposite manifestation — that one is collision; this is divergence).

## Bug

When a file is processed by both the AST extractor (Step 3A) and a semantic subagent (Step 3B), the two paths can produce different IDs for the same physical file. The AST extractor generates IDs from `Path(f).stem` (bare filename, no path prefix). Semantic subagents, following the Step 3B prompt, naturally use the relative path as context and produce IDs like `script_pipeline_step` or `src_pipeline_step`. The Step 3C merge deduplicates by `id` — so the two nodes never merge.

## Result

One physical file ends up as two unconnected nodes in `graph.json`:

- **AST node** (`pipeline_step`) — island containing only internal `contains` edges to its own functions. Appears fully disconnected in the HTML viz.
- **Semantic node** (`script_pipeline_step`) — carries all cross-file edges: `references`, `shares_data_with`, `implements`, etc.

The file looks broken in the visualization. Any graph traversal asking "what does this file connect to externally?" starts from the AST node and finds nothing, even though the semantic node has the correct edges.

## Repro

Run graphify on any project where Python (or other code) files live under a subdirectory (`script/`, `src/`, `lib/`, etc.) so the relative path has a prefix beyond the stem. The semantic subagent will naturally prefix the ID; the AST extractor will not. Any such file that also appears in doc/config files cross-referenced by relative path will produce split nodes.

Verify by inspecting `graph.json`: search for both `pipeline_step` and `script_pipeline_step` — both will exist with disjoint edge sets.

## Expected

Step 3C (or the AST extractor) should normalize all node IDs to a consistent relative-path-based slug before deduplication, so AST and semantic nodes for the same file always land on the same ID and merge. The fix direction in #952 is correct — it just needs to apply symmetrically to the semantic subagent prompt as well.

## Version

graphifyy 0.8.16

title: Wiki export crashes on merged graphs: TypeError on NoneType source_file
body:
`graphify export wiki` crashes with a `TypeError` when run on a large merged graph where some nodes have `source_file: null` instead of a missing key.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Merge ~45 repo graphs into one
graphify merge-graphs g1.json g2.json ... --out /tmp/graphs/graphify-out/graph.json

# Try to generate wiki
cd /tmp/graphs
graphify export wiki
```

## Error

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../graphify/__main__.py", line 2294, in main
    n = _to_wiki(G, communities, str(out_dir / "wiki"),
  File ".../graphify/wiki.py", line 262, in to_wiki
    article = _community_article(G, cid, nodes, label, labels, cohesion.get(cid), node_community)
  File ".../graphify/wiki.py", line 57, in _community_article
    sources = sorted({G.nodes[n].get("source_file", "") for n in nodes} - {""})
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'
```

## Root cause

`wiki.py` line 57:
```python
sources = sorted({G.nodes[n].get("source_file", "") for n in nodes} - {""})
```

`dict.get("source_file", "")` returns `None` when the key exists with value `None` (common in merged graphs where not all source repos have `source_file` on every node). The `sorted()` then fails comparing `None` with `str`.

## Suggested fix

```python
sources = sorted({G.nodes[n].get("source_file") or "" for n in nodes} - {""})
```

Using `or ""` handles both missing keys and explicit `None` values.

Same pattern may affect `_god_node_article` line 84:
```python
src = d.get("source_file", "")
```

## Environment

- graphify 0.8.14
- Graph: 168,997 nodes, 413,300 edges, 14,199 communities (merged from ~45 repos)

> [!Note]
> Responses generated with Claude

title: fix: evict stale nodes in _rebuild_code for graphify update (#1007)
body:
## Fix `graphify update` failing to evict stale nodes from deleted files (#1007)

### Problem

`graphify update` (`_rebuild_code` with no `changed_paths`) silently preserved nodes
from deleted files. The fix in `build_merge` (eef623a) covered `graphify extract`
but `_rebuild_code` has its own eviction logic that was not touched.

Reproduction with v8 branch after eef623a:

```
graphify extract corpus        # → 7 nodes (module-a + module-b)
rm -r corpus/module-b
graphify update corpus         # → "No code-graph topology changes detected" ✗
                               #    graph.json still has 7 nodes
```

### Root cause

When `changed_paths is None` (plain `graphify update`), `evict_sources` is never
populated — deleted files are simply absent from the new extraction and end up in
`preserved_nodes` unchanged:

```python
# watch.py — before this fix
evict_sources: set[str] = set(deleted_paths)   # always empty when changed_paths is None
if changed_paths is not None:
    ...                                         # evict_sources never filled for plain update
preserved_nodes = [
    n for n in existing.get("nodes", [])
    if n["id"] not in new_ast_ids
    and (not evict_sources or n.get("source_file") not in evict_sources)  # guard is no-op
]
```

Additionally, `str(cand.relative_to(project_root))` produces backslash paths on
Windows (`module-b\utils.py`) while `graph.json` stores forward-slash paths
(`module-b/utils.py`) — causing eviction to silently fail even when
`changed_paths` is provided.

### Fix

**watch.py — three changes:**

1. `_relativize_source_files` (line 141): `str(...)` → `.as_posix()` —
   fixes forward-slash normalization for absolute-path conversion.

2. `deleted_paths` / `evict_sources` (lines 379, 415): `str(...)` →
   `_norm_source_file(str(p), root)` — same function used in `build_merge`,
   so prune keys are normalized identically to node `source_file` attrs.

3. `_rebuild_code` reconciliation: when `changed_paths is None`, iterate
   existing graph nodes and build `current_sources` — both sides normalized
   via `_norm_source_file` so prune keys and node `source_file` attrs are
   compared identically (mirrors `build_merge` fix in eef623a).
   Any code node whose normalized source is absent from disk is added to
   `evict_sources` and `deleted_paths` (to pass the shrink-guard).

### Test

`tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_code_evicts_nodes_from_deleted_files` —
builds a two-file corpus, deletes one file, calls `_rebuild_code` directly,
asserts the deleted file's nodes are gone and the surviving file's nodes remain.

Full test run: 47 passed, 7 skipped across `test_build.py` and `test_watch.py`
(skipped: POSIX fcntl + watchdog — not applicable on Windows).

title: Post-commit hook still races on graph.json with rapid same-repo commits (follow-up to #791)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #791 (closed 2026-05-09). The fix added a timeout (`GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT`) and `_apply_resource_limits()` to `_rebuild_code`, but the post-commit hook still has **no serialization across concurrent invocations**. When a user lands 2+ commits within ~30s, multiple background rebuilds race on reads/writes of `graph.json` and at least one fails with a misleading parse error.

## Symptom (graphify 0.8.18, Windows 11, Git Bash)

After 3 back-to-back commits today, `~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log` contained only this single line (because the hook uses `> $LOG` not `>> $LOG`, so the last process's stdout overwrites earlier ones):

```
[graphify hook] 1 file(s) changed - rebuilding graph...
[graphify watch] Rebuild failed: Invalid control character at: line 43270 column 41 (char 1625216)
```

The "Invalid control character" message is misleading — the actual byte at line 43270 col 41 in `graph.json` is `0x61` (`'a'`), a normal letter. The error fires when one rebuild process parses a *partial write* from another mid-`json.dump`.

`graph.json` mtime did not update after any of the 3 commits. The next session would have loaded a stale graph.

## Why this slipped through #791's fix

#791 focused on **multi-repo** runaway memory (10+ rebuilds across different repos eating 32 GB). The fix added per-process limits and a timeout but didn't address **same-repo** concurrent rebuilds racing on the shared `graph.json` file. As long as resource caps prevented OOM, the silent JSON parse failures went unnoticed.

## Repro (single repo)

```bash
graphify hook install
# Make 3 commits in quick succession (any content):
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "test $i" >> README.md
  git add README.md && git commit -m "test $i"
done
# Wait ~30s for background rebuilds to finish
cat ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log
# Expect to see a JSON parse error from at least one process
stat -c %Y graphify-out/graph.json  # mtime won't have advanced for all 3 commits
```

## Root cause

`hooks.py` (current `D:/History vs Hype/.git/hooks/post-commit` excerpt):

```bash
nohup $GRAPHIFY_PYTHON -c "
    from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code, _apply_resource_limits
    _apply_resource_limits()
    ...
    _rebuild_code(Path('.'), changed_paths=changed, force=_force)
" > "$_GRAPHIFY_LOG" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
disown 2>/dev/null || true
```

Two compounding problems:

1. **No file lock around `_rebuild_code`.** Concurrent processes race on reading/writing `graph.json`. One process's atomic-write window can land mid-read by another. The `json.load` on the partial write sees garbage bytes and dies — but the error position is wrong because the file changes again before the trace prints.
2. **`> $LOG` truncates per process.** Multiple racing processes overwrite each other's logs. Only the last finisher's output survives. This actively hides the underlying race.

## Suggested fix

- **Serialize via `flock` (POSIX) or `msvcrt.locking` (Windows).** Lock on `graphify-out/.graphify_rebuild.lock` before entering `_rebuild_code`. If already held, either skip (next commit will re-trigger) or coalesce by waiting and merging the changed-paths list.
- **Append to log with PID prefix.** Replace `> $_GRAPHIFY_LOG` with `>> $_GRAPHIFY_LOG`, prepend lines with `[$$ $(date +%H:%M:%S)]` so concurrent failures stay visible.
- **Document the limitation** in the hook docstring if a lock is too invasive: "do not commit faster than `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT` allows the last rebuild to finish."

## Severity

**Low-medium.** Graph remains internally consistent (a later single commit rebuilds it correctly), and Python's `json.load` of the persisted `graph.json` succeeds — the parse failure is only in the racing intermediate state. But silent failures undermine the "always-fresh graph" promise of the hook, and the misleading error message makes diagnosis hard.

## Verification that the underlying tooling is fine

Running `_rebuild_code` manually after the failed background rebuilds succeeded cleanly:

```
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 54136 nodes, 54077 edges, 6325 communities
[graphify watch] graph.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md updated in graphify-out
```

So the bug is purely in the hook's concurrency model, not in `_rebuild_code` itself.

## Related

- #791 — original concurrency report (closed). This follow-up addresses the residual same-repo race.
- Downstream tracker: benoitdebecker1995-png/history-vs-hype#3

title: fix: normalize file-level node IDs and inline rationale metadata
body:
## Description

### Problem

Two related bugs caused split/orphan nodes in `graph.json` when files lived under subdirectories:

1. **ID format mismatch**  
   The AST extractor generated file-level node IDs from the full relative path including extension (`_make_id(str(path))`), producing IDs like `script_pipeline_step_py`.

   Semantic subagents follow the `skill.md` spec and generate IDs in `{parent_dir}_{stem}` format (without extension), e.g. `script_pipeline_step`.

   Since Step 3C deduplication is keyed on `id`, the nodes never merged, causing duplicated disconnected graph nodes with separate edge sets.

2. **Rationale orphan nodes**  
   The AST extractor emitted docstrings and `# NOTE:` comments as standalone `file_type="rationale"` nodes connected via `rationale_for` edges.

   These created single-edge islands similar to the semantic-side rationale issue fixed in `0.8.16`.

---

## Fix

### `extract.py`

- Replace all `file_nid = _make_id(str(path))` usages (27 call sites) with `_make_id(_file_stem(path))`.
- Reuse the existing `_file_stem()` helper to normalize IDs into `{parent_dir}_{stem}` format.
- Rewrite `_add_rationale()` to store rationale/docstring text directly on the parent node (`file`, `class`, or `function`) as a `"rationale"` attribute instead of creating separate rationale nodes + `rationale_for` edges.

### `build.py`

- Add `_strip_ext_suffix()` with regex coverage for known language suffixes (`_py`, `_ts`, `_js`, etc.).
- Apply normalization during `build_from_json()` canonicalization to all node IDs and edge endpoints.
- Existing cached `graph.json` files now normalize on load without requiring `--force` re-extraction.

### `tests/test_rationale.py`

- Update tests to assert against the new inline `"rationale"` attribute instead of standalone rationale nodes and `rationale_for` edges.

---

## Verification

### Before

```py
_make_id(str(Path("script/pipeline_step.py")))
# -> "script_pipeline_step_py"

title: `--project` flag creates non-discoverable skill path for OpenCode platform
body:
## Summary

When running `graphify install --platform opencode --project`, the `SKILL.md` is written to `./.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, which is **not** a path that OpenCode discovers for project-scoped skills. As a result, OpenCode silently ignores the installed skill.

The `AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js`, and `.opencode/opencode.json` files are written correctly, so the always-on hook behavior still works — but the skill itself is invisible to OpenCode's skill discovery.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Shell:** PowerShell
- **graphify version:** 0.8.20 (installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`)
- **Project path:** `D:\workspace\vibe-java\loan-eval`

## Reproduction

```powershell
cd D:\workspace\vibe-java\loan-eval
graphify install --platform opencode --project
```

### Actual output

```
skill installed  ->  .config\opencode\skills\graphify\SKILL.md
graphify section written to D:\workspace\vibe-java\loan-eval\AGENTS.md
.opencode\plugins\graphify.js  ->  tool.execute.before hook written
.opencode\opencode.json  ->  plugin registered
Opencode will now check the knowledge graph before answering
codebase questions and rebuild it after code changes.
Project-scoped install. Add to version control:
  git add .config/ AGENTS.md .opencode/
```

Notice the first line: `.config\opencode\skills\graphify\SKILL.md` — a `.config/` directory is created **inside the project root**.

### Expected output

```
skill installed  ->  .opencode\skills\graphify\SKILL.md
```

The `SKILL.md` should live under the project's `.opencode/skills/` directory, alongside the plugin that's already being placed there correctly.

## Why this is a bug

According to the [OpenCode official documentation on Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/), OpenCode searches **exactly these six locations** for skills:

- Project config: `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
- Global config: `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
- Project Claude-compatible: `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
- Global Claude-compatible: `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
- Project agent-compatible: `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
- Global agent-compatible: `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`

The path `./.config/opencode/skills/` is **not in this list**. This is also confirmed in OpenCode issue [#14370](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14370), which explicitly lists the hardcoded project-scope skill paths as `.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, and `.agents/skills/` — nothing else.

It appears graphify's `--project` implementation may be doing a simple substitution of the global path (`~/.config/opencode/skills/`) by replacing `~/` with the current directory, producing `./.config/opencode/skills/`. This works for some platforms (Claude → `.claude/skills/`, agent → `.agents/skills/`) because their global and project paths share the same top-level directory name, but it breaks for OpenCode specifically, since OpenCode uses different directory names between global (`~/.config/opencode/`) and project (`./.opencode/`).

## Impact

- **Skill itself is invisible** to OpenCode's skill discovery — `/skills` listing, skill autocomplete, and the native `skill` tool will not see graphify.
- **The always-on hook still works** because `AGENTS.md`, `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js`, and `.opencode/opencode.json` are placed in standard OpenCode-recognized locations. So end users may not immediately notice the bug — graphify still functions via the plugin path, but the skill registration is effectively dead.
- **Output messages are misleading:** the install command claims success and the `git add .config/` hint suggests committing a directory that OpenCode never reads.

title: feat: ReScript (.res, .resi) extraction
body:
> This contribution was AI-authored end-to-end (Claude Opus 4.7), reviewed and tested by a human (bjornj12) before submission. Happy to revise anything that doesn't match the style of the repo.

## Summary

Adds AST extraction for ReScript so `.res` and `.resi` files emit Function / Variable / Module / Type nodes and `imports` / `calls` / `references_type` edges. Today graphify's pipeline silently drops them — on a working ReScript codebase with over 100 files the current `v8` build produces 15 nodes total, all from `README.md`, with zero ReScript symbols. After this PR every `.res` / `.resi` file produces a file node plus a node per top-level entity, with `imports` / `calls` / `references_type` edges resolving cross-file when both endpoints are in the scan.

ReScript shops gain code-graph parity with TS/Java/Scala.

## What changed

### Vendored binding (`graphify/_vendor/tree_sitter_rescript/` + `setup.py`)
No `tree-sitter-rescript` exists on PyPI. Upstream `rescript-lang/tree-sitter-rescript@v6.0.0` ships a complete Python binding (`bindings/python/.../binding.c` + `setup.py`) but it isn't published. Vendored the binding + grammar + LICENSE; `setup.py` compiles the C extension at install time with upstream's exact compile flags. `graphify/__init__.py` aliases the vendored package into `sys.modules["tree_sitter_rescript"]` so `_extract_generic`'s `importlib.import_module(...)` resolves with no per-language detour.

### `_RESCRIPT_CONFIG` + walker hooks (`graphify/extract.py`)
Follows the `LanguageConfig` pattern (Lua/Swift/Scala were the closest templates). `_rescript_extra_walk` (mirrors `_js_extra_walk` and `_csharp_extra_walk`) owns every entity-declaration form:
- `let_declaration` → Function or Variable based on whether `let_binding[body]` is a `function` node, or whether the type annotation is `function_type` (`.resi` signature). Tuple/record destructure emits one Variable per bound name.
- `module_declaration` → Module node; nested modules recurse into the definition block via `walk_fn` with `parent_class_nid` threaded through.
- `type_declaration` → Type node.
- `external_declaration` → Function (callable) when the annotation is `function_type`, Variable otherwise.
- **Function-locals are NOT registered.** Same convention as Python's `function_definition` (returns without descending) and JS's `_js_extra_walk` (module-scope only). Architecture view stays at module surface.

Call dispatch handles `f(x)` (`value_identifier`), `Foo.bar(x)` / `Belt.Array.some(...)` (`value_identifier_path` → last `value_identifier`), and pipe expressions (`arr->Belt.Array.some(...)`) picked up by generic recursion.

### `references_type` edges
Emitted when a `type_identifier_path` appears in a record field, variant/polyvariant arm payload, function signature, let-binding annotation, or external. Targets the leftmost module of nested paths (`Animal.Habitat.species` → `Animal`). Bare local types (`option`, `int`) parse as `type_identifier` not `type_identifier_path` so they emit no edges. Same-file self-references EXTRACTED; cross-file INFERRED until the multi-file resolver rewrites them.

Currently ReScript-only — Java/TS/Scala stay call-edge-only. ReScript codebases are type-driven enough that call edges alone produce a misleading dependency graph. Happy to follow up with the same treatment for the others in a separate PR.

### Cross-file resolver in `extract()`
Two `.res`/`.resi` passes: `open Foo`/`include Foo` import targets rewritten from bare module name to real file node id; `references_type` targets rewritten from `<module>.<type>` to real type-node ids when both sides are in scan. `build.py`'s node-existence filter drops the rest (third-party `Belt.list`/`React.element`/etc.) — same as Swift's `import UIKit` against a non-Apple-SDK scan.

### `graphify/detect.py`
Adds `.res`, `.resi` to `CODE_EXTENSIONS` next to `.swift`.

### Tests + fixture
Single canonical fixture `tests/fixtures/sample.res` (flat, matches every other language) covering every documented surface. 34 new ReScript tests under a `# ── ReScript ──` section in `tests/test_languages.py`, modelled on Scala. Cross-file scenarios use `tmp_path` inline sources, matching `test_cross_file_call_*` in `tests/test_extract.py`. Two "snapshot" tests assert the EXACT set of node labels and edge triples produced by `sample.res` as a forcing function against unintended drift.

### One shared-infra touch
`graphify/extract.py` (per-file `clean_edges` filter) adds `"references_type"` to the survives-unresolved tuple alongside `imports`/`imports_from`/`re_exports`. Same lifecycle. No other language emits `references_type` so the change is functionally ReScript-only.

## Why

Today graphify's pipeline silently drops `.res` / `.resi` files: on a working ReScript codebase with over 100 files the current `v8` build produces only 15 nodes — all from `README.md`, none from any ReScript source. After this PR every `.res` / `.resi` file produces a file node plus a node per top-level entity (types, modules, values, functions, externals, including nested-module members), with `imports` / `calls` / `references_type` edges resolving cross-file when both endpoints are in the scan.

Bundled fixture (`tests/fixtures/sample.res`): 23 nodes / 28 edges from a single file exercising the polyvariant + module + nested-let + function + method + type-reference surface — the qualitative shape any ReScript file produces.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_languages.py -k rescript -v` → 34/34 pass
- [x] `pytest tests/` → no new regressions vs. v8 baseline
- [x] `graphify update tests/fixtures/sample.res` → produces the snapshot-tested node/edge set
- [x] Full `graphify update` on a real-world ReScript codebase with over 100 files → file + symbol nodes per file, cross-file edges resolved as expected. Before this PR the same corpus produced 15 nodes total, all from `README.md`.
- [x] Fresh `pip install -e .` on macOS Apple Silicon (Python 3.14) compiles the vendored C extension successfully

## Risk

- **Adds a C extension to the build.** First one for graphify. Users without a C toolchain installing from sdist will fail; cibuildwheel would fix that — happy to follow up.
- **No behavior changes for any other language.** Only shared-infra touch is the one-line tuple addition in the per-file edge filter.
- **`references_type` is ReScript-only.** No cross-language interference.
- **Function-locals stay invisible** — matches Python and JS, no surprises for users coming from those.

title: Pass 2 fuzzy dedup merges identical-label nodes across unrelated source_files (leaks #895's fix)
body:
# Pass 2 fuzzy dedup merges identical-label nodes across unrelated source files

## Summary

`dedup.py:deduplicate_entities()` Pass 1 was fixed in #895 to only merge nodes within the same `source_file`. Pass 2 (MinHash+Jaro-Winkler, `dedup.py` L195-254) still freely merges across files. When two distinct nodes have **identical** normalized labels in different files, they hit Pass 2 with JW score = 100 and silently pass through every guard (`_is_variant_pair`, `_short_label_blocked`) because those guards only block *similar-but-not-equal* cases.

Result: the fix for #895 leaks straight through Pass 2 for the most common collision pattern — identical method names across modules.

## Reproducer (real corpus: 605 files, ~880k words, mixed Rust/TS/Svelte)

After `/graphify --update` with the merged extraction, build_merge reported:

```
[graphify] Deduplicated 792 node(s) (253 exact, 475 fuzzy).
```

Of the 475 fuzzy merges, ~231 are cross-`source_file`. Spot-checking 200 of them, ~150 are false positives (different functions with the same name in different files). Concrete examples:

| Old node (`source_file`) | New node (`source_file`) | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `state.borrow_from_vault()` (`src/rumi_protocol_backend/src/state.rs`) | `main.borrow_from_vault()` (`src/rumi_protocol_backend/src/main.rs`) | Same canister, state-layer method merged with main-layer endpoint wrapper |
| `analytics/storage/mod.from_bytes()` (`src/rumi_analytics/src/storage/mod.rs`) | `3pool/storage.from_bytes()` (`src/rumi_3pool/src/storage.rs`) | Different canisters, different `Storable::from_bytes` impls |
| `threePoolService.getSwapEventCount()` | `ammService.getSwapEventCount()` | Different frontend services calling different canisters |
| `icusd_ledger.did.d.ts:Transaction` | `rumi_amm/lib.rs:Transaction` | Same name, completely different types (Candid TS binding vs Rust struct) |
| `GuardPrincipal::new()` (`guard.rs`) | `ICP::new()` (`numeric.rs`) | Different types, same trait method name |
| `InterpolationMethod::default()` | `Mode::default()` | Different types, same trait method name |

Verified directly: querying `src_main_repay_and_close_vault` after dedup shows 4 outgoing edges — 2 to internal vault.rs functions (correct) and 2 to **frontend TypeScript services** (false). The Rust public endpoint was merged with the TS `ProtocolManager.repayAndCloseVault` wrapper that calls it, fusing two distinct nodes into one.

## Root cause

`dedup.py` L210-253 (Pass 2):

```python
for node in candidates:
    norm_label = _norm(...)
    neighbors = lsh.query(minhashes[node_id])
    for neighbor_id in neighbors:
        ...
        neighbor_norm = _norm(...)
        score = JaroWinkler.normalized_similarity(norm_label, neighbor_norm) * 100

        if _is_variant_pair(norm_label, neighbor_norm):
            continue
        if _short_label_blocked(norm_label, neighbor_norm, score):
            continue
        # ↑ both guards only fire on similar-but-unequal labels

        if score >= _MERGE_THRESHOLD:
            ...
            uf.union(winner["id"], node_id)
            uf.union(winner["id"], neighbor_id)
```

`JaroWinkler.normalized_similarity(x, x)` = 1.0 → score = 100, which is ≥ `_MERGE_THRESHOLD` (92). `_is_variant_pair` returns `False` if `a == b`. `_short_label_blocked` only handles insertion/deletion differences. So **identical normalized labels in different files always merge** regardless of length, entropy, or context.

Pass 1's source_file partition (the #895 fix) is the natural pattern but it doesn't extend to Pass 2.

## Proposed fix

Mirror Pass 1's source_file partition for the *identical-label* sub-case of Pass 2. Concrete:

```python
if score >= _MERGE_THRESHOLD:
    # If the labels are byte-identical after normalization, treat the same
    # way Pass 1 does: only merge within the same source_file. Cross-file
    # identical-label matches almost always indicate same-named-but-different
    # symbols (trait impls, wrapper methods, common type names).
    if norm_label == neighbor_norm:
        sf_a = node.get("source_file") or ""
        sf_b = neighbor.get("source_file") or ""
        if sf_a != sf_b:
            continue
    # otherwise proceed with normal Pass 2 merge
    ...
```

This preserves Pass 2's value for genuinely similar-but-distinct labels (e.g. `parseUserInput` vs `parse_user_input`) while closing the identical-label leak that bypasses #895's fix.

Alternative / additive: a denylist of common trait-impl method names (`.from_bytes()`, `.to_bytes()`, `.new()`, `.default()`, `.from()`, `.fmt()`, `.clone()`, `.into()`, `.eq()`, `.hash()`, `.drop()`, `.cmp()`, `.next()`, `.iter()`, …). Refuse Pass 2 merges when the normalized label is on this list and source_files differ. Could ship as data alongside (a).

## Environment

- graphify version: 0.8.17
- Python: 3.13
- Install: `uv tool install graphifyy`
- Corpus: ~6700 nodes, mostly Rust + SvelteKit, mixed `.rs`/`.ts`/`.svelte`/`.md`
- Triggered via `/graphify --update` after committing 4 backend Rust files + 9 doc files

## Related

- #895 — Pass 1 cross-file exact merge (fixed; this issue is the Pass 2 leak)
- #878 — Pass 2 fuzzy on chip-name variants (fixed for similar-but-unequal labels)
- #896 (search-found-related, didn't verify)

Happy to send a PR with the identical-label source_file partition if there's appetite.

title: detect() carve-out for graphify-out/memory/ leaks: gitignore filter still applies even though the dir is walked
body:
# `detect()` carve-out for `graphify-out/memory/` is half-implemented — gitignore still filters memory files

## Summary

`detect.py` L26-29 includes special-case logic to always walk `graphify-out/memory/` so that `save-result` Q&A artifacts can be folded back into the graph on the next `--update`:

```python
# Always include graphify-out/memory/ - query results filed back into the graph
memory_dir = root / "graphify-out" / "memory"
scan_paths = [root]
if memory_dir.exists():
    scan_paths.append(memory_dir)
```

But the downstream `_is_ignored(p, root, ignore_patterns)` filter on L73 still applies the normal gitignore rules to every file found. If the user's `.gitignore` contains `graphify-out/` (a very common pattern — graphify itself suggests it in the post-commit-hook installer), all memory files get filtered out even though the scan deliberately walked the directory.

Net effect: the `save-result` → `--update` → graph loop silently breaks for any user who gitignores `graphify-out/`. Memory artifacts pile up on disk and never become graph nodes.

## Reproducer

```bash
# In a project where graphify-out/ is gitignored (the common case):
cd /path/to/your/project
echo 'graphify-out/' >> .gitignore

# Run a query and save the result
graphify query "How does X work?"
graphify save-result --question "How does X work?" --answer "..." --type query --nodes "..."
ls graphify-out/memory/   # ← file is on disk

# Try to fold it into the graph
graphify --update         # ← memory file is silently filtered

python3 -c "
from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
r = detect(Path('.'))
mem = [f for files in r['files'].values() for f in files if '/memory/' in f]
print(f'Memory files detected: {len(mem)}')   # 0
"
```

In our project (`safishamsi/graphify` users testing, also confirmed in a CDP protocol repo, 9 memory files):

```python
>>> from graphify.detect import _is_ignored, _load_graphifyignore
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> root = Path('.').resolve()
>>> test = root / 'graphify-out' / 'memory' / 'query_2026...md'
>>> _is_ignored(test, root, _load_graphifyignore(root))
True                # ← filtered, even though detect() walks the dir
```

## Why the carve-out leaks

The L73 `_is_ignored` call is unconditional. It runs on every walked file, regardless of which `scan_root` it came from. The scan correctly includes memory_dir, but the filter doesn't know it's supposed to exempt files inside that path.

A `.graphifyinclude` workaround doesn't help either — `_load_graphifyinclude`'s docstring states include patterns are for "opt[ing] hidden files/dirs into traversal", and the include_patterns variable isn't passed to `_is_ignored`.

## Workarounds (what users have to do today)

1. **Fenced gitignore rule** — replace `graphify-out/` with `graphify-out/*\n!graphify-out/memory/\n!graphify-out/memory/**`. Works but ugly; users have to figure this out themselves and edit project-level gitignore.

2. **Don't gitignore `graphify-out/`** — keeps the loop alive but bloats the repo with regenerated `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and per-rebuild backup dirs (6+ MB each).

3. **Move memory dir elsewhere via symlink** — `mv graphify-out/memory docs/graphify-qa && ln -s ../docs/graphify-qa graphify-out/memory`. Works but fragile and not discoverable.

## Proposed fix

Either:

**(a) Apply the carve-out in `_is_ignored`.** Inside `detect.py` L73, mirror the existing `in_memory` short-circuit from L67-68 by skipping the gitignore check for paths inside `memory_dir`:

```python
in_memory = memory_dir.exists() and str(p).startswith(str(memory_dir))
if in_memory:
    pass  # carve-out: memory files are always included
elif _is_ignored(p, root, ignore_patterns):
    continue
```

This matches the intent stated in the L25 comment. The user's gitignore is opt-in tracking for the rest of `graphify-out/`; memory files should be exempt because they're explicitly meant to round-trip.

**(b) Make the memory dir configurable** via env var (`GRAPHIFY_MEMORY_DIR`) or a `.graphifyrc`. Users who want memory artifacts elsewhere (e.g. under `docs/graphify-qa/`) can point graphify at the new path, and the same exemption applies to whatever path is configured.

(a) is the minimum fix. (b) is the larger improvement that solves "I want memory artifacts under `docs/` not `graphify-out/`" cleanly.

## Environment

- graphify version: 0.8.17
- Python: 3.13
- Install: `uv tool install graphifyy`
- Project gitignore: `graphify-out/` (single line, common pattern)

## Related

- `save-result --memory-dir` flag exists for writing memory to a custom path, but the read-side (detect carve-out) is hardcoded to `graphify-out/memory/`. Asymmetric.

title: Add Nix Language Support
body:
Issue: #1049 

This PR adds native Nix (`.nix`) parser and AST extractor support to `graphify`. This enables the tool to discover `.nix` files, parse them using `tree-sitter-nix`, extract code symbols (let-bindings, attributes, recursive attribute sets), and map relationships (such as relative imports and list-based module declarations) into the knowledge graph.

**Key Changes**
1. **Parser & Extractor**:
   - Added `tree-sitter-nix` to project dependencies in `pyproject.toml`.
   - Implemented AST traversal logic in `extract_nix` in `graphify/extract.py` to parse Nix expressions (bindings, `import` statements, recursive `rec { ... }` sets, and list attributes like `imports = [ ... ]`).

2. **AST Build, Scoping, and Presentation**:
   - Added Nix suffix checks and mapped them to the `"nix"` language family in `detect.py`, `build.py`, `analyze.py`, `symbol_resolution.py`, and `callflow_html.py` to prevent false-positive cross-language references and format Nix module labels and HTML descriptions correctly.

3. **Verification**:
   - Added automated tests in `test_nix_extraction` in `tests/test_languages.py`.
      
**Manual Verification**

Tested against a couple of nix based projects I already knew deep and wide.

To manually verify the changes against a Nix configuration project:

1. **Install dependencies and the package**:
   ```bash
   pip install -e .
   ```
2. **Run extraction against a Nix project**:
   ```bash
   graphify extract /path/to/nix/project
   ```
3. **Inspect output**:
   - Verify that communities are correctly grouped and the generated `graphify-out/graph.html` and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` show the extracted Nix attributes and import edges cleanly.

title: AST: @property/@staticmethod methods get class-unqualified node ids but class-qualified rationale_for edge targets → docstring nodes orphaned at build
body:
## Summary

The Python AST extractor generates **inconsistent node ids** for methods decorated with `@property` / `@staticmethod`: the method **node** gets a *class-unqualified* id, but the `rationale_for` **edge** that links the method's docstring/comment targets a *class-qualified* id. The two ids don't match, so `build_from_json` treats the edge as dangling and drops it (the `src not in node_set or tgt not in node_set: continue` branch). The result is **orphaned (degree-0) `rationale` nodes** — every docstring/comment on a decorated method becomes a disconnected node in the graph.

The same class-qualified-vs-not mismatch can also drop `calls` / `references` edges that point *into* decorated methods, so those methods are under-connected in general.

## Minimal reproduction

`repro.py`:
```python
class Bar:
    @property
    def baz(self) -> int:
        """Return the baz value."""
        return 1

    def normal(self) -> int:
        """A normal instance method."""
        return 3
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
from graphify.build import build_from_json

ast = extract([Path("repro.py")])

# method NODE ids:
#   baz (@property)      -> id "..._baz"          label "baz()"      (NO class segment, NO leading dot)
#   normal (instance)    -> id "..._bar_normal"   label ".normal()"  (class segment present)

# rationale_for EDGE targets:
#   baz docstring    -> target "..._bar_baz"     -> target_in_nodes = False  (class-qualified, does not match node)
#   normal docstring -> target "..._bar_normal"  -> target_in_nodes = True

G = build_from_json(ast)
# baz's docstring rationale node  -> degree 0  (ISOLATED)
# normal's docstring rationale node -> degree 1 (connected)
```

Observed output:
```
NODE ids:
  id=..._baz           label='baz()'
  id=..._bar_normal    label='.normal()'
rationale_for edges:
  target=..._bar_baz       target_in_nodes=False   <-- dropped at build
  target=..._bar_normal    target_in_nodes=True
after build:
  rationale ..._rationale_4   degree=0   'Return the baz value.'   <-- orphaned
  rationale ..._rationale_13  degree=1   'A normal instance method.'
```

## Root cause

For a decorated method, the **node-id derivation omits the enclosing class** (id `file_method`, label `method()` with no leading dot), while the **`rationale_for` edge-target derivation keeps the class** (id `file_class_method`). The two code paths disagree, so the edge endpoint never resolves and the edge is silently discarded as "external/stdlib".

## Larger-corpus evidence

On a real ~8k-LOC Python project (294 docstring/comment `rationale` nodes): **38 `rationale` nodes were isolated**. For all 38, the source endpoint (the rationale node) was present and only the target (the parent method) was missing; **all 38 targets resolved by removing exactly one interior id segment** (the class), and every parent was verified to be a `@property` or `@staticmethod`.

## Suggested fix

Make the decorated-method **node id** consistent with the **edge-target id** — i.e. include the enclosing class segment for `@property` / `@staticmethod` methods just as for regular instance methods (and ideally keep the leading-dot label convention too). Either derivation is fine as long as both sides use the same one.

## Workaround (post-extraction)

Remap an edge endpoint that is missing from the node set by dropping one interior id segment when exactly one candidate exists:

```python
def declassify_unique(eid, node_set):
    p = eid.split("_")
    hits = [h for i in range(1, len(p) - 1) if (h := "_".join(p[:i] + p[i+1:])) in node_set]
    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
```

This reconnected 37/38 orphaned nodes in the corpus above (the 1 remainder had an ambiguous declassification and was left alone). Empty `__init__.py` files and pure HTML header boilerplate remain legitimately isolated — they have nothing to connect to.

## Environment

graphify `v8` (installed via `uv pip install`; `graphify.__version__` is not exposed and `importlib.metadata.version("graphify")` raises `PackageNotFoundError`, so I can't give an exact build string). Python 3.12. The behavior is deterministic and reproduces from the snippet above.
