title: perf: collect_files walks the whole tree once per extension (~85 rglob passes) and descends into noise dirs before filtering
body:
### Problem

`collect_files` in `graphify/extract.py` (the `follow_symlinks=False` default branch) does one full recursive `rglob` pass per supported extension:

```python
for ext in sorted(_EXTENSIONS):
    results.extend(
        p for p in target.rglob(f"*{ext}")
        if not any(_is_noise_dir(part) for part in p.parts)
        and not _ignored(p)
    )
```

With ~85 entries in `_DISPATCH`, that's ~85 complete directory-tree walks. Each pass also descends into `node_modules/`, `.git/`, `venv/`, etc. and only filters those paths *after* enumerating them — on a JS monorepo, `node_modules` alone can be hundreds of thousands of entries scanned 85 times.

On top of that, every `_is_ignored` call re-evaluates the gitignore patterns for the file's whole ancestor chain from scratch: the shared `_cache` parameter that `detect.py`'s scan walk already uses (added in 5504c84) is not passed here.

Quick synthetic benchmark (200 source files, plus a `node_modules` with 5,000 files, warm page cache):

| implementation | time |
|---|---|
| current (rglob per extension) | 0.295s |
| single `os.walk` with pruning | 0.007s |

The gap grows with tree size and is much worse on cold caches/network filesystems.

### Proposed solution

Replace the per-extension `rglob` loop with a single `os.walk` that prunes `dirnames` in place — the exact pattern already used in the `follow_symlinks=True` branch directly below and in `detect.py`'s scan walk:

- prune noise dirs (`_is_noise_dir`) before descending,
- prune ignored dirs too, except when negation (`!`) patterns exist (same conservatism as `detect.py`),
- match files by `p.suffix in _EXTENSIONS` (same check the `follow_symlinks=True` branch already uses; preserves the deliberate `.f`/`.F` Fortran case distinction),
- pass a shared `_cache` dict to `_is_ignored`.

Result-set parity with the current implementation is verifiable on the test fixtures and on synthetic trees with noise dirs, hidden dirs, and gitignore negations.

Related: #819 (performance umbrella) — this is a concrete fix for the file-collection stage.

title: fix(extract): collect files in a single pruned walk instead of one rglob per extension (#1261)
body:
Fixes #1261. Related: #819 (performance umbrella) — this is the concrete fix for the file-collection stage.

## Problem

`collect_files` (default `follow_symlinks=False` branch) ran one full recursive `rglob` pass per supported extension — ~85 complete tree walks with the current `_DISPATCH` table. Each pass descended into `node_modules/`, `.git/`, `venv/` etc. and filtered those paths only **after** enumerating them, and every `_is_ignored` call re-evaluated the gitignore patterns for the whole ancestor chain without the shared cache that `detect.py`'s scan walk already uses.

## Fix

Single `os.walk` with in-place `dirnames` pruning — the same pattern used in the `follow_symlinks=True` branch directly below and in `detect.py`'s scan walk:

- noise dirs are pruned before descending;
- ignored dirs are pruned too, **except** when negation (`!`) patterns exist, so re-included files stay reachable (same conservatism as `detect.py`);
- the noise check on `target`'s own path components is kept, matching the old `p.parts` filter;
- extension matching uses `p.suffix in _EXTENSIONS`, identical to the `follow_symlinks=True` branch, preserving the deliberate `.f`/`.F` Fortran case distinction;
- a shared `_cache` dict is passed to `_is_ignored` so ancestor-directory results are memoised.

Synthetic benchmark (200 source files across 40 dirs + a 5,000-file `node_modules`, warm cache): **0.295s → 0.007s**, identical result set. The gap grows with tree size and on cold caches.

## Tests

- `test_collect_files_parity_with_legacy_on_fixtures` — keeps the old rglob implementation as a parity oracle (`_legacy_collect_files`) and asserts identical output on `tests/fixtures`.
- `test_collect_files_parity_with_legacy_synthetic` — parity on a synthetic tree exercising noise dirs, hidden dirs, multiple extensions, `.f`/`.F`, and gitignore rules including a `!` negation.
- `test_collect_files_walks_each_directory_once` — counts `os.scandir` calls: every directory is read at most once and noise dirs are never entered. Fails on the old implementation.

Existing `test_collect_files_*` tests (symlink following, cycle detection, hidden handling) pass unchanged; full suite is green locally apart from the pre-existing `test_ollama.py` backend-detection failures caused by API-key env vars on my machine.

title: feat(extract): Cargo manifest extractor — workspace crate→crate dependency edges
body:
**Add an opt-in `--cargo` extractor that emits crate→crate dependency edges from `Cargo.toml`.**
Mirrors the existing `--postgres` path. Zero change for current users.

## Problem

graphify's Rust graph is AST-only. Edges come from source-level `relation`s (`imports_from`,
`calls`), each tagged with a syntactic `context` (`call`, `generic_arg`, `return_type`,
`parameter_type`, `field`). The extractor never opens `Cargo.toml`.

Consequence: the graph cannot express crate→crate dependencies or a dependency-layer view of a
workspace. On a Rust workspace, graphify can't adjudicate the top-value architectural claims —
a crate dependency-layers table, for one — even though every fact sits in
`Cargo.toml [dependencies]`.

## Precedent

graphify already merges non-AST extractors. `pg_introspect.py::introspect_postgres(dsn)` returns
a `{nodes, edges}` fragment that `__main__.py` folds into the result when `--postgres DSN` is
passed (`__main__.py:4314-4331`). A Cargo extractor mirrors this exactly.

## Proposal

Add `cargo_introspect.py` exposing `introspect_cargo(root)`, wired to an opt-in `--cargo` flag:

- Walk `Cargo.toml` manifests under the scan root (workspace root + members).
- Emit one node per crate, plus directed crate→crate edges.
- Name the relation `crate_depends_on`, not `depends_on` — `depends_on` is already used by the
  Terraform extractor (`extract.py:11046`).
- Default to workspace-internal crates only (both ends are members). Gate external deps
  (serde, tokio, …) behind a sub-flag — they add hundreds of leaf nodes and bloat the graph.
- Opt-in flag ⇒ zero behavior change for existing users.

## Direction (out of scope)

Crate→crate edges are inherently directed (A depends on B). The built graph is undirected by
default (`build.py:107`, `directed: bool = False`), so direction round-trips in
`links[].source/target` but flattens in traversal — same as today's AST edges. Making the graph
directed is a separate change.

title: fix: resolve_seed matches bare names against ()-decorated callable labels
body:
## Problem

`graphify affected "classifyProperty"` returns **No unique node match** even when exactly one callable named `classifyProperty` exists in the graph.

Callable nodes are labeled with a trailing `()` decoration (`classifyProperty()`), so a bare-name query:
1. misses the exact-label pass (`classifyproperty` ≠ `classifyproperty()`), then
2. ties with any prefix sibling (e.g. `classifyPropertySafe()`) in the contains pass → `None`.

Users hit this on any codebase where one symbol name is a prefix of another — common with `foo` / `fooSafe` / `fooImpl` naming. The workaround (quoting the decorated label `"classifyProperty()"`) is not discoverable from the error message.

## Fix

Add a bare-name pass in `resolve_seed` between exact-label and exact-source matching: compare query and label with the trailing `()` stripped from each side. Bare queries now resolve decorated labels (and decorated queries resolve undecorated labels); genuine duplicates still return `None`.

## Testing

- 3 new tests in `tests/test_affected_cli.py` (bare→decorated, decorated→bare, true-duplicate still ambiguous); red before the fix, green after.
- Full suite run on Windows: failure set identical to a clean checkout (pre-existing platform failures only).
- Verified end-to-end on a 21.8k-node graph of a production TypeScript monorepo: `affected "classifyProperty"` went from "No unique node match" to the complete caller/importer set.

Proposed changelog line:
> Fix: `resolve_seed` (used by `affected`) now matches bare symbol names against `()`-decorated callable labels, instead of returning "No unique node match" whenever a prefix sibling exists (`foo` vs `fooSafe`).

title: fix: claude-cli backend works headlessly on Windows npm installs
body:
## Problems (both Windows + npm-installed Claude Code)

1. **`graphify label --backend=claude-cli` fails every batch with `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified`.** The `_call_llm` path spawns a bare `["claude", ...]`; CreateProcess does not apply PATHEXT, so the npm `claude.cmd` shim is never found. The extraction path already resolves `shutil.which("claude.cmd")` — the labeling path was missed.

2. **Each `claude -p` spawn pops a visible console window.** With Windows Terminal as the default terminal, a labeling run materializes one on-screen window per batch (~1/min for minutes on a large graph) on the user's desktop. Reported from a 21.8k-node production graph — the user described it as windows appearing and hanging until each model call finished.

## Fix

- `_call_llm` claude-cli branch mirrors the extraction path's `claude.cmd` resolution (regression test included — red before, green after).
- New `_no_window_kwargs()` helper passes `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW` at both `claude -p` spawn sites on win32; no-op on other platforms. Same idiom hooks.py already uses for its detached rebuild launcher.

## Testing

title: uv.lock sync, SystemVerilog class-level extraction + Dart mixin fix
body:
## SystemVerilog: class-level extraction

`extract_verilog` gains a regex second pass (`_augment_systemverilog_semantics`) that runs after the tree-sitter walk:

- `class Foo extends Bar` → `inherits` edge; `implements IFace, ...` → separate `implements` edges
- Field type annotations → `references` edges with `field` context
- Function return/parameter types → `return_type` / `parameter_type` contexts
- `#(...)` generic args → `generic_arg` context; `#(type T = ...)` class type parameters are excluded from references
- The tree-sitter walk now skips class subtrees (their methods were previously emitted with return-type-derived names) and resolves module/function/task names against the tree-sitter-verilog 1.0.3 AST shape
- New fixture `tests/fixtures/sample.sv` + 7 tests; no new dependency (`tree-sitter-verilog` is already a default dep)

## Dart: `with`-clause mixins emit `mixes_in`

Mixins from a `with` clause previously emitted `implements`, making them indistinguishable from actual interface contracts. They now emit `mixes_in`, matching how Scala `with` and PHP traits are already labelled — `implements` is now exclusively an interface contract.

> [!NOTE]
> This changes existing Dart graph output.

## `uv.lock` sync

Regenerated to match `pyproject.toml`: the committed lock lagged the datasketch → numpy MinHash migration (0.8.35 → 0.8.37), so any local `uv lock` / `uv run` reproduces this diff. Drop this hunk if you prefer to sync the lock separately.

title: Community labeling fails on Windows (WinError 2): claude-cli path in `_call_llm` uses bare subprocess.run(["claude"])
body:
**Summary:** `graphify label . --backend=claude-cli` fails every batch on Windows with `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified`, falling back to `Community N` placeholders — even though the `claude` CLI is installed and authenticated.

**Environment:** Windows 11 · `graphifyy` 0.8.36 (uv tool, Python 3.12) · Claude Code CLI 2.1.170 (npm global).

**Symptom:**
```
[graphify label] batch 1/7 (100 communities) failed: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
... (all 7 batches) ...
[graphify label] warning: community labeling failed (...); using Community N placeholders.
```

**Root cause:** There are two Claude-CLI invocation paths and only one has the Windows fix:

- `_call_claude_cli()` (`llm.py`) correctly resolves `claude.cmd` on Windows (the issue #1072 fix) → **works**.
- The `claude-cli` path reached via `_call_llm()` → `label_communities()` invokes **bare** `subprocess.run(["claude", ...])`. On Windows `CreateProcess` only appends `.exe`, and there is **no `claude.exe` on PATH** — npm installs `claude` / `claude.cmd` / `claude.ps1`, while the real `claude.exe` lives in `…/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/`, which isn't on PATH. → `FileNotFoundError`.

**Evidence** (traced via monkeypatched `subprocess.run`, same process/PATH where the direct call succeeds):
```
_call_claude_cli (direct):        exe='...\npm\claude.cmd'   -> OK
_call_llm(backend="claude-cli"):  exe='claude'               -> FileNotFoundError(2)
```

**Repro:** On Windows with Claude Code installed via npm (and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), build any graph, then run `graphify label . --backend=claude-cli`.

**Suggested fix:** Route the `claude-cli` backend in `_call_llm()` / `label_communities()` through the same Windows-aware resolver as `_call_claude_cli()` — ideally extract a shared `_resolve_claude_cmd()` used by both call sites. Surfacing a clearer error than a raw `WinError 2` would also help diagnosis.

**Workaround:** Prepend `…\npm\node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-code\bin` (which contains `claude.exe`) to PATH before running `graphify label`.

title: fix: resolve tsconfig path aliases relative to baseUrl
body:
## Problem

`_read_tsconfig_aliases` resolves `compilerOptions.paths` against the tsconfig's **directory** and ignores **`baseUrl`**. In the common monorepo / NestJS layout — `baseUrl: "./src"` with `"@services/*": ["services/*"]` — the alias resolves to `<dir>/services` instead of `<dir>/src/services`. Every aliased import then fails to resolve and the import edge is **silently dropped**, leaving cross-file caller graphs nearly empty on alias-heavy TypeScript codebases.

I hit this on a ~960-file NestJS API: of 18 real importers of one class, the graph captured **1** (the lone relative import). `affected` / caller queries were unusable. After the fix: **all 18** recovered, and a full rebuild went from 11,481 → 18,705 edges (+63%) and 425 → 262 communities as previously-isolated nodes reconnected.

## Fix

Resolve `paths` relative to `baseUrl` (TypeScript's actual semantics), defaulting to `.` so configs without `baseUrl` keep their current behavior. One-line change in `_read_tsconfig_aliases`.

## Test

Adds `test_tsconfig_alias_with_subdirectory_baseurl_resolves_existing_ts_file`. The existing alias test only used `baseUrl: "."`, which is why this slipped through. The new test fails on the current resolver and passes with the fix. Full `pytest tests/` suite + `ruff` are green.

title: fix: emit symbol edges for default imports/exports
body:
## Problem

JS/TS symbol resolution (`_collect_js_symbol_resolution_facts`) only handles **named** imports. A default-exported symbol — `export default class Foo {}` imported as `import Foo from './foo'` — produces only a file→file `imports_from` edge; the class node receives **no incoming symbol edge**.

On codebases that default-export most of their classes (NestJS-style services/helpers/models, factories, etc.) the effect is large:
- `graphify affected "<Class>"` and `graphify explain "<Class>"` report **no callers**, because they seed the class symbol whose only in-edge is `contains`.
- Those symbols look like isolated leaf nodes.

Concrete example from a ~960-file NestJS API: a service class with 18 real importers showed **0** incoming symbol edges. After this change it has direct `imports` edges from all 18 (plus `references` edges from call sites), and `affected`/`explain` work as expected.

## Fix

Entirely in fact collection — the exported-origin resolver is already generic:
- Record default imports with `imported_name="default"` (`_js_default_import_name`), including the mixed form `import Foo, { Bar } from './x'`.
- Register a `"default"` export for `export default <class|function|abstract class|identifier>` (`_js_default_export_name`).
- The existing `resolve_exported_origin` then wires the `imports` edge to the origin symbol, and — because the default binding now lives in the file's alias table — calls/refs through the local binding resolve too, **even when the binding is renamed** (`import Bar from './foo'; new Bar()`).

`export { X as default }` was already handled via the export-clause path. Anonymous defaults (`export default class {}`, `export default {...}`) have no resolvable symbol and stay file-level only.

## Tests

Adds four regression tests (default-export class, `export default <identifier>`, renamed-binding import, and a renamed-binding **call** that can only resolve via the default-import alias). Each fails on `v8` and passes with the fix. Full `pytest tests/` (1987 passed) + `ruff` green.

title: feat(extract): add opt-in --cargo crate dependency extractor
body:
Closes #1264

## What / why

Graphify's Rust graph is source-AST only today. Crate-level dependencies live in
`Cargo.toml`, so workspace dependency layers are invisible to the graph.

This adds an opt-in `--cargo` extractor, mirroring the existing `--postgres` extractor path.
There is zero behavior change unless `--cargo` is passed.

This PR also includes one small watch-mode fix outside #1264. The repo requires the full
`pytest tests/` gate before review, and that gate failed locally because watch-mode ignored valid
files when the temp directory had a hidden parent like `.ctx-mode-*`. The fix scopes hidden-path
filtering to the watched corpus root, so hidden directories inside the corpus are still ignored but
hidden parents outside the corpus no longer suppress valid file events.

## Design

- Emits one node per workspace crate: `crate:<name>`.
- Emits directed internal crate edges with relation `crate_depends_on`.
- Keeps scope to workspace-internal crates only.
- Uses the raw extractor shape; `build.py` remains unchanged.
- Uses lazy `tomllib` / `tomli` loading with a clear Python 3.10 error.
- Does not change `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`.

Deferred on purpose:

- External dependency nodes (`serde`, `tokio`, etc.).
- `dev-dependencies` / `build-dependencies`.
- Renamed dependency resolution.
- Directed graph behavior changes.

## Changes

- `graphify/cargo_introspect.py`
  - New Cargo manifest extractor.
- `graphify/__main__.py`
  - Adds `--cargo` flag, help text, usage text, extractor call, and merge wiring.
- `tests/test_cargo_introspect.py`
  - Adds focused Cargo manifest tests.
- `graphify/watch.py`
  - Fixes hidden-parent path filtering so the full local test gate can run reliably.
- `tests/test_watch.py`
  - Adds explicit hidden-parent coverage for the watch handler.
- `README.md`
  - Adds one quick-reference `--cargo` example.

title: A single negation (!) rule in .graphifyignore disables all directory pruning
body:
### Summary

If `.graphifyignore` contains **any** negation pattern (`!…`), directory-level
pruning is switched off for the **entire** `detect()` walk. The walk then
descends into every ignored directory — `node_modules/`, `bin/`, `obj/`,
`.git/`, `graphify-out/`, etc. — even though those are still excluded from the
output. On a large repo this is a major, silent slowdown.

Output stays correct (the per-file `_is_ignored` filter still drops those
files), so this is a **walk-performance bug, not a correctness bug** — but the
detection pass can take dramatically longer than it should.

### Where it happens

`graphify/detect.py` (verified on `v0.8.37` / current `v8` HEAD):

- `detect.py:1047` — `has_negation = any(p.startswith("!") for _, p in ignore_patterns)`
- `detect.py:1051` — directory kept if `(has_negation or not _is_ignored(...))`

Because `has_negation` is computed once for the whole walk, one unrelated `!`
rule keeps **every** ignored directory in the traversal.

### Why it matters

The natural way to do a scoped build is a repo-wide exclude plus a re-include —
e.g. ignore everything but `docs/`:

```
node_modules/
*.md
!docs/**
```

That single `!docs/**` rule silently makes the scan walk the whole tree,
including all of `node_modules/`. We hit this building a docs-only graph: the
scoped extract appeared to hang because it was descending into every
`node_modules/`.

### Repro

```
mkdir -p proj/bin/Debug proj/docs && echo x=1 > proj/bin/Debug/a.py
printf 'bin/\n*.md\n!docs/**\n' > proj/.graphifyignore
# detection descends into bin/ (a pattern-ignored, non-noise dir) despite the bin/ rule
```

### Expected

A negation should re-include matching files **without** disabling pruning of
unrelated ignored directories. `_is_ignored` already honours negations
correctly — last-match-wins lets `!dir/` un-ignore a directory (so it isn't
pruned), and gitignore's parent-exclusion rule means a `!` cannot rescue a file
beneath an excluded directory — so descending an ignored directory to find a
re-included file is never necessary. Pruning can rely purely on `_is_noise_dir`
+ `_is_ignored`.

### Workaround (until fixed)

Keep `.graphifyignore` negation-free for large/whole-repo scans; for a scoped
build, place an ancestor-scoped inner ignore (e.g. a `docs/.graphifyignore`
with `!*.md`) instead of a root-level re-include.

I have a fix + regression test ready and will open a PR shortly.

title: fix: a single negation (!) in .graphifyignore no longer disables all directory pruning
body:
Fixes #1274

### Problem

A single `!` rule in `.graphifyignore` set a blanket `has_negation` flag
(`detect.py:1047`) that disabled directory-level pruning for **every** ignored
directory during the `os.walk` in `detect()` (`detect.py:1051`). One unrelated
`!docs/**` therefore made the walk descend `node_modules/`, `bin/`, `obj/`,
`wwwroot/`, … on large repos — a major slowdown.

Output stayed correct (the per-file `_is_ignored` filter still excluded those
files), so this is a **walk-performance bug, not a correctness one** — but the
detection pass visited the entire tree unnecessarily.

### Fix

Remove the `has_negation` bypass and prune purely on `_is_noise_dir` +
`_is_ignored`. The bypass was unnecessary: `_is_ignored` already honours
negations correctly —

- last-match-wins lets `!dir/` un-ignore a directory, so it isn't pruned, and
- gitignore's parent-exclusion rule means a `!` cannot rescue a file beneath an
  excluded directory,

so descending an ignored directory to find a re-included file is never needed.

### Test

Adds a regression test that tracks `os.walk` and asserts the ignored directory
is never descended while the negation still re-includes its target.

title: `cluster-only` has no `--model` flag, auto-detects wrong Gemini model and hits free-tier rate limits
body:
## Version
0.8.38

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `extract` with an explicit model:
   ```
   graphify extract . --backend gemini --model gemini-3.1-flash-lite --token-budget 30000 --max-concurrency 1
   ```
   → Succeeds. No rate limit errors. Uses `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (free tier: 500 RPD).

2. Run `cluster-only` on the resulting graph:
   ```
   graphify cluster-only <path>
   ```
   → Immediately hits 429 rate limit errors on nearly every batch.


## What happened

`cluster-only` auto-detects `gemini-3-flash` for community labeling, ignoring the model that was explicitly specified (and worked) during `extract`.

Free tier limits:
- `gemini-3-flash`: **5 RPM** and **20 RPD**
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`: **500 RPD**

With 135 labeling batches and a 20 RPD daily cap, the process fails repeatedly:

```
[graphify label] batch 7/135 (100 communities) failed: Error code: 429
  quotaId: GenerateRequestsPerMinutePerProjectPerModel-FreeTier, quotaValue: 5, model: gemini-3-flash

[graphify label] batch N/135 (100 communities) failed: Error code: 429
  quotaId: GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier, quotaValue: 20, model: gemini-3-flash
```

The process eventually completes via retries, but takes significantly longer than necessary and is unreliable on the free tier.

## Expected behavior

Either:
- **a)** `cluster-only` and `label` accept a `--model` flag (same as `extract`) so the user can specify the model explicitly.
- **b)** The model used during `extract` is persisted (e.g. in `.graphify_analysis.json`) and reused automatically by `cluster-only`.

## Workaround

None. The `label` command has the same gap (no `--model` flag). Passing `--no-label` avoids the rate limit errors but leaves all communities as `Community N` — which defeats the purpose.

## Notes

- `cluster-only` documentation shows `--backend=<name>` but no `--model` flag.
- The `label` command has the same gap.
- `extract` ran 48 semantic chunks against the same API key with zero rate limit errors because it used `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. The model switch in `cluster-only` is the sole cause of the failures.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- graphify: 0.8.38
- Install method: `uv tool install graphifyy[gemini]`
- Graph size: 121,500 nodes, 13,409 communities, 135 labeling batches

title: `cluster-only` skips labeling batch on JSON parse error without retry or chunk split (inconsistent with `extract`)

title: Extractor produces edges missing required field `source_file`
body:
## Version
0.8.38

## Steps to reproduce

Run a full extraction:

```
graphify extract <path> --backend gemini --model gemini-3.1-flash-lite
```

## What happened

After extraction completes, the following warning is printed:

```
[graphify] Extraction warning (8 issues): Edge N missing required field 'source_file'
```

The same warning repeats on subsequent `cluster-only` runs, confirming the affected edges are persisted in `graph.json`.

`source_file` is listed as a required field by graphify itself. Edges missing it cannot be traced back to a source location. If `graphify query` returns a result that traverses one of these edges, the response will have no file reference — making it harder to navigate to the relevant code.

All edges produced by the extractor should have `source_file` populated. If an edge genuinely cannot be attributed to a source file, the warning should identify which extractor (AST or semantic LLM) produced it to help narrow down the root cause.

title: fix(affected): handle "edges"-keyed graph.json in load_graph (KeyError: 'links')
body:
## Summary

`graphify affected` fails to load graphs produced by `graphify extract`,
exiting with `error: could not load graph: 'links'`. Every other reader works.

## Root cause

`graphify/affected.py::load_graph` calls
`json_graph.node_link_graph(raw, edges="links")`, but `extract` writes
`graph.json` with an **`"edges"`** key. networkx then raises `KeyError: 'links'`,
which the surrounding `except TypeError` does not catch.

`__main__.py` already normalizes this everywhere it loads a graph:

```python
if "links" not in raw and "edges" in raw:
    raw = dict(raw, links=raw["edges"])
```

`affected.load_graph` is the only loader missing that normalization. Same class
of bug as #1198 (benchmark `KeyError: 'links'`).

## Fix

Mirror the existing normalization in `affected.load_graph` before calling
`node_link_graph`. `links`-keyed graphs and older networkx fall through unchanged.

## Repro

```
$ graphify extract . --no-cluster      # writes an "edges"-keyed graph.json
$ graphify affected "SomeSymbol" --depth 1
error: could not load graph: 'links'   # before; after: reverse-traversal output
```

## Tests

Added `test_affected_cli_loads_edges_keyed_graph` — writes an `"edges"`-keyed
graph (as `extract` does) and asserts `affected` reverse-traverses it. The
existing `_write_graph` helper only ever emitted the `"links"` key, so this path
was untested. Fails before the fix (`KeyError: 'links'`), passes after.

---

Found this while running graphify against a ~8,200-file monorepo (52k nodes /
186k edges) — after the fix, `affected` correctly reverse-traverses 621 nodes
from a core DB accessor. Happy to adjust if you'd rather hoist the
normalization into a shared helper instead of mirroring it per-loader.

title: build_merge(prune_sources=...) prunes AFTER merging — modified files passed per the bundled skill update templates lose their freshly re-extracted nodes
body:
### Summary

`build_merge()` applies `prune_sources` **after** merging `new_chunks` into the base graph. Any node/edge whose `source_file` is in the prune set is removed from the **merged** graph — including the freshly re-extracted nodes that were just passed in `new_chunks`. So the documented incremental flow for a *modified* file (re-extract it, pass it in `prune_sources` to drop the stale copies) deletes the new extraction too: the changed file ends up with **zero nodes**.

This is not a hypothetical misuse: the bundled skill templates (`graphify/skills/*/references/update.md`, step "Also prune old nodes for re-extracted (changed) files before inserting fresh AST", added for #1178) explicitly build `prune = deleted + changed` and call:

```python
G = build_merge([new_extraction], graph_path='graphify-out/graph.json', prune_sources=prune)
```

Under the current ordering, every `--update` driven by those templates wipes the changed files' fresh nodes right after extracting them.

### Reproduction (verified on 0.8.22, 0.8.37, 0.8.38, and current `main`)

```python
import json, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.build import build_merge

tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); gp = tmp / "graph.json"
old = {"directed": False, "multigraph": False, "graph": {},
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "x_old", "label": "Old A", "file_type": "document", "source_file": "x.md"},
    {"id": "y_b", "label": "B", "file_type": "document", "source_file": "y.md"},
  ],
  "links": [{"source": "x_old", "target": "y_b", "relation": "references",
             "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "confidence_score": 1.0, "source_file": "x.md"}]}
gp.write_text(json.dumps(old))

# x.md was MODIFIED — fresh re-extraction:
chunk = {"nodes": [{"id": "x_new", "label": "New A", "file_type": "document", "source_file": "x.md"}],
         "edges": [{"source": "x_new", "target": "y_b", "relation": "references",
                    "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "confidence_score": 1.0, "source_file": "x.md"}]}

G = build_merge([chunk], graph_path=gp, prune_sources=["x.md"], dedup=False)
print(sorted(G.nodes()))   # ['y_b']  ← x_new was pruned together with x_old
```

Output: `[graphify] Pruned 2 node(s) from 1 deleted source file(s).` — the "2" includes the fresh node.

### Why this matters / interaction with existing issues

The API currently has no correct option for modified files:

- **Don't** pass changed files in `prune_sources` → stale symbols from previous versions of the file survive forever (grow-only merge; that's #1152).
- **Do** pass them (as the bundled skill templates instruct) → the fresh extraction is destroyed.

For context: the same stale-symbol leak in the `watch._rebuild_code` path (#1116) was fixed in #1118 by stamping `_origin="ast"` and dropping absent AST nodes on rebuild — but `build_merge` never got an equivalent per-file replace mechanism, which is why #1152 remains open and the skill templates fall back to `prune = deleted + changed`.

### Proposed fix

Prune the **base** graph (the nodes/edges loaded from `graph.json`) *before* merging `new_chunks`, instead of pruning the merged result. Then:

- modified files become an atomic per-file replace: stale copies dropped, fresh chunk kept — which also gives `--update` flows the mechanism to eliminate the #1152 ghosts;
- genuinely deleted files (no chunk) behave exactly as today;
- base edges from unchanged files that pointed at a pruned node become dangling and are already dropped inside `build()` (same outcome as `G.remove_nodes_from()`'s implicit incident-edge removal);
- the #1007 dual-form path matching (raw + `_norm_source_file`) is preserved, applied to the as-stored base JSON (including legacy `"source"`-keyed nodes, which only gain `source_file` during `build_from_json`).

**Fix submitted: PR #1285** — prune-before-merge with three regression tests (changed-file replace, #1152 ghost-drop, legacy `"source"`-keyed nodes); full test suite passes (2024 passed, 27 skipped).

title: Fuzzy dedup still merges distinct non-code nodes across files (near-identical labels) — rationale/document/concept lack the #1205 protection
body:
### Summary

#1205 fixed label-based dedup for code symbols (`file_type == "code"` is now exempt from both exact and fuzzy passes), and the exact-label cross-file block (#1046/#895) works. But **non-code nodes — `rationale`, `document`, `concept` — get no equivalent protection**, and pass-2 fuzzy matching still merges *distinct* entities across files whenever their labels are merely near-identical (Jaro-Winkler above `_MERGE_THRESHOLD` but not exactly equal, so the cross-file same-label block never fires).

### Evidence (full merge audit, real graph)

Method: on an 11.7k-node graph built from a Django monorepo + its docs (graphifyy 0.8.37), I wrapped `graphify.dedup._UF.union` to log every union call, ran `deduplicate_entities`, and reconstructed every merge group:

- 145 groups: same normalized label, same `source_file` → benign duplicate collapse ✅
- 0 groups: same label across files → the #1046 guard holds ✅
- **49 groups with different labels — many destructive:**
  - **15 distinct Django `AppConfig` rationale nodes merged into 1.** Every app's `apps.py` docstring is the same boilerplate ("Django app config for `apps.<name>`. No business logic here…") differing only in the module path → JW ≈ 0.95+. Fifteen different files, one surviving node.
  - **Antonym metrics merged:** a success criterion label `40%+ <metric>` absorbed the failure criterion `<20% <metric>` from the same PRD — opposite meanings, high string similarity.
  - **Three distinct SQL DDL fence nodes → 1:** `code:sql (create table topics (` absorbed `…topic_items (` and `…topic_candidates (`.
  - **Parallel provider modules merged:** "Structured devtools facts…" (`providers/github.py`) ⇄ "Structured travel facts…" (`providers/places.py`) — same boilerplate shape, different adapters.
  - `VideoAnalyzer` ⇄ `FakeVideoAnalyzer` (interface vs test fake), `…(ADR 0013 D4)` ⇄ `…(ADR 0011 §D5)`, `Module layout (… VAN-375)` ⇄ `(… VAN-376)`, section headings `3.1 Product Goals` (doc A) ⇄ `1.1 Product Goals` (doc B).

These are exactly the failure modes #1205's docstring describes for code ("a function name shared by two parallel backends"), reproduced one layer up: file-anchored *prose* nodes with templated/boilerplate labels.

### Why current guards miss this

- `_is_code()` returns true only for `file_type == "code"`; `rationale` nodes (module docstrings — as file-anchored as the code they sit in) and document section/fence nodes are eligible for label-based merging.
- The cross-file block inside pass 2 requires `norm_label == neighbor_norm` *exactly*; one differing word or number bypasses it.
- Long boilerplate labels have high entropy and high pairwise JW similarity, so they sail past `_ENTROPY_THRESHOLD` and `_MERGE_THRESHOLD`. (#1243 covers the related prefix-bonus inflation; this report is about the residual class that isn't prefix-shaped.)

### Proposed mitigations

1. **Numeric-token mismatch guard (cheap, high yield)** — *implemented in draft PR #1286:* before unioning in pass 2, extract digit sequences from both normalized labels; if the multisets differ, block the merge. This alone kills the ADR/VAN/phase/section/percent/`create table` cases above and is a near-zero false-positive heuristic (two labels that differ in embedded numbers are almost never the same entity).
2. **Treat `rationale` as file-anchored, like code** — *implemented in draft PR #1286:* docstring-derived nodes inherit code's identity semantics — require same `source_file` for any label-based merge of a `rationale` node (mirrors the #1205 rationale verbatim).
3. *(Optional, more opinionated — not implemented; your call:)* Restrict cross-file fuzzy merging to `concept` nodes only — `document` nodes (headings, fences) are positional artifacts of a specific file, and cross-file unification of them loses provenance more often than it removes duplication.

Versions: audited on 0.8.37 and **re-verified against current `v8` HEAD** (which includes the #1247 winner-selection fix): identical result — 49 different-label merge groups, and the flagship cases above (15× AppConfig, the antonym metric pair, the multi-table SQL group) all still merge.

### Status

**Draft PR #1286 implements proposals 1 + 2** (guards mirrored into the `--dedup-llm` pair collection), validated on the graph that produced this report: **49 → 19** different-label merge groups, all flagship cases above eliminated, the 144 benign same-label-same-file groups untouched, nodes absorbed by fuzzy dedup 249 → 195. It is marked draft deliberately so you can choose the direction — especially how it should compose with #1243 — and proposal 3 stays open. Happy to adjust thresholds, scope, or approach.

title: fix: prune base graph before merging in build_merge so modified files keep their fresh nodes
body:
Fixes #1283.

### Problem

`build_merge()` merged the base graph + `new_chunks` first, then pruned every node/edge whose `source_file` ∈ `prune_sources` from the **merged** graph. For *modified* files — re-extracted into `new_chunks` and passed in `prune_sources` to drop their stale copies — the prune deleted the fresh extraction too: the changed file ended up with zero nodes (`[graphify] Pruned 2 node(s) …` on a 1-node file).

The bundled skill update templates (`graphify/skills/*/references/update.md`) already instruct exactly that flow (`prune = deleted + changed`, added for #1178), so the shipped documentation triggers the data loss on every `--update` with modified files. Not passing changed files isn't an option either — that leaves stale-symbol ghosts (#1152). The API had no correct choice for modified files.

### Fix

Prune the **base** graph (the `existing_nodes` / `existing_edges` loaded from `graph.json`) *before* the merge:

- **Modified files become an atomic per-file replace** — stale copies dropped, fresh chunk nodes always survive. This also gives `--update` flows the mechanism to eliminate the #1152 ghosts (the skill templates' `deleted + changed` prune now does what its comment intends).
- **Genuinely deleted files behave exactly as before** (existing prune tests for #1007 absolute/Windows paths pass unchanged).
- Base edges from unchanged files that pointed at a pruned node become dangling and are dropped inside `build()` — same outcome as the old `G.remove_nodes_from()`'s implicit incident-edge removal (`build_from_json` only adds edges whose endpoints exist).
- The #1007 dual-form matching (raw + `_norm_source_file`) is preserved; since the base JSON is now checked as-stored (the old code compared against build-time-normalised attributes), the filter also falls back to the legacy `"source"` node key that `build_from_json` migrates — without the fallback, legacy-keyed nodes would have escaped the prune. Edges deliberately get no such fallback (their `source` is an endpoint id, not a path).
- The `#479` shrink-guard and all stderr messages are unchanged.

### Tests

Three new regression tests in `tests/test_build.py`:

- `test_build_merge_prune_changed_file_keeps_reextracted_nodes` — fresh node + fresh edge survive; stale node + stale edge pruned; unrelated file untouched (fails on the previous ordering).
- `test_build_merge_prune_changed_file_drops_removed_symbols` — a symbol deleted from a modified file does not survive as a ghost (#1152 scenario).
- `test_build_merge_prune_matches_legacy_source_keyed_nodes` — legacy `"source"`-keyed nodes are still pruned.

Full suite: **2024 passed, 27 skipped**.

title: fix: block fuzzy-dedup merges of numbered siblings and cross-file rationale boilerplate (#1284, proposals 1+2)
body:
Implements proposals **1 + 2** from #1284. Submitted as a **draft** deliberately — #1284 lists three possible directions and the choice is yours; this PR makes the two least-controversial ones concrete and reviewable. Proposal 3 (restricting cross-file fuzzy merging to `concept` nodes) is intentionally omitted as the more opinionated call.

### Problem (from #1284)

#1205 exempted code symbols from label-based merging and #1046 blocks exact-label cross-file pairs, but non-code nodes (`rationale`/`document`/`concept`) with *near*-identical labels still fuzzy-merge across files. On a real 11.7k-node graph: 49 destructive different-label merge groups, including 15 distinct Django `AppConfig` docstring rationale nodes → 1, antonym metric labels (`40%+ X` absorbed `<20% X`), and ADR/issue-numbered sibling notes.

### Change

Two targeted guards in pass 2 (placed with the existing `_is_variant_pair` / `_short_label_blocked` / prefix-extension guards, and mirrored in `_llm_tiebreak`'s ambiguous-pair collection so decisively-distinct pairs never reach the LLM):

1. **`_numeric_tokens_differ`** — digit runs of the normalized labels compared as zero-padding-insensitive multisets (`"09"` ≡ `"9"`; string-normalized rather than `int()` so a pathological >4300-digit run can't hit Python's int-conversion limit). Any mismatch blocks the merge: `ADR 0011 §D5` vs `ADR 0013 D4`, `3.1 Product Goals` vs `1.1 Product Goals`, `block3` vs `block13`, `40%+ …` vs `<20% …` are numbered siblings, not duplicates. Digitless labels are unaffected.
2. **`_crossfile_rationale_blocked`** — `rationale` nodes are docstring-derived and as file-anchored as the code they describe (#1205's reasoning, one layer up). Label-based merging of a rationale node is allowed only within one file, so parallel modules' boilerplate ("Django app config for `apps.<name>`. No business logic…") no longer collapses; same-file rationale duplicates still merge.

Known false-negative trade-off (accepted): pairs like `OAuth2 flow` / `OAuth 2.0 flow` are now blocked. Given that this engine's observed failure mode is destructive merging, a missed merge is the cheaper error.

### Validation on the real graph that produced #1284

| | upstream `v8` | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| different-label merge groups | **49** | **19** (−30) |
| benign same-label-same-file groups | 144 | 144 (unchanged) |
| nodes absorbed by fuzzy dedup | 249 | 195 |

All flagship destructive cases eliminated (15× AppConfig, antonym metrics, ADR 0034/0035, VAN-375/376, github/places providers, cross-doc numbered headings). The 19 survivors are predominantly legitimate same-file near-duplicates; the cross-file remainder is the class proposal 3 would address.

### Tests

4 new tests in `tests/test_dedup.py` (helper semantics incl. zero-padding; numbered-siblings blocked; cross-file rationale blocked; same-file rationale control still merges). Both guard tests verified to **fail** against the pre-patch `dedup.py`. Full suite: **2025 passed, 27 skipped**.

title: graphify update: support --out <dir> to redirect output directory
body:
Currently graphify update <path> always writes to <path>/graphify-out/, with no way to redirect the output. The read commands (query, path, explain, etc.) already support --graph <path>, so reading is flexible — but writing is not.

Use case: monorepos where multiple projects live under one root folder. Each project needs its own graph, but putting graphify-out/ inside each project repo means either committing generated output or adding it to .gitignore. A shared graphs folder at the root (e.g. .graphs/<project>/) would be cleaner.

Requested change: Add an --out <dir> flag to graphify update:


graphify update ./foo --out ./.graphs/foo
graphify update ./bar   --out ./.graphs/bar
The read commands already accept --graph <path> so they'd work with the new location without any changes.

title: claude-cli community labeling silently fails on Windows (WinError 2) — _call_llm uses bare "claude" while _call_claude_cli resolves claude.cmd
body:
## Summary

`graphify label --backend=claude-cli` (and any `_call_llm` text path) silently falls back to `Community N` placeholders on Windows. The community-naming call dies with `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified`, which `generate_community_labels` swallows into placeholder degradation, so the run reports success with no real labels.

## Environment

- graphify 0.8.35
- Windows 11, Python 3.12.10
- Claude Code CLI installed via npm (`claude.cmd` on PATH, no `claude.exe`)

## Root cause

Two functions shell out to the CLI, and only one has the Windows fix:

- ✅ `_call_claude_cli` (extraction) — `llm.py` ~L853–896 — explicitly resolves `claude.cmd` via `shutil.which("claude.cmd")` and invokes the full path. There is even a comment documenting this exact trap.
- ❌ `_call_llm` (generic text path, used by `label_communities`) — `llm.py` L1572–1575 — guards with `shutil.which("claude")` but then runs the **bare** `subprocess.run(["claude", "-p", "--output-format", "json", "--no-session-persistence"], ...)`.

On Windows, `shutil.which("claude")` honors `PATHEXT` and finds `claude.CMD` (so the guard passes), but Python's `subprocess`/`CreateProcess` only auto-appends `.exe` and ignores `PATHEXT` — so the bare name cannot launch the npm `.cmd` wrapper → WinError 2.

## Reproduction

```python
import subprocess, shutil
print(shutil.which("claude"))                                  # -> ...\claude.CMD  (guard passes)
subprocess.run(["claude", "-p"], input="hi", text=True)        # -> FileNotFoundError [WinError 2]
subprocess.run([shutil.which("claude.cmd"), "-p"], input="hi", text=True)  # -> works, exit 0
```

## Suggested fix

Port the `_call_claude_cli` resolution into `_call_llm`'s claude-cli branch — prefer `shutil.which("claude.cmd")` on Windows and invoke the resolved path instead of the bare string. Ideally factor the launcher resolution into one shared helper so the two paths cannot drift again.

## Impact

Silent — no error is surfaced to the user; the graph ships with placeholder community names and the failure is only visible by inspecting `.graphify_labels.json`.

title: perf: skip MinHash/LSH dedup for AST-located nodes
body:
AST-extracted nodes carry source_location (e.g. "L42") and are uniquely keyed by file path + position, so cross-node fuzzy merging via MinHash/JW is both unnecessary and harmful (same function name in two files = two distinct symbols).

Excluding source_location nodes from the pass-2 candidate set reduces candidates by 94.9% (91,268 → 4,670 on a 100k AST + 5k semantic dataset), yielding a 6.35x wall-clock speedup (10.7s → 1.7s median). Mixed AST+semantic runs are also faster since only the small pool of LLM-generated nodes without source_location goes through MinHash.

I included before/after benchmark on this:
```
> uv run python tests/bench_dedup.py

Generating dataset: 100,000 AST nodes + 5,000 semantic nodes (~400 near-dups)...

  MinHash candidates after  : 4,670  (semantic-only)

  before  run 2/2: 10.460s

=== Results ===

title: refactor(extract): begin per-language extractor split (#1212)
body:
First slice of #1212: `extract.py` (12,059 lines, 44 extractors) starts splitting into
`graphify/extractors/`, one small reviewable batch at a time. This batch moves four
bespoke, low-churn extractors (~565 lines): **blade, zig, elixir, razor**.

## What's in the diff

- `graphify/extractors/base.py` — four shared names moved verbatim (`_make_id`,
  `_file_stem`, `_read_text`, `_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS`); `extract.py` re-imports them.
- One module per language; each function moved **byte-identically** (verify with
  `git diff --color-moved`). Internal closures/consts/imports stay inside their functions.
- `extract.py` keeps every public and private name via a marked facade block — zero
  changes to `__main__.py`, `watch.py`, `pg_introspect.py`, or any existing test.
- `extractors/__init__.py` — a registry seed (`LANGUAGE_EXTRACTORS`); dispatch sill flows
  through `graphify.extract`. **Mechanical code motion only** — registry-driven dispatch,
  class protocols, or lazy imports can layer on later if wanted.
- `extractors/MIGRATION.md` — a playbook so any contributor (or AI agent) can port one
  language per small, conflict-free PR: verbatim-move rules, helper classification by
  grep, facade invariants, pre-flight churn checks.
- `pyproject.toml` — `packages` now lists the subpackage (first-ever subpackage in the
  distribution; without this, wheels build green but break on `import graphify.extract`).

## Proof of behavior preservation

- Full suite: **2041 passed, 14 skipped** — zero test edits outside the new
  `tests/test_extractors_registry.py` (7 identity/registry guards).
- elixir and razor are covered by existing behavioral tests, unchanged and green.
- blade and zig have no behavioral tests upstream — for them the byte-identity of the
  moved blocks (checked against this PR's base) is the proof.

## Prior art

- #1212 proposes exactly this package shape and explicitly suggests landing it
  language-by-language; #1213 (file-size guardrail) becomes enforceable as the monolith
  shrinks.
- #1121 set the in-repo precedent for splitting a monolith behind generated/verified
  artifacts (the skill progressive-disclosure split with its drift-fence CI) — this PR
  applies the same philosophy to `extract.py`, with byte-identity instead of roundtrip
  checks.
- Batch 2 candidates (fortran, julia, objc, pascal, …) follow the MIGRATION.md playbook;
  the config-driven extractors (python/js/java/…) wait until the shared
  `_extract_generic` core moves as its own coordinated batch.

title: perf: 74x speedup in deduplicate_entities via bulk MinHash + O(1) remap
body:
Continuation of PR #1234

Three optimizations:
- MinHash.bulk_update(): process all shingles in one numpy broadcast (num_perm x len(shingles)) instead of a per-shingle loop with repeated array allocations
- In-place np.minimum in MinHash.update() — eliminates one array allocation per shingle
- id_to_node dict in remap building — O(1) dict lookup per member instead of an O(N) list scan per merge group (was O(N x K))

Also fixes _pick_winner to use ID as a final tiebreaker so winner selection is stable regardless of node list ordering.

Includes benchmarks/benchmark_dedup.py: deterministic before/after benchmark with fixed seed, warmup pass, and output verification. Measured 6x speedup at 10k nodes, 74x at 50k nodes.

Benchmark output:
```

title: feat: label-match node enumeration subcommand — query is a traversal, agents need a name harvester
body:
## Problem

Agents working against a graph need two different read operations:

1. **Enumeration** — "list every node whose name matches *candidate*" (cold start: the agent has a concept word, not an exact symbol yet)
2. **Traversal** — "what is connected to X" (`query`, `explain`, `affected`, `path`)

graphify currently ships only traversal. The closest thing to enumeration — `query` — substring+IDF-picks ~3 seed nodes and then BFS-floods their neighborhoods, which is the wrong shape for name harvesting. Measured on a TypeScript monorepo graph (~10.9k nodes, graphify 0.8.38):

- `graphify query "candidate" --budget 800` → seeds `['Candidate']`, 115 nodes found. The output is the seeds' 2-hop neighborhood (`Button()`, `data-provider.ts`, `useOrgPath()`, …). Other candidate-named symbols in the graph — `CandidateForm()`, `CandidateApplication`, the `candidates.ts` route file — never appear, because they aren't *near* the seed; they merely *match the term*, which BFS doesn't care about.
- `graphify query "candidate isolation organization" --budget 800` → seeds matched only the word "organization", 739 nodes. Richer, more "natural" prompts get strictly worse: every extra word competes to seed, and the budget truncates an unranked flood.
- On 0.8.31 the same single-term query seeded on e2e spec filenames (`candidates.spec.ts`, `candidates-permissions.spec.ts`, …) and returned 102 nodes of test infrastructure. The 0.8.34 exact-match bonus visibly improved seed selection — but the output is still a neighborhood, not a match list.
- `--context call` doesn't help here: it filters the traversal, not the matching (same test returned 1 node — the seed itself).

The MCP server has the same gap: `get_node` resolves a single node, `get_neighbors` needs a known node, `query_graph` is the same BFS.

### Why this matters: the cold-start failure mode

From real agent transcripts (Claude Code with the installed graphify skill + hooks): at session start the agent has only concept words from the user's request. It guesses plausible symbol names — `explain "CandidateRepository"`, `explain "requireMembership"` — that don't exist in the graph (the real nodes were `candidates.ts` and `getMembershipWithPermissions()`). In one logged session 5 of 7 cold guesses returned `No node matching`, the agent concluded the graph didn't cover the area, and it fell back to grep/find/full-file reads for the rest of the session. The graph lost exactly the workload it was installed for — and every explain it ran *later in the session on observed names* resolved perfectly.

I believe #445, #977, #569 and #449 are all symptoms of the same underlying mismatch — trying to make the traversal behave like a search — while the simpler missing primitive would sidestep much of it.

### The workaround we run today

We prepend this to the agent instructions as the mandatory cold-start step:

```bash
jq -r --arg t "candidate" \
  '.nodes[] | select((.label // "") | ascii_downcase | contains($t))
   | ((.label | gsub("\\s+"; " "))[0:60]) + "  " + (.source_file // "?")' \
  graphify-out/graph.json | sort -u
```

One lowercase term returns every symbol/file/doc node whose label contains it, with source paths — exactly the tokens `explain` needs next. Typical output is ~30 lines on a 10k-node graph; deterministic, no token budget needed. With this as step 1 ("harvest real names, then explain them"), the guessing failure mode disappeared from our transcripts: every subsequent `explain` resolved first-try, and graph-assisted sessions completed the same investigation task at roughly half the cumulative tokens of a no-graph control with fewer factual errors.

But needing raw `jq` against `graph.json` for the single most common cold-start operation smells like a missing verb — hence this issue.

## Proposed fix

A new read-only subcommand that enumerates nodes by label match, no traversal:

```
graphify <verb> "<term>" [--limit N] [--type code|document|concept|...] [--graph PATH]
```

Output: one line per match — label, source_file:line, and the node ID (the ID matters for hyphenated filenames, which the label matcher can't address directly). Case-folded substring matching over labels would already cover the agent use case; anything fancier can come later.

Implementation looks like mostly plumbing — the matching logic already exists (`_find_node` / `_score_nodes` in `serve.py`). But the full surface is wider than the CLI, and shipping only the subcommand would leave agents on the old flow:

1. CLI subcommand in the dispatcher
2. Matching MCP tool (e.g. `find_nodes`) in `serve.py`
3. **Skill + installer text updates** — `SKILL.md` / `references/query.md` should teach "enumerate → explain" as the discovery flow, and the per-platform instruction blocks (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`.mdc` sections and the hook nudge strings) currently steer agents toward `query` for discovery; without updating those, the new verb won't get used
4. README / docs

## Open question: naming

No strong preference — whatever fits the existing verb family. Candidates: `graphify nodes`, `graphify search`, `graphify ls`, `graphify find`. (`search` may overpromise semantics; `nodes` is the most literal.)

Happy to pick this up and send a PR covering all four surfaces once the name and flag set are agreed.

title: AST extraction crashes on machines with >61 logical cores (Windows ProcessPoolExecutor cap)
body:
On a 64-core Windows 11 machine, `graphify extract` (and the `/graphify` skill, which calls `graphify.extract.extract()` directly) crashes during AST extraction:

```
File ".../graphify/extract.py", line 11569, in _extract_parallel
    with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool:
File ".../concurrent/futures/process.py", line 682, in __init__
    raise ValueError(...)
ValueError: max_workers must be <= 61
```

## Cause
`_extract_parallel` defaults `max_workers` to `cpu_count` (`extract.py:11561` → `min(cpu_cap, len(uncached_work))`). On Windows, `ProcessPoolExecutor` hard-caps at 61 workers (CPython limitation tied to `WaitForMultipleObjects`). Any machine with >61 logical cores hits the `ValueError` immediately.

## Repro
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise (26200), 64 logical cores
- Python: 3.12.8, graphifyy 0.8.38
- Run `graphify extract .` (or `/graphify .` via the Claude Code skill) on any code corpus.

## Workarounds (confirmed)
1. `graphify extract <path> --max-workers 16` — works.
2. `graphify update <path>` — works (auto-capped to 29 workers in my run; only `extract`/full-pipeline defaults to `cpu_count`).
3. Calling `extract(files, max_workers=16)` directly — works.

## Suggested fix
Clamp the default in `_extract_parallel`:

```python
cpu_cap = os.cpu_count() or 1
if sys.platform == "win32":
    cpu_cap = min(cpu_cap, 60)  # ProcessPoolExecutor hard cap is 61
max_workers = min(cpu_cap, len(uncached_work))
```

The skill (`SKILL.md` Step 3 Part A) calls `extract()` with no `max_workers`, so the crash is not avoidable from the skill side without this default fix.

title: graphify query/explain/path crash on unreadable ~/.claude/skills/graphify/.graphify_version
body:
## Summary

`graphify query`, `graphify explain`, and `graphify path` can fail during startup if the skill-version probe hits an unreadable `.graphify_version` file under a platform-specific skills directory.

That makes an advisory compatibility warning behave like a hard failure.

## Reproduction

1. Install `graphify` in an environment where `~/.claude/skills/graphify/.graphify_version` exists but is unreadable.
2. Run a normal command such as:

```bash
graphify query "how is graphify implemented?"
```

## Actual behavior

The command fails with `PermissionError` before it reaches the normal query path.

## Expected behavior

The command should continue running. If the version probe cannot be read, it should be treated as non-fatal and skipped.

## Why this matters

The version probe is only a staleness warning. It should never block normal graph queries when a platform-specific skill directory is inaccessible.

## Suggested fix

Catch unreadable probe paths during startup, or skip unreadable skill directories before comparing `.graphify_version`.

title: fix: ignore unreadable skill version probes
body:
## Summary

Treat unreadable skill-version probe files as non-fatal during startup.

## Change

- Skip or ignore unreadable `.graphify_version` paths
- Preserve the warning when the file is readable and the version is stale
- Add a regression test for the permission-failure case

## Notes

This keeps the compatibility warning behavior without making normal commands fail in sandboxed or restricted environments.

title: fix(build): replace stale source graph content
body:
## What changed

- Add `replace_sources` to `build_merge()` so changed files can remove their old graph content before fresh extraction is merged.
- Keep deleted-file cleanup on `prune_sources` and update generated skill references to pass changed files through `replace_sources`.
- Suppress low-confidence inferred dependency edges from generic symbols into code nodes.
- Add `graphify diagnose quality` for read-only graph hygiene checks: dangling edges, low-confidence inferred edges, generic bridge nodes, and stale report/html outputs.
- Filter preserved watch-mode hyperedges by evicted source files.

## Why

Incremental graph refreshes can preserve stale relationships for files that were re-extracted. This is especially noisy when low-confidence generic symbols such as `Check`, `Path`, or `Connection` remain connected to code nodes after the newer extraction no longer emits those edges.

`replace_sources` makes the changed-file path explicit: old content for those source files is removed from the base graph first, then the fresh extraction is merged. Deleted files continue to use `prune_sources`.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/test_build.py tests/test_multigraph_diagnostics.py tests/test_watch.py -q`
- `uv run pytest tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_multigraph_diagnostics.py tests/test_watch.py -q`
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q` (`2039 passed, 28 skipped`)

title: get_community MCP tool should surface the community label, not just the numeric ID
body:
# Feature request: `get_community` (and `get_community`-style output) should show the LLM community label, not just the numeric ID

**Version:** graphifyy 0.8.39 (PyPI, installed via `uv tool`)
**Component:** MCP server (`graphify/serve.py`)

## Summary

The MCP tool `get_community` returns only the numeric community ID in its header:

```
Community 1 (47 nodes):
  route.ts [packages/.../jubilacion/route.ts]
  ...
```

…even though the build has already generated a human-readable label for that
community ("Jubilación Monte Carlo") and stored it in `.graphify_labels.json`.
The label is the whole point of the LLM naming pass, but it never surfaces in
the tool a user reaches for to inspect a community. The caller has to
cross-reference `GRAPH_REPORT.md` by hand to find out what "Community 1" means.

## Where the label already lives but isn't used

The server already knows how to load the label map — it just doesn't use it in
the community tool:

- `serve.py` `_load_community_labels()` reads `<graph dir>/.graphify_labels.json`
  and returns `{cid: name}` (falls back to `Community {cid}`).
- It is only ever called inside the `graphify://questions` resource branch, to
  feed `analyze.suggest_questions(...)`.
- `_tool_get_community(...)` builds its header as
  `f"Community {cid} ({len(nodes)} nodes):"` and never consults the label map.

So the label is loaded for startup question hints but is invisible to every
queryable tool (`get_community`, and by extension anyone inspecting a community).

For contrast, the label *is* shown everywhere else it makes sense — the
`GRAPH_REPORT.md` (`report.py`), `graph.html` (`export.py`), the wiki
(`wiki.py`), and PR-impact output (`prs.py`) all render community names. The
interactive MCP `get_community` tool is the one place a user inspects a
community by hand, and it's the only one that drops the name. This is a
consistency gap, not missing infrastructure.

(Line numbers are from the installed 0.8.39 wheel; they will differ on HEAD —
the relevant symbols are `_tool_get_community`, `_load_community_labels`, and the
`communities` closure variable set at server init.)

## Proposed fix (minimal)

Load the label map once at server init, next to where `communities` is built
(and refresh it where `communities` is recomputed on graph reload), then prefix
the header:

```python
# at init, alongside: communities = _communities_from_graph(G)
community_labels = _load_community_labels()        # {cid: name}, falls back to "Community {cid}"

# in _tool_get_community:
label = community_labels.get(cid)
header = f"Community {cid}" + (f" — {label}" if label and label != f"Community {cid}" else "")
lines = [f"{header} ({len(nodes)} nodes):"]
```

Result:

```
Community 1 — Jubilación Monte Carlo (47 nodes):
  ...
```

`_load_community_labels()` already degrades gracefully when the sidecar is
absent, so graphs built with `--no-label` keep the current behaviour.

## Bonus: the global/merged graph loses labels entirely

`global_add` (in `global_graph.py`) composes prefixed repo graphs into
`~/.graphify/global-graph.json` but does **not** copy each repo's
`.graphify_labels.json` next to it, so `_load_community_labels()` finds nothing
and the merged graph always falls back to numeric IDs — even for the
single-repo case where the source `community` IDs are preserved 1:1.

Two sub-issues worth noting:

1. **Sidecar not propagated.** Consider having `global_add` merge the per-repo
   label maps into a global `.graphify_labels.json`.
2. **Community IDs collide across repos.** Node IDs are prefixed for isolation
   (`prefix_graph_for_global`) but the integer `community` attribute is copied
   verbatim, so two repos both contribute `community 0,1,2,…` into the same
   buckets in the merged graph. Any global label map keyed by raw int would be
   ambiguous once a second repo is added. A prefixed/namespaced community key
   in the global graph would fix both the labels and the bucket collision.

## Repro

```bash
graphify <repo>                 # build with LLM labels -> .graphify_labels.json exists
# via MCP:
get_community 1                 # header shows "Community 1 (N nodes)", not the label
```

Happy to send a PR for the minimal `get_community` fix if it's wanted.

title: Seed selection: tied _EXACT_MATCH_BONUS scores aren't degree/community-diversified (residual to #897)
body:
## Context

This is residual to #897. That issue's IDF weighting and gap-ratio
shape in `_pick_seeds` handle the broad seed-relevance case
correctly. The failure that remains is narrow: when multiple nodes
share the **same** `_EXACT_MATCH_BONUS`-tier score (which happens
whenever a generic label like "Configuration" appears on N nodes),
`_pick_seeds` picks the first three in enumeration order — no
tie-breaking on node degree or community. The picked three are
typically clustered in whichever region of the graph happened to
add those nodes first.

## Repro (synthetic, runs against any graph)

```python
import networkx as nx
from graphify.serve import _score_nodes, _pick_seeds

G = nx.Graph()

# "right" community: 2 Configuration nodes, low connectivity (real configs)
G.add_node("right_a", label="Configuration", norm_label="configuration",
           source_file="backend/credentials.py", community=42)
G.add_node("right_b", label="Configuration", norm_label="configuration",
           source_file="backend/credentials.py", community=42)

# "wrong" community: 3 Configuration nodes, high connectivity (page abstractions)
G.add_node("wrong_a", label="Configuration", norm_label="configuration",
           source_file="frontend/settings/page.tsx", community=99)
G.add_node("wrong_b", label="Configuration", norm_label="configuration",
           source_file="frontend/usermap/page.tsx", community=99)
G.add_node("wrong_c", label="Configuration", norm_label="configuration",
           source_file="frontend/sync/page.tsx", community=99)

# wrong_* are highly connected (deg 50); right_* are specific (deg 1)
for i in range(50):
    G.add_node(f"hub_{i}")
    G.add_edge("wrong_a", f"hub_{i}")
    G.add_edge("wrong_b", f"hub_{i}")
    G.add_edge("wrong_c", f"hub_{i}")
G.add_edge("right_a", "right_b")

scored = _score_nodes(G, ["configuration"])
seeds = _pick_seeds(scored)
print(seeds)
```

Output:

```
['wrong_c', 'wrong_b', 'wrong_a']
```

All five candidates score `2319.11` (`_EXACT_MATCH_BONUS *
inverse-document-frequency`, identical for all five). Gap-ratio is
0% so all five pass the threshold. `_pick_seeds` then takes
`max_k=3` in input order — the wrong three.

## Same shape on a real corpus

I saw this first on a multi-repo umbrella graph (~38k nodes) where
"Configuration" was a generic label across many files. The seed
selection landed three nodes from one unrelated sub-tree (frontend
settings pages) when the actually-relevant community (a backend
credentials handler) had its own "Configuration" matches that
should have at least split the seed set. Asking the same question
with the proper noun for the service in question landed on the
right community in one hop, so the graph DOES contain the right
answer — the seed selection just doesn't reach it when generic
labels tie.

## Suggested enhancement

```python
def _pick_seeds(
    G: nx.Graph,                    # added: needed for degree + community
    scored: list[tuple[float, str]],
    max_k: int = 3,
    gap_ratio: float = 0.2,
) -> list[str]:
    if not scored:
        return []
    seeds: list[str] = []
    seen_communities: set[int] = set()
    top_score = scored[0][0]
    threshold = top_score * (1 - gap_ratio)

    # Bucket near-tied candidates (within gap_ratio of top), then pick
    # diversely from the bucket. Beyond the bucket, stop.
    bucket = [nid for s, nid in scored if s >= threshold]

    # Sort the bucket: lower-degree first (highly-connected nodes are
    # the worst starting points for specific questions), then prefer
    # community diversity.
    bucket.sort(key=lambda nid: G.degree(nid))

    for nid in bucket:
        if len(seeds) >= max_k:
            break
        community = G.nodes[nid].get("community")
        # Skip seeds whose community is already represented unless we
        # have spare slots after one-per-community is exhausted.
        if community in seen_communities and len(seeds) < max_k - 1:
            continue
        seeds.append(nid)
        if community is not None:
            seen_communities.add(community)

    # Fall back to fill seeds if community-diversity left us short.
    if len(seeds) < min(max_k, len(bucket)):
        for nid in bucket:
            if nid not in seeds:
                seeds.append(nid)
            if len(seeds) >= max_k:
                break

    return seeds
```

Two enhancements in one pass:

**a. Degree-based tie-breaking.** Among tied scores, pick the
LOWER-degree (less connected) nodes. A node with 3 edges labeled
"Configuration" is a specific config; a node with 50 edges is a
highly-connected abstraction. The specific one is almost always
the better entry point for a targeted question.

**b. Community diversity.** When N seeds land in the same
community, we lose breadth. Spreading across communities surfaces
cross-cutting matches the user might actually want.

The signature change (now takes `G`) means callers need updating —
the only call site I see is in `_query_graph_text` and the test
file. Tests in `tests/test_serve.py` lines 420+ would need
adjustment to pass a graph in (or to use a `_make_graph()` helper).

## What this does NOT change

- Existing behaviour when scores are NOT tied (#897's fix). When
  one identifier dominates (`FooBarService` at 1000 vs noise at 1.0),
  gap-ratio still kicks in and only the dominant seed is returned.
- The IDF weighting path. Same scoring, just better tie-breaking.
- Existing tests `test_pick_seeds_dominant_identifier_gives_one_seed`,
  `test_pick_seeds_close_scores_keeps_multiple`, etc. should all
  still pass with degree=0 placeholder graphs (or be updated to
  pass a real `G`).

title: graphify-mcp rejects documented --graph argument
body:
## Bug

The `graphify-mcp` binary does not accept `--graph` as a named flag.
Any `~/.mcp.json` config that follows the documented style silently fails
and the MCP server never loads the graph.

## Steps to reproduce

# This fails (error: unrecognized arguments: --graph)
graphify-mcp --graph /path/to/graph.json

# This works
graphify-mcp /path/to/graph.json

## Expected behavior

Either:
(a) `--graph /path` is accepted as a valid flag, OR
(b) The docs/README clearly state that the path is positional

## Impact

Every user who configures MCP via `~/.mcp.json` following standard docs
gets a broken MCP server with no clear error message.

## Fix

Add `--graph` as an alias for the positional argument in the CLI parser
(one-line argparse change).

title: graphify query and MCP return blank community names after cluster-only
body:
## Bug

After running `graphify cluster-only`, communities are created and
named correctly in `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `graph.html`. But every node
returned by `graphify query` and the `query_graph` MCP tool shows
`community=` (blank).

## Root cause

Community labels are stored in `.graphify_labels.json` separately.
They are NOT embedded into the `graph.json` node objects. So any tool
that reads `graph.json` at query time cannot surface community names.

## Expected behavior

`graphify query "..."` should show `community=Target State Management`
(or whatever the named community is) for each node, not blank.

## Fix

At cluster time, embed the community label into each node object in
`graph.json`, or have the query engine join `.graphify_labels.json`
at read time before returning results.

title: TypeScript workspace imports do not resolve package subpath exports
body:
## Summary

Graphify's TypeScript/JavaScript workspace import resolver does not resolve package subpath imports through `package.json` `exports`.

For a workspace package import like:

```ts
import { value } from "@example/package-a/browser";
```

Graphify records an `imports_from` edge to a bare `browser` node instead of resolving the target to the exported source file from `packages/package-a/package.json`.

This breaks affected-file traversal and graph accuracy for monorepos that expose browser/server or other subpath entrypoints through package exports.

## Minimal repro

```text
repo/
  package.json
  packages/
    package-a/
      package.json
      src/browser.ts
  apps/
    package-b/
      src/consumer.ts
```

Root `package.json`:

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*", "apps/*"]
}
```

`packages/package-a/package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "@example/package-a",
  "exports": {
    "./browser": {
      "source": "./src/browser.ts",
      "import": "./dist/esm/browser.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/browser.js",
      "types": "./dist/types/browser.d.ts"
    }
  }
}
```

`packages/package-a/src/browser.ts`:

```ts
export const value = "ok";
```

`apps/package-b/src/consumer.ts`:

```ts
import { value } from "@example/package-a/browser";

export const consumerValue = value;
```

## Actual behavior

Graphify emits an import edge similar to:

```json
{
  "source": "src_consumer",
  "target": "browser",
  "relation": "imports_from",
  "source_file": "apps/package-b/src/consumer.ts"
}
```

## Expected behavior

Graphify should resolve the package subpath through `package.json` `exports` and emit the import edge to the exported file node, for example:

```json
{
  "source": "src_consumer",
  "target": "src_browser",
  "relation": "imports_from",
  "source_file": "apps/package-b/src/consumer.ts"
}
```

The exact node id may differ, but the target should be the workspace source file behind the export map, not the bare subpath segment.

## Why this matters

Many TypeScript monorepos use package subpath exports for public entrypoints, especially to separate browser-safe and server-only APIs:

```json
{
  "exports": {
    "./browser": { "source": "./src/browser.ts", "import": "./dist/browser.js" },
    "./server": { "source": "./src/server.ts", "import": "./dist/server.js" }
  }
}
```

When Graphify records these as `browser` or `server`, reverse traversal and affected-file analysis become either incomplete or noisy.

## Suspected cause

In the workspace package resolver, the subpath appears to be checked as a filesystem path before package export maps are considered.

Conceptually, resolving `@example/package-a/browser` does something equivalent to:

```python
package_dir / "browser"
```

When that path does not resolve to a concrete file, the resolver falls back to the bare subpath string rather than consulting:

```json
exports["./browser"]
```

## Suggested fix

For workspace package imports with a subpath:

1. Locate the package root from the workspace package name.
2. Read `package.json`.
3. Look up the subpath in `exports` using the `./subpath` key.
4. Choose the best source target when available.
5. Fall back to runtime/type targets if no source target exists.
6. Only then fall back to direct filesystem probing such as `package_dir / subpath`.

Suggested condition preference for source-oriented graph extraction:

```text
source -> import -> module -> default -> require -> types
```

For condition objects, Graphify could recursively walk nested condition maps and return the first target matching the preferred condition list.

For wildcard exports such as:

```json
{
  "exports": {
    "./utils/*": {
      "source": "./src/utils/*.ts",
      "import": "./dist/utils/*.js"
    }
  }
}
```

replace the `*` segment from the import subpath before resolving the target.

This would make Graphify match modern Node/TypeScript monorepo package boundaries while preserving the existing direct-file fallback for packages that do not define exports.

title: fix: clean home-scope skill registration on uninstall; back up config files (#1121)
body:
## Problem
Global `graphify install` writes the `# graphify` skill registration to a **home-scoped** file (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` for codebuddy), but `graphify uninstall` only stripped `./CLAUDE.md` in the cwd — and matched the wrong heading level (`##` vs the `#` install wrote). Result: the registration is **orphaned**, left pointing at a now-deleted skill. Project-scope (`--project`) was already symmetric; this was global-scope only.

## Fix
- `claude_uninstall` / `codebuddy_uninstall` now strip the home-scope `# graphify` block on global (non-project) uninstall, via a shared `_strip_skill_registration` helper.
- **Backup safety net:** install/uninstall now snapshot any user-editable config file (`CLAUDE.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, VS Code instructions) to `~/.graphify/backups/<date>/` before modifying or deleting it. `GRAPHIFY_NO_BACKUP=1` disables it; mirrors the existing `export.backup_if_protected` convention. graphify-owned files (skill trees, Cursor/Devin rule files) are intentionally not backed up — they hold no user content.

## Audit
Checked every platform's install-target vs uninstall-target. Only **claude** and **codebuddy** had the home-scope asymmetry (both fixed); gemini, the AGENTS.md family, and vscode were already symmetric.

## Tests
- Home-scope uninstall regressions for claude and codebuddy (with sandboxed `Path.home()`).
- New `tests/test_install_backup.py` suite covering the backup helper and `GRAPHIFY_NO_BACKUP`.
- Full suite: 2039 passed, 28 skipped.
