title: feat: add VB.NET (.vb) language support
body:
# feat: add VB.NET (.vb) language support

## What

Adds extraction support for **VB.NET** (`.vb`) source files.

VB.NET has no maintained tree-sitter grammar, so `.vb` files are parsed with a
line-oriented **regex scanner** that mirrors the existing Pascal/Delphi fallback
(`_extract_pascal_regex`) and emits the **same node/edge schema** as the
tree-sitter pass.

## Why

Large VB.NET / WinForms codebases are currently invisible to graphify — `.vb`
isn't in `CODE_EXTENSIONS`, so every `.vb` file is treated as a non-code asset
and routed to semantic (LLM) extraction. This PR makes them first-class code,
extracted fully offline (no API key).

Tested on a real ~1,500-file VB.NET ERP: **1,127 / 1,129** logic files land in
the graph (99.8%), 100% offline.

## What it extracts

- `Namespace`
- `Class` / `Module` / `Structure` / `Interface` / `Enum`
- `Sub` / `Function` / `Property` / `Operator`
- `Inherits` (inherits), `Implements` (implements)
- `Imports` (imports)
- intra-file `calls`

## Details

- Reads with `utf-8-sig` so a declaration on **line 1 of a BOM-prefixed file**
  (e.g. `Public Class X`) still matches the `^\s*` anchored patterns. (Without
  this, BOM files silently lost their top-level type node.)
- `_vb_strip` scans each line char-by-char to blank string literals and strip
  `'` / `REM` comments **without** collapsing line numbers — a stray quote inside
  a comment can't swallow later lines. Handles `""` escaped quotes.
- Case-insensitive throughout (`re.IGNORECASE`), as VB is.

## Changes

- `graphify/detect.py` — add `'.vb'` to `CODE_EXTENSIONS`
- `graphify/extract.py` — add `_extract_vb_regex` / `extract_vb`, register `.vb` in `_DISPATCH`

## Notes / possible follow-ups

- Pure-regex like the Pascal fallback; if a tree-sitter VB grammar appears later,
  this can become the fallback path behind it.
- Cross-file resolution (imports point at namespaces, not files) is intentionally
  left simple, matching how other module-style imports are handled.

title: feat: intra-file markdown slicing and adaptive retry (1/3)
body:
## Context

Split from former [#1326](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/pull/1326) (closed) per review feedback — **part 1 of 3**. See also the follow-up PRs for incremental safety and cross-file stitch.

## Motivation

Graphify incremental `extract` is how we maintain a knowledge graph as a corpus grows file-by-file. In production we hit failures where large documents **silently overflow** the model context: semantic extraction appears to succeed (exit 0) but returns empty or invalid JSON — especially under token pressure (local Ollama, tight budgets, or long `.md` files).

Without fixing chunking, downstream merge can proceed as if extraction worked when it did not.

## Problem: silent truncation on large documents

**Symptom:** Semantic extraction on large `.md` files returned empty graphs or unparseable JSON while the CLI still exited 0.

**Root cause:** `_pack_chunks_by_tokens` treated each file as atomic. A single file larger than the chunk budget was sent whole; the model truncated output (`finish_reason="length"`) or returned JSON that failed to parse. The chunk was dropped or merged as empty with no hard failure.

## Fix

New module `graphify/file_slice.py`:

- Splits oversized **splittable** text (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.rst`) into `FileSlice` units at heading / paragraph boundaries before packing.
- Adaptive retry can **bisect** a slice when a chunk still overflows context (`split_unit_for_retry`, `split_chunk_for_retry`).
- `llm.py` orchestrates only: `expand_oversized_files()` → pack → extract; slice logic lives in `file_slice.py`.

This matches how full runs co-pack related files for cross-file edges, but fixes the case where **one file alone** exceeds the budget.

## Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `graphify/file_slice.py` | New — slicing + bisect helpers |
| `graphify/llm.py` | Wire `SemanticUnit` / slices into packing and adaptive retry |
| `tests/test_file_slice.py` | New |
| `tests/test_chunking.py` | Slice-aware chunking regressions |

**Not included here (other parts of #1326):** incremental abort-on-failure (PR 2), cross-file stitch (PR 3), OpenRouter/BYOK backend wiring (upstream #1273 covers env-based OpenAI URLs).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_file_slice.py tests/test_chunking.py tests/test_llm_parser.py tests/test_extract.py`
- [ ] Upstream CI on Linux

title: feat: abort incremental update on failed or empty re-extraction (2/3)
body:
## Context

Split from former [#1326](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/pull/1326) (closed) per review feedback — **part 2 of 3**.

- Part 1: #1369 (intra-file slicing)
- Part 3: cross-file stitch — **stacked on this branch** (see follow-up PR)

Reconciled with upstream **#1344** (re-extracted files replace prior contribution in `build_merge`) and **#1350** (`--no-cluster` incremental no-op). This PR does **not** change the `--no-cluster` raw-write contract.

## Motivation

Incremental `extract` is the practical way to update a graph file-by-file. We hit a **critical data-loss bug**: after editing one markdown file and re-running incremental extract, nodes for that file could disappear entirely while exit code stayed 0.

## Problem: incremental update silently shrank the graph

**Symptom:** Changed file’s nodes vanished after incremental re-extract; unrelated files could survive.

**Root cause:** Incremental merge always **pruned** changed files before inserting fresh extraction (`prune_sources = deleted + changed`). If the LLM chunk “completed” but produced zero nodes (invalid JSON, connection blip, truncation), merge still ran: old nodes pruned, nothing replaced.

Upstream #1344 now auto-replaces nodes/edges for `source_file` values present in the re-extract batch; this PR adds the **guardrail** that prevents merge when re-extraction itself failed or returned nothing.

## Fix

**`graphify/build.py`** — path coverage helpers:

- `source_path_aliases`, `source_files_in_extraction`
- `path_covered_by_extraction`, `paths_missing_from_extraction`

**`graphify/__main__.py`** (incremental mode only):

1. After semantic re-extract, **abort with exit 1** if any uncached changed file has no nodes/edges in the fresh result, or if any chunk failed.
2. Do **not** write `graph.json` or update the manifest on failure — existing graph is preserved.
3. Build `prune_sources` from deleted files + changed code + **successfully re-extracted** semantic files only (via `path_covered_by_extraction`).

Stitch wiring (`stitch.py`, `_stitch_new_ids`, etc.) is intentionally **not** in this PR — see part 3.

## Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `graphify/build.py` | Path coverage helpers for incremental safety |
| `graphify/__main__.py` | Abort + `_incremental_prune` (clustered incremental path) |
| `tests/test_build.py` | Import formatting |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_build.py tests/test_extract.py`
- [ ] Upstream CI on Linux

title: feat: cross-file reference stitch for incremental updates (3/3)
body:
## Context

Split from former [#1326](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/pull/1326) (closed) per review feedback — **part 3 of 3**.

### Stacked on part 2

**Merge [#1370](https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify/pull/1370) (incremental safety) before this PR.**

This branch is based on `feat/incremental-safety` (`c5fa2ff`). Because that branch lives on the fork, the GitHub base is `v8` here — the PR diff therefore includes both part 2 and part 3. For a **stitch-only review**, compare on the fork:

https://github.com/Const011/graphify/compare/feat/incremental-safety...feat/cross-file-stitch

- Part 1: #1369 (intra-file slicing) — independent

## Motivation

Incremental `extract` sends **only changed files** to the LLM. Re-extracting one changed doc produced entities and edges **inside that chunk only**. Mentions of symbols elsewhere (e.g. `` `calculateWorkingTimeFromTeamsCalendar` `` referencing a calendar doc already in the graph) did not create edges to existing nodes. BFS / `query` / `path` could not reach the updated region from the rest of the corpus — breaking the “add files one at a time” workflow.

## Problem: incremental updates were not discoverable (isolated subgraph)

**Root cause:** By design, incremental semantic extraction lacks stable node IDs for the rest of the graph; the model often hallucinates `source_file` paths instead of wiring references.

## Fix

New module `graphify/stitch.py` — deterministic **post-merge stitch pass** (incremental only):

- After `build_merge`, scan each changed file **on disk** for backtick identifiers and path-like markdown links.
- Resolve symbols against the **full merged graph** (unique label match; skip ambiguous names — same conservatism as AST cross-file resolution).
- Add `references` edges from an anchor node in the changed file to external targets.
- When the LLM mis-attributes `source_file` on fresh nodes, use `new_node_ids` from the extraction and exclude nodes correctly placed under a **different on-disk file**.

**Why stitch (and not alternatives alone)?**

| Alternative | Why we did not rely on it alone |
|-------------|----------------------------------|
| Full corpus re-extract | Correct but expensive; defeats incremental purpose |
| Pack neighbor files into LLM context | Higher token cost; still no guaranteed stable IDs |
| LLM-only “wire edges” pass | Extra cost + variance; mentions are already in source text |
| Bidirectional / rewrite unchanged files | Out of scope; outbound stitch + undirected search is enough |

Stitch is **deterministic, cheap, and testable** — it reuses `source_path_aliases` from `build.py` (#1370) and label indexing patterns from `symbol_resolution.py`.

## `__main__.py` note (`--no-cluster`)

This PR wires stitch into both the **clustered** and **`--no-cluster` incremental** paths. The latter routes incremental updates through `build_merge` before writing raw JSON so stitch can run on a `NetworkX` graph. **This changes the documented no-cluster contract** (parallel edges may collapse via merge dedup). Flagging explicitly per review on #1326 — happy to gate behind a flag if preferred.

## Files added in part 3

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `graphify/stitch.py` | New — post-merge cross-file `references` edges |
| `graphify/__main__.py` | `_stitch_new_ids`, `_changed_for_stitch`, `stitch_incremental_links` hooks (requires #1370 `__main__` / `build.py` base) |
| `tests/test_stitch.py` | New (self-contained `tmp_path` fixtures) |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_stitch.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_extract.py`
- [ ] Upstream CI on Linux
- [ ] Incremental smoke: re-extract changed doc → stitch adds cross-file `references`, verified with `graphify path`

title: OpenAI backend caps output at 8192 tokens (half the 16384 other backends use) → truncated semantic chunks on dense repos
body:
### Summary
The `openai` backend has no `max_tokens` key in its `BACKENDS` config (`llm.py`), so it falls through `_resolve_max_tokens(cfg.get("max_tokens", 8192))` to **8192** — while every other backend (claude, gemini, kimi, deepseek, bedrock) is set to **16384**. On dense repos/chunks the model's JSON output hits this ~8192-token (~32k-char) ceiling mid-generation (`finish_reason == "length"`), producing `LLM returned invalid JSON … Unterminated string starting at … char ~32000`, forcing the chunk-split-retry path. Inferred edges in the truncated tail are lost.

### Repro
```
graphify extract <large-code-repo> --backend openai --token-budget 20000
```
→ `LLM returned invalid JSON, skipping chunk: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column ~32000`
→ `chunk of N truncated at depth 0, splitting into halves …`

Truncation char positions cluster at 29k–36k chars (≈ 7–9k output tokens — just over 8192).

### Impact
- Suppressed INFERRED/semantic edges on big repos (measured: an 8.9k-node repo gained +67 INFERRED edges once the cap was raised; 4 truncation events → 0).
- Wasted tokens on truncated-then-retried chunks.
- Silent inconsistency vs other backends — openai users get half the output headroom, no signal.

### Workaround (works today)
`export GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=16384` restores parity. Bonus: truncated chunks aren't cached (they errored), so a `--force` re-run only re-does the failed chunks — recovery is cheap.

### Suggested fix (RFC — pick the altitude)
1. **Parity:** add `"max_tokens": 16384` to the openai backend config (one line; removes the surprise).
2. **Output-aware:** chunking is sized by *input* (`--token-budget`) but the cap is about *output*. On `finish_reason == "length"` (already detected), auto-retry the chunk once at a higher cap before falling back to split — or size chunks by estimated output (≈ f(#entities)).
3. **Per-model introspection:** derive the cap from the model's actual `max_completion_tokens` capability rather than a hardcoded default.

Happy to PR option 1. The env override is a fine interim; the ask is (a) fix the default for parity, (b) consider output-aware chunking so dense repos don't silently lose edges.

title: Java Records and constructor call relationships not recognized
body:
**Because the graph build missed the kinds of links that class has, and it also appears to miss the record declaration itself.**

What I found:

- In the graph, the node is just the file node:
  `OidcAuthenticationProperties.java` → **degree 0**
- But in the code, it is clearly used:
  - `OidcJwtAuthenticationConfiguration.java` references it in `@EnableConfigurationProperties(...)`
  - `InteractionCodeTokenHelper.java` constructs it with `new OidcAuthenticationProperties(...)`
  - `OidcAuthenticationPropertiesTest.java` references it multiple times

The likely reasons it ends up isolated are:

1. **Graphify’s Java extraction is mostly structural AST, not full semantic code analysis.**  
   In this run, code relationships were coming from AST extraction, and semantic extraction was only applied to docs/images. So body-level usages like constructor calls and class literals were not added as graph edges.

2. **It appears to miss Java `record` declarations as first-class type nodes.**  
   For `OidcJwtAuthenticationConfiguration.java`, the graph has both the file node and a contained class node. For `OidcAuthenticationProperties.java`, it only has the file node — not a separate type node for the record declaration. That strongly suggests the extractor is not modeling Java records the same way as classes.

3. **Its only import is external framework code.**  
   `OidcAuthenticationProperties.java` imports `ConfigurationProperties`, but external library symbols are not being represented as graph nodes here, so that import does not save it from isolation.

So the short answer is: **your IDE is right; the graph is incomplete here.** The isolation is an extraction limitation, not a real architecture signal.

**What would fix it**
1. Add Java AST support for **record declarations** so the record becomes a proper symbol node.
2. Add extraction of **type references in annotations** like `@EnableConfigurationProperties(OidcAuthenticationProperties.class)`.
3. Add extraction of **constructor/type usages in method bodies** like `new OidcAuthenticationProperties(...)`.
4. Optionally run **semantic extraction on code files too**, not only docs/images.

title: Markdown links not accurately represented as edges
body:
### Use Case I have a Microsoft Agent Package Manager (APM ) mono-repo (defines packages and a marketplace to distribute those package). The repo is mostly composed of skill packages that define coding standards. Within a standards package there are index.md and table-of-contents.md, that clearly should be hub nodes out to all other documents in that package. Those hub nodes don't seem to be represented at all. The following is the self analysis. The graph was generated, queried and root cause analyzed using GPT 5.4. ---

They’re not connected because those links were mostly never extracted into the graph. The issue is in semantic extraction of the C# markdown navigation files, not in clustering.

In the rebuilt graph:

Source file | Expected role | Extracted outgoing links -- | -- | -- packages/coding-standards-csharp/index.md | connect many C# concepts to many standards docs | 1 packages/coding-standards-csharp/table-of-contents.md | connect the package to its major standards sections | 3 packages/coding-standards-cpp/index.md | same pattern for C++ | 16 packages/coding-standards-cpp/table-of-contents.md | same pattern for C++ | 24

The C# source files clearly contain the missing links. For example:

  • packages/coding-standards-csharp/table-of-contents.md:39 links to C# Repository Standards
  • ...:45 links to C# HTTP Client Standards
  • ...:67 links to C# Dependency Injection Standards
  • ...:88 links to C# Unit Test Standards

And packages/coding-standards-csharp/index.md has many table rows linking into repository, HTTP client, messaging, DI, error handling, and unit test docs. But the graph only captured:

  • from index.md: 1 edge, to the ASP.NET MVC index note
  • from table-of-contents.md: 3 edges, to ASP.NET MVC plus two unit-test-related nodes

So the C# communities are split because the graph does not actually contain the cross-community edges you expected. The community detector is grouping based on the extracted graph it has, and for C# that graph is sparse.

Root cause: the markdown semantic extraction for the C# index/table-of-contents under-extracted references, while the equivalent C++ files were extracted much more completely. That’s why the C#/.NET communities look artificially disconnected.

title: Microsoft Agent Package Manager: Parent Package Nodes Duplicated
body:
[Microsoft Agent Package Manager (APM)](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/) behaves in a similar manner to other package managers, allowing packages to declare dependencies on other packages.  Below are the apm.yml files for a parent core language agnostic coding standards package and a dependent language specific package.  In some cases a child package will show linkage to the core package.  In other cases, the core package is represented as a duplicate node in the graph.

Core package apm.yml file

```yml
name: coding-standards-core
version: 1.0.4
description: General code standards and clean code evaluation standards applicable to all languages.
```

Package with dependency on core apm.yml file

```yml
name: coding-standards-csharp
version: 1.1.0
description:
  C# and .NET coding standards including services, repositories, HTTP clients, cross-cutting concerns, and unit testing.
dependencies:
  apm:
    - MyPrivateGithubOrg/apm-internal-marketplace/packages/coding-standards-core
```

Notably, the first two path segments are the github org and repo and the remaining path portion is the path within the repo.


The directed graph was constructed using GPT 5.4 and root cause analyzed using the same

---

**Root cause: the extractor has no canonical rule for APM package dependencies, so `coding-standards-core` gets materialized as whatever local node a chunk happened to invent first.** That fragments one real dependency target into multiple graph nodes, and some package edges end up pointing at different stand-ins.

In the fresh graph there are already **three** different core-related nodes:
- `coding-standards-core package` from `packages/coding-standards-core/apm.yml`
- `coding-standards-core` from `packages/coding-standards-python/apm.yml`
- `coding-standards-core dependency` from `packages/coding-standards-python-fastapi/SKILL.md`

The key tell is that some edges point to a node whose ID is anchored to the **wrong source file**. For example, several Go standards docs reference target ID `coding_standards_python_apm_coding_standards_core`, which is a node sourced from **Python’s** `apm.yml`, not from Go. That means the semantic subagent created one shared “coding-standards-core” concept inside a mixed chunk and anchored it to an arbitrary file in that chunk, then reused that ID for unrelated files.

So the failure is:

1. **Dependencies are being extracted semantically from YAML/docs instead of structurally canonicalized** to the actual package node in `packages/coding-standards-core/apm.yml`.
2. **Node IDs are file-anchored by design** (`{parent}_{file}_{entity}`), which is fine for file-local concepts but wrong for a global package identity.
3. **Cross-file chunk extraction reuses whichever local core node was created first**, so one chunk can anchor core to Python, another to FastAPI prose, while another correctly points to the real core package node.

That is why packages that truly depend on the same core package do not all connect through one hub: **the graph has multiple semantically equivalent but structurally different targets for “coding-standards-core.”**

title: Unify node-ID normalization into a single source of truth (#1)
body:
extract._make_id and build._normalize_id each carried a copy of the same NFKC -> \w -> underscore-collapse -> casefold recipe, kept in sync only by mirrored docstrings. That duplication is the root of the recurring ID-drift bug class (#811, #550, #1033, #1104): the AST extractor, the LLM subagents, and the graph builder must all produce identical node IDs or a single entity splits into disconnected ghost nodes.

Move the recipe into a new graphify/ids.py (normalize_id + make_id). extract and build now both delegate to it, so they can no longer diverge. Behavior is unchanged — both copies were already identical.

Add tests/test_id_normalization_contract.py: parametrized regression cases for the cited issues, plus hypothesis property tests asserting _make_id(s) == _normalize_id(s) and idempotency. The shared-implementation guard fails if a future change re-forks the normalization.

title: fix(llm): adaptive split-and-retry for label_communities on parse failure (#1278)
body:
## What

Fixes #1278.

`label_communities` previously logged-and-skipped any batch where the LLM returned malformed JSON or a non-object payload. On large graphs (the reporter's case: 121k nodes / 135 batches), a single failed batch silently lost ~100 community names with no recovery and no warning beyond the per-batch stderr line.

This mirrors the recovery shape `_extract_with_adaptive_retry` already uses for the extract path: when a batch fails to parse, split it at the midpoint and retry each half recursively. Most transient LLM JSON glitches go away at the first or second split (smaller prompt → smaller output → less likely to truncate or mangle).

## Fix

- New helper `_label_batch_with_retry()` in `graphify/llm.py`. Catches `(json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError)` from `_parse_label_response`, splits `batch_cids` and `batch_lines` together at `mid = len(batch_cids) // 2`, recurses on each half with `depth + 1`. Recursion capped at `max_depth=3` (same as extract).
- Non-parse exceptions (network errors, missing API keys, programming bugs) propagate unchanged via bare `raise`. The retry net is intentionally narrow.
- `label_communities` is now a thin wrapper: builds slices, calls the helper, tracks `first_error` and `written` exactly as before. The outer graceful-degradation contract is preserved — when retries exhaust at the base case, the original parse error re-raises so `generate_community_labels` still falls back to placeholders rather than silently returning empty.

## Test

New `tests/test_label_retry.py` adds a unit test with a stateful mock that returns malformed JSON on the first call and clean JSON on subsequent (smaller) calls. Confirms:

- All 4 input communities end up labeled despite the initial failure
- `_call_llm` was called more than once (proving the retry actually happened)

All 15 existing tests in `tests/test_labeling.py` continue to pass — including `test_label_communities_malformed_raises` (the old contract is preserved) and `test_generate_community_labels_degrades_on_error` (graceful fallback still works when retries exhaust).

## Design choices worth flagging

- **Exception types caught** — only `(json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError)` (the two things `_parse_label_response` raises). Network errors / config errors are not retried because they're not the recoverable case the issue describes.
- **`max_depth=3`** for consistency with `_extract_with_adaptive_retry`. With `batch_size=100`, this allows up to 8 leaf batches of ~12-13 communities each before giving up. If real-world cases need deeper recursion, that's a follow-up tuning.
- **Re-raise at base case (not silent return)** so the existing `first_error` tracking in `label_communities` still fires. A partial-success edge case (left half succeeds, right half exhausts) loses the left half's labels — but in exchange, the existing graceful-degradation contract is preserved. The alternative (return empty dict at base case) breaks `test_label_communities_malformed_raises` semantics.

## Notes

- Reproducible context: the original issue was on a 121k-node corpus with `batch_size=100` and Gemini backend. I was unable to reproduce the LLM-side malformed-JSON nondeterminism directly; the test uses a stateful mock to simulate the documented failure mode.
- The fix touches only `llm.py` — no API surface changes.
- Ran the full test suite. One pre-existing failure unrelated to this change: `tests/test_cli_export.py::test_export_wiki_accepts_edges_only_graph_json` fails on unmodified v8 with `KeyError: 'links'`. Looks like the same `edges`-vs-`links` key pattern already fixed in `affected.py` (#1280); the wiki export path appears to have been missed. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if useful.

title: fix(extract): stamp manifest when LLM source_file is relative
body:
## Motivation

`graphify extract` writes two artifacts that together gate **incremental** semantic updates:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `graphify-out/graph.json` | Merged knowledge graph |
| `graphify-out/manifest.json` | Per-file `semantic_hash` / `mtime` stamps for change detection |

Graphify enters incremental mode when **both files exist** (`incremental_mode = manifest_path.exists() and existing_graph_path.exists()` in `__main__.py`). On incremental runs, `detect_incremental()` compares corpus files against the manifest to decide what to re-extract.

### Symptom

After a **successful** first extract (populated `graph.json`, LLM tokens consumed, exit 0), `manifest.json` could be written as **`{}`** — an empty object with no file entries.

On the next extract:

- Graphify still sees both files exist → enters **incremental scan**
- But every document file looks **new** (no `semantic_hash` in manifest) or downstream tooling treats the manifest as unusable
- Integrators that require a non-empty manifest for “incremental ready” fall back to **full init** (wiping `graphify-out/`) even though the graph was valid
- Adding a second document could trigger a destructive full re-extract instead of merging into the existing graph

This was observed in production on a **docs-only** corpus: first file extracted nodes successfully; manifest stayed `{}`; adding a second document triggered a full re-init wipe instead of an incremental merge.

### Why it is subtle

- Extract **succeeds** (exit 0, graph written, tokens logged)
- No error about “re-extraction produced no nodes”
- The bug is entirely in **manifest stamping**, not in LLM extraction or merge
- String equality between detect paths and LLM `source_file` values fails silently

---

## Root cause

When building `_manifest_files` before `save_manifest()`, extract filtered semantic document files with:

```python
_sem_extracted: set[str] = {
    n.get("source_file", "") for n in sem_result.get("nodes", [])
} | {
    e.get("source_file", "") for e in sem_result.get("edges", [])
}
_manifest_files = {
    ftype: [f for f in flist if ftype not in _sem_types or f in _sem_extracted]
    for ftype, flist in files_by_type.items()
}
```

Two different path conventions collide:

| Source | Typical path form | Example |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| `detect()` / `files_by_type` | **Absolute** path string | `/home/user/project/notes.md` |
| LLM extraction `source_file` | **Repo-relative** (per prompt spec) | `notes.md` |

`f in _sem_extracted` is plain string equality → **never matches** for the common case where detect emits absolute paths and the model emits relative `source_file`.

Result:

1. All semantic document paths filtered **out** of `_manifest_files`
2. `save_manifest(_manifest_files, …)` called with empty document lists
3. On first run, no prior manifest entries to seed → **`manifest.json` = `{}`**
4. Graph is valid; manifest is not → incremental pipeline broken on next run

The pre-filter should still stamp `semantic_hash` only for files that **actually produced** semantic output (see comment above `_manifest_files` in `__main__.py`). That intent is unchanged — matching now uses path aliases instead of plain string equality.

---

## Fix

### 1. `graphify/build.py` — path alias helpers

Add three small functions (same pattern as incremental safety work elsewhere on the fork line):

- **`source_path_aliases(p, root)`** — normalized forms of a scan/manifest path (absolute, relative-to-root, `_norm_source_file`)
- **`source_files_in_extraction(extraction, root)`** — union of aliases for every `source_file` on nodes/edges/hyperedges in an extraction dict
- **`path_covered_by_extraction(p, extraction, root)`** — true when a detect path and extraction output refer to the same file

These are reusable for future incremental guards (`paths_missing_from_extraction`) but this PR only **consumes** them for manifest stamping.

### 2. `graphify/__main__.py` — manifest file filter

Replace `_sem_extracted` set membership with:

```python
from graphify.build import path_covered_by_extraction as _path_covered

_manifest_files = {
    ftype: [
        f
        for f in flist
        if ftype not in _sem_types or _path_covered(f, sem_result, target)
    ]
    for ftype, flist in files_by_type.items()
}
```

After fix, a successful single-doc extract writes e.g.:

```json
{
  "notes.md": {
    "mtime": 1781804099.04,
    "ast_hash": "b7807e2…",
    "semantic_hash": "b7807e2…"
  }
}
```

(relative key on write, with hashes populated)

### 3. `tests/test_extract_manifest.py`

Regression coverage:

- Absolute detect path + relative LLM `source_file` → `path_covered_by_extraction` is true
- Unrelated `source_file` → false
- End-to-end: `_manifest_files` filter + `save_manifest()` → non-empty manifest with `semantic_hash`
- `source_path_aliases` includes relative and absolute forms

### 4. `CHANGELOG.md`

Unreleased entry documenting the fix.

---

## Files changed

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| `graphify/build.py` | +37 | `source_path_aliases`, `source_files_in_extraction`, `path_covered_by_extraction` |
| `graphify/__main__.py` | ~14 | Manifest filter uses path-aware coverage |
| `tests/test_extract_manifest.py` | +102 | Regression tests |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | +1 | Unreleased note |

**No** LLM, clustering, incremental prune, or cache behaviour changed in this PR — manifest stamping only.

---

## How to verify

### Automated

```bash
pytest tests/test_extract_manifest.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_extract_cli.py tests/test_detect.py -q
```

169 passed locally against `v8` @ `d12eb28`.

### Manual

```bash
# Fresh docs-only corpus, one markdown file
rm -rf /tmp/corpus-out/graphify-out
graphify extract /tmp/corpus --out /tmp/corpus-out --backend <your-backend>

# Before fix: manifest.json == {}
# After fix:  manifest.json has an entry for the doc (relative key) with semantic_hash

# Add second doc; second run should show:
#   [graphify extract] incremental scan of …
# not a blind full re-init wipe
```

---

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/test_extract_manifest.py` — alias matching + manifest stamp
- `pytest tests/test_build.py tests/test_extract_cli.py tests/test_detect.py` — no regressions
- single-doc extract → non-empty `manifest.json`
- two-doc incremental add → incremental scan, graph grows

title: hook install writes a junk directory and reports false success when core.hooksPath resolves to a non-POSIX (Windows) path
body:
## Summary

When `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` returns a path that is not a resolvable POSIX directory — e.g. a Windows-style absolute path such as `C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks` — `graphify hook install` does not detect this. It path-joins the unresolvable value onto the current working directory, creating a **literal junk directory** (backslashes and all) inside the repository working tree, writes the hooks there, and prints a **false "installed" success message**. The real `.git/hooks` directory receives nothing, so no hook ever fires.

Reproducible in **WSL** when operating on a repo whose git config has `core.hooksPath` set (local scope) to a Windows absolute path — a common state when the same repo is used from both Windows-native git and WSL git.

## Environment

- graphify 0.8.41 (installed via `uv tool`)
- WSL2 (Linux) operating on a repo checked out on the Windows filesystem (`/mnt/c/...`)
- `git config --local --get core.hooksPath` → `C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks`
- Consequently `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` → `C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks` (unresolvable as a POSIX path from WSL)

## Steps to reproduce

1. In WSL, in a repo whose **local** git config has `core.hooksPath` set to a Windows-style absolute path (so `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` returns `C:\...\.git\hooks`).
2. Run `graphify hook install`.

## Actual behavior

Output (paths genericized):

```
post-commit: installed at /mnt/c/Users/<user>/<repo>/C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks/post-commit
post-checkout: installed at /mnt/c/Users/<user>/<repo>/C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks/post-checkout
```

- A directory **literally named** `C:\Users\<user>\<repo>\.git\hooks` (with backslashes in the name) is created inside the working tree, containing `post-commit` / `post-checkout`.
- The real `.git/hooks` directory is untouched — no hook is installed where git looks.
- The command exits 0 and reports success.

This junk path is also a hazard: it is an untracked file in the working tree that can easily be `git add`-ed by accident.

## Expected behavior

`hook install` should validate the resolved hooks directory and either:
- correctly resolve / normalize a non-POSIX `core.hooksPath` (e.g. translate a `C:\...` path to its `/mnt/c/...` equivalent under WSL), or
- fail loudly with a clear error (e.g. "hooks path `<x>` is not a writable directory on this platform; check `core.hooksPath`") and write nothing.

It should never path-join an unresolvable value onto the cwd and write a junk directory into the working tree, nor report success when nothing was installed where git looks.

## Workaround

If `core.hooksPath` is pointing at the default hooks location anyway (just expressed as a Windows absolute path), unsetting it makes git resolve `$GIT_DIR/hooks` relatively, which works from both WSL and Windows:

```
git config --local --unset core.hooksPath
# then `graphify hook install` installs into .git/hooks correctly
```

## Additionally: merge driver not configured (possible README/behavior mismatch)

The README states `graphify hook install` "also sets up a git merge driver" so `graph.json` is union-merged on concurrent commits. On 0.8.41, `hook install` installed only the `post-commit` / `post-checkout` hooks — no `merge.*.driver` was configured in git config and no `graph.json` entry was added to `.gitattributes`. Either the README or the behavior should be reconciled.

title: extract_corpus_parallel raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'parent' when passed string paths
body:
## Summary

`graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")` crashes when `files` is a list of `str` paths. It only works if the paths are `pathlib.Path` objects. The failure occurs in `_pack_chunks_by_tokens`, which calls `f.parent` on each entry.

## Environment

- graphify 0.8.41

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from graphify.llm import extract_corpus_parallel
files = ["a/b/file1.md", "a/b/file2.md"]   # str paths
extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")
```

## Actual behavior

```
File ".../graphify/llm.py", line 1420, in _pack_chunks_by_tokens
    by_dir.setdefault(f.parent, []).append(f)
                      ^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'parent'
```

Passing `[Path(f) for f in files]` instead works fine.

## Expected behavior

`extract_corpus_parallel` should accept string paths (coerce to `Path` internally — e.g. `f = Path(f)` at the entry point or top of `_pack_chunks_by_tokens`), or validate the input type up front and raise a clear, actionable error. A raw `AttributeError` deep in a private helper is hard for callers to diagnose.

title: Tip: Graphify file writes invalidate prompt cache in Claude Code (Recommended docs update)
body:
Hello Graphify team!

Graphify is an awesome tool for providing structured context to AI coding agents. However, when run interactively inside Anthropic's **Claude Code** CLI, we detected a performance/cost gotcha that we wanted to share along with a recommended documentation update.

We developed [claude-code-optimizer](https://github.com/Korck-lab/claude-code-optimizer) to audit local session logs for cache misses and token waste. Across **515 active projects utilizing Graphify** (with 2,404 total command calls):

* **The Issue:** In **54 sessions**, the Graphify tool generated output file writes (such as `graph.json` or `graphify-out`) in unignored workspace directories.
* **The Cost Impact:** Every time a file in the workspace is written to without being ignored, it instantly **invalidates Claude's prompt cache**. On the subsequent turn, Claude is forced to re-upload and re-parse the entire codebase context at full cache-write rates ($3.75/M tokens), losing the 90% caching discount.
* **Recommended Mitigation:** We suggest adding a tip in your README recommending that users add Graphify's output directories to their project's `.claudignore` file:

```text
# .claudignore
graph.json
graphify-out/
```

This keeps the prompt cache warm and prevents costly invalidation loops when graphing the codebase!

title: Feature request: `--max-concurrency` and `--batch-size` for `cluster-only` / `label`
body:
### Environment

graphify v0.8.42 (graphifyy package)

### Problem

Community labeling (`cluster-only`, `label`) runs **sequentially** with a fixed batch size of 100 communities per LLM call. For large graphs this creates an unnecessary bottleneck: a graph with 19 094 communities requires **191 sequential API calls**, even when the configured backend supports thousands of concurrent requests (e.g. DeepSeek V4-Flash has a concurrency limit of 2500).

By contrast, `graphify extract` already exposes `--max-concurrency` and uses a `ThreadPoolExecutor` to parallelise semantic extraction chunks. The labeling path has no equivalent.

### Current behavior

`llm.py::label_communities` iterates batches sequentially:

```python
# llm.py
_LABEL_BATCH_SIZE = 100        # hardcoded; not exposed to CLI

for batch_idx in range(n_batches):
    ...
    text = _call_backend(...)  # one request at a time
    labels.update(parsed)
```

`cluster-only` / `label` CLI commands accept `--backend` and `--model` but no concurrency or batch-size flags.

### Proposed solution

1. **`--max-concurrency N`** — parallelise batch LLM calls via `ThreadPoolExecutor`, mirroring the implementation already used in `extract_corpus_parallel`. Default: 4 (safe for all backends).

2. **`--batch-size N`** — expose `_LABEL_BATCH_SIZE` as a CLI flag so users can tune prompt size vs. request count. Default: 100 (current behavior preserved).

Example usage:

```
graphify cluster-only ./work --backend=deepseek --model=deepseek-v4-flash --max-concurrency=32 --batch-size=200
```

With `--max-concurrency=32` and `--batch-size=200`: 96 batches running 32 at a time → ~3 rounds instead of 191 sequential calls.

### Implementation hint

`label_communities` already accepts `batch_size` as a keyword argument — it just isn't wired up to the CLI. Adding `max_concurrency` and replacing the `for` loop with a `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out (same pattern as `_extract_corpus_parallel`) should be a small, self-contained change.

title: graphify claude install (v0.8.41): 26 validated bugs in the generated Claude Code skill (interpreter, --directed, shrink-guard, cleanup ordering)
body:
## Bug bundle: `graphify claude install` skill (v0.8.41) — 26 validated issues in the generated Claude Code skill

The auto-generated Claude Code skill produced by `graphify claude install` (pinned `.graphify_version = 0.8.41`) ships several reproducible bugs in `SKILL.md` and the `references/*.md` runbooks. We vendored this snapshot into a monorepo and an automated reviewer (plus manual checks) surfaced the issues below. **Each was verified against the installed `graphify` v0.8.41 Python source** (`build.py`, `export.py`, etc.), not just read off the markdown.

Reporting upstream because the skill is regenerated by `graphify claude install`, so any downstream edit to the vendored copy is overwritten on the next install/upgrade — the fix has to live in the generator.

Happy to open individual issues or send a PR against the skill template if that's easier; grouping here so the pattern is visible.

### A. Interpreter resolution — generated commands call system `python3`, which can't import `graphify` under `uv tool install`
1. **SKILL.md interpreter bootstrap** — `uv tool run graphifyy python` selects no package and falls through to system `python3`. The skill should resolve and persist the tool's interpreter (e.g. read the shebang of the installed `graphify` bin) — we use `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)`.
2. **references/add-watch.md `--watch`** — runs bare `python3 -m graphify.watch`; not importable under `uv tool install`. Must use the resolved interpreter.
3. **references/exports.md `--mcp`** — `python3 -m graphify.serve` and the generated Claude Desktop config `command` both point at system python; not importable. Must use the resolved interpreter / its absolute path.

### B. Environment variables set but never exported — child Python reads `os.environ` and never sees the override
4. **references/transcribe.md** — `GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_MODEL=base` set as an unexported shell var; transcriber silently uses the default model.
5. **references/transcribe.md** — Step 1 sets `WHISPER_PROMPT` but the transcriber reads `GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_PROMPT`; domain hint silently ignored (name mismatch + missing `export`).

### C. `--directed` not propagated — directed builds silently produce undirected graphs
6. **SKILL.md Steps 4/5** — `build_from_json(extraction)` omits `directed=`, so `--directed` builds undirected.
7. **references/update.md merge** — the update-only merge calls `build_merge(...)` without `directed=`; `build_merge(..., directed: bool = False)` (build.py:448) then builds undirected via `build(all_chunks, directed=directed)`. On `--directed --update`, reciprocal A↔B edges collapse to one when the merged graph is written back through `G.edges()`, and the later directed rebuild cannot recover the dropped edge.

### D. Output path uses scan-root, but later steps read cwd `graphify-out/` (or vice-versa)
8. **SKILL.md (CHUNK_PATH)** — chunk output path is derived from `.graphify_root` (the scanned dir) but Step B3 merges from cwd `graphify-out/`; a non-cwd scan (`graphify <subdir>`) writes chunks where the merge never looks → "no nodes".
9. **references/add-watch.md ingest** — `/graphify add <url>` ingests into cwd `Path('./raw')`, but the following `--update` scans `$(cat .graphify_root)`; a non-cwd build saves the file outside the scanned root → "no new files". Ingest into `root/'raw'`.

### E. File-list / category scoping
10. **SKILL.md Step B0** — `all_files` flattens *every* `detect['files']` category, including `code`, into the semantic-extraction list. `code` is already covered structurally by the AST pass, so LLM subagents re-read every source file — a repo-root run with even one README becomes unexpectedly expensive. Scope to content categories only (`{document, paper, image}`; `video` → `document` via transcription).
11. **references/update.md / transcribe.md** — on `--update`, the non-code branch jumps straight to extraction without running transcription, so changed `.mp4/.mp3` stay in `files.video` and feed unreadable media paths into semantic extraction (and a video-only corpus hits the code-only fast path → empty graph). Route media through transcription, then rewrite `.graphify_detect.json` to move transcripts into `files.document` and drop `files.video`.
12. **SKILL.md ~230 (stale semantic cache)** — `.graphify_cached.json` is only (re)written when `check_semantic_cache` returns hits (`if cached_nodes or ...:`). If a prior run took the all-cached shortcut and skipped Part B cleanup, the file is left behind; on a later run with zero cache hits but some uncached files the conditional is false, the stale file survives, and Step B3 merges its unrelated nodes/edges into the new graph. Always rewrite (empty) or delete the cache file before the check.

### F. Cleanup deletes intermediate files that later steps still read
13. **SKILL.md / code-only path** — code-only runs skip Part C but the merge reads `.graphify_semantic.json` / `.graphify_extract.json` → `FileNotFoundError`. Write an empty semantic file and run Part C so the merge input exists.
14. **references/update.md `--cluster-only`** — instructs "run Steps 5–9 as normal", but a prior build's Step 9 deletes `.graphify_{extract,detect,analysis}.json` that Step 5 reads → `FileNotFoundError`. The `graphify cluster-only` CLI is self-contained (re-clusters, regenerates outputs) — rely on it, don't re-run Steps 5–9.
15. **references/update.md update tail** — "run Steps 4–9 as normal" then "after Step 4 show the diff", but Step 9 cleanup deletes `.graphify_extract.json` which the diff block reads → every successful update fails at the diff. Order must be Steps 4–8 → diff (+ `rm .graphify_old.json`) → Step 9 last.

### G. `graph.json` overwrite / shrink-guard safety (`#479`)
16. **references/update.md prune** — `prune` was built from `deleted + changed`. `build_merge` already drops every re-extracted source_file from the base before merging (re-extracted files *replace* their prior contribution), then applies `prune_sources` to the *final* merged graph — so passing `changed` files in `prune` deletes the freshly re-extracted nodes, leaving `graph.json` missing that file. `prune` should be deleted-files-only.
17. **SKILL.md Step 4** — the `to_json(...)` return value was ignored; it returns `False` and writes nothing when the new graph is smaller than the existing `graph.json` (`#479` shrink-guard, export.py). A deletion `--update` then saved the manifest/report over a *stale* `graph.json`. Capture the return; abort loudly on refusal.
18. **SKILL.md Step 4 (zero-node guard)** — the empty-extraction guard ran *after* `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, `to_json(force=...)`, and `.graphify_analysis.json` were written, so an empty extraction on `--update` (with `force=True`) overwrote a good `graph.json` before aborting. Move the `G.number_of_nodes() == 0` check to immediately after `build_from_json(...)`, before any write.
19. **SKILL.md `is_update`** — `force` was decided by the mere presence of `.graphify_old.json`. An update that aborts after creating the backup but before cleanup leaves the file behind, so a later plain rebuild reads it, passes `force=True`, and bypasses the shrink-guard. Decide `force` from an explicit substituted `IS_UPDATE` flag instead (fail-safe: guard stays on if unset).
20. **SKILL.md ~438 (report before export)** — `GRAPH_REPORT.md` is written *before* the `to_json` shrink-guard runs. On a non-`--update` rebuild that produces fewer nodes, `to_json` returns `False` and aborts without replacing `graph.json`, but the report has already been overwritten — leaving the report describing a graph that queries (still on the old `graph.json`) never see. Write the report only after a successful export (or stage it in a temp file).

### H. Misc
21. **references/extraction-spec.md** — schema example uses a forbidden filename-only node ID (`session_validatetoken`), which the spec itself warns creates ghost/duplicate nodes. Use the immediate-parent+filename form (`auth_session_validatetoken`).
22. **references/query.md fallback traversal** — token filter `len(t) > 3` drops valid 3-letter vocabulary tokens (`api`, `jwt`, `ios`); the vocab threshold is `>= 3`. Align to `len(t) >= 3`.
23. **references/transcribe.md** — the transcription block redirects *all* Python stdout to `.graphify_transcripts.json` via shell `> ...json`, but `transcribe_all`/`download_audio` print progress to stdout → polluted JSON → the next `json.loads` fails. Write the file from Python (`Path.write_text(json.dumps(...))`), send status to stderr.

---

Environment: `graphifyy` v0.8.41 (PyPI), installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`; skill generated by `graphify claude install --platform claude`. All line references are to the generated v0.8.41 skill files.

title: Add native installation support and context mapping for Windsurf IDE
body:
### Main context
Currently, `graphify` provides excellent native installation profiles and hook orchestration for platforms like Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, and Antigravity. 

However, there is no direct support for Windsurf IDE (by Codeium), which is one of the most widely used AI-first editors.  
Windsurf relies heavily on autonomous context-tracking via its "Flow" state. Without a dedicated configuration pathway, developers using Windsurf cannot seamlessly feed Graphify's semantic indices (`graphify-out/graph.json`) directly into the editor's background reasoning models without manual copy-pasting.
I would like to propose adding native Windsurf integration to the CLI orchestrator. This would include:

1. **New Platform Flag**: Implementing a `graphify install --platform windsurf` target command.
2. **Automated Context Mapping**: Automatically generating or updating a `.codeium/config.json` or project-scoped rules file that explicitly points Windsurf's internal AI agent to prioritize `graphify-out/graph.json` during codebase exploration.
3. **Documentation**: Adding Windsurf configuration setups to the repository's README.

### Additional context
Adding Windsurf support will open up Graphify to a large segment of developers who rely on Codeium's AI-first editing environment.

title: v0.8.43 regression: FileSlice crashes semantic extraction for oversized Markdown
body:
## Summary

`graphify 0.8.43` regresses semantic extraction for oversized Markdown/text files that are expanded into `FileSlice` units. The string-path coercion added for #1386 now runs inside `extract_files_direct()` and attempts `Path(FileSlice(...))`, which crashes before any backend call is made.

This breaks normal `graphify extract . --backend <backend> --out .` when the changed semantic/doc corpus includes large Markdown files.

This looks related to the interaction between:

- #1369 / v0.8.42: oversized Markdown/text slicing via `FileSlice`
- #1386 / v0.8.43: `str` path coercion in semantic extract entry points
- #1389: appears to move coercion to `extract_corpus_parallel()` and allow `extract_files_direct()` to receive `Path | FileSlice`, but it is currently open/conflicting while v0.8.43 is released with the regression.

## Environment

- graphify: `0.8.43`
- install: `uv tool upgrade graphifyy`
- OS: WSL2 Ubuntu
- backend: observed with `--backend deepseek`; the minimal repro also shows the failure happens before any backend request, so this is not DeepSeek-specific

## Minimal reproduction without making an API call

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from graphify.file_slice import expand_oversized_files
from graphify.llm import extract_files_direct

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    root = Path(d)
    doc = root / "large.md"
    doc.write_text("# Large doc\n\n" + ("body text\n" * 5000), encoding="utf-8")

    units = expand_oversized_files([doc], 20_000)
    print([type(u).__name__ for u in units])  # includes FileSlice

    # api_key is dummy; the failure happens before any backend request.
    extract_files_direct(units, backend="deepseek", api_key="dummy", root=root)
```

## Actual behavior

```text
TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'FileSlice'
```

In the CLI path this is surfaced as:

```text
[graphify extract] semantic extraction on 2 files via <backend>...
[graphify] chunk 1/1 failed: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'FileSlice'
[graphify] WARNING: 1/1 semantic chunk(s) failed — see errors above. Partial results returned.
[graphify extract] error: all semantic chunks failed for backend '<backend>' (2 uncached files)
```

## Expected behavior

`extract_corpus_parallel()` may coerce user-supplied `str | Path` inputs before slicing, but after `expand_oversized_files()` the internal units are `Path | FileSlice`. `extract_files_direct()` should preserve `FileSlice` units and use existing helpers such as `unit_path()` / `_partition_semantic_files()` / `_read_files()` instead of coercing every unit through `Path(...)`.

## Suspected root cause

In the v0.8.43 installed package, `graphify/llm.py` contains:

```python
def extract_files_direct(...):
    ...
    files = [Path(f) for f in files]
```

That line is safe for `str`/`Path` inputs, but unsafe for `FileSlice` units produced by the slicer. The PR #1389 head appears to remove this coercion from `extract_files_direct()` and type it as `Sequence[Path | FileSlice]`, which matches the needed behavior. A patch release with that fix would unblock large-doc semantic extraction.

title: fix: Fix for the slicer (0.8.42, #1369), regression from 0.8.43 (#1386)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a wiring bug introduced when **#1369** (intra-file slicing, shipped in 0.8.42) meets **#1386** (str→`Path` coercion in semantic extract entry points, 0.8.43): packed extraction chunks can contain `FileSlice` objects, but `extract_files_direct` still coerced every item with `[Path(f) for f in files]`, which crashes at runtime.

## What was wrong

After #1369, `extract_corpus_parallel` does:

1. `expand_oversized_files()` — split large text docs into `FileSlice` units covering the whole file
2. `_pack_chunks_by_tokens()` — pack those units (mix of whole `Path` files and `FileSlice` slices) into parallel extraction chunks
3. `_extract_with_adaptive_retry(chunk)` → `extract_files_direct(chunk)`

#1386 correctly added str→`Path` coercion at the extract entry points, but both `extract_files_direct` and `extract_corpus_parallel` used:

```python
files = [Path(f) for f in files]
```

`Path()` cannot wrap a `FileSlice`, so any chunk that contained a slice failed immediately:

```text
argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'FileSlice'
```

This only surfaces when slicing actually produces `FileSlice` chunks — e.g. a large markdown corpus with a lowered `--token-budget` (so packing yields multiple slice-bearing chunks). With the default token budget and a small corpus, whole files may still pack as plain `Path` objects and the bug stays hidden.

## Fix

- Introduce `SemanticUnit = Path | FileSlice` and `_coerce_semantic_units()` — coerce `str`/`Path` inputs to `Path`, pass `FileSlice` through unchanged
- Use `_coerce_semantic_units()` in `extract_files_direct`, `extract_corpus_parallel`, and update type hints on `_extract_with_adaptive_retry` / `_run_one`
- Add regression test `test_extract_files_direct_accepts_file_slice`

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_file_slice.py tests/test_chunking.py` — 37 passed
- [x] Full suite with project venv — 2092 passed (5 failures unrelated: local Gemma env vars affecting backend-detection tests, wheel build dev-deps)

title: TypeError in extract_files_direct: FileSlice not handled by Path() coercion
body:

title: extract_files_direct crashes with TypeError on FileSlice (Path() wraps FileSlice; one-line fix)
body:
## Summary

`graphify extract` crashes a whole semantic chunk with:

```
argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'FileSlice'
```

whenever a chunk contains a `FileSlice` unit. This happens in two ways:
1. An oversized (>`_FILE_CHAR_CAP`, i.e. >20 000 chars) splittable doc (`.md/.txt/.rst/.mdx/.markdown`) is pre-split by `expand_oversized_files`.
2. The **adaptive-retry** path bisects a chunk into `FileSlice` halves after the model returns a hollow/oversized response (very common with local Ollama models). This makes it intermittent and size-independent — excluding large files does not avoid it.

## Root cause

`graphify/llm.py` in `extract_files_direct`:

```python
files = [Path(f) for f in files]   # line ~1311
```

This blindly wraps **every** element in `Path()`, including `FileSlice` objects (which have no `__fspath__`). The docstring just above even states the intent is to coerce only `str` entries ("string entries are coerced up front").

Traceback:
```
_run_one -> _extract_with_adaptive_retry (llm.py:1585)
         -> extract_files_direct (llm.py:1311)
         -> pathlib.Path.__init__  -> TypeError
```

## Fix (one line)

```python
files = [Path(f) if isinstance(f, str) else f for f in files]
```

Downstream consumers (`_read_files`, `read_slice_text`, `unit_path`, `_pack_chunks_by_tokens`) already handle `FileSlice` correctly via `unit_path()`, so leaving `FileSlice` untouched is safe.

## Reproduction

`graphify extract . --backend ollama` on a corpus containing a >20 000-char `.md`/`.txt`, **or** any corpus large enough that a local model returns a hollow response and triggers adaptive bisection (log shows `... truncated at depth 0, splitting into halves ...` immediately followed by the chunk failing).

## Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.8.43 (PyPI), Python 3.12, macOS arm64
- backend: ollama (OpenAI-compat `/v1`)

title: Cross-file type-annotation refs create phantom duplicate nodes (sourced stub blocks _rewire_unique_stub_nodes)
body:
## Summary

Cross-file type-annotation (and other bare-name) references create **phantom duplicate nodes** instead of resolving to the single canonical definition. A class defined once but referenced via type annotations in N other files appears as **1 + N nodes** in the graph, inflating node counts and god-node/centrality rankings, and splitting edges across duplicates.

Observed on `graphifyy==0.8.44` (AST/structural extraction, no LLM key set), Python, but the faulty code path is shared across all 6 language extractors.

## Minimal reproduction

```
pkg/thing.py
  class Thing:
      def run(self):
          return 1

pkg/a.py
  from pkg.thing import Thing
  def use_a(obj: Thing) -> Thing:
      return obj

pkg/b.py
  from pkg.thing import Thing
  def use_b(obj: Thing) -> Thing:
      return obj
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract
from pathlib import Path
r = extract([Path('pkg/thing.py'), Path('pkg/a.py'), Path('pkg/b.py')], cache_root=Path('.'))
print(sorted(n['id'] for n in r['nodes'] if n['label'] == 'Thing'))
```

**Actual (0.8.44):**
```
['pkg_a_py_thing', 'pkg_b_py_thing', 'pkg_thing_thing']   # 3 nodes
```
Note `pkg_a_py_thing` / `pkg_b_py_thing` — the file path **with extension** baked into the id, the signature of the bug.

**Expected:**
```
['pkg_thing_thing']   # 1 canonical node; the annotation refs become edges to it
```

## Root cause

`ensure_named_node` (defined identically as a nested closure in all 6 per-language extractors) builds the bare cross-file reference node via `add_node`, which always stamps `source_file = str_path` (the **using** file):

```python
def ensure_named_node(name: str, line: int) -> str:
    nid = _make_id(stem, name)
    if nid in seen_ids:
        return nid
    nid = _make_id(name)
    if nid not in seen_ids:
        add_node(nid, name, line)   # <-- stamps source_file = using file
    return nid
```

A *sourced* stub looks like a real definition, which breaks the two passes that are supposed to clean it up:

1. `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids` sees the same bare id (`thing`) emitted from two files with two different `source_file`s, treats them as distinct same-named symbols, and scatters them into per-file ids `_make_id(source_key, old_id)` → `pkg_a_py_thing`, `pkg_b_py_thing`.
2. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` — which would merge a stub into the unique real definition by label — only considers **no-source** stubs (`if node.get("source_file"): ... continue`), so the now-sourced phantoms are never merged.

This contradicts the documented design intent in `_resolve_cross_file_*` (extract.py ~9038-9046): *"Cross-file type references resolve by bare name and fall back to a no-source 'shadow' stub. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` repairs that."* The fallback simply isn't sourceless.

## Suggested fix

Make `ensure_named_node`'s bare fallback emit a **no-source** shadow stub (matching the documented intent), so disambiguation leaves it alone (`source_keys == {""}`, len < 2) and `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` merges it into the unique canonical def:

```python
def ensure_named_node(name: str, line: int) -> str:
    nid = _make_id(stem, name)
    if nid in seen_ids:
        return nid
    nid = _make_id(name)
    if nid not in seen_ids:
        seen_ids.add(nid)
        nodes.append({
            "id": nid,
            "label": name,
            "file_type": "code",
            "source_file": "",
            "source_location": "",
        })
    return nid
```

Applied to all 6 closures, this fixes the repro (3 → 1 node). On a real 348-file Python project it dropped the graph from 3771 → 3574 nodes (−197 phantoms merged repo-wide) with no over-merge: multi-definition names (`main()`, `__init__`, etc.) stay distinct because `_rewire` only merges when **exactly one** real def exists. Orphan count stayed low (8) and top god-node rankings were unchanged except the previously-split classes consolidated to their correct single node.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #1332 (skip Python primitive/library annotation nodes) — suppresses a *different* class of annotation node (primitives/external types); this issue is about cross-file refs to types that **do** have a canonical def in the corpus.
- #438 (node id collisions for same-stem files) — different mechanism (file nodes), but same family of id-scheme issues.

title: bug: `graphify install --platform hermes` installs skill to wrong directory on Windows
body:
## Bug Description

On Windows, running `graphify install --platform hermes` copies the skill to `~/.hermes/skills/` instead of `~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/`. Hermes Agent on Windows looks for skills in `~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/`, so the installed skill is never discovered.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install graphify: `uv tool install graphifyy`
2. Run: `graphify install --platform hermes`
3. Check where the skill was placed: `ls ~/.hermes/skills/graphify/` — it exists here
4. Check where Hermes expects it: `ls ~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/graphify/` — not found

## Expected Behavior

`graphify install --platform hermes` should detect the Windows environment and install the skill to `~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/` (which is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\skills\` in Windows terms).

## Actual Behavior

The skill is installed to `~/.hermes/skills/`, which is the Linux/macOS path. On Windows (using Git Bash / MSYS2), `~` resolves to `C:\Users\<username>`, so the skill ends up at `C:\Users\<username>\.hermes\skills\graphify\` — a path that Hermes Agent never scans.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Shell: Git Bash (MSYS2)
- Python: 3.11 (via uv)
- graphify version: 0.8.44
- Hermes Agent: latest

## Workaround

Manually copy the skill to the correct location:

```bash
cp -r ~/.hermes/skills/graphify ~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/graphify
```

## Additional Context

The `~/.hermes/` directory does exist on Windows (Hermes creates it for config), but the **skills** directory specifically lives under `~/AppData/Local/hermes/` (the `%LOCALAPPDATA%` equivalent). The install script should check for the Hermes skills directory at:

- Linux/macOS: `~/.hermes/skills/`
- Windows: `~/AppData/Local/hermes/skills/` (or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\skills\`)

A simple platform check like `if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "msys" || "$OSTYPE" == "cygwin" || "$OSTYPE" == "win32" ]]` would handle this.

title: feat: fall back to claude-cli backend when no API key is configured
body:
## Summary

The `claude-cli` backend is fully implemented and works great. This PR wires it into `detect_backend()` as a last-resort fallback for **headless / terminal runs** — when `graphify extract .` or `graphify .` is called directly from a shell with no API key configured.

**Context:** When `/graphify` is invoked as a Claude Code skill, semantic extraction already works without any API key — the skill spawns a Claude Code subagent that uses the active session. No change needed there. The gap is the CLI path: a user who runs `graphify extract .` from a terminal, has no API key set, but has Claude Code installed currently sees:

```
error: no LLM API key found (N doc/paper/image file(s) need semantic extraction). Set GEMINI_API_KEY ...
```

With this PR, graphify checks `shutil.which("claude")` as a final fallback and auto-selects `claude-cli`, so the extraction works without any environment setup.

## Changes

- **`graphify/llm.py` — `detect_backend()`**: add `shutil.which("claude")` check after the custom-providers loop, immediately before `return None`. Windows-aware (`claude.cmd` first). Updates docstring to reflect new priority chain.
- **`graphify/__main__.py`**: update the "no LLM API key found" error message and the post-`graphify update` tip to mention `claude-cli` as a zero-config option.
- **`tests/test_llm_backends.py`**: three new tests — (1) falls back to `claude-cli` when no keys and CLI present, (2) API key wins over CLI, (3) returns `None` when neither key nor CLI is available.

## Behaviour

| Situation | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| No API keys, `claude` on PATH (terminal run) | Error | Auto-selects `claude-cli` |
| `/graphify` as Claude Code skill | Works (subagent) | Unchanged |
| API key set + `claude` on PATH | Uses API key | Uses API key (unchanged) |
| No API keys, no `claude` | Error | Error (unchanged) |
| `--backend claude-cli` explicit | Works | Works (unchanged) |

`claude-cli` remains last in the chain — a real API key always wins.

title: Bug: `graphify install` does not install its skill to `.agents\skills`
body:
## Description

On Windows, running `graphify install` successfully installs the skill to:

```text
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills
```

However, it does not install the skill to:


which is used by other agent frameworks that support the Skills specification.

   ```bash

   ```

2. Run:

   ```bash
   graphify install
   ```

The skill should be installed to

```text
%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills
```

at least.
(or otherwise provide an option to install to `.agents\skills`).

The skill is installed only to:

```text
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills
```

No skill is created in:

```text
%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills
```

   ```bash
   npx skills init
   ```


title: Investigation: evaluate Graphify for codebase knowledge-graph workflows
body:
## Context

We've added Graphify as a git submodule in our research repo and want to evaluate it as a knowledge-graph tool that maps code, docs, PDFs, images, and video into a queryable graph.

## Goals of this investigation

- [ ] **Core workflow** — Run `/graphify .` and `graphify export callflow-html` on representative projects; assess the quality of `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `graph.json` outputs.
- [ ] **Multi-modal ingestion** — Evaluate how well it ingests non-code assets (docs, PDFs, images, video) and how those map into the graph.
- [ ] **Tooling integration & query** — Test integration across our AI coding assistants and assess querying the graph vs. grepping files (the "memory layer" workflow).

## Questions to answer

- How accurate and complete is the generated graph for our stack?
- What's the runtime/cost on large repos, and is re-indexing incremental?
- What data leaves the machine, and what are the privacy/security implications?

## Deliverable

A short write-up summarizing findings and a go/no-go recommendation.

title: to_obsidian: all-punctuation labels emit punctuation-only filenames (e.g. @.md) that break downstream slug/indexers (qmd handelize crash)
body:
## Summary

`to_obsidian()`'s `safe_name()` can emit a note whose filename is **only punctuation** (e.g. `@.md`) when a node label is all-punctuation after the unsafe-char strip (e.g. a `@/*` node extracted from a `tsconfig.json` `paths` entry). Such a filename is valid on disk, but any downstream tool that re-slugs the stem on *word* characters reduces it to empty and fails.

Concretely, it crashes `qmd` (the Quick Markdown Search CLI) on `qmd update`, because its `handelize()` reduces `@` → `""` and raises:

```
Error: handelize: path "graphify-out/obsidian/@.md" has no valid filename content
    at handelize (.../@tobilu/qmd/dist/store.js:1493:15)
    at reindexCollection (.../store.js:969:22)
```

Since `qmd update` indexes collections in a batch, this **one generated file aborts the entire run** — every other collection on the machine stops being reindexed too. Found on `graphifyy==0.8.33`.

## Root cause

In `graphify/export.py`, `safe_name()` (used in both the node export and the community export of `to_obsidian`):

```python
def safe_name(label: str) -> str:
    cleaned = re.sub(r'[\\/*?:"<>|#^[\]]', "", label. ...).strip()
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\.(md|mdx|qmd|markdown)$", "", cleaned, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return _cap_filename(cleaned) if cleaned else "unnamed"   # <-- "@" is truthy, slips through
```

For label `@/*`: the unsafe-char strip removes `/` and `*`, leaving `@`. `@` is non-empty, so the `else "unnamed"` fallback never fires, and the stem becomes `@` → file `@.md`.

## Proposed fix

Require at least one *word* character; otherwise fall back (so an all-punctuation label can never produce a punctuation-only filename):

```python
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\.(md|mdx|qmd|markdown)$", "", cleaned, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    # A stem of only punctuation ("@", "*", "#") survives the unsafe-char strip but
    # is empty once a downstream tool re-slugs on word chars (e.g. qmd's handelize()
    # → crash). Require at least one word char; else fall back.
    if not re.search(r"\w", cleaned, flags=re.UNICODE):
        return "unnamed"
    return _cap_filename(cleaned)
```

Applies to **both** occurrences of `safe_name` in `export.py`. The existing dedup logic already handles multiple `unnamed` collisions (`unnamed_1`, …).

## Repro

A node whose label is all punctuation after the unsafe-char strip (e.g. `@/*` from a `tsconfig.json` `paths` key) → `graphify-out/obsidian/@.md`. Other `@*.md` files with a word char (`@types/node` → `@typesnode.md`) are fine; only the bare-punctuation case breaks.

Happy to send a PR if the fix looks right.

title: fix(export): never emit punctuation-only Obsidian filenames (e.g. @.md)
body:
Fixes #1409.

### Problem
`to_obsidian()`'s `safe_name()` can produce a **punctuation-only filename** (e.g. `@.md`) when a node label is all-punctuation after the unsafe-char strip — e.g. a `@/*` node from a `tsconfig.json` `paths` key leaves a bare `@`, which is truthy and so slips past the `else "unnamed"` fallback.

The file is valid on disk but **empty once a downstream tool re-slugs the stem on word chars**. In particular it crashes `qmd update` (handelize() reduces `@` → `""` and raises), and because qmd indexes collections in a batch, that one generated file aborts reindexing for *every* collection on the machine.

### Fix
Require at least one `\w` char in the stem; otherwise fall back to `"unnamed"`. Applied to **both** `safe_name` occurrences (node export + community export). The existing dedup logic already disambiguates multiple `unnamed` collisions.

Behavior is unchanged for any label containing a word char (`@types/node` → `@typesnode.md` as before); only the pathological all-punctuation case changes.
