title: Python: `@receiver.name(...)` decorators bind to an unrelated module-level function of the same bare name — false edges create a god node (regression from #2154, 0.9.27+)
body:
## Summary

Python decorators of the form `@receiver.name(...)` are resolved by their **bare attribute name only** — the receiver is dropped. If any module-level function in the corpus happens to share that name, every decorated function gets a false `references` (and at scale, `calls`) edge to it, across files that never import it.

The common real-world trigger is web frameworks: `@app.get(...)`, `@router.get(...)`, `@app.post(...)`. Any project that also defines a helper named `get`/`post` gets a fabricated hub.

This appears to come from decorator edges added in #2154 (v0.9.27).

## Minimal reproduction

Two files, no import between them:

```python
# settings_store.py — project-defined module-level function named `get`
def get(key: str):
    return key
```

```python
# routes.py — deliberately does NOT import settings_store
class _App:
    def get(self, path):
        def deco(fn):
            return fn
        return deco

app = _App()

@app.get("/health")
def health():
    return "ok"

@app.get("/status")
def status():
    return "ok"
```

```
graphify . --no-cluster
```

**Actual** — `graph.json` contains:

```
references  health() (routes.py)  -->  get() (settings_store.py)
references  status() (routes.py)  -->  get() (settings_store.py)
```

**Expected** — no cross-file edge. `app` is a local `_App` instance; `settings_store.get` is unrelated and never imported.

Note the resolver also skips the *correct* candidate: `_App.get` is defined in the same file (it appears in the graph as a `.get()` node) and is the actual receiver's method, but the edge goes to the unrelated module-level function instead.

## Control experiment (isolates the cause)

Rename only the project-defined function, `def get` -> `def get_knob`, leaving the `@app.get` decorators untouched:

```
references  health()  -->  get   [stub node, source_file empty]
references  status()  -->  get   [stub node, source_file empty]
```

The edges now land on an unresolved **stub** — correct behaviour. So the binding keys purely on the bare decorator attribute name matching a module-level definition; nothing about the receiver or the import graph is consulted.

## Real-world impact

On a FastAPI codebase (197 Python files, 3.3k nodes) upgrading 0.9.26 -> 0.9.30:

- `settings_store.get()` degree: **27 -> 149**, becoming the **#1 god node** in `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, above genuine core abstractions.
- **122 of the 200 newly added edges (61%)** were this artifact (`references` 67 + `calls` 55), all `confidence: EXTRACTED`.
- Sources correlate 1:1 with route decorators, not with call sites: `api.py` has **12 `@app.get` decorators, zero `dict.get(` calls, and exactly 12 false edges**; `api_infra.py` 6/0/6. Files with both produce ~2 edges per decorator.
- Query impact: the node bridges **16 otherwise-unconnected files**, so depth-2 BFS context from any route handler is **~71% nodes pulled in through this one hub**; blast radius (nodes with it within 2 hops) went 6.7% -> 15.7% of the graph.

## Suggested direction

For `@receiver.attr(...)` decorators, either resolve `attr` against the receiver's type when known, or leave it unresolved (stub) rather than falling back to a bare-name match against module-level definitions. That matches how the rename control already behaves.

This is the same class as #2241 (call arguments binding to an unrelated same-named symbol), which was fixed for JS/TS closure parameters; the Python decorator path still has it. Possibly related: #2041 (bare-vs-dotted call resolution via label-text match), #2313 (god-node guards).

## Environment

- graphify 0.9.30 (also reproduces the artifact on a 0.9.30 clean rebuild)
- Python 3.13.12, Linux x86_64
- `graphify . --no-cluster`, AST-only (no LLM)

title: update writes manifest.json to the CWD instead of the target — cross-project contamination, and the target gets no manifest
body:
## Summary

`graphify update <target>` writes `manifest.json` into **the current working directory's** `graphify-out/`, not the target's — while every other artifact (`graph.json`, `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, `cache/`, `.graphify_root`) goes to the target correctly.

Two things break at once:

1. **The CWD project gets a foreign manifest.** Its `graphify-out/manifest.json` now describes another project's files. Any tool that reads the manifest as "what the indexer saw for this project" gets a confidently wrong answer.
2. **The target ends up with no manifest at all**, so its incremental detection has nothing to compare against on the next run.

Running `graphify update` over a list of N projects from one script therefore leaves N-1 manifests wrong and one project's `graphify-out/` holding the last-processed project's file list.

This is the same root cause family as #2081 (`built_at_commit` read from CWD instead of the extraction target), but a different field and a different code path — #2081 is `extract`, this is the `watch`-based `update` path.

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/projA /tmp/repro/projB
printf 'def alpha_only_in_A():\n    return 1\n' > /tmp/repro/projA/a_file.py
printf 'def beta_only_in_B():\n    return 2\n'  > /tmp/repro/projB/b_file.py
for d in projA projB; do (cd /tmp/repro/$d && git init -q . && git add -A && git commit -qm init); done

# run from projA, targeting projB
cd /tmp/repro/projA
graphify update /tmp/repro/projB

ls /tmp/repro/projA/graphify-out/
ls /tmp/repro/projB/graphify-out/
cat /tmp/repro/projA/graphify-out/manifest.json
```

**Actual** (graphify 0.9.13):

```
/tmp/repro/projA/graphify-out/:   manifest.json          <-- only this, and it is projB's
/tmp/repro/projB/graphify-out/:   cache/ graph.json graph.html GRAPH_REPORT.md
                                  .graphify_labels.json .graphify_root
                                  (no manifest.json)

$ cat /tmp/repro/projA/graphify-out/manifest.json
{
  "b_file.py": {                 <-- projB's file, in projA's output dir
    "mtime": 1785360486.2794108,
    "ast_hash": "259d778f11c851feb2ab5285781ebcd3",
    "semantic_hash": ""
  }
}
```

**Expected** — `manifest.json` lands next to the graph it describes, in `projB/graphify-out/`, and `projA` is not touched.

## Root cause

`detect.py:28` freezes the manifest location at **import time**, from a relative path:

```python
# graphify/paths.py:23
GRAPHIFY_OUT = os.environ.get("GRAPHIFY_OUT", "graphify-out")   # relative by default

# graphify/paths.py:224
def out_path(*parts: str) -> Path:
    return Path(GRAPHIFY_OUT, *parts)

# graphify/detect.py:28
_MANIFEST_PATH = str(out_path("manifest.json"))   # module-level -> resolves against the CWD
```

`save_manifest`, `load_manifest` and `detect_incremental` all default `manifest_path=_MANIFEST_PATH`.

`cli.py` does the right thing and passes the path explicitly (e.g. `cli.py:2472`):

```python
_save_manifest(_manifest_files, manifest_path=str(manifest_path), kind="both", root=target)
```

But the `watch` rebuild path does not — `watch.py:970`, `1009`, `1087`:

```python
save_manifest(detected["files"], kind="ast", root=project_root)
```

It passes `root=project_root`, so the correct root is already in hand, but lets the *file location* fall back to the CWD-frozen constant. The correct output dir is also already in scope as `out` — used two lines earlier:

```python
(out / ".graphify_root").write_text(str(watch_path), encoding="utf-8")

try:
    from graphify.detect import save_manifest
    save_manifest(detected["files"], kind="ast", root=project_root)
except Exception:
    pass
```

## Suggested fix (verified)

One line at each of the three `watch.py` call sites:

```python
save_manifest(detected["files"], manifest_path=str(out / "manifest.json"), kind="ast", root=project_root)
```

Applied locally against 0.9.13 and re-ran the reproduction above:

| | `projA/graphify-out` (CWD) | `projB/graphify-out/manifest.json` (target) |
|---|---|---|
| before | `manifest.json`, containing `b_file.py` | absent |
| after | not created at all | present, containing `b_file.py` |

## Side note

The three call sites are wrapped in `except Exception: pass`. A manifest write that fails for any other reason is also silent, so incremental detection would quietly degrade to a full rescan with nothing in the output to say why. Not the bug reported here, but it is why this one was invisible for so long — worth a log line even if the swallow stays.

## Workaround

`cd` into the target before calling `update` (or set the process CWD to the target per project when driving `update` from a script). With CWD == target, the frozen relative path happens to resolve to the right place.

## Environment

- graphify 0.9.13
- Windows 11, Python 3.10 (uv tool install), also reproducible with a POSIX shell

title: Semantic extractor over-attributes "uses" edges to all sibling classes in a file, not just the class that references the import
body:
## Summary
The AST/semantic extractor generates a `uses` (INFERRED) edge from *every* class defined
in a source file to a shared module-level import, rather than scoping the edge to only
the class(es) whose body actually references that import. This produces systematic
false-positive edges whenever a file mixes a "heavy" class (does real work, uses most
imports) with "light" sibling classes (a dataclass, a plain Exception subclass, a thin
container).

## Evidence
Verified by hand against source in a real project (14 false positives found across 3 files):

**app/services/audio/stream_service.py** — `StreamService` and `StreamSession` share 8
imports (Settings, 5 WebSocketEvent subtypes, AudioBuffer, AudioBufferOverflowError,
AudioValidator, AudioValidationError, VadService).
- `StreamService`: all 12 generated `uses` edges are correct — it genuinely references
  every one of them inside `process_audio_frame()` / `connect()` / etc.
- `StreamSession` (a bare `@dataclass` with 4 fields: `buffer: AudioBuffer`,
  `voice_active: bool`, `last_heartbeat_at: float`, `frames_received: int`): 11 of its
  12 generated `uses` edges are false positives. Only `→ AudioBuffer` is real (it's an
  actual field type); the other 11 (Settings, WebSocketEvent, ReceivingAudioEvent,
  VoiceStartedEvent, VoiceStoppedEvent, BufferReadyEvent, HeartbeatEvent,
  AudioBufferOverflowError, AudioValidationError, AudioValidator, VadService) are never
  referenced anywhere in the dataclass body.

**app/services/audio/audio_buffer.py** — `AudioBuffer` and `AudioBufferOverflowError`
share the `Settings` import.
- `AudioBuffer → Settings`: correct (`self._settings.max_stream_buffer_bytes`,
  `.stream_sample_rate`, etc. read directly).
- `AudioBufferOverflowError → Settings`: false positive — it's `class
  AudioBufferOverflowError(Exception): pass`, no body, no reference to Settings.

**app/services/audio/audio_validator.py** — `AudioValidator`, `AudioFrame`,
`AudioValidationError` share the `Settings` import.
- `AudioValidator → Settings`: correct (4 real reads in `.validate()`).
- `AudioFrame → Settings`: false positive — `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with only
  `data: bytes`, `duration_ms: int`.
- `AudioValidationError → Settings`: false positive — `__init__(self, message: str)`
  only stores `message`.

## Control cases (confirm the hypothesis)
- **app/schemas/websocket.py** (9 Pydantic model classes, all inheriting
  `WebSocketEvent(BaseModel)`): zero false positives. The shared relationship
  (inheritance) is captured structurally via `inherits` edges instead of an
  import-based `uses` heuristic, so there's nothing for the bug to attach to.
- **app/services/audio/vad_service.py** and
  **app/services/conversation/conversation_service.py** (one class each): zero false
  positives. With no sibling class in the file, there's no other node to
  mis-attribute the import to.

The false-positive rate is 0% in every single-class file and every file where
sibling relationships are captured structurally (inheritance) — and only appears
when a file has ≥2 classes of unequal "weight" tied together only by a shared
top-of-file import.

## Suggested fix
Scope `uses` edge generation to the specific class body (or its `__init__`/method
bodies) that references the imported name, e.g. by checking the import name appears
in that class's AST subtree, rather than emitting one edge per (class, import) pair
for every class in the file.

## Impact
Confidence score on these edges is uniformly 0.5 regardless of whether the "uses"
relationship is real (verified structural evidence, e.g. `self._settings.` reads) or
entirely fabricated — so the current scoring gives no signal to distinguish the 0%
false-positive single-class case from the ~92% false-positive case (`StreamSession`).
This also means `god_nodes`/`surprising_connections`/community detection downstream
can be skewed by degree inflation on lightweight dataclasses/exceptions that happen
to share a file with a busy class.

title: Hardcoded global skill path in _ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOW when installing with `--project`
body:
When running `graphify install --project --platform antigravity` / `uv run graphify antigravity install --project`, the files generated `.agents/workflows/graphify.md` incorrectly reference the global skill path (`~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`).

Because `--project` was specified, the workflow should point to the project-relative skill file rather than hardcoding the global user directory.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `uv run graphify install --project --platform antigravity` inside a project.
2. Inspect the generated workflow file: `.agents/workflows/graphify.md`.
3. Observe that the prompt/instructions explicitly reference `~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.

### Root Cause

The path to `SKILL.md` is currently hardcoded in the `_ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOW` template inside `graphify/install.py`:

https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/ecfcd160d56b420eb8241430fa7b5b1951c7829f/graphify/install.py#L918-L929

### Expected Behavior

When passing the `--project` flag, the generator should dynamically interpolate the correct project-level path (or relative path) for `SKILL.md` into `_ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOW` instead of defaulting to the global `~/.gemini/config/...` path.

### Environment

- **Graphify Version:** 0.9.3
- **Installation Command:** `uv run graphify install --project --platform antigravity` / `uv run graphify antigravity install --project`

title: feat(export): opt-in Focus Lens for graph.html — read dense regions as a layered tree
body:
## What

An opt-in **Focus Lens** for the interactive `graph.html` viewer: a small dotted **capture region** follows the cursor and selects the nodes under it; a larger **display panel** re-lays-out that selection as a layered tree (longest-path levels, width-aware wrapped rows, community-colored boxes, arrowed edges) that updates live as the mouse moves. Dense hairball regions become readable flow diagrams in place.

**Interaction**
- `f` / **Lens** button toggles it (off by default — the existing explorer is untouched until then)
- Move the mouse to sweep; `[` `]` resize the capture region; arrow keys nudge
- **Double-click / `h` holds** the lens: hover a box for the longer label + `file_type · source_file` tooltip (its edges highlight), click a box to inspect it in the existing sidebar panel; `Esc` releases, then exits
- The HUD legend explains the two rectangles (dotted = capture area, solid = tree panel)

## Why

Force-directed layouts are great for global structure and bad for reading a specific dense region. The lens gives a magnifier-style *focus+context* view — capture small, display big — without leaving the page, adding a mode, or touching the data model.

## Scope decisions (kept deliberately tight)

- **No CLI surface.** In-page toggle only, so generated skill artifacts are untouched — `skillgen --check`: 134 artifacts OK.
- **Byte-identical when inactive.** The lens block is emitted only for graphs with ≥15 nodes and ≥2 communities (one with ≥2 members — this also suppresses it in the aggregated community meta-graph, where every community is a single super-node). Gated-off output is byte-identical to pre-feature HTML, mirroring the `learning_overlay` inert-when-unused guarantee — test-enforced.
- **Gates on `communities`, not `community_labels`** — unlabeled builds (`--no-label`, missing labels sidecar) keep the lens.
- **No new dependencies.** Vanilla JS drawn on the existing vis.js canvas via the same `afterDrawing` hook the hyperedge hull uses; single-file HTML, offline, no build step.
- **Respects existing UI state:** legend-hidden communities are excluded from capture; node positions are read live (node drags honored); vis selection is disabled while the lens is on so clicks can't act on invisible nodes behind the panel; browser chords (Cmd/Ctrl+F etc.) are never intercepted.

## Security

Follows the #1838 discipline: all lens text renders via canvas `fillText` (inert sink) from the already-`sanitize_label`'d labels; the sole DOM sink is the HUD count via `textContent`; click-to-inspect delegates to the existing audited `showInfo()`. The lens block itself is a static, data-free constant. Tests pin a sink denylist (`.innerHTML`, `.outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `srcdoc`) with hostile node- and community-label fixtures.

## Testing

8 new tests in `tests/test_export.py`:
- emission with static-block equality (pins placement + staticness in one assertion)
- emission for unlabeled builds
- gate boundary exactly at 14/15 nodes; single-community and aggregated meta-graph suppression; small-graph absence incl. no partial CSS leakage
- sink denylist + hostile-label fixtures
- byte-determinism

`uv run pytest tests/ -q` green (3792 passed; the 4 `test_ollama_retry_cap` failures are a missing optional `openai` dep locally and reproduce on clean `v8`). `ruff` clean, `pyright` clean on new code, all inline scripts verified with `node --check`.

## Try it

```
graphify extract <some-repo> --code-only --out /tmp/lens-demo
# render graph.html from /tmp/lens-demo/graphify-out/graph.json, open in a browser
# press f, glide over a dense hub, double-click to hold, hover/click the boxes
```

Happy to adjust anything — naming, gate thresholds, default sizes, or splitting the HUD copy — to fit maintainer preferences. A `--viz lens` CLI dial could be a follow-up if #2235's `--viz` convention lands.

title: Kotlin: cross-file import + receiver-typed member-call resolution
body:
## Summary

Kotlin extraction currently produces almost no usable cross-file structure -- measured on a real ~1170-file Kotlin/Android production module:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cross-file `calls` edges | 2576 | 7543+ |
| ...of which EXTRACTED confidence | 7 | 1600+ (200x+) |
| resolved `imports` edges | 691 | ~2900 explicit + ~34.7k same-package `imports_from` |

This PR bundles five fixes, all discovered while verifying against real production Android/Kotlin code (not just synthetic cases) -- each one closes a gap that made an otherwise-correctly-typed receiver still fail to resolve.

## 1. Import resolution was silently broken

`_import_kotlin`'s edge target never matches a real node id -- it builds `target = _make_id(module_name)` from the bare imported name, but Kotlin symbol ids are file/class-qualified (e.g. `crypto_messagecrypto_messagecrypto`, not `messagecrypto`). `build.py`'s dangling-edge filter silently drops the mismatch. On the measured corpus: 14616 source `import` lines -> 691 surviving edges.

**Fix:** new `graphify/extractors/kotlin.py` -- `_resolve_cross_file_kotlin_imports`, same two-pass strategy as `_resolve_cross_file_java_imports` (global name index, re-parse per file, resolve `import a.b.C`), plus a same-package pass Java doesn't need -- Kotlin requires no `import` for same-package visibility, so every same-package file pair gets one file-to-file `imports_from` edge (not one edge per symbol -- that's the exact granularity `_has_import_evidence`'s module-import check already consumes, ~3x smaller than symbol-level for identical promotion power).

## 2. Kotlin member calls never carried a receiver

The call-walk branch for `tree_sitter_kotlin` sets `is_member_call = True` for `recv.method()` but never captures `recv` into `member_receiver` -- unlike the Swift/Java/C#/C++/ObjC/TS branches right next to it. The shared cross-file pass's `if rc.get("is_member_call"): continue` then drops every Kotlin member call with no receiver-typed resolver to pick them back up.

**Fix:** receiver capture in the call-walk (mirrors Swift's `#1356`) -- only a direct identifier or `this` receiver; a chained receiver (`a.b().c()`) is left untyped rather than guessed, same policy as everywhere else. A Kotlin `type_table` (property declarations -- explicit type or constructor-call/static-factory-call inference -- primary-constructor `val`/`var` parameters, function-body locals) is threaded out as `kotlin_type_table`, and `_resolve_swift_member_calls` is extended to also read it -- its receiver-typing algorithm doesn't care which language produced the table, so no new resolver function, just a second lookup and `.kt`/`.kts` added to the registration's suffix set.

## 3. Companion-object members had no class ownership at all

`companion object { fun getInstance() }` -- the standard Kotlin/Android singleton/factory idiom -- fell through the generic walk's default recurse, which resets `parent_class_nid`. This meant `getInstance()` got extracted with **no `method` edge from the outer class whatsoever**, so even a correctly receiver-typed call to `Foo.getInstance()` could never resolve past the class itself (a `references` edge, not `calls`).

**Fix:** treat `companion_object` as a transparent wrapper -- but recurse into its own **body's children** (mirroring exactly how the `class_types` branch recurses via `_find_body`/`body.children`), not into `companion_object`'s direct children, which include the nested `class_body` node itself and would otherwise still hit the default-recurse reset one level down. (Caught this by testing an isolated companion-object fixture after the receiver-typing fix above resolved everything *except* this pattern -- worth flagging in review since it's a subtle two-level indirection.)

## 4. Constructor-default-value and `by lazy {}` calls were invisible

Two extremely common Kotlin idioms hold their initializer call in a place the existing initializer-walk (which only looks at direct `call_expression`/`navigation_expression` siblings) doesn't see:
- `class Foo(private val bar: Bar = Bar.getInstance())` -- a call as a **primary-constructor default parameter value**.
- `private val bar: Bar by lazy { Bar.getInstance() }` -- a call inside a **property delegate**'s lambda body.

**Fix:** both get queued into `initializer_nodes` the same way Swift's `#1356` property initializers already are -- `walk_calls` naturally recurses through either node on its own, no special unwrapping needed.

## Verification

- Synthetic fixture covering all paths (explicit cross-file import, primary-constructor param typing, explicit-typed property, constructor/static-factory-inferred untyped property, function-body local, companion-object singleton via constructor-default AND via `by lazy`) -- all resolve EXTRACTED/INFERRED as expected, reproduced bit-identically from a from-scratch checkout (clean clone -> patch -> build -> same edges every time).
- Ground-truthed against real production code:
  - `MessageCrypto.encrypt()` (line 140) calling `vault.listKeys()` resolves to the correct target with the correct source line.
  - `BCryptoSecureStorage.getInstance()` (a companion-object singleton) is now correctly `method`-owned by `BCryptoSecureStorage`, and a real cross-file caller (`VoicePrintVault`, via a primary-constructor default-value call) now resolves it as `calls`/EXTRACTED -- this exact call site was completely invisible to the graph before fix #3+#4 combined.
- Zero dangling edges introduced by either new Kotlin pass, checked against the final built graph.
- No cross-language contamination risk: `type_table` is already shared per-file infra (Swift/C++ both write into it, one language per file in practice); the resolver's suffix-gate change only adds `.kt`/`.kts` to when the pass *runs*, doesn't change Swift-only corpora behavior at all (empty `kotlin_type_table` contributes nothing).

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest` full suite (I ran manual functional checks against a from-scratch checkout + real production code, not the project's test harness -- happy to add/run whatever's expected, let me know the convention)
- [x] Byte-compiles clean (`py_compile` on all three touched files)
- [x] Fresh checkout smoke test (synthetic fixture, all paths, all correct, reproduced identically across two independent clean clones)
- [x] Real-corpus before/after measurement (numbers above)
- [x] Ground-truth spot checks against multiple real call sites, including one that needed fixes #2, #3, and #4 together to resolve

Happy to split into smaller PRs if that's easier to review -- the five pieces share the same `type_table`/`initializer_nodes` infra and were each found by testing the *previous* fix against real code and hitting the next gap, so bundling them together is also how they were verified together.

title: `graphify query` omits edges between seed nodes and other visited nodes
body:
## Summary

`graphify query` returns the relevant nodes but can omit real edges between them. This occurs when both endpoints are selected as seed nodes, and more generally for cross-edges between nodes that have already been visited.

Tested against Graphify `0.9.30` and the current `v8` branch at `ecfcd16`.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
# app.py
from pricing import discounted_total

def checkout(subtotal: float, discount_rate: float) -> float:
    return discounted_total(subtotal, discount_rate)
```

```python
# pricing.py
def discounted_total(subtotal: float, discount_rate: float) -> float:
    return subtotal * (1 - discount_rate)
```

```bash
graphify extract . --code-only
graphify query "How does checkout calculate the final total?"
```

`graphify-out/graph.json` correctly contains a `checkout() --calls--> discounted_total()` edge. Both functions are selected as query seeds and both nodes appear in the output, but the `calls` edge is missing.

## Root cause

`_bfs()` and `_dfs()` in `graphify/serve.py` append an edge to `edges_seen` only when that edge discovers an unvisited neighbor:

```python
if neighbor not in visited:
    next_frontier.add(neighbor)
    edges_seen.append((n, neighbor))
```

Because all seed nodes are marked visited before traversal begins, an edge between two seeds is never recorded. The same behavior omits non-tree/cross-edges between other already-visited nodes. The rendered result is therefore a traversal tree rather than the induced subgraph described by the returned node set.

## Expected behavior

Every graph edge whose endpoints are both in the visited node set should be eligible for rendering, while preserving traversal-edge order and avoiding duplicates.

With that behavior, the reproduction includes:

```text
EDGE checkout() --calls [EXTRACTED context=call]--> discounted_total() at=app.py:L5
```

## Proposed fix

After BFS/DFS determines the visited node set, retain the traversal edges and append missing edges from `G.edges()` whose endpoints are both visited. Deduplicate using ordered endpoint pairs for directed graphs and unordered endpoint pairs for undirected graphs.

Validated locally with regression coverage for:

- an edge directly between two seed nodes;
- a cross-edge in a triangle where all three nodes are visited;
- the original CLI reproduction.

Relevant upstream tests passed:

```text
tests/test_serve.py + tests/test_query_cli.py
133 passed
```

## Disclosure

This report was prepared with OpenAI Codex at the user's request after reproducing the issue on a synthetic fixture. No private repository data is included.

title: Absolute-path node IDs with no canonical twin in SQL `references` and JS `calls` edges (0.9.28) — not covered by the #1961/#1967 fix
body:
## Summary

On graphifyy **0.9.28**, the AST extractor emits `references` and `calls` edges whose **target** ID carries the absolute scan path, while the **source** ID from the same file in the same run is correctly repo-relative. The target never matches a node and the edge is dropped at build.

This looks like #1961 (fixed in 0.9.18 via #1967) but is **not covered by that fix**. #1961 was a *duplicate* edge: the absolute-path variant always had a canonical repo-relative twin, and the fix drops the duplicate so the correct edge survives. In my corpus there is **no twin** — I checked all 224 affected refs and **0** resolve after stripping the prefix, because the repo-relative node was never created either. So the relationship isn't doubled, it's **lost**.

It also isn't limited to JS/TS tsconfig-alias imports: the clearest case here is a **SQL foreign key**.

*(Paths redacted to `users_<username>_...`; real IDs embed the absolute home directory.)*

## Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.9.28, Python 3.13, macOS 15, `tree_sitter_sql` installed
- Corpus: 187 code files (52 `.tsx`, 39 `.js`, 14 `.ts`, 11 `.sql`)
- AST extraction: 1330 nodes / 3376 edges → **615 dangling**, of which **224 (184 distinct IDs)** are this absolute-path shape

## Reproduction — SQL foreign key, both endpoints in one file

`prisma/migrations/20260723140000_kc_stock_gap_p0/migration.sql` declares `Tenant` and `StockCountSession` and adds an FK between them. The emitted edge:

```
relation        : references
source          : prisma_migrations_20260723140000_kc_stock_gap_p0_migration_stockcountsession   [node exists: True]
target          : users_<username>_yys_..._prisma_migrations_20260723140000_kc_stock_gap_p0_migration_tenant   [node exists: False]
source_file     : prisma/migrations/20260723140000_kc_stock_gap_p0/migration.sql
source_location : L92
confidence      : EXTRACTED
```

`Tenant` **is** a node — as `prisma_migrations_20260723140000_kc_stock_gap_p0_migration_tenant`. But no edge is emitted to that ID; the absolute-path one is the only edge for this FK. Same pattern on L95, L101, L104 (`stockgapevent → tenant`, `→ user`).

JS/TS `calls` targets are affected the same way, e.g. `users_<username>_yys_..._src_components_planningview_fetchinboxdata`.

Dangling edges by relation (all 615):

| relation | count |
|---|---|
| `imports_from` | 348 |
| `calls` | 179 |
| `imports` | 43 |
| `indirect_call` | 33 |
| `references` | 12 |

## Why the #1961 fix doesn't help

The #1967 fix drops the absolute-path edge *when its canonical twin exists*. Measured on this corpus:

```
absolute-leaked dangling refs recoverable by stripping the prefix : 0   (0 distinct)
absolute-leaked dangling refs with NO relative twin               : 224 (184 distinct)
```

Examples with no twin (prefix already stripped for readability):

```
prisma_migrations_20260728132311_add_record_comments_reactions_migration_user   (4 refs)
src_components_planningview_fetchinboxdata                                      (4 refs)
src_components_planningview_handlesaveinlinecontact                             (3 refs)
src_components_pushnotificationsettings_handleenable                            (3 refs)
src_components_settingsview_handlesaveofficelocations                           (3 refs)
```

So a twin-based dedupe has nothing to fall back on here — the fix needs to be at ID construction, or the referenced entity needs a node.

## Verified *not* the cause

Each measured rather than assumed; all three give byte-identical results (1330 nodes / 3376 edges / 615 dangling):

1. **Omitting `root=`.** `SKILL.md` Step 3 Part A calls `extract(files, cache_root=Path(INPUT_PATH))` with no `root=`, while Step 4 passes `root=INPUT_PATH` to `build_from_json`. Adding `root=Path('.')` to `extract()` changes nothing.
2. **Cache pollution.** A fresh empty `cache_root`, so no pre-0.9.18-shaped entry can be replayed, changes nothing.
3. **Parallel workers.** `parallel=False` reproduces exactly.

## Could not isolate a single-file repro

Extracting that `migration.sql` alone gives **0 dangling** under every variation tried — relative vs absolute input path, nested vs top-level directory, with and without `root=`. The trigger seems to need the multi-file corpus resolution context. Happy to run any diagnostic you want against the real corpus.

Incidentally, a single-file extraction of a nested path produces a *different* file-node ID depending on whether the input path is relative (`..._migration`) or absolute (`..._migration_sql`, extension retained) — possibly the same normalization seam.

## Diagnostic script

```python
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import collect_files, extract
from graphify.detect import detect

det = detect(Path('.'))
files = []
for f in det['files']['code']:
    files.extend(collect_files(Path(f)) if Path(f).is_dir() else [Path(f)])

res = extract(files, cache_root=Path('.'), root=Path('.'), parallel=False)
ids = {n['id'] for n in res['nodes']}
bad = [e for e in res['edges'] if e['source'] not in ids or e['target'] not in ids]
print(f'{len(res["nodes"])} nodes, {len(res["edges"])} edges, dangling {len(bad)}')
print('by relation:', Counter(e.get('relation') for e in bad).most_common())

miss = Counter()
for e in bad:
    for side in ('source', 'target'):
        if e[side] not in ids:
            miss[e[side]] += 1

# how many absolute-path targets have a canonical twin?  (0 here)
PREFIX = 'users_<username>_...._'   # scan root rendered as an id
rec = sum(v for k, v in miss.items() if k.startswith(PREFIX) and k[len(PREFIX):] in ids)
orph = sum(v for k, v in miss.items() if k.startswith(PREFIX) and k[len(PREFIX):] not in ids)
print(f'recoverable by stripping: {rec} | no twin: {orph}')
```

## Note on the other 347

The remaining `ref_*` external-module danglers (`ref_react` 64, `ref_lucide_react` 57, `ref_express` 40, …) are already tracked in #2191 / #2130 / #2265 / #2143, so I'm not re-filing those. Mentioning them only because together they make the health warning fire on every run, which is what sent me looking.

Thanks for graphify — the AST-only path on a code corpus is genuinely useful. Building a 1500-node graph with zero LLM spend on the code side is exactly what we needed under a token budget.

title: fix(install): stop hardcoding the global skill path in the Antigravity workflow
body:
Fixes #2319.

## Problem

`_ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOW` is one constant shared by both install scopes, but the two scopes write `SKILL.md` to different places:

| scope | skill destination |
| --- | --- |
| global — `antigravity install` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` |
| project — `install --project --platform antigravity` | `.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` |

The template named the global path unconditionally, so a project-scoped install emitted a workflow pointing at a file that scope never writes. On a machine with no prior global install the reference dangles outright; with one, it silently points at a different (possibly stale) copy of the skill than the one just installed.

## Reproduction

Both command forms from the issue, in a clean project with an empty `HOME`, before this change:

```
$ graphify install --project --platform antigravity
$ sed -n 8p .agents/workflows/graphify.md
Follow the graphify skill installed at ~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md to run the full pipeline.

$ ls ~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
ls: No such file or directory          # dangling

$ find . -name SKILL.md
./.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md      # where it actually went
```

`graphify antigravity install --project` produces the identical result.

## Fix

Rather than interpolating the correct path per scope, the workflow now names no path at all:

```diff
-Follow the graphify skill installed at ~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md to run the full pipeline.
+Follow the graphify skill to run the full pipeline.
```

This follows the convention the rest of the installer already uses. None of the six blocks in `always_on/` names a skill location — they describe behavior (`graphify query`, read `graphify-out/`) and are therefore correct in every scope. Kiro's steering file is the clearest example, and Antigravity's own `.agents/rules/graphify.md` already follows it. The workflow was the one generated artifact naming a `SKILL.md` path anywhere in `install.py`, and unlike the `always_on/` blocks it is an inline constant rather than a `tools/skillgen` artifact, so it never went through the drift guard that keeps the others path-free.

Naming the skill instead of its location resolves in both scopes: the installed `SKILL.md` declares `name: graphify` in its frontmatter, which is how Antigravity discovers it under `.agents/skills/` or `~/.gemini/config/skills/`. It also removes the interpolation, the `~`-contraction edge case, and a latent wrinkle in the idempotency check at `install.py:1013`, which would otherwise compare a project install's workflow against the global text and rewrite it every run.

Happy to switch to per-scope interpolation instead if you'd prefer the workflow keep an explicit path.

## Verification

After the change, both command forms emit a path-free workflow while the skill still lands in `.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`. Global `antigravity install` is unchanged: the skill still installs to `~/.gemini/config/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, only the workflow text differs.

## Tests

The existing tests asserted only that the workflow file exists, which is why this shipped. Added two that assert the generated workflow names no skill path — one per scope, since the constant is shared. Both fail on the parent commit and pass here.

`uv run pytest tests/ -q` after `uv sync --all-extras`: **3877 passed, 1 failed**. The one failure is `tests/test_labeling.py::test_label_communities_batches_when_over_batch_size`, which fails identically on the parent commit (3875 passed, same single failure). It is order-dependent — it asserts batch call ordering and fails 5/5 when run in isolation while passing when its module's earlier tests run first — so it looks pre-existing and unrelated to this change. Flagging it rather than touching it.

`ruff check` clean; `python -m tools.skillgen --check` reports all 134 artifacts matching.

title: dedup._score() crashes with TypeError when LLM emits non-string node id (int)
body:
## Summary

`graphify extract --backend ollama` crashes with `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'int'` during the final dedup/build step when the LLM backend emits a node with a non-string (integer) `id` field. `dedup.py`'s `_score()` calls a regex `.search()` directly on `n["id"]` with no type check/coercion.

## Traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
  File "graphify.exe\__main__.py", line 10, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File ".../graphify/__main__.py", line 466, in main
    _run_cli()
  File ".../graphify/__main__.py", line 708, in _run_cli
    dispatch_command(cmd)
  File ".../graphify/cli.py", line 3199, in dispatch_command
    G = _build_merge([merged], ..., root=target)
  File ".../graphify/build.py", line 1023, in build_merge
    G = build(all_chunks, directed=directed, dedup=dedup, dedup_llm_backend=dedup_llm_backend, root=root)
  File ".../graphify/build.py", line 864, in build
    combined["nodes"], combined["edges"] = deduplicate_entities(
        combined["nodes"], combined["edges"], communities={},
        dedup_llm_backend=dedup_llm_backend,
    )
  File ".../graphify/dedup.py", line 487, in deduplicate_entities
    winner = _pick_winner([node, neighbor])
  File ".../graphify/dedup.py", line 561, in _pick_winner
    return min(nodes, key=_score)
  File ".../graphify/dedup.py", line 558, in _score
    has_suffix = bool(_CHUNK_SUFFIX.search(n["id"]))
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'int'
```

## Root cause

For at least some image-file chunks, the LLM backend returned a node with a bare integer `id` instead of a string, e.g. (found in the semantic cache):

```json
{
  "id": 10,
  "file_type": "image",
  "source_file": "Android-Cookbook-Examples-master/RecyclerViewDemo/app/src/main/res/mipmap-xhdpi/ic_launcher.png",
  "label": "Launcher Icon (XHDPI)"
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 12,
  "file_type": "image",
  "source_file": "<another mipmap-density variant of the same launcher icon>"
}
```

Both confirmed occurrences are Android launcher-icon images at different mipmap densities. Both instances crashed the entire extraction run (a large, multi-hour, otherwise-successful pass over a 10k+ file corpus) at the very last step, after all AST + semantic extraction had already completed and been cached.

## Repro context

- `graphify extract . --backend ollama --model qwen2.5-coder:3b --max-concurrency 1`
- Corpus: ~10,600 code files + ~800 docs + ~4,600 images (large mixed reference/sample-code corpus, not a single project)
- Windows, graphify installed via `uv tool install`

## Suggested fix

In `dedup.py`'s `_score()` (and anywhere else a node `id` is assumed to be a string), coerce with `str(n["id"])` before matching, or validate/normalize `id` to string immediately after parsing LLM output, before it reaches the dedup/build pipeline. Coercing at ingestion is probably more robust since other downstream code likely makes the same string assumption about `id`.

## Workaround used

Excluded image extensions via `.graphifyignore` (`*.png`, `*.jpg`, etc.) for this corpus and re-ran — unblocks the crash, at the cost of losing image nodes (acceptable for our use case, images are low-value nodes for a code-reference corpus anyway).

title: Stale .graphify_detect.json (skill-workflow intermediates) survive repo moves with old absolute paths; never refreshed by CLI update
body:
## Summary

`graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json` (and sibling agent-workflow intermediates) keep **absolute paths from a previous repository location** indefinitely. `graphify update .` (pure CLI, also used by the post-commit hook) never refreshes, validates, or prunes them — and because they sit inside the commonly-committed `graphify-out/` directory, they travel with the repo across moves/copies/clones.

## Environment

- graphifyy **0.9.30** (uv tool), Windows 11
- Repo moved to a new absolute path (directory copy, including `.git` and `graphify-out/`)

## What happened

After the move, `graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json` still listed **555 files under the OLD absolute path** (`needs_graph: true`). It survived **three** `graphify update .` runs untouched — confirmed with a byte-level check after each rebuild.

## Root cause

`.graphify_detect.json`, `.graphify_ast.json`, `.graphify_chunks_plan.json`, `.graphify_incremental.json`, `.graphify_uncached.txt`, etc. are **skill-workflow scratch files**: written by the agent following `SKILL.md` / `references/update.md`, and only deleted by the skill's Step 9 cleanup (`rm -f ...`). The CLI itself has zero references to most of them (only `benchmark` reads `.graphify_detect.json` from the CWD, and `cache-check` writes `.graphify_uncached.txt`).

Consequences:

1. If a run is interrupted before Step 9, or the files get committed (very common since `graphify-out/` snapshots are meant to be versioned), the stale state persists forever.
2. Any later **skill-driven** run reads those stale absolute paths and can operate on the wrong tree (e.g., an abandoned previous clone of the repo).
3. There is no `doctor`/`clean`/`prune` CLI command to recover.

## Suggestions

1. **`graphify update` / `watch`**: before or after the run, prune (or regenerate) scratch files whose embedded absolute paths don't match the current scan root — a cheap root-prefix sanity check.
2. **`graphify hook install`** (or a new `graphify doctor`): also write/verify a `.gitignore` block for the known intermediates (the same list as the skill's Step 9 cleanup), so they can't be committed.
3. **Own the intermediates in the CLI**: write + delete them within a single invocation instead of relying on agent-run cleanup; or make the skill runbooks delete them in a `finally`-style step so failures don't leak state.
4. **`graphify doctor`** (nice-to-have): report stale absolute paths in `.graphify_root`, `manifest.json`, `.graphify_labels.json`, and a `core.hooksPath` that points outside the current repo.

Related: #2259 and #1151 (absolute-vs-relative path mismatch class on Windows).

## Workaround (in case it helps others)

We shipped a repo-local hygiene script that (a) deletes the known intermediates, (b) resets `.graphify_root` to `.` when it points at a foreign path, (c) fails CI (`--check`) when `manifest.json`/labels contain absolute paths or `core.hooksPath` points outside the repo, and (d) gitignores the intermediate list. Happy to contribute it upstream if there's interest.
